calls.title: The Rfotofolio Call 2026
calls.description: Rfotofolio's annual portfolio call, framed by the organisation as "community building not competition". Work is considered as a portfolio of seven images rather than as single frames, and each year a guest juror is invited to select the work that speaks to them, with Rfotofolio always sitting as a juror alongside. Photographers whose work is selected are featured on the Rfotofolio site, in future interviews and publications, and are added to The Photographers Index. Entries are accepted from 4 October 2026 and the call closes 2 November 2026 at midnight CST; selections are announced 14 December 2026. All work must be your own — AI-generated work is not accepted. There is no set entry fee: the amount is left to the entrant as a donation, and donations support Rfotofolio and the grants it awards each year.
jury: Rfotofolio and an annual guest juror

calls.title: Under My Skin Issue #2 — Euphoria
calls.description: Second issue of Under My Skin, the magazine published by the California Aggregation for Gender Diversity, a nonprofit building community, resources and public education around Transgender, Genderqueer, Intersex and Nonbinary (TGIN+) history and art. The issue asks Transgender, Genderqueer, Intersex and Nonbinary artists how they experience euphoria — a counterpoint to the clinical framing of gender dysphoria, and an attempt to imagine what affirming care for gender euphoria might look like. Photography and all other forms of visual art are welcome alongside poems, essays and articles; music and film can be promoted even though they cannot be printed on paper. Submissions are especially encouraged from artists who are multiply marginalised, chronically ill, disabled, trans, intersex, undocumented, incarcerated or formerly incarcerated, low-income and otherwise systemically excluded, and contributors may use a pseudonym. Contributors receive a digital copy of the published issue, credit lines and artwork descriptions alongside their images, and promotion through the organisation's website and social channels.
calls.summary: TGIN+ artists on how they experience euphoria. Print and digital magazine from a trans-led nonprofit; pseudonyms welcome.

calls.title: LSI 2026 Photography Grant
calls.description: Tenth edition of the Leica Society International's annual project-based grant, supported by the LSI Philanthropy Fund and Leica North America. The 2026 theme is 'To Be Seen': photographers worldwide are invited to submit an in-progress personal project in still images that creates space for people, places, communities, histories, or issues to be witnessed with care, dignity, and intention. Applications include a project description, a portfolio of 10 JPEG images from the project, a bio, and a CV. Judging runs in two phases — each juror ranks ten candidates from the qualified pool, then the jury meets to agree on a single winner from the ten finalists. The recipient receives $7,500 USD, a Leica camera and lens, and a gallery showing in Paris. Using a Leica camera is not required and LSI membership is not required. Entries are capped at 200 applications; the call closes on 4 September or when the cap is reached, whichever comes first.

calls.title: Tasweer Residency 2026–2027: As the Image Unfolds
calls.description: The second edition of the residency from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Three emerging photographers and visual storytellers based in Qatar, aged 21+, are selected for a five-month residency (1 October 2026 – 1 March 2027) at Bayt Al Wakrah in historic Old Al Wakrah City. Built around the concept of 'athar' — an Arabic word for traces, imprints and legacies — residents develop a project across documentary, conceptual, or experimental image-making. Each receives studio space at Bayt Al Wakrah, mentorship and professional development, access to local networks, and a monthly stipend of 4,000 QAR. Completed projects are presented in the exhibition 'As the Image Unfolds — The Language of Athar' during the 2027 Tasweer Photo Festival, accompanied by an online zine documenting the process. Apply with a cover letter, artist bio and statement, CV, a 15–20 image portfolio (PDF), a residency statement of intent, and 1–2 recommendation letters. Free to apply.
calls.summary: Five-month funded residency for Qatar-based photographers from Qatar Museums' Tasweer festival. 4,000 QAR/month stipend + 2027 exhibition.

calls.title: In Community: LACP's Annual Members' Exhibition
calls.description: The Los Angeles Center of Photography's annual members' exhibition, open to current LACP members — membership can be purchased online before submitting. Juror Chandra Glick, Photo Director at Artforum, selects works for the show at LACP's downtown Los Angeles gallery, October 1–November 5, 2026, with an opening reception on October 1. Prizes: 1st place $500 cash; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card plus a one-year membership; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card; honorable mentions also awarded. Entry fees are tiered from $18.75 for a single image to $150 for 31–35 images. Images and texts created by AI are not accepted.

calls.title: Raghu Rai MA-g Awards for Photography 2026
calls.description: The Museum of Avant-garde's annual photography award, chaired in 2026 by the Raghu Rai Foundation in his honour following his passing. Open to all — professionals, students and enthusiasts — on any theme; winning and shortlisted works are selected for the Museum's contemporary collection and featured online and in future exhibitions. The MA-g Awards name each edition after its judges; past photography jurors include William Klein, Nobuyoshi Araki, Graciela Iturbide and Antanas Sutkus. Photography entry is €55 single / €110 series, with early-bird, student and low-income-country discounts.

calls.title: (S)Light of Hand 2026
calls.description: The Photographer's Eye Collective's annual juried celebration of alternative, historical, and experimental photographic processes, staged at its nonprofit gallery on Grand Avenue in Escondido, California. Handmade, photo-based work is welcome — from albumen and cyanotype to ziatype, plus hand-worked digital or silver prints incorporating collage, stitching, or three-dimensional elements. The 2026 edition is juried by Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art in Carmel, with Juror's Choice and Director's Choice honors receiving an online exhibition and a printed catalog in 2027. Selected works are shown in the gallery 12 September – 31 October 2026, opening with a reception on 12 September. Open to photographers 18 and older; up to ten images per artist.
jury: Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art

All selected entries receive permanent online display, social media promotion, a digital certificate, and a profile page linking to the photographer's site. The exhibition opens 1 September 2026.

calls.fee: €6–€60 by image count & country; students free
calls.description: The annual open call from Eyeshot, the Italy-based street and documentary photography publisher, framed as 'a reading' rather than a contest. Singles (1–15 photographs) compete for cash prizes of €1,000, €500 and €250, while series of 9, 12 or 15 photographs are considered for a fully funded monograph editorial contract described as a €20,000+ investment; all finalists are published in the Open Call book. Open to everyone, everywhere, with entry fees scaled by country income band and free entry for students and those facing economic hardship. Jury: Newsha Tavakolian (Magnum Photos), Bill Shapiro (formerly LIFE), Matt Stuart, Shin Noguchi and Tavepong Pratoomwong (UP Photographers), with Eyeshot editors Marco Savarese and Lucrezia Bonarota. Submissions 3 July – 6 September 2026; winners announced 9 October 2026.

calls.title: Paper Photo Award 2026

Open to photobooks published in paper form between 1 January 2025 and 30 June 2026, whether self-published or from a publisher, with a minimum print run of 30 copies and photography as the primary medium. Enter via the online form and mail a copy of the book (delivery date decisive) by 18 August 2026; shortlist announced by 1 September.
jury: Magdalena Guzik, Museum of Photography Kraków

calls.title: PhotoMonth 2026 Open Call — Unity and Community
calls.description: PhotoMonth, East London's international photography festival (founded in 2001, relaunched in 2025), returns in October 2026 with an open-call group exhibition on the theme 'Unity and Community' — reflecting, questioning and celebrating the relationships that shape communities, identities and collective experience amid a drift toward division and discrimination. Open to all photographers and lens-based artists worldwide, regardless of age or career level, in any photographic style or medium, with experimental and expanded forms encouraged. Free to submit up to 3 images; selected artists pay a £20 participation fee (£12 concessions). Selected work is shown at The Art Pavilion, Mile End Park, London, 15–25 October 2026, with an opening celebration on 14 October. Curated by Cherelle Sappleton, Tom Hunter, Ishy Pryce-Parchment and Leah Mclaine.
calls.summary: PhotoMonth's East London festival open call on 'Unity and Community'. Free to enter; selected work shown at The Art Pavilion, Mile End Park.

calls.title: Create! Magazine Tenth Anniversary Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Create! Magazine's flagship annual juried art prize, marking the publication's tenth anniversary. Open worldwide across four categories — Photography and Digital Art (film, digital photography and new media, AI excluded), Painting and Two-Dimensional Media, Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Design, and Fiber and Textile Art. The grand-prize winner receives $1,000, a six-page editorial spread and interview in the print magazine, a podcast guest appearance, a spot in the Philadelphia pop-up exhibition (October 2026) and a social feature to an audience of 200,000+. First-place winners in each category receive a one-year Create! Collective membership ($390 value), a two-page feature, exhibition participation and a blog interview. Enter three images for $35; a limited number of fee-waiver scholarships are available on request.

calls.title: Nature in Gaudí — Ángeles Omedas Millán Prize 2026
calls.description: An international photography competition from the Fundación Antonio Gaudí, marking the centenary of Antoni Gaudí's death in 1926 — the year Barcelona holds the title of world capital of architecture. Photographers are invited to reflect, in up to three original images (individually or as a series), the inspiration that nature gave Gaudí's architectural work. A first prize of €5,000 — the 'Ángeles Omedas Millán' Award, named after one of the Foundation's benefactors — is joined by two second prizes of €500 each. The call is open to photographers, architects and the general public, with entries judged on originality and creativity, emotional impact, and narrative storytelling.
calls.summary: Antonio Gaudí Foundation's centenary contest on nature in Gaudí's architecture. €5,000 top prize, free, open to all.

calls.title: AFC Nature Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: Free nature photography contest from Arroyos & Foothills Conservancy, a Pasadena-based land trust protecting Southern California wildlife habitat. Seven categories — Birds, Mammals, Other Wildlife, Plants, Landscapes, People in Nature, and Abstract/Conceptual — plus a public-vote Viewer's Choice Award announced at a September event. Winning images are professionally printed at AFC's expense and displayed at a public awards event (2025 winners were shown at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County). Open to anyone 15 or older; images must have been taken in Southern California within the last 5 years. Up to 2 photos per category; manipulated images only in Abstract/Conceptual; no AI-generated images. Deadline 11:50pm PST.
calls.summary: Free Southern California nature contest from a Pasadena land trust — 7 categories, winners printed and shown at a public awards event.

calls.title: Elemental: Earth, Air, Fire, Water
calls.description: An international juried online exhibition built on the four elements — earth, air, fire and water — not merely as scenery but as pressure, weather, heat, erosion, breath, flood, smoke, stone, ash and atmosphere. Work may engage the elements directly or symbolically, exploring beauty, danger, memory, destruction, renewal and transformation. All two-dimensional images with an analog or digital photographic base are welcome, with no restrictions on size or year of production. The show runs online October 1 – November 1, 2026.
calls.summary: Juried online show on the four elements — earth, air, fire, water — at TCG Gallery. All photographic media; AI not accepted.

calls.title: Out of Time / Out of Place
calls.description: Photographers are invited to explore imagery that disrupts chronological and geographic sense — work addressing dislocation, anachronism, nostalgia, surreal encounters, unexpected juxtapositions, or moments that resist easy placement in time and space. Documentary, conceptual, landscape, portraiture and experimental approaches are all encouraged, in color or black and white. Selected work is shown at the A Photographer's Place gallery in Raleigh (August 7–31, 2026), with a reception on August 7.
calls.summary: Juried show on dislocation, anachronism and surreal juxtapositions at A Photographer's Place, Raleigh. Juror Dawn Willis.

calls.title: Rebecca Morse Selects 2026
calls.fee: Members from $40 (2 works); students from $30; need-based scholarships available
calls.description: An open-themed juried exhibition selected by Rebecca Morse, Curator in the Wallis Annenberg Photography Department at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), who has organized major exhibitions of work by Ed Ruscha, Barbara Kruger and Thomas Joshua Cooper. Selected work is shown at the APG Gallery in Atlanta (August 25 – September 25, 2026), with a reception on August 27.
calls.summary: APG members' juried show selected by LACMA curator Rebecca Morse. $3,000 MFA Houston Purchase Award; Atlanta exhibition.
jury: Rebecca Morse, Curator, Wallis Annenberg Photography Department, LACMA

calls.title: MONOCHROME
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: NYC4PA's international juried call MONOCHROME celebrates the special nature of the monochrome print — black and white, sepia, or shades of a single color — where emotion, texture and beauty are expressed in gradations from light to dark. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; any photographic process is welcome (2-D work only) and judging is blind. $4,000 in cash awards go to ten prizewinners — a $1,100 Grand Prize, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325 and three Third Prizes of $250 — alongside 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions, all featured in the NYC4PA online gallery and Prize Winners catalog with an award certificate. Images awarded an NYC4PA prize within the past two years are not eligible.
calls.summary: NYC4PA international juried call on the monochrome print — B&W, sepia or single-color. $1,100 Grand Prize; juror Ann Jastrab.
jury: Ann Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art

calls.title: Future Figurations Residency
calls.org: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity
calls.fee: CAD $65 application fee; tuition covered by scholarship (accommodation & meals approx. CAD $4,385)
calls.description: A five-week faculty-led thematic visual-arts residency (January 25 – February 26, 2027) exploring speculative futures, science fiction, myth-making and world-building, using futurity as an anti-oppressive, restorative and decolonizing force. Artists receive individual studio space, faculty mentorship and studio visits, weekly talks and workshops, open studios, and access to specialized production facilities and the Paul D. Fleck Library and Archives. Eligible mediums explicitly include photography and digital media. All participants receive the Banff Centre Arts Scholarship (100% tuition plus 25% of meals and accommodation).
calls.summary: Five-week Banff Centre visual-arts residency on speculative futures & world-building; photography eligible. Tuition-covered scholarship.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Artist's Book Residency Grant
calls.description: An eight- to ten-week residency for artists to produce a limited-edition book work (edition of 50–100), printing and binding their own books in WSW's studios with technical support. The grant includes a weekly stipend of $350, up to $1,000 for materials, up to $250 for US travel, free on-site housing and 24/7 studio access. Completed books enter collections at over 450 institutions worldwide, including the Library of Congress. Applications open August 1, 2026; the residency takes place the following September–June. Relevant to photographers working with the photobook and artist-book form.
calls.summary: WSW residency to print & bind a limited-edition artist book; stipend, materials, travel & housing. For photobook & book artists.

calls.title: One in Eight

Each selected artist receives €1,500 and exhibition at Fotografiska Berlin and Stockholm (October 2026), with possible activations across Sweden, Austria, Germany and Switzerland.

calls.title: Visual / Mixed-Media Artist Residency
calls.description: A 30-day funded residency (October 2026) in the Ribeira Sacra, Galicia, explicitly welcoming photography alongside video, installation and land art within hybrid visual practices. Residents stay in on-site geodesic domes and receive a travel allowance, daily stipend, meals and mentorship, with accessibility support available on request. Open to legal residents of European countries other than Spain (proof of residency required).
calls.summary: Funded 30-day October residency in Galicia's Ribeira Sacra for European residents outside Spain, welcoming photography. Domes, travel allowance, €30/day stipend and mentorship.

calls.title: Myoju Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: A fully-sponsored month-long residency (September 1–28, 2026) in Omihachiman, Shiga, Japan — about 35 minutes from Kyoto — open to visual arts, media/digital arts, literary arts and curatorial practice. Residents receive a private bedroom and studio plus shared communal facilities; artists cover their own travel and meals.
calls.summary: Fully-sponsored month-long residency near Kyoto, Japan, open to visual & media artists. Private bedroom and studio; artist covers travel.

calls.title: ECHOES — Cambridge Photography Gallery
calls.description: Open call on the idea that every photograph is an echo — of the past, of visited spaces, lived experiences and fleeting encounters, and perhaps even of things that never happened: untold stories, imagined narratives, distant futures. Both single images and series are welcome, with no single correct approach to the theme. Selected work is shown in an online exhibition July 15–30, 2026, with priority consideration for the gallery's physical Cambridge exhibition in October.
calls.summary: Every photograph as an echo — of the past, of lived spaces, even of what never happened. Online show + a physical Cambridge exhibition.

calls.title: On Film — Carlotta Gallery
calls.description: Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition celebrating film and analogue photography — work made accepting time as irreversible and every exposure as a point of no return. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with a PDF catalogue, permanent Collections-page listing, and Certificate of Recognition.
calls.summary: Celebrating film and analogue photography — every exposure a point of no return. Free to apply; virtual exhibition.

calls.title: perspective
calls.description: A Smith Gallery's juried online exhibition on the theme of 'perspective' — from point of view and camera placement to opinion, style, commentary, image collaging and post-processing, all as ways to visually articulate a personal perspective. Juror Debra Klomp Ching, Director and co-founder of Klompching Gallery in New York, selects up to 47 images. Selected work is featured across the gallery's online exhibition, Facebook and Instagram, a GalleryTalk, the online store and an exhibition catalogue, with 27 images chosen for 'The 27' hardbound fine-art book. The Juror's Award is an online solo exhibition plus 'The 27'; a Directors' Award and a $100 Visitors' Award (most Instagram likes) are also given. Open to all photographers worldwide, professional and amateur, working in any photographic medium. Online exhibition 11 September – 15 October 2026.
jury: Debra Klomp Ching, Director & Co-founder, Klompching Gallery

calls.title: John Chervinsky Emerging Photographer Scholarship 2026
calls.description: Annual scholarship from the Griffin Museum of Photography honouring photographer and scientist John Chervinsky, recognising emerging photographers with the potential to build a sustained body of work and solo exhibitions. The recipient receives a $3,000 cash award, a solo exhibition at the Griffin Museum, and a volume from Chervinsky's personal library of photography books. Open to photographers without gallery representation who have not had a solo exhibition in a commercial, academic, organisational or museum gallery — coffee shops, community galleries, libraries and academic thesis shows are eligible settings — and who have not received grant funding over $3,000; those enrolled in a photography degree programme may apply only in their graduating year. Entry is free: submit ten photographs in intended viewing order along with a bio/CV, a statement of artistic purpose and a statement on the work. The submission window opens 1 October 2026 and closes 22 November 2026, with the awardee announced by January 2027.

calls.title: Maghreb Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography award spotlighting contemporary work from the 'Greater Maghreb' and the wider Mediterranean basin — a region underrepresented in most awards. calls.title: 10th Singapore Young Photographer Award
calls.description: The 10th edition of the Singapore Young Photographer Award (SYPA), organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, the non-profit behind the Singapore International Photography Festival. This year's theme, "Echoes of Home", asks young photographers to reflect on what defines home — exploring the stories, history and heritage of place and the relationships between people, their environments, and their origins. Two age categories: Junior (13–18) submit a portfolio of 5–7 images drawn from at least three of five subjects (architecture, nature, landscape, portrait, still life); Youth (19–25) submit a connected photo series of 7–10 images. Over $8,000 in total prizes across categories, including cash awards, Nikon cameras, rental vouchers and certificates. Finalists' work is exhibited during the Singapore International Photography Festival in October 2026. Free to enter; open to photographers aged 13–25 based in Singapore.
calls.summary: SYPA award for Singapore-based photographers aged 13–25 on the theme 'Echoes of Home'. Free, $8,000+ in prizes, festival exhibition.
prose: The Singapore Young Photographer Award (SYPA) is an annual award organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, a registered Singapore charity and the organiser of the Singapore International Photography Festival. Now in its 10th edition, the award nurtures the next generation of Singapore-based image-makers aged 13 to 25.

The 2026 theme, "Echoes of Home", invites entrants to reflect on what home means to them and to those around them — the stories, history and heritage of place, and the interrelationships between people, their environments, and their origins. Submissions are made in two age categories: Junior (13–18), a portfolio of 5–7 images drawn from at least three of five subjects (architecture, nature, landscape, portrait, still life); and Youth (19–25), a connected photo series of 7–10 images.

Over $8,000 in prizes is awarded across the categories, including cash, Nikon cameras, rental vouchers and certificates. Finalists are announced in August 2026, winners in September, and the finalist works are exhibited at an awards ceremony during the Singapore International Photography Festival in October 2026. Entry is free, with submissions made through Judgify.

calls.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub Editions' series of photobooks exploring the emotional, symbolic and visual power of a single colour. The editors seek images in which yellow is present, dominant or symbolically charged, across all photographic styles. 100 images are selected for a perfect-bound printed book held in national archives including the British Library and the V&A. Pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide, up to 10 images per submission. Selected photographers receive a publication credit and a dedicated promotion page; no royalties or free copies.
calls.summary: Shutter Hub Editions photobook celebrating the colour yellow. 100 images selected; pay-what-you-can, worldwide.
prose: The Colour Library is a series from Shutter Hub Editions, each volume a visual exploration of one colour — its presence, symbolism, and emotional range across different photographic styles. Following earlier volumes, this edition turns to yellow.

The editors are looking for photographs in which yellow is present, dominant, or symbolically charged. One hundred images are selected for a perfect-bound, portrait-format printed book produced by Shutter Hub Editions and held in national archives worldwide, including the British Library and the V&A.

Submission terms are accessible: pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum, and free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. The call is open worldwide, with up to 10 images per submission. Selected photographers receive a publication credit and a dedicated promotion page linking to their portfolio; Shutter Hub does not pay royalties or supply free copies.
Submission is through the Shutter Hub website. The deadline is 16 July 2026 at 5pm UK time; entrants are notified within 12 weeks.

calls.title: Motion > Blur
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring how blur conveys velocity, gesture, and emotional tone — capturing movement within still photography to introduce surreal, kinetic qualities. All genres and processes welcome. Up to 38 images are selected for the physical gallery show (August 22 – September 12, 2026). Awards include Directors' Choice (free entry into two future calls) and five honorable mentions featured in the exhibition, printed catalog, and online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible; Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5.
calls.summary: Praxis Gallery (Minneapolis) on motion and blur in still photography. Physical show Aug–Sep 2026; printed catalog.

calls.title: Glasgow Photography Zine
calls.description: The Glasgow Gallery of Photography invites photographers worldwide to submit work for a forthcoming zine celebrating Glasgow — its people, streets, architecture, music, communities, weather, industry, nightlife, green spaces, rituals, and everyday moments. Work must relate to or have been made in Glasgow, but photographers need not be Glaswegian. All styles and processes are welcome, including digital, analogue, documentary, conceptual, portraiture, landscape, street, and experimental. Submit up to five images, individually or as a short series; selected work appears in the printed zine (£10 to buy), promoted across the gallery's social media and network. Free to submit.
calls.summary: Free open call for a Glasgow-celebrating photography zine; submit up to 5 images of the city. Worldwide submissions welcome.

calls.title: FORMAT27 Open Call — PLAY
calls.description: The FORMAT International Photography Festival in Derby, UK, invites exhibition and event proposals worldwide for its 2027 biennale on the theme 'PLAY' — experimentation, improvisation, and rule-breaking, from fun and exploration to questions of authorship and the politics of images. Open to artists, collectives, and curators working across documentary, multimedia, VR, moving image, installation, publications, performance, and participatory projects. Up to five projects are selected from around 250 shortlisted entries by FORMAT curators and an international jury. Selected artists exhibit at FORMAT27 (March 11 – April 11, 2027), receive a £1,000 artist fee plus up to £300 travel and accommodation during the launch weekend, and join a London group show at Photofusion Gallery in May 2027. Additional awards include a £2,500 production grant, a £1,000 printing credit, and exhibition opportunities at the Glaz (France) and Lishui (China) festivals.

calls.org: The Joe Center for the Arts
calls.description: Free juried DIGITAL exhibition ('Photography Without Walls') from The Joe Center for the Arts, a community non-profit art center in Port St. Joe, Florida, held online while the physical building undergoes renovations. calls.title: 19th Fòrum Fotogràfic Can Basté
calls.description: The 19th edition of the Fòrum Fotogràfic Can Basté (FFCB), a Barcelona photography forum run since 1996 by the Can Basté civic centre in the Nou Barris district. Held November 24–28, 2026 under the theme 'Retornar a les utopies' (Return to Utopias), the forum awards two kinds of free-to-enter, open-theme production grants. Three exhibition production grants of €2,000 each fund new photographic projects, with the winning works shown individually at the Sala Cava for at least 45 days between 2027 and 2028. A separate €3,000 photographic publication grant funds a photobook, edited and distributed by Ediciones Posibles. Finalists present their projects before a professional jury during the festival. Open to emerging photographic artists and collectives resident in Spain; any format or photographic technique is welcome, provided the project has not been previously exhibited or published in full.
calls.summary: Barcelona's Can Basté forum: free grants — 3 × €2,000 exhibition production plus a €3,000 photobook. For Spain-based emerging artists.

calls.title: Solstitium: Incandescent — Summer Solstice Exhibition
calls.description: Free, global open call for an online group exhibition in the Griffin Museum's Virtual Gallery, marking the summer solstice. The theme is light itself — its beauty and mythology, and how it helps us reflect on the cycles of nature and life. The museum seeks photographs that treat light as the primary subject rather than incidental: delicate, dynamic, and intentional. Juror: Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Selected works are exhibited online July 15–31, 2026. Open worldwide.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: Free global online exhibition for the summer solstice — light as the subject. Juror: Crista Dix, Griffin Museum.

calls.title: Dog Days of Summer
calls.description: Free, global open call for an online group exhibition presented by the Griffin Museum of Photography, exploring the place dogs hold in our lives — as companions, workers, protectors, muses, and family members. The museum welcomes photographs that celebrate, question, or reveal the complex relationship between humans and dogs, from photographers of all backgrounds and experience levels. Juror: Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Selected works are exhibited online August 1–30, 2026.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: Free global online exhibition on the human–dog bond. Juror: Crista Dix, Griffin Museum of Photography.

calls.title: strands of silver

All media and styles are welcome, including photography. Open to artists worldwide.
calls.summary: All-media juried online exhibition on time, aging, and memory. Photography welcome. From midwest nice art, Sioux Falls.

calls.title: Real And Wild — RAW Photography Awards 2026

Blind judging by professionals. Open worldwide, with a free RAW Junior tier for under-18s. Fees: $10 for one image, $25 for five, $40 for ten. AI-generated or AI-composited images are not permitted.

calls.description: Analog Forever Magazine's Summer 2026 online group exhibition, guest-curated by Dana Stirling and Yoav Friedlander of Float Photo Magazine. The brief turns to the outdoors — photographs that capture the sense of wonder, curiosity, nostalgia, and discovery that accompanies time spent in the landscape, and the feeling of standing where others have stood before. prose: Analog Forever Magazine is a publication and online platform dedicated to analog and alternative-process photography, founded by Michael Behlen. Standing Where Others Stood is the platform's Summer 2026 themed group exhibition, guest-curated by Dana Stirling and Yoav Friedlander of Float Photo Magazine.

The brief looks to the outdoors — photographs that capture the sense of wonder, curiosity, nostalgia, and discovery that accompanies time spent in the landscape, and the feeling of standing where others have stood before.

Eligibility is restricted by process: this is an analog/film exhibition and every submitted work must include at least one analog component. Fully digital photographs and AI-generated images are not eligible. One image per artist.

Application is free, submitted through a Google Form. Entrants provide a short bio, a note on how the photograph reflects the theme, and a formatted caption listing camera type and film stock or process.
The exhibition launches online on August 28, 2026; the submission deadline is August 1, 2026.

calls.title: Legacy
calls.description: Founding exhibition of Ajanaku Gallery — a photo-and-text show exploring Afro-Caribbean heritage, transmission, and memory, built on the idea of 'what our ancestors left us, and what we will leave to the world.' Open internationally to photographers, writers, and poets: works pair images (portraits, symbolic scenes, ritual objects, revisited traditional garments) with integrated texts such as original poems, African and Caribbean proverbs, letter fragments, and meditative writing. Free to enter through the gallery's online form; submit up to two works as high-resolution JPG, PNG, or PDF (max 10MB each, no zip files). Selected artists become part of the gallery's founding narrative, with their work shown in the exhibition and an accompanying publication. The exhibition runs 16–23 December 2026 in Neuilly-Plaisance, France.
calls.summary: Ajanaku Gallery's founding photo-and-text show on Afro-Caribbean heritage. Free; up to two works pairing image and text. Neuilly-Plaisance, France, Dec 2026.

calls.title: The City Series: London — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for The City Series: London, the next volume in Shutter Hub Editions’ ongoing series of photobooks exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Rather than documenting a location as a fixed subject, the series invites photographers to respond to a city as an idea — something experienced, observed, imagined, and interpreted through the photographic eye. Selected images are featured in a printed 100-image photobook, sold through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists, with a launch event in London on 20 November 2026. Pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide, up to 10 images per submission.
calls.summary: Shutter Hub Editions photobook responding to London as an idea — experienced, observed, imagined. Pay-what-you-can, worldwide.
prose: The City Series is an ongoing publication series from Shutter Hub Editions exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Each volume is built around a single city; following the inaugural Cambridge edition, the next volume turns to London.

The brief is interpretive rather than documentary. Rather than documenting a location as a fixed subject, the series invites photographers to respond to a city as an idea — something experienced, observed, imagined, and interpreted through the photographic eye.

Selected images are featured in a printed 100-image photobook produced by Shutter Hub Editions, sold through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Shutter Hub does not pay royalties or supply free copies; the reward is inclusion, attribution, and promotion across Shutter Hub networks, with selected photographers invited to a launch event in London on 20 November 2026.

Submission terms are accessible: pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum, and free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. The call is open worldwide, with up to 10 images per submission.
Submission is through the Shutter Hub website. The deadline is 12 November 2026 at 5pm UK time; selections are communicated within 12 weeks of the deadline.

calls.title: Festival di Fotografia a Capri 2026 — Viaggi e Miraggi
calls.description: Open call for the 18th edition of the Festival di Fotografia a Capri, organised by Fondazione Capri, on the theme 'Viaggi e Miraggi' (Travels and Mirages) — inspired by the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto and exploring real and imagined journeys. Open worldwide to photographers, amateurs and professionals, free of charge. Submit a project as a single PDF in a .zip folder (max 10MB) by email to festival@fondazionecapri.org, with the images, a short descriptive text, and a biography. A jury formed by the Directorate of Museums and Archaeological Parks of Capri and Fondazione Capri selects the winning project, exhibited at the Chiostro della Certosa di San Giacomo during the festival, 30 August – 11 October 2026.
calls.summary: Free open call for the 18th Festival di Fotografia a Capri, theme 'Viaggi e Miraggi'. Winner exhibited at the Certosa di San Giacomo.
prose: The Festival di Fotografia a Capri is an annual photography festival organised by Fondazione Capri, held at the Chiostro della Certosa di San Giacomo — a 14th-century charterhouse on the island of Capri. The 18th edition runs 30 August – 11 October 2026, opening 29 August, and is themed 'Viaggi e Miraggi' (Travels and Mirages), inspired by the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto.
The open call invites photographers worldwide — amateurs and professionals alike — to submit a project responding to the theme of real and imagined journeys. There is no entry fee.

Submissions are made by email to festival@fondazionecapri.org as a single PDF inside a .zip folder no larger than 10MB, containing the project images, a brief descriptive text, and the author's biography. The open call opened 30 March 2026 and closes 5 July 2026 at 23:59.

A jury formed by the Directorate of Museums and Archaeological Parks of Capri together with Fondazione Capri selects one winning project, announced 13 July 2026, which is exhibited at the Certosa di San Giacomo as part of the festival programme alongside the invited photographers.
jury: Musei e Parchi Archeologici di Capri & Fondazione Capri

calls.title: Gaze – The Queer Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Annual queer photo award created by and for the LGBTQIA+ community, hosted in Germany by Brendel, Vogel & Weber GbR (agency Vielformat) with camera reseller MPB as sponsor. The 2026 theme, 'HOW TO / GATHER – Queer Communities in Photography', seeks work exploring queer spaces, forms of community, care and chosen families — relationships beyond heteronormative-patriarchal norms, and what happens when queer spaces are under threat. Open to LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists aged 18+ resident in Germany, the EU or the UK. Submit a project of 1–5 photographs or a series of up to 5 images, taken within the last five years. A National and an International first prize of €1,000 each (MPB vouchers) plus a €500 Audience Prize are awarded; winning entries are shown in an exhibition in Berlin in winter 2026.
calls.summary: Queer photo award (theme 'HOW TO / GATHER') for LGBTQIA+ artists in Germany, EU & UK. Two €1,000 MPB vouchers plus a Berlin exhibition.
prose: GAZE – the queer Photo-Award is an activist cultural project with a nationwide presence in Germany and international reach, created by and for the LGBTQIA+ community. It is run by Nadja Brendel, Judith Weber and Han Vogel under the agency Vielformat, hosted by Brendel, Vogel & Weber GbR as a non-profit project, with MPB — Europe's leading used-camera reseller — as its 2026 sponsor.

The 2026 theme, 'HOW TO / GATHER – Queer Communities in Photography', focuses on queer spaces as places of gathering where identities can unfold freely. It asks what friendship, romantic love and family mean beyond heteronormative-patriarchal norms, and what happens when queer communities are threatened and access to queer spaces is denied.

Entry is open to lens-based artists who identify as part of the LGBTQIA+ community, are at least 18, and reside in Germany, the EU or the UK. Participants submit one project of 1–5 individual photographs, or a series of up to five images, taken no more than five years ago, via Picter. The entry fee is €15 per submission; submissions opened 15 June and close 31 August 2026.

GAZE awards a National first prize and an International first prize of €1,000 each (as MPB vouchers), plus a €500 Audience Prize. Winning entries are presented in an exhibition in Berlin in winter 2026.

calls.title: Are Men OK?
calls.description: Open call from Fotografiska Emerging and Fotografiska Stockholm, in partnership with the men's-issues organisation MÄN and timed to Men's Health Week, inviting emerging photographers and visual artists to explore what it means to be a man in Sweden today. Submissions may address identity, belonging, loneliness, friendship, care, vulnerability, strength, community, tradition or change — through personal stories, documentary perspectives, staged images, intimate observations or broader social reflections, with a particular welcome for voices and experiences rarely given space. Selected works will be presented in a group exhibition at Fotografiska Stockholm in autumn 2026. Curated by Fotografiska's Johan Vikner and Sofia Liljergren. Free to enter.
jury: Johan Vikner, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Sofia Liljergren, Exhibition Producer, Fotografiska Stockholm

calls.title: FLOAT Magazine — Let's Get the F@!#k Outta Here

FLOAT is an independent photography magazine that welcomes all photographic styles and looks for cohesive, thought-out bodies of work. Selected photographers are published in the printed issue and receive a complimentary contributor copy (the artist covers shipping); additional copies are sold online and at book fairs, and photographers retain full copyright. Submit 1–10 images for a $9 entry fee via the magazine's store and a linked form.
calls.summary: FLOAT Magazine's print issue on looking beyond Earth — Mars, UFOs, space, escape. Lens-based work, 1–10 images, $9 entry.
prose: FLOAT is an independent photography magazine that publishes themed print issues alongside online portfolios, exhibitions, and Instagram takeovers. For this call, the issue "Let's Get the F@!#k Outta Here" invites artists to consider humanity's growing fascination with looking beyond Earth — Mars, UFOs, space travel, and extraterrestrial life — and the search for meaning, possibility, or escape it reflects.

The magazine accepts all photographic styles and looks for cohesive bodies of work. Entry is $9 for 1–10 lens-based images (JPEG, 1200px on the long side), paid through the FLOAT store, with submissions completed via a linked Google form. Selected photographers appear in the printed issue and receive a complimentary copy (shipping paid by the artist); they retain full copyright. The deadline is July 10, 2026 at midnight EST.

calls.title: Raccont'Arti: Contemporary Photography Award 2026
calls.description: Free international award mapping the state of contemporary photography, promoted by Fondazione Teatro del Popolo, Ente Cambiano, Centro Culturale Cambio and the Municipality of Castelfiorentino in Tuscany. The 2026 theme is 'Beyond the visible: the image of absence' — absence as space-time stratification, mapping what remains when action subsides. Submissions are projects only (10–30 images) in documentary, artistic or hybrid approaches, in two categories: Open (€3,000) and Student (€500, for current students or graduates within the past year). Winners plus four finalists per category join a group exhibition at Centro Culturale Cambio, with exhibition production and award-ceremony accommodation fully covered by the Prize.
calls.summary: Free call on 'the image of absence' — €3,000 Open and €500 Student awards plus a fully produced group exhibition in Tuscany.

calls.title: San Francisco Photobook Fair 2026
calls.description: The San Francisco Photobook Fair returns to the Harvey Milk Photo Center on October 17–18, 2026, following its first edition in 2025. Photobook publishers, individual artists, collectives and zine makers worldwide can apply for a table to display and sell image-forward publications — anything from zines and hand-bound books to folios, sculptural books and coffee-table titles. Accepted vendors are notified July 16; tables are $200 (full, wall access), $150 (full) or $75 (half), and limited scholarships for free or discounted tables are allocated based on need. Vendors handle their own sales and may also propose a talk or workshop for the event.
calls.summary: Photobook fair at the Harvey Milk Photo Center, Oct 17–18. Publishers, artists and zine makers apply for tables; scholarships available.

calls.title: Women Street Photographers Exhibition Call 2026
calls.description: Annual exhibition call from Women Street Photographers, open to women and non-binary photographers of any age, anywhere in the world, using any camera or phone. calls.title: God Is Dead — Premio BìFoto Fest 2026

calls.title: ProfiFoto New Talent Award 26/2
calls.description: Second 2026 round of the New Talent Award from German photography magazine ProfiFoto, run in cooperation with Canon, WhiteWall and Hahnemühle for aspiring photographers who want to present their work to a professional audience. Submit a project concept (max. 2,000 characters) with 5 to 10 sample images reflecting your personal visual language — the call is open theme and open to any photographer. Winning works are published in ProfiFoto and shown as WhiteWall prints in a group exhibition; from the ten winning works across the year's two rounds, the jury selects the three best for cash prizes totaling €3,000.
calls.summary: German photo magazine's open call for emerging talent. Winners published in ProfiFoto, WhiteWall print exhibition, €3,000 cash pool.
jury: Editors of ProfiFoto, brand partners & independent photo curators

calls.title: Street Photography Barcelona Contest 2026 — 2nd Edition
calls.description: Second edition of the Street Photography Barcelona Contest (SPBC), run by the team behind Ibizacinefest under the theme 'The Street Is Art'. Open worldwide to photographers 18+, with 1, 3 or 5 single images (€10/€25/€40) of spontaneous street photography taken in public spaces within the last two years — no AI or manipulated work, no journalistic photos or artificially lit portraits. Twenty-five finalists are exhibited at Galerie Art Nomade in Barcelona's Born district, November 6–9, 2026, with printing, framing and installation fully covered, and screened at Ibizacinefest in March 2027. Cash prizes of €500 (overall winner, including a flight and hotel to present in Ibiza) and two €250 special mentions are paid before the festival. Jury led by Xavi Herrero and Olivier Verdier.

calls.title: TSHOW PHOTO.1
calls.description: First photography-dedicated edition of TSHOW, the international juried exhibition from Texas nonprofit Tyler Art Lift, created to highlight the diversity of contemporary photographic practice — traditional, experimental, documentary, conceptual, film and digital. Juried by Latvian fine art and fashion photographer Kristine Madjare, whose work has appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and Financial Times. Exhibition at Gallery Main Street in Tyler, Texas, October 15–24, 2026, with cash prizes of $1,000 Best in Show, $500 runner-up and a $500 People's Choice chosen at the opening. Open internationally to artists 18+; $45 for the first entry, $5 each additional; 30% sales commission supports the show.
calls.summary: First photography edition of Tyler Art Lift's international TSHOW, juried by Kristine Madjare. $2,000 in cash prizes at Gallery Main Street.

calls.title: Hamburg Portfolio Review 2026
calls.description: Annual call from the Hamburg Portfolio Review, hosted by the FREELENS Foundation and supported by the Hamburg Ministry of Culture and Media and Canon Europe. A jury selects 100 photographers, who each meet one-on-one with up to 4 of more than 50 international reviewers — editors, publishers, curators, festival and museum professionals — in virtual sessions, and selected portfolios are also shown in exhibitions in Hamburg. Open to photographers over 18 worldwide; the focus is narrative photography rather than commercial or advertising imagery. Submit two projects of up to 10 images each or one project of up to 20 images. Free to enter; the 2026 deadline has been extended to June 14.
calls.summary: Free FREELENS call — 100 photographers get 1:1 virtual reviews with 50+ international experts plus exhibitions in Hamburg.

calls.title: Bourse Photographe 2026 — Fondation Jean-Luc Lagardère
calls.description: Annual €10,000 grant from the Fondation Jean-Luc Lagardère for a professional photographer aged 35 or under who wants to carry out a documentary photography production — in the social, economic, political or cultural field — in France or abroad. Applicants must already have published at least two documentary projects in the press, in a book or in an exhibition catalogue. The application dossier is submitted online and the project must be presented in French. Recent laureates include Marion Péhée, Aline Deschamps and Adrienne Surprenant.
calls.summary: €10,000 from the Fondation Jean-Luc Lagardère for a documentary photography project by a photographer aged 35 or under.

calls.title: The Big Picture
calls.description: Texas Photographic Society juried exhibition celebrating large-format photography, on view at the Arlington Museum of Art from August 7 to November 1, 2026. Juror Dornith Doherty, 2012 Guggenheim Fellow, selects work that holds a monumental wall — monumentality, intimacy through detail, excess, immersion and presence. All accepted works are professionally printed at around 40 inches wide at no cost to the artist, sponsored by Fort Worth Camera, the Print Refinery and Red River Paper. Open internationally to photographers 18 and over; submit up to 12 images. Works previously exhibited in a TPS show are not eligible.
calls.summary: TPS juried show at the Arlington Museum of Art — accepted works printed ~40 inches wide at no cost. Juror Dornith Doherty.

calls.title: PhotoMidwest Biennial Exhibition 2026
calls.description: 14th biennial juried exhibition from PhotoMidwest, the Madison, Wisconsin photography nonprofit, presented in collaboration with Promega Art Showcases. Open to photographers living or working in 13 Midwest states (IA, IL, IN, KS, KY, MI, MN, MO, ND, NE, OH, SD, WI), with all photographic approaches welcome — film, digital and alternative processes. Juror Karen Irvine, Chief Curator and Deputy Director of the Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia College Chicago, awards a $1,000 Best of Show and three $250 Images of Distinction. The exhibition runs September 17, 2026 – February 26, 2027 across Promega's Art Showcase gallery, PhotoMidwest Studio and UW–Madison's Pyle Center. PhotoMidwest members receive a $10 discount on the entry fee.
jury: Karen Irvine, Chief Curator, Museum of Contemporary Photography
calls.summary: Juried biennial for photographers in 13 Midwest states — $1,000 Best of Show, juried by MoCP chief curator Karen Irvine.

calls.title: Penland Resident Artist Program
calls.description: Penland School of Craft's long-running residency for professional craft artists at a pivotal moment in their practice, on its campus in the North Carolina mountains. Two options are offered: a 1-year project-based residency and a 3-year career-transition residency, both beginning March 15, 2027. Photography is among the accepted media alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, paper, printmaking, textiles and wood (hot glass excluded this cycle). Residents receive a private studio and apartment with utilities included, meals while school is in session, one tuition-free workshop annually and studio representation at the Penland Gallery — no housing or studio rental fees. No prior connection to Penland is required; reduced application fees are available on request.
calls.summary: 1-year and 3-year residencies at Penland School of Craft — private studio, housing and meals; photography included.

calls.title: Penland Winter Residency 2027
calls.description: A self-directed project residency during Penland's quiet winter season, offering artists two- or four-week sessions of studio time and equipment access with no classes, assignments or critiques. Residents work independently in one of Penland's teaching studios — photography is among the available studios, alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, papermaking, printmaking, textiles and wood — with studio assistants on hand for orientation and equipment help. Sessions run January 3–15 and January 17–29, 2027; the residency fee is $500 for two weeks (more for flameworking and hot shop) plus housing, and limited fellowships cover the residency fee and partial housing, with preference given to first-time applicants and artists from underrepresented backgrounds. Open to artists at any career stage who are comfortable working independently.
calls.summary: Self-directed 2- or 4-week winter residency at Penland with studio and equipment access; photography included. Fellowships available.
jury: National panel of artist peers, curators & Penland staff

calls.title: Celebrate Colorado: Show Us Your Downtown
calls.description: Colorado Photographic Arts Center juried online exhibition celebrating downtowns across Colorado — historic landmarks, civic spaces, contemporary developments and architectural details, with interpretations of 'downtown' intentionally open. Open to Colorado photographers 18 and over; film, digital, mobile and screen-capture work are all accepted. Thirty images are selected by juror Darrin Alfred, Curator of Architecture and Design at the Denver Art Museum, for an online exhibition on CPAC's website from August 21 to December 31, 2026. Best in Show and honorable mentions receive CPAC memberships.
jury: Darrin Alfred, Curator of Architecture and Design, Denver Art Museum
calls.summary: CPAC juried online show of Colorado downtowns, selected by Denver Art Museum curator Darrin Alfred. Colorado artists 18+.

calls.title: Grenze OFF Circuit 2026 — Nachleben
calls.description: Open call for the OFF Circuit of Grenze – Arsenali Fotografici's Nachleben photography festival in Verona, Italy. Free to enter and open to professional, emerging, and self-taught photographers 18 and over, individually or as collectives. Submit a photographic project of up to 10 images on the theme Nachleben — the survival and afterlife of images, after Aby Warburg. Selected projects are shown in an open-air exhibition at Corte Dogana Fiume and the Garden of the Bastione delle Maddalene during the festival, September 18–30, 2026, with the official OFF opening on September 18. Finalists are contacted by July 15; selected artists cover their own printing and shipping costs following the curator's instructions. Projects exploring water, borders, archives, identity, and natural landscape are favoured for the Antica Dogana di Fiume venue.
jury: Yvonne De Rosa, Founder & Artistic Director, Magazzini Fotografici
calls.summary: Free open call for the OFF circuit of Grenze's Nachleben festival in Verona — selected projects shown open-air, September 2026.

calls.title: The Extravagance of the Quotidian — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Miami-based artist Hermes Berrío. The theme invites work that transforms the everyday — ordinary objects, domestic rituals, street corners, gestures, and fragments of daily life — into something undeniable, holding memory, identity, struggle, humor, and grace. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages. Selected works are displayed on Miami bus shelters for at least one month starting July 31, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard and transit exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.
calls.summary: Miami bus-shelter public art show curated by Hermes Berrío. Theme: the beauty and weight of everyday life.

calls.title: Ephemere Triptychs — Publication & Exhibition
calls.description: Open call for the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo (October 17–27), themed 'Triplicities.' Submit photographic triptychs — three horizontal images forming a deliberate narrative, conceptual, or aesthetic sequence. Selected triptychs are featured in a curated group photobook and shown in a dedicated exhibition at the festival (Three Space Tokyo, Asakusabashi). Three 'Best Triptychs' are additionally featured in the Ephemere Photo Journal Volume 2, printed in newspaper format with Kyoto Shimbun, and receive complimentary copies. Curated on a rolling basis by Ephemere founder Anne Murayama with Sarah Mae Bombay and Alfred Ong. Color or black-and-white; digital, film, or alternative process welcome. The $60 flat fee covers 1–3 triptychs (up to 9 images) and funds curation, design, printing, and the gallery installation; all contributors receive a 25% shop discount.
calls.summary: Submit photographic triptychs for Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo — selected work published in a group photobook and exhibited.

calls.title: 7th Annual Spotlight Member Exhibition
calls.org: Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Annual juried exhibition for members of the Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts (RICPA), juried by photographer and educator Neal Rantoul. Each entry is a set of five photographs that together tell a story or present a unified idea, juried as a complete set. One selected member wins a solo show in RICPA's Focus Gallery in 2026. Open to all current RICPA members — membership can be purchased at the time of entry; entry is free for Supporting Members and above and $35 for Exhibiting and Community Members. Selected work is shown in the gallery from August 20 to September 11, 2026 and online, and every entrant receives a live Zoom portfolio review with the juror.
calls.summary: Juried members' show at the Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts. Five-image sets; one member wins a 2026 solo show.

calls.description: Free online photography exhibition exploring the emotional residue of human connection — the invisible architecture that feelings leave behind through atmosphere, absence, intimacy, silence, longing, routine, emotional distance, and memory. Curated and juried by the Decagon Gallery team. Selected work appears in a curated online exhibition with catalog, a dedicated exhibition page, an Instagram feature, and individual curatorial reflections responding to each submission. Exhibition August 15 – October 15, 2026. Open to photographers worldwide; all styles and processes welcome.
calls.summary: Free online photography exhibition on the emotional residue of human connection. Catalog plus individual curatorial reflections.

calls.title: Abandoned
calls.description: Themed call exploring abandonment — physical, emotional, environmental, social, or symbolic — through images of absence, decay, isolation, memory, transition, and what remains. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: Marty Evans. Exhibition July 8–31, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC, with an opening reception July 10, 7–9 PM. Selected artists may optionally have work printed in-house on the gallery's Canon ImagePROGRAF Pro-1100.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition on abandonment — decay, absence, what remains. Juror Marty Evans. Optional in-gallery printing. Raleigh, NC.

calls.title: Summer Open 2026
calls.description: Open-theme juried photography exhibition at Gallery PHOTIQ, a fine-art photography gallery in Royal Leamington Spa. Selected works are printed, mounted and framed at no cost to the artist, with a percentage of any sales paid to the photographer. The Curator's Award may lead to a solo exhibition.
jury: Nat Coalson ARPS, Director, Gallery PHOTIQ
calls.summary: Open-theme juried show at a Leamington Spa fine-art gallery. Free printing & framing, cash prizes, possible solo exhibition.

calls.title: Viewpoint Photographic Art Center — 2027 Call for Exhibit Proposals
calls.description: Sacramento non-profit photography center seeking proposals for solo and group exhibitions running January–December 2027. Maximum two proposals per artist; past solo exhibitors must wait three years before another solo show.
calls.summary: Proposals for solo/group photography exhibitions in 2027 at Sacramento's Viewpoint center. Submit 20 images + statement.

calls.summary: Two photographers exhibit at Millepiani, Rome. Theme: Cycle(s). Printing covered. Guest juror Carolyn Mendelsohn.

calls.title: Still, Life
calls.description: Quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms on the theme Still, Life — everyday photography sitting in the tension between motion and pause, living and lingering, presence and aftermath — with guest judge Elliott Gunn. 35 selected photographers are featured in a group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London, each receiving a complimentary zine copy and their exhibition print to take home. Three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition at year's end with curatorial direction from Elliott Gunn. Any photographic method accepted — analog, digital, or alternative process. Exhibition opens July 30, 2026.
calls.summary: Quarterly themed open call — Still, Life. 35 photographers in a group show and zine at The Photobook Cafe, London.
prose: The Photobook Cafe is a London photography venue with a café, exhibition space, and bookstore focused on photobooks. Rapid Eye Darkrooms is a London photographic printing service. Together they run a quarterly themed open call; Still, Life follows LOVE and Womanhood in the series.

The brief is everyday photography — the moments that sit in the tension between motion and pause, living and lingering, presence and aftermath. Any photographic method is accepted: analog, digital, or alternative process, with images from anywhere in the world.
The guest judge is Elliott Gunn, known for candid, cinematic photographs built on fleeting gestures, shadow and light, and the quiet tension of public spaces.

Selection structure has two tiers. Thirty-five selected photographers are featured in a group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe, each receiving a complimentary zine copy and their physical exhibition print to take home. From the 35, three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition at the end of the year with curatorial direction from Elliott Gunn.

Submission is through Photobook Cafe's website at £25 per entry of 10 images; multiple entries are allowed. Open to emerging, established, and amateur photographers of any age, background, and identity. The deadline is July 20, 2026 at midnight, with the exhibition opening July 30.

calls.title: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 (CUPOTY 8)
calls.description: The 8th edition of CUPOTY, the international competition dedicated to close-up, macro, and micro photography. Eleven categories cover Animals, Insects, Invertebrate Portrait, Arachnids, Butterflies & Dragonflies, Underwater, Plants, Fungi & Slime Moulds, Intimate Landscape, Studio Art, and Young CUPOTY (under 18). The overall winner receives £2,500 plus a macro kit and trophy; category winners receive £250 each. Earlybird pricing runs to June 7; entries accepted up to a week after the July 12 deadline.
jury: Karine Aigner, Wildlife Photographer of the Year
calls.summary: International macro & close-up competition — 11 categories from insects to intimate landscapes. £2,500 top prize.
prose: Close-up Photographer of the Year (CUPOTY) is an international competition celebrating the small world — the macro, micro, and close-up imagery that rewards patience and a careful eye. The 8th edition (CUPOTY 8) is open for entries now, judged by a panel of specialist photographers.

Entries are spread across eleven categories: Animals, Insects, Invertebrate Portrait, Arachnids, Butterflies & Dragonflies, Underwater, Plants, Fungi & Slime Moulds, Intimate Landscape, Studio Art, and a dedicated Young CUPOTY category for entrants under 18. Each category carries its own shortlist, so a single strong frame can rise on its own merits.

The overall winner receives £2,500 in cash, a macro kit, and a trophy; each category winner receives £250 and a certificate, and the Young CUPOTY winner receives £300. More than 60 shortlist places are awarded per category, and finalists gain wide exposure through the competition's books and exhibitions.

Entry is tiered: £22 for 6 pictures, £33 for 15, or £44 for 30 (earlybird discounts apply until June 7), with Young CUPOTY entry at £5 for 15 pictures. Registration takes only a couple of minutes and images can be uploaded later. The final deadline is July 12, 2026, with submissions accepted up to one week afterwards.

calls.title: Self — Carlotta Gallery
calls.description: Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition on self-portraiture — a practice as old as photography itself. The call welcomes portraits that examine how one appears and how one is momentarily held by the camera, from literal self-portraits to conceptual approaches to identity and presence. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, Collections-page listing, and certificate.
calls.summary: Self-portraiture virtual exhibition — how one appears and is held by the camera. Free to apply, pay if selected.
prose: Carlotta Gallery is a UK-based virtual photography gallery that runs themed open calls roughly bi-monthly. "Self" turns to self-portraiture — a practice as old as photography itself — inviting work that examines how one appears and how one is momentarily held by the camera.

Both literal and conceptual approaches are welcome: a straight self-portrait, a study of identity and presence, or a more oblique meditation on the self. The jury is open to any interpretation that engages seriously with the theme.

The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected: £20 for one accepted artwork, £30 for two, or £35 for three. There are no cash prizes — selection is the recognition. Selected work is shown in a virtual online exhibition for a minimum of six months and up to a year, with permanent placement on the Carlotta Gallery Collections page, a free PDF catalogue, a Certificate of Recognition, and possible feature on the gallery's Instagram (@carlottagallery).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. Each photographer submits up to 3 JPG images by email with name, Instagram handle, biography, artist statement, and artwork details. The deadline is July 10, 2026.

calls.title: Colours III — Carlotta Gallery
calls.description: The third edition of Carlotta Gallery's themed virtual exhibition celebrating colour — work that engages with colour in bold, unexpected, and original ways, from saturated compositions to subtle tonal variations. Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for 6–12 months with catalogue, permanent Collections-page listing, and certificate.
calls.summary: Third edition celebrating colour — from saturated compositions to subtle tonal variation. Free to apply.
prose: Carlotta Gallery is a UK-based virtual photography gallery that runs themed open calls roughly bi-monthly. "Colours III" is the third edition of its colour-themed call, inviting photographers to engage with colour in bold, unexpected, and original ways.

The brief spans the full range: saturated, high-impact compositions at one end and subtle tonal variations at the other. What the jury is after is an original use of colour — work where colour is a deliberate, expressive choice rather than an incidental property of the scene.

The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected: £20 for one accepted artwork, £30 for two, or £35 for three. There are no cash prizes — selection is the recognition. Selected work is shown in a virtual online exhibition for six months to a year, with permanent placement on the Carlotta Gallery Collections page, a free PDF catalogue, a Certificate of Recognition, and possible feature on the gallery's Instagram (@carlottagallery).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. Each photographer submits up to 3 JPG images by email with name, Instagram handle, biography, artist statement, and artwork details. The deadline is July 20, 2026.

calls.title: Intentional Unconventional — Experimental Photography & Video
calls.description: Photo Cleveland's avant-garde multimedia exhibition for work that breaks from conventional imagery and storytelling, favoring abstraction, non-linear structures, and unconventional techniques. The focus is on how an image was made rather than its subject — work where the artist pushed beyond traditional methods. Accepts photography, video, and mixed media (mixed media must have photography as its main component). Selected works are shown in a physical exhibition at The Brownhoist in Cleveland, opening Saturday July 11 (6–9 PM, with a live audio-visual installation by Ryan Kinney and Jim Szudy) and running July 11–31, 2026. No nudity (all-ages event); no religious or political themes. Artists may submit up to three works.
calls.summary: Photo Cleveland's experimental photo & video show — abstraction and unconventional technique. Physical Cleveland exhibition.
prose: Photo Cleveland is a Cleveland, Ohio photography community and exhibition project led by Jim Szudy. "Intentional Unconventional" is its open call for an avant-garde multimedia exhibition built around experimentation within the medium — work that breaks away from conventional imagery and mainstream storytelling.

The brief is specific about what "non-traditional" means here: not unusual subject matter, but unusual making. The jury wants images where the artist experimented and thought outside the box in how the work was created — abstract concepts, non-linear structures, and unconventional techniques. Photography, video, and mixed media are accepted, with mixed media required to use photography as its main component.

Selected works are shown at The Brownhoist (4403 St. Clair Ave, Cleveland), with an opening on Saturday, July 11 from 6–9 PM that includes a live immersive audio-visual installation by Ryan Kinney and Jim Szudy. The show runs July 11–31, 2026 and is free to the public.

Entry is $35 for up to three photo or mixed-media works, or $20 for two videos, with a maximum of three works total. Because it is an all-ages event, work containing nudity is not accepted, and submissions addressing religious or political themes are excluded. The deadline to submit is June 27, 2026.

calls.title: New South, Volume III
calls.description: Open call for the Atlanta Center for Photography's 2026 group publication, New South, Volume III — a self-published photo book featuring lens-based work made in, of, from, and about the American South. The 2025 edition featured over 81 artists. ACP frames the South broadly: defined by relationship and impact rather than personal Southern heritage, location, or 'quintessentially Southern' imagery. Open to emerging and established photographers; ACP especially encourages submissions from those who identify as Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities. Submit 1–5 images. Selected works appear in a high-quality 8x10 printed book (60 to 100+ pages), produced and sold through the ACP website, approved retailers, and in person in Atlanta by early October 2026.
calls.summary: ACP's self-published group photo book on the American South. 1–5 images; emerging & established photographers welcome.
prose: The Atlanta Center for Photography (ACP) is an Atlanta, Georgia nonprofit running exhibitions, workshops, fellowships, and publications. "New South" is its annual self-published group photo book gathering lens-based work made in, of, from, and about the American South; the 2025 volume featured more than 81 artists.

ACP deliberately resists a narrow definition of the region. As described in the foreword to the first volume, "the only constant is that the region can't be codified" — the publication pursues the South through nuance defined by relationship and impact, not strictly by Southern heritage, location, or 'quintessentially Southern' imagery.

The call is open to both emerging and established photographers, and ACP especially encourages submissions from artists who identify as Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities. Photographers may submit 1–5 images representing their lens-based practice.

Selected works are featured in a high-quality 8x10 printed book ranging from 60 to 100+ pages, with the number of contributing artists and copies determined by the strength of submissions. The book is produced and sold through the ACP website, approved retailers, and in person in Atlanta by early October 2026. The application fee is $15, and the deadline is June 15, 2026.

calls.title: Space to Feel — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Leah Guzman, a board-certified art therapist and professional artist. The theme explores emotional honesty, tenderness, healing, and human connection — celebrating vulnerability and mental health through art. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on Miami bus shelters for at least one month starting August 14, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard and transit exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.
calls.summary: Miami bus-shelter public art show curated by art therapist Leah Guzman. Theme: vulnerability, healing, mental health.
prose: SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial billboard and transit advertising space since 2015 — turning public ad space into open-air exhibitions seen by far larger audiences than gallery shows reach.

"Space to Feel" is curated by Leah Guzman, a board-certified art therapist and professional artist specializing in creative wellness. The theme invites work about emotional honesty, tenderness, healing, and human connection, celebrating vulnerability and mental health.

The call is open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, Florida for at least one month beginning August 14, 2026.
Submission is $35 for one to three images and $10 for each additional image, structured as a tax-deductible donation supporting exhibition production. The deadline is June 29, 2026.

SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art exhibitions since 2015; fees are tax-deductible donations supporting production.
calls.summary: NYC billboard & bus-shelter show curated by photographer Ceres. Theme: womanhood and counterculture perspectives.
prose: SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial billboard and transit advertising space since 2015, turning public ad space into open-air exhibitions across the city.

"Ode to Womanhood" is curated by Ceres (Diaja), an award-winning photographer. The theme celebrates womanhood in all its authenticity, with particular emphasis on counterculture perspectives that challenge societal expectations around aging, career, marriage, and motherhood.

Selected works are displayed on billboard and bus shelter advertising space throughout New York City for at least one month starting August 7, 2026, with selection notifications going out after July 6, 2026.
