calls.title: Black and White
calls.description: Celebrating the power and timelessness of black and white photography — the deep, unending shades of grey. All photographic genres welcome. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition July 4 – July 25, 2026.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: B&W photography — all genres. Pro printing on Ilford Pearl paper and museum framing included. Exhibition in Tucson, AZ.
prose: Black and White is Decode Gallery's themed call dedicated specifically to monochrome photography — celebrating the depth and tonal range of black and white photography across all genres. The brief is medium-specific rather than subject-specific: portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, conceptual, and abstract work all qualify, provided the work is in monochrome.
At least 26 images are selected for the physical exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, Arizona, running July 4 through 25, 2026.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 inch white framing, and custom matting. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years after the exhibition for further promotion.
Sales terms split commission 50/50. Selected work is also promoted across Decode's website and social media. Selection is by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer.
Entry fees: $40 for 5 images or $45 for 10 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. The 2026 deadline is May 23, with selection announced approximately June 6.

calls.title: Global Ability Photography Challenge 2026
calls.description: 5th edition of the world's largest inclusive photography competition, exclusively for persons with disabilities. Open to all styles — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. No theme restriction, no age limit. Top 20 photographs exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with works featured across media and global campaigns. Custom trophies by designer Michael Foley. Award ceremony June 24, 2026. Travel and accommodation support provided for winners. Over 4 editions, GAPC has reached 8 million people and 50,000+ participants from 30+ countries. Organized by Not Just Art (Youth4Jobs) with Adani GreenXTalks.
calls.summary: Free photography competition exclusively for persons with disabilities — ~$20K in prizes, top 20 exhibited in Ahmedabad.
prose: The Global Ability Photography Challenge (GAPC) is an inclusive photography competition exclusively for persons with disabilities. Founded approximately in 2022, the 2026 cycle is the 5th edition. The program is organized by Not Just Art / Youth4Jobs in partnership with Adani Plus and other sponsors, and the organizers describe it as the largest disability-led photography competition globally.

There is no thematic restriction. Submissions span all approaches — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. The brief encourages, but does not require, work capturing stories of inclusion, dignity, resilience, hope, and the everyday lives of persons with disabilities.

Cash prizes total approximately ₹17,00,000 ($20,000 USD) across ten placements: 1st ₹5,00,000; 2nd ₹3,00,000; 3rd ₹2,00,000; and 4th through 10th at ₹1,00,000 each. The top 20 photographs are exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with custom trophies designed by Michael Foley. Travel and accommodation are sponsored for selected winners attending the award ceremony.

Eligibility is restricted to persons with disabilities; there is no age restriction. Submission is free. Each photographer submits a maximum of 3 photos in JPEG format, RGB, maximum 2000 pixels on the longest side, minimum 4 MB file size, with no watermarks or identifying marks.

Across its first four editions, GAPC reports reaching 8 million people, 50,000+ lives inspired, and participants from 30+ countries. The 2026 deadline is May 25; results announced before the June 24 award ceremony.

calls.title: #HopperHappens Juried Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Photography-only juried exhibition inspired by the #HopperHappens Instagram series — real-world moments evoking Edward Hopper's style, light, and mood. 55 photographs selected and displayed across 55 businesses and nonprofits in Nyack, NY, birthplace of Edward Hopper. $1,000 in cash prizes: First $500, Second $300, Third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. Juror: Richard Tuschman, celebrated for his 'Hopper Meditations' series. Exhibition June 1 – July 5, 2026. Open internationally, ages 18+. Work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at EHHM. MFA student discounts available.
calls.summary: Photography inspired by Hopper's light and mood — 55 works displayed across 55 Nyack venues. Juror: Richard Tuschman.
prose: The Edward Hopper House Museum operates from Hopper's childhood home in Nyack, New York. The #HopperHappens series began on the museum's Instagram, collecting real-world photographs that evoke Hopper's light, mood, and compositional sensibility — the painter's domestic American spaces translated into photographic seeing. The juried exhibition extends that Instagram premise into a physical group show.

The 2026 juror is Richard Tuschman, a photographer best known for his Hopper Meditations series, which restages Hopper paintings as constructed photographic dioramas. The selection structure is unusual: 55 photographs are chosen and dispersed across 55 different businesses and nonprofits throughout Nyack — the show is the town for the duration.
Cash prizing is $1,000 total: first $500, second $300, third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. The exhibition runs June 1 – July 5, 2026.

Eligibility is open internationally to photographers 18+. Submitted work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at the Edward Hopper House Museum. MFA student discounts on entry fee are available.
Submission is through ArtCall with up to 3 images. Fee is $30 for members and $60 for non-members. The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced May 11, 2026.

calls.title: Narrative
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring visual storytelling through single images or cohesive series. Documentary, street, conceptual, staged, and experimental approaches welcome. Exhibition at Chico Art Center gallery, August 15 – September 18, 2026, with opening reception September 4. Member fee $25. Free exhibition catalog via Blurb. Opportunity to sell work (30% commission to center). Previously exhibited work at CAC ineligible.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition on visual storytelling — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, or experimental approaches.
prose: Chico Art Center is a community arts gallery at 450 Orange Street, Suite 6 in Chico, California. "Narrative" is the gallery's open call for photography that explores visual storytelling — work that communicates a narrative through a single image or cohesive series, whether personal journey, cultural or historical commentary, political statement, or fiction.

All photographic mediums and styles are welcome — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, experimental — with no thematic constraint beyond the storytelling brief. AI-generated images are not currently accepted. Work previously exhibited at CAC is ineligible.

Selected work is exhibited at Chico Art Center August 15 through September 18, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4. The gallery handles installation. Each artist receives a free copy of a printed exhibition catalog produced via Blurb, and selected work is promoted through the gallery's website and social channels.
Sales are facilitated by the gallery, which requests a 30% donation but pays the artist the full listed price. Artists are responsible for shipping and insurance.

Entry fee is $35 (general) or $25 for CAC members. Submissions take up to 7 images via JotForm. The 2026 deadline is June 14 at 11:59 PM. Selection is by Gallery Director Cameron Kelly with a CAC board member.

calls.title: The Art of Abandonment

Curator's Choice, Director's Choice, and Honorable Mentions awarded. Blind jury process — juror sees only the image and title.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition exploring forgotten structures, objects, and places — what they reveal about humanity and time.
prose: TCG Gallery (also operating as Chateau Gallery) is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs. "The Art of Abandonment" is the gallery's open call for photography exploring abandoned and rediscovered objects, locations, and structures — work that examines what forgotten spaces reveal about humanity, memory, and the passage of time.

Approximately 35 images are selected for the online exhibition, running June 1 through July 1, 2026. The selection structure includes Curator's Choice and Director's Choice awards plus Honorable Mentions. The jury is structured as a rotating assortment of past exhibitors, curators, editors, and arts professionals using a blind jury process — jurors see only the image and its title.
Selected work is included in the published catalog, promoted across the gallery's website and social media with attribution, and offered for sale through the gallery (which retains 30% commission).

Eligibility is restricted to photographers aged 18 and over. AI-generated and AI-altered work is not accepted. Citizens of countries under U.S. comprehensive sanctions (Iran, Cuba, North Korea, Sudan, Syria, Belarus, Russia) cannot submit.

Entry fee is $15 for up to 3 images, with merit-based and hardship waivers available. Submissions are JPG at minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side, 500 KB minimum file size. The 2026 deadline is May 25 at 11:59 PM; notification May 27.

calls.title: Encontros Da Imagem Award 2026
calls.description: Open call for the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem, one of Europe's oldest photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. Three projects selected for solo exhibitions during the festival across multiple northern Portuguese cities, September 18 – November 1, 2026. One overall winner receives €2,000. Seventeen further projects included in a collective video screening. Theme: Territory And Identity. Projects must use photography or video with coherent narrative structure, produced within the last five years. Maximum three projects per applicant.
calls.summary: Major European photo festival (36th edition). €2,000 prize + solo exhibition. Theme: Territory And Identity. Open worldwide.
jury: Arianna Catania, Independent Curator & Photo Editor
Arianna Rinaldo, Independent Curator & Photography Consultant
prose: Encontros da Imagem is one of Europe's longer-running photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. The 2026 edition is the festival's 36th, running September 18 through November 1, 2026 across multiple cities in northern Portugal. The festival's main award and its photobook award (separately covered) are the two flagship prize tracks.

The 2026 theme is "Territory and Identity" — though the open call explicitly does not require submitted work to align with the theme. Selection is based on coherent narrative structure rather than thematic fit.

The selection structure is layered. The grand prize winner receives €2,000 cash. Three projects (including the grand prize winner) are selected for solo exhibitions during the festival. Seventeen additional projects are included in a collective video screening — bringing total recognized projects to 20.

The 2026 jury comprises Arianna Catania (independent curator and photo editor), Alexia Alexandropoulou (independent curator), and Arianna Rinaldo (independent curator and photography consultant who has appeared on multiple Italian/Portuguese juries throughout 2026).

Eligibility is open globally to artists 18 and over. Each applicant submits up to 3 projects, with each project containing 15 to 20 images and a brief synopsis. Work must have been produced within the last five years. Both photographic and video practices are eligible. Entry fee is €35 per submission. Submissions go through Picter; the deadline is May 10, 2026 at 9:59 PM.

calls.title: 31st National Competition 2026
calls.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 31st annual National Competition. Approximately 60 photographs selected for exhibition at the gallery's spacious W23rd Street location in Chelsea, New York. Juror: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects at Museum of the City of New York. Open to photographers who are residents of the United States. Exhibition July 2026.
calls.summary: Annual photo competition at Soho Photo Gallery NYC. ~60 works exhibited. $400 first, $200 second. US residents only.
jury: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects, Museum of the City of New York
prose: Soho Photo Gallery is a photographer-run cooperative gallery in New York, founded in 1971 by photojournalists. calls.title: Light Dreams
calls.description: Juried exhibition of alternative and historical process photography at Light Art Space gallery in Silver City, New Mexico. calls.summary: Alt-process juried show in New Mexico. Cyanotype, platinum, wet-plate & more. Open worldwide, student rate $20.
prose: Light Art Space is a gallery at 209 West Broadway in Silver City, New Mexico, with a program focused on alternative and historical process photography. "Light Dreams" is the gallery's juried exhibition for 2026 — the brief explores light as an internal, psychological, and symbolic presence, asking how light and dreams intersect through hand-made photographic processes.

Eligible media span the full range of alt-process work: cyanotype, platinum/palladium, silver gelatin, wet-plate collodion, gum bichromate, and other historical and alternative processes. Digital negatives are acceptable as long as the print itself involves a hand-made process. Straight digital and AI-derived work are ineligible. 3D and experimental approaches are explicitly encouraged.

The 2026 jury is Jill Enfield, the photographer and educator known for her own substantial alt-process practice and her instruction on collodion, wet plate, and other historical techniques. The exhibition runs July 4 through September 6, 2026, with an opening reception July 5. Sponsor support is provided by Freestyle75.
The gallery actively invites submissions from LGBTQ+, Black, Latinx, Indigenous, and artists of color, framing this not as a separate track but as part of the broader open call.

Entry fee is $35 for 3 images, with a $20 student rate. Submissions go through CaFÉ. Eligibility is open globally to artists 18 and over. The 2026 deadline is May 19 at midnight MST; results announced May 24.

calls.title: COAL Prize 2026 — The Night
calls.description: Annual art and ecology prize from French foundation COAL. 2026 theme: The Night — defending darkness as a common good, a major ecological issue for regeneration of life, a refuge, and a right to rest. Main prize: €12,000 grant plus creative residency at Domaine de Belval (François Sommer Foundation). Special Jury Prize: €3,000. Centre Wallonie-Bruxelles mention: €2,000 plus exhibition. Ateliers Médicis mention: residency near Paris. Ten artists nominated by committee, winners chosen by jury. Submit single PDF (max 30MB) with project description, technical note, budget, 2+ HD visuals, CV, and portfolio. Open worldwide, all disciplines including photography and lens-based media.
calls.summary: €12,000 art & ecology prize with residency. Theme: defending darkness. Jury Prize €3,000. Free, open worldwide.
prose: COAL is a French foundation focused on the intersection of contemporary art and ecology. The annual COAL Prize is awarded to a project addressing an environmental theme that shifts each year. The 2026 theme is The Night — framed as defending darkness as a common good, a major ecological issue for regeneration of life, a refuge, and a right to rest.
Selection structure: ten artists are nominated by an internal committee, and the final winners are chosen by an external jury.

The main prize is €12,000 plus a creative residency at Domaine de Belval, run by the François Sommer Foundation. The Special Jury Prize is €3,000. There are two additional partner mentions: the Centre Wallonie-Bruxelles mention (€2,000 plus exhibition) and the Ateliers Médicis mention (residency near Paris).
Eligibility is open worldwide across all disciplines — including photography and lens-based media. The award is project-based: applicants submit a proposal rather than a finished body of work.

Each application is a single PDF (max 30MB) including project description, technical note, budget, 2+ HD visuals, CV, and portfolio. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 28; results announced Autumn 2026.

calls.title: 1st Photobook Grants 2026
calls.description: Fourth edition of the 1st Photobook Grants supporting photographers who have never published a monograph. Three grants of €5,000 each in three categories: photographers from the Global South (Africa, Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Latin America, Middle East), French photographers or those residing in France (SAIF grant), and female photographers of any nationality. Must partner with an independent French publisher and provide a letter of commitment. Supported by the French Ministry of Culture and SAIF. Winners announced June 2026; books must be published by November 30, 2027.
calls.summary: Three €5,000 grants for debut photobook projects. Categories: Global South, French, and female photographers. Free, needs French publisher.
prose: The 1st Photobook Grants is a French photobook program initiated by the Eyes Wide Open association, the cultural production entity of The Eyes label. The program is supported by France's Ministry of Culture and SAIF (Société des Auteurs des arts visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The 2026 cycle is the fourth edition.

The program is unusually targeted: each cycle awards three separate €5,000 grants in three category-specific tracks. The Global South grant is reserved for photographers from Africa, the Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Latin America, or the Middle East. The SAIF grant is reserved for French photographers or photographers residing in France. The third grant is open to female photographers of any nationality.

All three grants share the same project requirement: photographers who have never previously published a monograph. The grant supports the production of a first photobook, with the structural requirement that applicants must partner with an independent French publisher and submit a letter of commitment from that publisher with their application — making this as much a publisher-photographer matchmaking program as a cash grant.

Submission is free. Applicants submit a single PDF (maximum 25 MB) via Google Form. The 2026 application window runs February 17 through May 17, with winners announced in June 2026. Books must be published by November 30, 2027 — a 17-month production window from announcement.

calls.title: Ten x Ten – 18th Annual Small Works
calls.description: Annual small works exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (November 14 – December 31, 2026). Celebrates creative expression within the square photographic format. All works are 10"×10" and priced at $200 each. MWCP provides printing at no cost to selected artists. Open to all photographers internationally.
calls.summary: Annual 10"×10" square-format exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Affordable collectible works, MWCP prints at no cost.
prose: Ten x Ten is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual square-format exhibition, now in its 18th year. The brief is unusually concrete: every accepted print is exactly 10 inches by 10 inches, and every print is sold at the same price — $200 each — for the duration of the show. The format levels the field across genres and career stages and produces a uniform grid hang that has become the show's signature.

MWCP is a small photography-focused space in Wichita, Kansas. Selected work is exhibited both physically and online; MWCP covers all printing costs for accepted entries, which is unusual for a juried show at this scale. A $30 frame rental is the only out-of-pocket expense for selected artists who want their work framed for the wall.

Submissions are open internationally to photographers working in any process — film, digital, iPhone, or alternative. The 2026 exhibition runs November 14 through December 31, with the submission deadline August 1.

calls.title: FOTOHOF>CALLING
calls.description: Biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in Salzburg on October 3, 2026, with an open-air projection on Inge-Morath-Platz. Projects must be no older than three years and never exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and residency programs are exempt from this rule. Open to artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe.
calls.summary: Biennial call for contemporary photo projects. 25 selected for publication, 10 finalists present in Salzburg. Open to European artists.
prose: FOTOHOF is a long-running photography institution in Salzburg, Austria — a gallery, archive, and publishing platform. FOTOHOF>CALLING is its biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. The call's structure is publication-plus-presentation rather than competition-prize.

Selection has two tiers. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. From these, 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in person in Salzburg on October 3, 2026 — with an open-air projection event on Inge-Morath-Platz, the public square named for the Magnum photographer.

Eligibility is restricted by recency and prior exposure: projects must be no older than three years and must not have been exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and projects done within residency programs are exempt from this rule.
Geographic eligibility: artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe.
Application is free, with up to 12 images per project. Submission is through the FOTOHOF>CALLING website. The 2026 deadline was April 26; final presentation October 3, 2026.

calls.title: Martin House Creative Residency 2026
calls.description: 2–4 week project-based residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Darwin D. Martin House in Buffalo, New York. Residents live in the Gardener's Cottage on campus and create new work inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, and social history of Martin House. Open to artists working in any discipline including photography, writing, and research. Residents receive $5,000 stipend paid in two installments and up to $1,000 travel allowance for non-local applicants. Residency term runs June–October 2026. Must deliver a free public program, performance, or exhibition sharing work with the community. Requires US social security number. Application window March 30 – May 13, 2026.
calls.summary: 2–4 week residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Martin House. $5,000 stipend + $1,000 travel. Work inspired by architecture and design.
prose: The Martin House Creative Residency is hosted at the Darwin D. Martin House (125 Jewett Parkway, Buffalo, NY 14214), Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie-style masterpiece designed for businessman Darwin D. Martin and built between 1903 and 1905. The complex is one of Wright's most ambitious residential designs and a National Historic Landmark.

The residency is project-based: applicants must propose work directly inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, or social history of the Martin House. The program is unusually broad in disciplinary scope — visual artists, writers, researchers, and creative makers from any field can apply, with photography explicitly eligible.

Residency length is 2 to 4 weeks onsite, either consecutively or split across multiple visits within the June through October 2026 term. Each resident receives a $5,000 stipend (paid in two installments — 50% on arrival, 50% on completion) plus up to $1,000 in travel expenses for non-local participants. Housing is provided in the Gardener's Cottage on the Martin House campus — a private bedroom and bathroom with utilities and high-speed wi-fi included.
Residents are required to deliver a free public program, performance, exhibition, or other creative presentation during or after the residency, sharing work with the Buffalo community.

Eligibility requires applicants to have a U.S. social security number (including permanent residents, OPT holders, and Indigenous peoples eligible under the Jay Treaty). Individual applicants only — collectives are not eligible. The program is free to apply. The 2026 application window runs March 30 through May 13, 2026.

calls.title: Loghaven Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency on 90 acres of forested land in Knoxville, Tennessee for practicing artists at any career stage. Sessions range from 2–6 weeks between February and October 2027. All fellows receive an $850/week living stipend, travel subsidy ($400–$800 on a sliding scale), and up to $200 in materials shipping reimbursement. Disciplines include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work. Applicants must be 21+, live 120+ miles from Knoxville, and have legal US work authorization. International artists are not eligible. Applications open June 1, 2026. Submit 8 JPEG images for visual art via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: 2–6 week residency on 90 forested acres. $850/week stipend plus travel subsidy. Visual arts, writing, and more.
jury: National selection committee of artist peers & arts professionals
prose: Loghaven is an artist residency on 90 acres of woodland at 1001 Loghaven Drive in Knoxville, Tennessee. Artists are housed in five historic log cabins that have been rehabilitated and modernized, with access to purpose-built studio space on the grounds.

The 2027 program runs across six sessions of varying lengths: a four-week February cycle, a six-week April–May cycle, a two-week June cycle for fellows only, a two-week July cycle for teaching/faculty artists, a two-week September cycle, and a four-week October–November cycle. Applicants choose their preferred session at submission.

Financial support is unusually substantive for a residency: an $850 per week living stipend for the duration of the stay, a sliding-scale travel subsidy of $400–$800, and up to $200 reimbursement for materials shipping. Disciplines accepted include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work.

Eligibility is restricted: artists must be at least 21 years old, hold U.S. work authorization, live at least 120 miles from Knoxville, and not be enrolled in a degree-seeking program. International artists are not eligible. Two professional references are required.

The application fee is $25, with waivers available June 1–July 15. Applications open June 1 and close July 15, 2026 at midnight Eastern Time. The selection panel — a national committee of artist peers and arts professionals — meets August through September, with applicants notified by November 1.

calls.title: FMoPA 2026 International Photography Competition
calls.description: International photography competition open to photographers worldwide. Submit up to 15 images across 7 categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash prize. Category winners receive goods and services. Winning works exhibited June 16 – August 2, 2026 at FMoPA in Tampa's Ybor City District.
calls.summary: International photography competition. $1,000 grand prize and exhibition at FMoPA Tampa. 7 categories.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Hiromi Nakamura, Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography
Elena Paraskeva, Photographer and Art Director
Bärbel Reinhard, Photographer, Curator and Educator
Kristen Roles, Photographic Artist and Educator
prose: The Florida Museum of Photographic Arts (FMoPA) is a Tampa-based museum dedicated to photography, located in Tampa's Ybor City Historic District. The annual International Photography Competition is the museum's flagship juried open call.

The 2026 edition runs across seven categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+.
Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash. Category winners receive goods and services rather than additional cash. Winning works are exhibited at FMoPA from June 16 to August 2, 2026.

The 2026 jury is built from international institutions: Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska), Hiromi Nakamura (Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography), Elena Paraskeva (photographer and art director), Bärbel Reinhard (photographer, curator and educator), and Kristen Roles (photographic artist and educator).
Submission is through Picter with up to 15 images. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced May 13, 2026.

calls.title: Fotograf Magazine 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for publication in Fotograf Magazine, a leading international photography publication based in Prague. Two selected projects published in the next printed issue. Open to professionals, amateurs, and students submitting independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects. Submit CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images via email.
jury: Felix Hoffmann, Curator and Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN
Peter Watkins, Visual Artist and Lecturer, FAMU
calls.summary: Publication opportunity in leading international photography magazine based in Prague. Two projects selected for print.
prose: Fotograf Magazine is an international photography publication based in Prague. The annual open call selects work for inclusion in a printed issue — two projects are selected for publication.

The brief is open across format — independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects are both eligible. The magazine accepts work from professionals, amateurs, and students without distinction.

The 2026 jury reflects the magazine's institutional reach: Felix Hoffmann (Curator and Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN), Markéta Kinterová (Editor-in-Chief, Fotograf Magazine), Michaela Nagyidaiová (visual artist), Marta Szymańska (curator), and Peter Watkins (visual artist and lecturer at FAMU, the Prague film school).
Submission is by email — applicants send a CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images. Fee is €35 per project. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced July 30, 2026.

calls.title: Grenze Arsenali Fotografici 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the ninth edition of Grenze - Arsenali Fotografici international photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists selected for exhibition during the festival opening September 2026.
jury: Aida Redžepagić & Jelena Janković, Sarajevo Photography Festival
David Pujado, Belgrade Photo Month Founder
Simone Azzoni, Co-Founder & Artistic Director, Grenze
calls.summary: International photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists exhibited. Strong international jury.
prose: Grenze – Arsenali Fotografici is an international photography festival held annually in Verona, Italy. The 2026 edition is the festival's ninth. The festival's open call selects three artists for exhibition during the festival opening in September 2026.

The 2026 theme is Nachleben — a German term taken from Aby Warburg's art-historical vocabulary, referring to the afterlife or survival of images and forms across time. The brief invites work that thinks photography in relation to memory, persistence, and the recurrence of visual motifs.

The 2026 jury draws from a network of European photography festival directors: Aida Redžepagić & Jelena Janković (Sarajevo Photography Festival), David Pujado (founder of Belgrade Photo Month), Marta Szymanska (director of Fotofestiwal in Łódź), and Grenze's own Simone Azzoni (Co-Founder and Artistic Director) and Francesca Marra (President).
Submission is by email with 10–20 images. Fee is €28. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced May 30, 2026.

calls.title: Photography 4 Humanity / Fotografiska Global Prize 2026
calls.description: Global photography prize exploring the theme HOME — safety, belonging, identity, memory, loss, and place. Open to photographers worldwide. Selected photographs exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day (December 10, 2026), guest-curated by James Nachtwey.
calls.summary: Theme: HOME. Selected work exhibited at UN Headquarters NYC, curated by James Nachtwey. Free entry.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction & Exhibitions, Fotografiska
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction & Exhibitions) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026; results are announced October 5, 2026.

calls.title: Minimalist Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Seventh edition of the international award celebrating minimalist photography as a visual language. Open to photographers worldwide. Submit single images or series (2–7 images) across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, and Street. Grand prize: €2,000 cash, hand-crafted trophy, title of Minimalist Photographer of the Year, and inclusion in the official annual book. Earlybird deadline May 1; final deadline June 2, 2026.
calls.summary: International award for minimalist photography. €2,000 grand prize, book publication, and exhibition. 12 categories.
calls.ai: Only accepted if incorporating a real photograph
jury: Milad Safabakhsh, Founder, Minimalist Photography Awards
prose: The Minimalist Photography Awards is an international competition focused exclusively on minimalist photography as a visual language. The 2026 cycle is the 7th edition; the awards have been running annually since the first edition in 2019. The program is based in Bregenz, Austria, and was founded by photographer Milad Safabakhsh.

Submissions are accepted across 12 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, Street, and others. Photographers may submit single images or series of 2 to 7 images per category.

The Grand Prize Winner receives €2,000 in cash, a hand-crafted trophy, and the title "Minimalist Photographer of the Year," along with inclusion in the official annual book and gallery exhibition opportunities. Category winners are featured in the annual book and online showcase.

The 2026 jury comprises Sylvia Janschek (photographer), Matthias Weissengruber (photographer), Leon Boch (photographer), and founder Milad Safabakhsh, with the international panel rounding out across editions.

Entry fees are tiered with an early bird deadline May 1 and final deadline June 2, 2026 (23:59 UTC). Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over. AI-generated work is accepted only if it incorporates a real photograph; fully AI-generated work is excluded.

calls.title: Villa Lena Foundation — Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency program for artists of all disciplines in a 19th-century villa in Tuscany, Italy. Residencies run 4–5 weeks between April and October 2027. Includes studio space, accommodation, and half-board meals five days a week. Residency fee of €150/week covers room, studio, and meals. Artists must donate a completed work to the foundation's collection. Access to ceramic and wood workshops, screening room, and weekly excursions.
calls.summary: 4–5 week residency in a Tuscan villa with studio, accommodation, and meals. €150/week residency fee. All disciplines.
prose: Villa Lena Foundation operates an artist residency from a 19th-century Tuscan villa on a 500-hectare estate near Pisa. The 2027 program runs residencies of 4–5 weeks between April and October. Multidisciplinary by design — artists across visual arts, photography, music, writing, and performance work alongside one another.

The residency provides a private studio, accommodation in a renovated farmhouse on the estate, and half-board meals five days per week. Beyond the basics, residents have access to ceramic and wood workshops, a screening room, and a program of weekly excursions in the surrounding countryside.

The cost structure is unusual: residencies are not free. Artists pay a €150-per-week residency fee that covers room, studio, and meals. Residents are also required to donate a completed work to the Villa Lena Foundation collection at the end of their stay.

Eligibility is open to artists of all disciplines and any career stage. Application requires a PDF portfolio, submitted via Google Forms. Application fee is €21. The 2027-cycle deadline was May 3, 2026; results announced November 2026.

calls.title: Taylor Wessing Photo Portrait Prize 2026
calls.description: One of the world's most prestigious portrait photography competitions. Open to photographers worldwide, aged 18+. Submit up to 6 portraits taken after 1 January 2025. First prize £15,000, second £3,000, third £2,000. Selected works exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London from November 2026 to January 2027. The prize celebrates contemporary portraiture, interpreting 'portrait' in its widest sense — photography concerned with portraying people with an emphasis on their identity as individuals.
calls.summary: Premier international portrait prize. £15,000 first prize. Exhibition at National Portrait Gallery, London, Nov 2026–Jan 2027.

calls.title: White: Absence of Color
calls.description: International achromatic photography exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (January 9–25, 2027). Explores photography emphasizing the lightest end of the color spectrum — minimal color saturation conveying striking imagery and psychological impact. All photographic media welcome. Selected artists' work printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display.
calls.summary: International achromatic photography exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Explores the lightest end of the spectrum with minimal color.
prose: White: Absence of Color is one of Midwest Center for Photography's themed juried exhibitions in Wichita, Kansas. The exhibition runs January 9–25, 2027.

The brief is restrictive in palette but open in approach: photography emphasizing the lightest end of the color spectrum, with minimal color saturation. The premise is achromatic image-making — high-key, washed-out, snow-bound, paper-white — where the absence of color does the psychological work. All photographic media are welcome.
Selected artists' work is physically printed and framed by MWCP for gallery display — production costs are absorbed by the gallery.
Eligibility is open internationally. Submission is by email with 5–10 images. Fee is $50 for 5 images. The deadline is October 1, 2026.

calls.title: Developed Work 2027
calls.description: National photography fellowship competition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (March 2027). Open to all US-based photographers. Seeks thematically developed bodies of work with cohesive conceptual frameworks demonstrating the pulse of contemporary American photography. Winner receives the $200 Developed Work Fellowship Award and one year of online representation by MWCP.
calls.summary: National fellowship for developed bodies of work. $200 award + one year online representation at MWCP, Wichita.
prose: Developed Work is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual national fellowship competition, focused on thematically developed bodies of work rather than individual standout images. The brief is explicit: selection emphasizes a cohesive conceptual framework — submissions are evaluated on the body of work as a whole rather than its strongest image.

The Wichita, Kansas gallery exhibits selected work in person, with the 2027 exhibition running in March 2027. The winner receives the $200 Developed Work Fellowship Award and one year of online representation by MWCP, which functions as ongoing visibility for the work beyond the exhibition window.

Submissions are limited to U.S.-based photographers and require 5 to 14 images plus a brief artist statement explaining the work's intent. Entry fee is $50 for up to 5 images. The 2027 cycle deadline is December 31, 2026.

The competition runs alongside MWCP's other open calls, including the international Ten x Ten Small Works exhibition. Where Ten x Ten samples individual 10×10 inch prints across many photographers, Developed Work selects a single fellow per cycle whose practice exemplifies sustained thematic exploration.

calls.title: Lisbon Street Photo Fest: Open Call 2026
calls.description: 2nd edition. Street photography open call in two categories: Singles (individual photos) and Series (10–15 images). Finalists exhibited at Faculdade de Belas-Artes da Universidade de Lisboa during festival weekend, 25–27 September 2026. €4,000 in cash prizes plus VSCO Pro memberships. Photos must be captured after 1 January 2024. No AI-generated content or watermarks.
calls.summary: 2nd edition. Street photography Singles & Series. €4,000 in prizes. Exhibition in Lisbon, Sept 25–27.
prose: Lisbon Street Photo Fest is organized by Associação 351 Foto, an independent non-profit based in Lisbon. The 2026 cycle is the festival's 2nd edition. The festival itself runs September 25–27, 2026 at Faculdade de Belas-Artes da Universidade de Lisboa.

The open call is split between two formats. The Singles category accepts individual photographs at €10 per entry, with cash prizes of €1,250 (1st), €750 (2nd), and €500 (3rd). The Series category accepts cohesive bodies of 10 to 15 images at €40 per series, with a €1,500 winner. A separate Special MPB Award is given to one Portugal-based photographer. Total cash prizes across the two categories are €4,000.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over. Photos must be captured after January 1, 2024, and applicants must not have won top-three or monetary prizes at major street photography awards previously. Watermarks, signatures, AI-generated content, and heavily manipulated composites are excluded. The brief favors layered, color-driven Lisbon-specific work but the call is open beyond the city.

All finalists are exhibited at the festival venue and receive a VSCO Pro membership. The 2026 jury comprises Daniel Postaer, Josh Edgoose, Nazile Bolat, Polly Rusyn, and Rui Palha — five photographers prominent in international street photography. Submissions go through Picter; the deadline is May 31, 2026. Early-bird discounts ran April 2–9. Results announced September 26.

calls.title: The Photo Review 41st Annual International Photography Competition
calls.description: 41st edition of one of photography's most respected annual competitions. Juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel, Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. Selected work exhibited at the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia and published in The Photo Review journal. $1,000 purchase prize from Haverford College plus equipment and printing prizes. All entrants receive a full-color catalogue.
jury: Dr. Sarah Kennel, Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography, Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
calls.summary: 41st edition. Juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel (VMFA). Exhibition at Woodmere Art Museum, Philadelphia. $1,000 purchase prize.
prose: The Photo Review is a Philadelphia-based photography journal founded in 1976 and one of the longer-running independent photography publications in the United States. The 2026 cycle is the journal's 41st Annual International Photography Competition — a continuous run since 1985.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Dr. Sarah Kennel, the Aaron Siskind Curator of Photography at the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. Selected work is exhibited at the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia and reproduced in The Photo Review journal — the journal-plus-museum format means selection produces both physical exhibition placement and ongoing editorial archival.

Cash and material prizes are layered across multiple sponsors: a $1,000 purchase prize from Haverford College, a $500 printing certificate from Booksmart Studio, $200 certificates from Digital Silver Imaging and Shades of Paper, smaller certificates from Red River Paper, PhotoLounge, Think Tank Photo, and PhotoFlasDrive, and a Wacom Intuos Pro tablet. All accepted entries appear on The Photo Review website and in partner email blasts. All entrants receive a full-color competition catalogue regardless of placement.

Entry fee is $40 for up to three images, with $8 per additional image. Submissions are made through Smarter Entry. The 2026 deadline was extended to May 31 after Woodmere pushed back the opening of the Best of Show exhibition; results announced June 30.

calls.title: Athens Street Photography Festival 2026
calls.description: First edition of the Athens Street Photography Festival. Submit up to three street photographs taken in 2025 or 2026. Finalists' work exhibited at TAF (The Art Foundation) in Athens during the festival (May 14–17, 2026). Winner selected by Magnum photographer Nikos Economopoulos. Free to submit; selected finalists pay €50 per exhibited image to cover production costs.
calls.prize: Exhibition at TAF + winner selected by jury
calls.summary: 1st edition. Free street photo submissions, finalists exhibited at TAF Athens. Winner chosen by Magnum's Nikos Economopoulos.
prose: Athens Street Photography Festival is a new annual festival held at TAF (The Art Foundation) in Athens. The 2026 edition is the festival's first cycle.
Submitted photographs must be street work taken in 2025 or 2026 — recency-restricted. Finalists' work is exhibited at TAF during the festival, May 14–17, 2026.

Selection structure: a panel of judges (Gabi Ben Avraham, Yiannis Yiasaris, Francesca Chiacchio, Latife Solak Baudet) shortlists finalists. The final winner is selected by Magnum photographer Nikos Economopoulos.
The fee structure is staged: free to submit. Finalists pay €50 per exhibited image to cover production costs — payment is contingent on selection.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email with up to 3 images. The 2026 deadline was April 5; results announced May 17, 2026.

calls.title: Abstract 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of abstract. Submit images exploring abstract concepts in any photographic style. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright.
calls.summary: Abstract photography in any style. Month-long Glasgow gallery exhibition plus online gallery. Fujifilm printing, copyright retained.
prose: The Glasgow Gallery of Photography is a UK gallery that runs themed international juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. Abstract 2026 is the gallery's call for work engaging with abstraction in any photographic style — from constructed studio work through long-exposure landscapes through experimental processes.

The gallery's fee structure is unusual: free to submit, with a £48 fee charged only if work is accepted for exhibition. Selected work is shown both in a month-long physical gallery exhibition in Glasgow and in an online gallery on the gallery's website.
Production is gallery-supplied: images are printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in standard gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email via file transfer with 1–8 images. The 2026 deadline was April 24; results announced April 29, 2026.

calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of portrait. Open to everyone. Selected work displayed in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow, with work also appearing in an online gallery on the gallery's website. Images printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright.
calls.summary: Portrait photography, open to all. Month-long Glasgow gallery exhibition plus online gallery. Fujifilm printing, copyright retained.
prose: The Glasgow Gallery of Photography runs themed international juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. Portrait 2026 is the gallery's portrait-themed cycle — open to all approaches: studio, environmental, candid, conceptual, and self-portraiture.

The gallery's fee structure is unusual: free to submit, with a £48 fee charged only if work is accepted for exhibition. Selected work is shown both in a month-long physical gallery exhibition in Glasgow and in an online gallery on the gallery's website.

Production is gallery-supplied: images are printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in standard gallery frames. Photographers retain all copyright — the gallery doesn't take rights along with the print production.
Eligibility is open globally to everyone. Submission is by email via file transfer with 1–8 images. The 2026 deadline was April 24; results announced April 29, 2026.

calls.title: Rancho Linda Vista — Summer Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month summer residency for visual artists at Rancho Linda Vista, a historic arts community on 100+ acres in Oracle, Arizona. Resident receives a furnished one-bedroom house, separate studio space, and $1,000 stipend. Access to swimming pool, library, and wilderness trails. Open studio exhibit at conclusion of stay. Available for July or August 2026. Must provide own transportation and materials. MFA preferred but not required.
calls.summary: One-month summer residency with $1,000 stipend, house, and studio on 100+ acres of Arizona wilderness.
prose: Rancho Linda Vista is a historic arts community in Oracle, Arizona, on 100+ acres of high-desert wilderness north of Tucson. The Summer Artist Residency program offers one-month residencies for visual artists during July or August.

Residents receive a furnished one-bedroom house, separate studio space, and a $1,000 stipend. Access to the community's swimming pool, library, and wilderness trails. The residency concludes with an open studio exhibit.
Practical requirements: residents must provide their own transportation and materials. The location is rural and remote — applicants should plan for that context.
Eligibility is open globally; MFA is preferred but not required. Application is by email to the residency coordinator. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was April 17; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: La Embajada 2026
calls.description: Third edition of La Embajada, a programme promoting contemporary Spanish photography within the European circuit through an exhibition during the opening week of Rencontres d'Arles. Six projects selected, each artist receiving €1,400 fee. Selected photographers exhibit during the festival's opening week (July 6–13, 2026) and participate in active mediation with audiences. La Embajada creates a temporary 'embassy' to showcase photographic projects and foster professional connections at the epicentre of world photography. Organised by El Local (independent space for contemporary photography in Madrid) in partnership with Plataforma Fotografía e Imagen, with support from Spain's Ministry of Culture. Submit one project per applicant via digital form. Work must be produced and exhibition-ready. Physical presence in Arles during opening week is mandatory.
calls.summary: Six Spanish photographers exhibit at Rencontres d'Arles opening week. €1,400 each. Free, supported by Ministry of Culture.
jury: Christoph Wiesner, Director, Les Rencontres d'Arles
Elisa Medde, Director, Foto Colectania Foundation
prose: La Embajada is a programme promoting contemporary Spanish photography within the European circuit. Its annual exhibition runs during the opening week of Rencontres d'Arles — the major French photography festival — placing Spanish photographers in front of the international curators, editors, and gallerists who travel to Arles each July. The 2026 edition is the third cycle.

The format is project-based: six projects are selected, each artist receiving a €1,400 fee plus inclusion in the exhibition during the festival's opening week (July 6–13, 2026). Selected artists are also expected to participate in active mediation with audiences during the week — talking visitors through their work.
The premise is the temporary 'embassy' — a Spanish photography presence at the epicentre of world photography for the duration of the opening week.

The 2026 jury reflects the international-positioning intent: Christoph Wiesner (Director, Les Rencontres d'Arles), Elisa Medde (Director, Foto Colectania Foundation), Kim Boske (FUTURES Residencies), Mathieu Asselin (Co-Founder, doubledummy), and Shinji Nagabe (visual artist).
Eligibility is restricted to Spanish photographers 18+. Work must be produced and exhibition-ready. Physical presence in Arles during opening week is mandatory.

Organised by El Local (Madrid-based independent contemporary photography space) in partnership with Plataforma Fotografía e Imagen, with support from Spain's Ministry of Culture. Submission is via digital form, one project per applicant. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 19.

calls.title: APhF Pick:26 Book Award
calls.description: Annual juried photobook award from the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photobooks worldwide produced or published between January 2025 and March 2026 with a minimum edition of 100 copies. Winner receives €2,000 cash prize and inclusion in the main festival exhibition programme at Benaki Museum. Ten photobooks featured in the APhF:26 print catalogue, twenty shortlisted and exhibited at Benaki Museum / Pireos 138. All submitted works added to the APhF Library and Athens Photo Research Center. Submit online entry form, cover image, project description, artist biography, and mail two physical copies to the Hellenic Center of Photography in Athens. €15 for each additional project by the same applicant.
jury: Marta Weiss, Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum
Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi, Publisher, Chose Commune
Sylvia Sachini, Curator, APhF Book Program
calls.summary: Photobook award from Athens Photo Festival. €2,000 prize. 20 shortlisted exhibited at Benaki Museum. Min 100-copy edition.
prose: APhF Pick:26 is the annual juried photobook award from the Hellenic Centre of Photography, run as part of Athens Photo Festival. The award is restricted by edition rather than category: open to photobooks worldwide produced or published between January 2025 and March 2026, with a minimum edition of 100 copies.

The 2026 jury is built from major institutional photography figures: Katerina Gregos (Artistic Director, EMST), Marta Weiss (Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum), Joan Fontcuberta (artist), Katy Hundertmark (Curator & Editor, Foam), Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi (Publisher, Chose Commune), and Sylvia Sachini (Curator, APhF Book Program).

Selection structure has multiple tiers. The winner receives a €2,000 cash prize and inclusion in the main Athens Photo Festival exhibition programme at the Benaki Museum. Ten photobooks are featured in the APhF:26 print catalogue. Twenty shortlisted books are exhibited at the Benaki Museum / Pireos 138 venue. All submitted works are added to the APhF Library and Athens Photo Research Center.

Submission is hybrid: an online entry form (cover image, project description, artist biography) plus mail two physical copies to the Hellenic Center of Photography in Athens. Fee is €25; €15 for each additional project by the same applicant.
The 2026 deadline was April 28; results announced June 16, 2026.

calls.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: First edition of a new international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2026. Fourteen winners honoured at an awards ceremony in Tours in early May. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award. Winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy — a physical gold statuette created specifically for the contest. All nominees exhibited in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Printing costs covered by organisers. AI-generated images not accepted. Fee varies by number of works submitted: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 images per registration.
calls.summary: First international festival for abstract & surrealist photography. Physical exhibition in Tours, France. Trophy + online 3D gallery.
prose: ABSURIA Festival is a new international photography festival in Tours, in France's Loire Valley. The 2026 edition is the inaugural cycle. The festival is restricted by genre: abstract and surrealist photography only — exclusively non-representational and dream-state work.

Selection structure has multiple layers. 100 photographs are selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, May through September 2026. Printing costs are covered by the organisers. All nominees are also exhibited in 3D online galleries on the festival website.

Fourteen winners are honoured at an awards ceremony in Tours in early May 2026. Categories run across two domains (Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography), each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award.
The prize is the ABSURIA Trophy — a physical gold statuette created specifically for the contest, awarded to category winners. There's no central cash prize. AI-generated images are not accepted.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+, amateur and professional. Selection is by Caroline Gasch (photographer), Marie-Pierre Cherrier (photographer and teacher), and Bob Jeudy (collector and patron). Fee is tiered by entry scale: €20–€40 (amateur) and €25–€50 (professional), up to 6 images per registration. The 2026 deadline was April 26; results announced early May 2026.

calls.title: Athens Photo Festival Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International photobook dummy competition run by the Hellenic Centre of Photography as part of Athens Photo Festival. Open to all photographers and artists who use photography, regardless of age or nationality. Winner receives a publishing contract with Chose Commune for the production of a photobook with a production budget of up to €15,000 and a minimum print run of 400 copies. Winning project included in the festival's main exhibition programme at Benaki Museum in Athens. Twenty shortlisted dummies exhibited at the festival, ten included in the printed catalogue. Submit digitally via online form (PDF, max 10 MB) and mail one physical dummy copy postmarked by the deadline. Projects should be finalized upon submission. If already printed, editions must be under 100 copies. Fee €25 per project, €15 for additional projects by the same applicant.
jury: Katerina Gregos, Artistic Director, EMΣT (National Museum of Contemporary Art, Athens)
Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi, Publisher, Chose Commune
Marta Weiss, Curator of Photography, Victoria and Albert Museum
Sylvia Sachini, Curator, APhF Book Program
calls.summary: Dummy award with Chose Commune publishing contract (up to €15K). 20 shortlisted exhibited at Athens Photo Festival, Benaki Museum.
prose: The Athens Photo Festival Dummy Award is the festival's annual photobook-dummy competition, run by the Hellenic Centre of Photography. The award is structured around publication: the winner receives a publishing contract with Chose Commune, the Paris-based independent photobook publisher, for production of a photobook with a budget of up to €15,000 and a minimum print run of 400 copies.

The 2026 jury is shared with the Pick:26 Book Award: Joan Fontcuberta, Katerina Gregos (Artistic Director, EMΣT, the National Museum of Contemporary Art Athens), Cécile Sayuri Poimboeuf-Koizumi (Publisher, Chose Commune), Marta Weiss (V&A), Katy Hundertmark (Foam), and Sylvia Sachini (APhF Book Program).

Selection has multiple tiers. The winning project enters the festival's main exhibition programme at the Benaki Museum in Athens. Twenty shortlisted dummies are exhibited at the festival; ten are included in the printed catalogue.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers and artists who use photography, regardless of age or nationality. Projects must be finalized at submission. If already printed in any form, editions must be under 100 copies — the award is for unpublished or barely-published work.

Submission is hybrid: digital online form with a PDF (max 10 MB) plus one physical dummy copy mailed postmarked by the deadline. Fee is €25 per project; €15 for additional projects by the same applicant. The 2026 deadline was April 28; results announced June 14, 2026.

calls.title: Motion
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring motion in still images. Photography cannot create the illusion of motion the way moving images can, yet photographers have developed powerful techniques for capturing and evoking it — from long exposures and motion blur to freezing split-second moments of action. PH21 Gallery invites submissions for a themed group show at their venue in Barcelona's historic Gothic Quarter. One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions will be announced. Curator's choice receives free entry (up to 15 images) for the next PH21 exhibition. Early bird deadline April 20 at reduced rates; final deadline April 27. Special rate for students and unwaged (€15–€20). All photographers 18+ worldwide may enter with original work. Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1200px. Exhibition June 27 – July 21, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on motion in photography. Physical exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. Student rates available.
prose: PH21 Gallery is a photography gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter that runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. Motion is the gallery's call for work engaging with movement — long exposures, motion blur, frozen split-second action, panning, sequence — photography's various technical strategies for capturing and evoking what it cannot literally show.

One curator's choice and up to three honourable mentions are announced. The curator's choice receives free entry (up to 15 images) for the next PH21 exhibition cycle. Selected work hangs at the gallery in Barcelona, June 27 – July 21, 2026.
Selection is by gallery director Zsolt Bátori (photographer and philosopher of art) and Borbála Jász (art historian and philosopher of art).
Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+ with original work. Submission is by email — JPEG, longest side max 1200px, 3–15 images.

Fee structure includes an early-bird discount (deadline April 20) and a special student/unwaged rate of €15–€20. Standard rates run €25–€50. The 2026 final deadline was April 27; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Manipulation & Illusion
calls.description: Open call exploring the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. Seeking work that engages with manipulation and illusion as they relate to perception, belief, identity, and power. Themes include optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; and altered materials, images, and data. All disciplines welcome — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft. Submissions accepted exclusively through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal. Selected work featured in a curated online collection. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Explore perception, belief, identity, and power through illusion and manipulation. All disciplines. Free, open worldwide.
prose: Manipulation & Illusion is an open call from Co-Ex Collaborative for work that engages with the terrain between what is seen and what is constructed. The brief is unusually expansive: applicants can address optical, sensory, and spatial illusion; distortion, misdirection, and scale; unreliable memory; propaganda and political persuasion; digital manipulation and curated environments; institutional narratives and manufactured truth; manipulation as artistic method; or altered materials, images, and data.

The call is interdisciplinary — photography, visual art, design, and fine craft are all eligible. Submissions go through the Co-Ex Collaborative website portal, with one image per applicant. There is no entry fee.

Selected work is featured in a curated online collection on Co-Ex's site. Specific prize structure, jury composition, and historical context aren't published on the call page; the platform appears to operate as a curated online publication rather than a competition with cash awards. The deadline is September 12, 2026.

calls.title: Epson International Pano Awards 2026
calls.description: 17th edition of the world's largest international competition for panoramic photography. Three main categories: Open (professional and amateur, $22/image), Amateur (non-professional photographers earning less than $20,000 from photography, $20/image), and VR/360 ($20/image) — plus a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images. Total prize pool over US$50,000 including $15,000 in cash prizes. Open category winner receives a package exceeding $11,000. Early-bird entries close June 22 at standard rates; late entries accepted through July 13 at higher rates. Photographers who enter during the early-bird period are eligible for the $1,000 Curator's Award. Images must be panoramic format with aspect ratio greater than 2:1 (or less than 1:2 for verticals). All photographic capture methods welcome including digital, film, and stitched panoramas. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: World's largest panoramic photography competition. $50K+ prizes incl. $15K cash. New Aerial category. Open, Amateur, VR/360.
prose: The Epson International Pano Awards is the world's largest competition exclusively for panoramic photography, now in its 17th edition. The prize is sponsored by Epson with major presence in Australia and Southeast Asia.

Three competition divisions run in parallel: Open (professional and amateur photographers, $22 per image), Amateur (restricted to non-professionals earning less than $20,000 annually from photography, $20 per image), and VR/360 ($20 per image). The 2026 cycle introduces a new Aerial category for drone and aircraft images, alongside the existing Nature/Landscapes and Built Environment subcategories.

The total prize pool exceeds US$50,000, with US$15,000 in direct cash. The Open category first prize is a package valued over $11,000. Early-bird entries (closing June 22) are eligible for the additional $1,000 Curator's Award; final-deadline entries (closing July 13) cost slightly more per image.

Submissions must meet the panoramic format requirement: an aspect ratio greater than 2:1 horizontally, or less than 1:2 vertically. All photographic capture methods are welcome — digital, film, and stitched panoramas. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The 2026 jury comprises Bill Bailey, Aaron Spence, Dan Zafra, Jacky Lee, Daniel Kordan, Abe Blair, Anette Mossbacher, and Jennifer Renwick. Eligibility is open worldwide. Results announced October 2026.

calls.summary: Square format photography — all genres. Pro printing and museum framing included. Three-month exhibition in Tucson, AZ.
prose: SQUARE is Decode Gallery's themed exhibition for photography composed within the square format — Decode treats square as both a constraint and a tradition (Hasselblad, Rolleiflex, Polaroid SX-70, Instagram), inviting photographers to engage with the format across genres rather than treat it as a separate style.

All photographic genres are welcome: portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, conceptual, abstract. Twelve photographs are selected for the three-month physical exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, Arizona, running November 7, 2026 through January 30, 2027.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 14×14 inch framing, and custom 7×7 inch mats. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for six months after the exhibition for further promotion.

Sales terms split commission 50/50. Selection is by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer with a BA from the Art Institute of Seattle. Entry fee is $40 for up to 10 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. The deadline is September 10, 2026; selected artists are notified within two weeks.

calls.summary: Juried museum exhibition on America's 250th anniversary themes. Open to MD, VA, WV, PA, DC photographers. $3K+ in cash prizes.
prose: Cumberland Valley Photographers is the annual regional juried photography exhibition at the Washington County Museum of Fine Arts (WCMFA) in Hagerstown, Maryland — a museum founded in 1931 with a permanent collection across American and European art.

The 2026 edition is built around the United States' approaching 250th anniversary. The brief structures four thematic prompts: Unfinished Revolutions, Power of Place, Tell Everyone's Story, and American Experiment. Photographers may respond literally or metaphorically through documentary, conceptual, figurative, or abstract approaches.
All photographic processes are accepted — no medium restriction. Eligibility is geographically restricted to photographers from Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Washington, DC.

Submission is through Smarter Entry with up to 4 works. Fee is $15. Prize pool is $3,000+. The 2026 application window was April 1–30; results announced May 8, 2026.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Issue 02: Eerie
calls.description: Second issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. Issue 02, guest curated by Karla Guerrero (Mexico City-based photographer, curator, and editor active in the contemporary photography scene), explores the theme Eerie — quiet disturbance, a poetics of phantasmagoria where images silently evoke meaning. The eerie as the fleeting suggestion that something unnameable lingers just beneath what we think we see. Something quietly disturbing. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px) with artist statement and bio. Upload work to Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files: Name_Series_Title_01. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Eerie. Guest curated by Karla Guerrero. Print publication.
prose: UNSTAGED is an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based work that engages with comforting and discomforting authenticity. Each issue is shaped by a different guest curator. Issue 02 is themed Eerie and guest curated by Karla Guerrero — a Mexico City-based photographer, curator, and editor active in the contemporary photography scene.

The brief reads the eerie as quiet disturbance — a poetics of phantasmagoria where images silently evoke meaning. The fleeting suggestion that something unnameable lingers just beneath what we think we see. Something quietly disturbing rather than frightening or grotesque.

Submission terms: 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px), with an artist statement and bio. The submission process is unusual: applicants upload work to a Google Drive folder and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Files must be named Name_Series_Title_01.
Selection results in inclusion in a free print publication. Application is free, eligibility is open globally. The Issue 02 deadline was April 20, 2026.

calls.summary: €8,000 grant for female photojournalists. 26th edition with Canon. Long-term documentary projects. Exhibited at Perpignan.

The grant is run in partnership with Canon, which provides primary funding. The 2026 cycle is the grant's 26th edition — among the longer-running specifically female-centered photojournalism awards.

The winner receives €8,000 to support the completion of an existing long-term documentary project or to facilitate the making of a new one. Beyond the cash, the winning project is exhibited at the Visa pour l'Image festival in Perpignan, September 2026 — Visa pour l'Image is one of the most prominent photojournalism festivals globally, drawing photo editors and agencies from around the world.

Eligibility is restricted to professional female photojournalists. There are no age or nationality restrictions. Submissions are free of charge. Each applicant submits 10 to 20 images of a documentary project, with project description and biography.

calls.title: MACK — Debut Photography Book Submissions
calls.description: MACK's annual submission window for first-time photobook authors. Founded by Michael Mack (former Managing Director of Steidl) in 2010, MACK is one of the most prestigious art and photography publishers in the world, releasing approximately 40 books per year with artists including Robert Adams, Alec Soth, and Wolfgang Tillmans. This window is specifically for artists who have not previously had a book published — seeking emerging voices and experimental approaches to the book form. Email subject line: 'Submission: Debut Photography Book'. Response within one month after the window closes.
calls.summary: MACK's window for first-time photobook authors. One of the world's most prestigious photography publishers.
prose: MACK is a London-based independent photobook publisher founded in 2010 by Michael Mack, formerly Managing Director of Steidl. The publisher releases approximately 40 photobooks per year and has published work with photographers including Robert Adams, Alec Soth, and Wolfgang Tillmans. The Debut Photography Book window is specifically reserved for first-time photobook authors — artists who have not previously had a book published.

The window favors experimental approaches to the book form. The brief is loose: MACK is looking for emerging voices working through book sequencing as a primary medium rather than treating the book as a passive container for finished images.

The window is edited by Michael Mack and Iman Hakimi, with both involved in the selection process. Each submission consists of a single PDF (a draft sequence of the project) plus a completed submissions form, sent to submissions@mackbooks.co.uk with the subject line "Submission: Debut Photography Book." WeTransfer, Dropbox, and other download links are not accepted.

MACK does not provide feedback on rejected submissions. From acceptance to publication, the publisher notes that "it typically takes between one and two years to develop and prepare a book for publication" — submission is the beginning of a long collaborative process rather than an immediate decision. The publisher commits to responding within one month of the window's deadline.
Submissions are accepted only during the May 1 through May 31, 2026 window.

calls.title: MACK — Photography Submissions
