calls.title: PhMuseum Days 2026 Open Call
calls.description: International photo festival competition offering 4 solo exhibitions plus additional opportunities. All approaches welcome, including experimental.
jury: Giuseppe Oliverio, Founding & Artistic Director, PhMuseum
Tara L. C. Sood, Photographer & Filmmaker
calls.summary: International festival competition. 4 solo exhibitions plus additional opportunities. All approaches welcome.
prose: PhMuseum Days is the annual photography festival organized by PhMuseum in Bologna, Italy. The 2026 cycle is the 5th edition, running October 1–4, 2026 at the Ex Ospedale dei Bastardini venue. The 2026 theme is "Archipelago," exploring crisis and new models of coexistence.

The selection structure is layered. At least 3 photographers receive solo exhibitions at the main venue with substantial production support: a production budget of up to €2,500 plus VAT, a €300 artist fee, and a travel contribution scaled by region (€300 for Italy, €500 for Europe, €800 for overseas). One additional photographer is selected for a public billboard installation across 11 sites in Bologna's historical center, with €300 fee plus travel support.

Beyond solo placements, up to 40 images are selected for a sculptural collective installation (running September 19 through October 8 alongside the festival), and up to 20 projects are chosen for video screenings. The MPB Special Mention awards a €1,000 voucher for used photography gear.

The 2026 jury comprises Tara L.C. Sood (photographer/filmmaker), Pacifico Silano (visual artist), Rita Puig-Serra Costa (photographer), and Giuseppe Oliverio (PhMuseum's Founding and Artistic Director).

Entry fee is $38 (extended-deadline pricing). Submissions accept 5 to 20 photos as JPG/PNG at maximum 20MB each. Collaborative projects, works-in-progress, and previously submitted work are all accepted. AI-generated work is accepted but must be disclosed. All applicants receive free festival passes. The 2026 deadline is May 14.

calls.title: Brussels Street Photography Festival 2026
calls.description: International street photography competition with Singles and Series tracks. Singles: up to 10 individual photos. Series: 5–7 cohesive street photos. Winners exhibited at the festival in Brussels, May 28–31, 2026.
calls.summary: International street photography competition with Singles and Series tracks. Exhibition in Brussels, May 2026.
prose: Brussels Street Photography Festival is an annual festival in Brussels, Belgium. The 2026 festival runs May 28–31. The competition has two parallel tracks: Singles (up to 10 individual photos) and Series (5–7 cohesive street photographs).
Total prize fund is €5,200. Winning work is exhibited at the festival.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through JotForm with 1–10 images depending on track. Fee is tiered €12–€45 by track and submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 25.

calls.title: Form Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Annual photography prize dedicated to contemporary image-making. Open theme, accepts single images and series. Top 5 winners exhibit at photo basel during Art Basel Week in June 2026. Shortlisted receive digital exhibition and catalogue inclusion.
jury: Sven Eisenhut-Hug, Co-Founder & Director, photo basel
calls.summary: Annual prize for contemporary image-making. Top 5 exhibit at photo basel during Art Basel Week, June 2026.
prose: Form Gallery is a Basel-based photography platform founded by Dimitri Bogachuk. The annual Form Photo Award is dedicated to contemporary image-making, with no thematic restriction. Both single images and series are accepted.

The structural premise is positioning: the top 5 winners exhibit at photo basel — the international photography fair held during Art Basel Week each June. Selected work reaches the audience that travels to Basel for the wider Art Basel program.
Beyond the top 5, shortlisted artists receive a digital exhibition and inclusion in the catalogue.
The 2026 jury is Sven Eisenhut-Hug (Co-Founder & Director, photo basel), Elwira Spychalska (art historian), and Dimitri Bogachuk (Form Founder).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Picter with 1–8 images. Fee is €35. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced March 30, 2026.

calls.title: Head On Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: Major international photography festival in Sydney with an AUD 80,000 total prize pool across Portrait, Landscape, and Exposure categories. Blind-judged. Selected work exhibited in print and online during the November 2026 festival.
calls.summary: Major international festival in Sydney. AUD 80,000 prize pool across Portrait, Landscape, and Exposure categories.
prose: Head On Photo Festival is the international photography festival held annually in Sydney, Australia. The festival's awards run across three categories: Portrait, Landscape, and Exposure (general open category). Total prize pool is AUD 80,000.
The judging is structural: blind-judged. Jurors review work without knowing the photographer's identity, which the festival presents as a deliberate equality measure.
Selected work is exhibited in print and online during the November 2026 festival.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the festival's website with 10 images. Fee is $35 AUD. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced November 2026.

calls.title: Sirmione Photo Residency 2026
calls.description: Two-week photography residency in Sirmione, Lake Garda (October 2026). Mentorship from Andrea Holzherr and Ludovica Pellegatta (Magnum Photos). Resulting work published as a book by the municipality.
jury: Andréa Holzherr, Global Cultural Director, Magnum Photos
Ludovica Pellegatta, Partnerships Director, Magnum Photos
calls.summary: Two-week residency at Lake Garda. Mentorship from Andrea Holzherr and Ludovica Pellegatta (Magnum Photos).
prose: Sirmione Photo Residency is organized by the Comune di Sirmione (the municipality of Sirmione) on the south shore of Lake Garda, Italy. The 2026 residency runs two weeks in October.

The residency is mentorship-led: Andréa Holzherr (Global Cultural Director, Magnum Photos) and Ludovica Pellegatta (Partnerships Director, Magnum Photos) work directly with the resident across the program — bringing Magnum's editorial and curatorial perspective to the project.
The selected resident receives a €2,500 fee. The work made during the residency is published as a book by the municipality.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the residency website with a PDF containing minimum 20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: 9th Chania International Photo Festival
calls.description: International photography exhibition in Chania's historic Grand Arsenali building. Submit 1–5 photos across 16 categories. Selected photos printed and framed at no cost by the festival.
jury: Maria Toutoudaki, Director, Blank Wall Gallery
Bob Patterson, Publisher, Street Photography Magazine
Frank Van Es, Professor, Grafisch Lyceum Rotterdam
calls.summary: International exhibition in Chania's historic Grand Arsenali. Selected photos printed and framed by the festival.
prose: The Chania International Photo Festival is held annually in Chania, on the Greek island of Crete. The festival is organized by Athens-based Blank Wall Gallery. The 2026 edition is the festival's 9th cycle.

Selected work is exhibited in the Grand Arsenali — Chania's restored Venetian-era arsenals, now used for cultural programming. The festival prints and frames selected photos at no cost to participants.

The brief is broad: 1–5 photos across 16 categories. Selection is by Maria Toutoudaki (Director, Blank Wall Gallery), Alain Schroeder (photographer), Bob Patterson (Publisher, Street Photography Magazine), and Frank Van Es (Professor, Grafisch Lyceum Rotterdam).
The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a €43 fee charged only if accepted for the exhibition.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced April 15, 2026.

calls.title: EuroNatur Photo Competition 2026
calls.description: Nature photography competition for photographers residing in Europe. Submit up to 5 photos of European flora, fauna, and landscapes. 33rd edition. Winners published in EuroNatur magazine and included in 2027 wall calendar.
jury: Christiane Stewen, Public Relations, GELSENWASSER AG
calls.summary: Nature photography for European residents. Winners published in EuroNatur magazine and 2027 wall calendar.
prose: EuroNatur is a German nature conservation foundation based in Radolfzell. The Photo Competition is the foundation's annual call for nature photography from across Europe. The 2026 edition is the competition's 33rd cycle — long-running.
Eligibility is restricted to photographers residing in Europe. Submitted work must depict European flora, fauna, or landscapes — geographically restricted by both photographer and subject.
Top prize is €1,500. Winners are published in EuroNatur magazine and included in EuroNatur's 2027 wall calendar.

Selection is by Kerstin Sauer (Art Director, EuroNatur), Robin Vornholz (Editor, natur magazine), Christiane Stewen (Public Relations, GELSENWASSER AG), Darja Wintersig (event photographer), and Peter Laufmann (environmental journalist).
Submission is by email with up to 5 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced Fall 2026.

calls.title: Vision(ary) 2026: Raising Our Voices
calls.description: Annual outdoor public art exhibition transforming downtown Winchester, MA into an open-air gallery (June–September 2026). Theme: advocacy and social justice. Submit 5–10 images of a complete project via CaFE. Juror: Elizabeth Krist (National Geographic).
calls.summary: Outdoor public art exhibition in Winchester, MA. Theme: advocacy and social justice. Juror: Elizabeth Krist (Nat Geo).
prose: Vision(ary) is the Griffin Museum of Photography's annual outdoor public art exhibition. The exhibition transforms downtown Winchester, Massachusetts into an open-air gallery — selected work is installed in public spaces around the town from June through September 2026.
The 2026 theme is Raising Our Voices: advocacy and social justice. The brief asks photographers to submit complete projects rather than single images that respond to the theme.
Selection is by Elizabeth Krist, independent visual editor formerly with National Geographic.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through CaFÉ with 5–10 images of a complete project. Fee is $45. The 2026 deadline was April 5; results announced after May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Griffin Museum — Self Published Photobook Exhibition 2026
calls.description: 16th annual exhibition showcasing up to 50 self-published photobooks at the Griffin Gallery during summer 2026. Submit up to 3 photobook PDFs via CaFE. Jurors: Karen Davis (Davis Orton Gallery) and Crista Dix (Griffin Museum).
jury: Karen Davis, Curator, Davis Orton Gallery
Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum
calls.summary: 16th annual exhibition showcasing up to 50 self-published photobooks at the Griffin Gallery, summer 2026.
prose: The Self Published Photobook Exhibition is the Griffin Museum of Photography's annual summer exhibition focused specifically on self-published photobooks. The 2026 edition is the show's 16th cycle.

Up to 50 self-published photobooks are selected for display at the Griffin Gallery in Winchester, Massachusetts during summer 2026. The exhibition treats self-publishing as a distinct mode of photographic practice rather than a stepping-stone toward commercial publication.
Selection is by Karen Davis (Curator, Davis Orton Gallery) and Crista Dix (Executive Director, Griffin Museum).
Each applicant submits up to 3 photobooks as PDFs. Submission is through CaFÉ. Fee is $45. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced after May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Siena Creative Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: International contest rewarding originality and experimentation in photography across 8 categories including Fine Art, People, Architecture, and Nature. Winners honored at the ceremony in Siena's Teatro dei Rinnovati.
calls.summary: International contest rewarding originality across 8 categories. Winners honored at ceremony in Siena's Teatro dei Rinnovati.
prose: Siena Awards is the umbrella organization that runs several annual photography competitions, including Siena International Photo Awards and Drone Photo Awards. The Creative Photo Awards is the umbrella's category-broad creative photography cycle.

The 2026 edition runs across eight categories including Fine Art, People, Architecture, and Nature. The brief rewards originality and experimentation rather than documentary fidelity. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Winners are honored at the awards ceremony at Siena's Teatro dei Rinnovati during the Siena Awards Festival. Selected work is shown in the festival's exhibitions, which run through Siena and travel to other cities.
The 2026 jury is six photographers: Gina Williams, Raphaelle Granger, Marianna Santoni, Tetiana Udovychenko, Daria Bonera, and Inessa Yurovskikh.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the awards website with unlimited images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced October 10, 2026.

calls.title: Objectif FEMMES 2026
calls.description: Open call for female photographers exploring the bicentennial of photography. Selected artists exhibit at Salons Aguado in Paris. Submit up to 10 photographs with artist statement. Open to professional and emerging photographers.
calls.summary: Open call for female photographers exploring the bicentennial of photography. Exhibition at Salons Aguado in Paris.
prose: Objectif FEMMES is an annual call from PARISARTISTES# focused on women photographers. The 2026 edition takes the bicentennial of photography (1826–2026) as its prompt — work that engages with photography's history, technique, or 200-year material lineage.

Selected artists exhibit at Salons Aguado, an exhibition space in Paris. Eligibility is restricted to women photographers, 18+, with the call open to both professional and emerging photographers — career stage is not a filter.
AI-generated work is not accepted.

Each application includes up to 10 photographs and an artist statement. Submission is through the Objectif FEMMES website. Fee is €40. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced November 10, 2026.

calls.title: Counter Histories Puerto Rico
calls.description: Fellowship for photographers engaging with Puerto Rico and its diaspora, supporting projects that creatively reframe the past. 8-month virtual fellowship with one in-person symposium. Up to 8 recipients. Applications in English or Spanish.
calls.summary: Fellowship for photographers engaging with Puerto Rico and its diaspora. 8-month virtual fellowship, up to 8 recipients.
prose: Counter Histories is a Magnum Foundation fellowship program that supports photographers engaging with specific historical contexts. The 2026 cycle is focused on Puerto Rico and its diaspora — supporting projects that creatively reframe the past rather than only document the present.
Eligibility is restricted by subject and ties: photographers engaging with Puerto Rican histories or working from within the Puerto Rican diaspora. Applications are accepted in English or Spanish.
The fellowship is structured as an eight-month virtual program with one in-person symposium. Up to eight recipients per cycle. Each fellow receives a $10,000 stipend.
Application is free, submitted through Submittable with work samples. The 2026 deadline was April 1; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Golden Shot International Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography competition across 16 categories including Portrait, Landscape, Street, Fine Art, Documentary, and Nature. Open to professional and amateur photographers. Winners announced July 2026.
calls.summary: International competition across 16 categories including Portrait, Landscape, Street, Fine Art, and Documentary.
prose: Golden Shot International Photography Awards (GSP Awards) is an annual international photography competition. The 2026 edition runs across 16 categories including Portrait, Landscape, Street, Fine Art, Documentary, and Nature.
Top prize is $1,000. Selection is by Tomas Neuwirth, Remi Masson, Muneera Alobaidli, and Dikye Ariani — all photographers — alongside the platform's founder Mehdi Nazeri.

Eligibility is open to professional and amateur photographers 18+ globally. Submission is through the awards website with unlimited images. Fee is tiered $25–$35 based on submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 10; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: Meitar Award for Excellence in Photography 2026
calls.description: International award recognizing a cohesive body of photographic work. 20 finalists exhibited at the International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv (November 2026). Winner receives a solo exhibition at the 2027 festival. 10th edition.
jury: Dafna Meitar Nechmad, Director General, Zvi and Ofra Meitar Family Fund
Laura Letinsky, Professor, University of Chicago
Anne Leighton Massoni, Director, Houston Center for Photography
Dr. Gilad Reich, Curator of Photography, The Israel Museum
calls.summary: International award. 20 finalists exhibited at Tel Aviv festival. Winner gets solo exhibition at 2027 festival.
prose: The Meitar Award for Excellence in Photography is an annual international photography prize organized by Photo Is:rael — the platform behind Israel's International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv. The 2026 edition is the award's 10th cycle.
The award is for a cohesive body of photographic work rather than single images. Top prize is $14,000.
Selection structure: 20 finalists are exhibited at the International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv in November 2026. The overall winner receives a solo exhibition at the 2027 festival.

The 2026 jury draws from international institutions: Dafna Meitar Nechmad (Director General, Zvi and Ofra Meitar Family Fund — the award's sponsoring fund), photographers Roger Ballen, Doron Oved, and Sarah Mei Hermann, Laura Letinsky (Professor, University of Chicago), Anne Leighton Massoni (Director, Houston Center for Photography), Michael Benson (Co-Founder, PHOTO LONDON), Dr. Gilad Reich (Curator of Photography, The Israel Museum), and Rivka Saker (Chairman, Sotheby's Israel). AI-generated work is accepted.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the award's website with 6–12 images. Fee is tiered $35–$45. The 2026 deadline was April 12; results announced November 2, 2026.

calls.title: Street Photography Barcelona Contest 2026
calls.description: International street photography contest seeking authentic images of urban life. Three geographic categories: Local (Barcelona), National (Spain), and International. 25 finalists exhibited at Galerie Art Nomade, Barcelona.
jury: Olivier Verdier, Curator, Galerie Art Nomade
calls.summary: Authentic images of urban life. Three categories: Local, National, International. Exhibited at Galerie Art Nomade.
prose: Street Photography Barcelona is a Barcelona-based street photography organization that runs an annual international contest. The 2026 edition is structured by geography rather than theme: three categories — Local (Barcelona), National (Spain), and International.
AI-generated work is not accepted — the contest restricts to authentic capture.
Top prize is €1,000. Twenty-five finalists are exhibited at Galerie Art Nomade in Barcelona.
Selection is by Xavi Herrero (festival director) and Olivier Verdier (curator, Galerie Art Nomade).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through Picter with 1–5 images. Fee is tiered €10–€40 by category and submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 20; results announced May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Impressum Photo Award 2026
calls.description: International photography contest with 7 open-theme sections and 2 themed projects (2026 theme: Rigenerare). Submit up to 25 photos. Free entry for ages 16–20. Finalists exhibited at the festival galleries for one month.
calls.summary: 7 open-theme sections and 2 themed projects (Rigenerare). Free entry ages 16-20. Finalists exhibited one month.
prose: The Impressum Photo Award is the open call for the Appennino Foto Festival, held in the Marche region of central Italy. The festival's structure is broad: nine award sections in total — seven with open themes plus two themed-project sections built around the 2026 theme Rigenerare (regeneration).
Total prize fund is €3,900 distributed across the nine sections. Selected finalists are exhibited in festival galleries for one month — the show is the festival's main public output.

The 2026 jury is a panel of ten Italian photographers: Alessandro Bergamini, Cinza Canneri, Giuseppe Capriotti, Edoardo Catini, Alessandro Curti, Barbara Dall'Angelo, Valerio Minato, Helmut Pilo, Christian Tasso, and Francesca Tilio. AI-generated work is accommodated through a dedicated category rather than excluded.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 16+. There's an unusual age-based fee waiver: free entry for ages 16–20. Standard fee is €30. Submission is through the festival's website with up to 25 photos. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced Autumn 2026.

prose: The Black & White Spider Awards is an annual international award restricted by process: black-and-white photography only. The 2026 edition is the award's 21st cycle.

The structure runs 235+ title awards across categories — winners are announced not only as overall prizes but as title-holders within sub-genres. Winners are announced at a live Photoshow in November 2026.

The 2026 (21st annual) jury has not yet been announced — the awards page lists it as "To Be Announced." Each year the Spider Awards select, by invitation, a rotating panel of internationally respected curators, gallerists, editors, publishers and photography professionals; recent panels have drawn from institutions such as Bonhams, Tate Modern and the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts.
AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally to professional and amateur photographers.

Submission is through the awards website. Photographers can submit unlimited images; fee is tiered $30–$35 based on submission scale. The 2026 closing deadline is July 24; results announced November 7, 2026.

calls.title: ND Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography competition across categories including Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special. Open to professional and non-professional photographers.
calls.summary: International competition across Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special categories.
prose: ND Awards is an annual international photography competition associated with ND Magazine. The 2026 edition runs across multiple categories: Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — covering most major commercial and editorial photography genres.

The total awards pool tops $10,000: the professional Photographer of the Year wins $3,500 cash and the non-professional Discovery of the Year $2,400, alongside $400–$500 category-winner prizes. Selected work is featured on the ND Awards platform and promoted through ND Magazine's channels.

The 2026 jury is large — over 25 photographers, photojournalists, professors, and interdisciplinary artists from multiple countries. Notable jurors include Lydia Panas, Mahe Elipe, Valery Poshtarov, Oded Wagenstein, and photojournalist Rui Caria.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+, professional and non-professional. Submission is through the ND Awards website with 1–5 images per entry. Fee is tiered $24–$34 by submission scale, plus $10 per additional category. The 2026 final deadline is September 20; results announced November 22, 2026.

calls.title: International Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: One of the world's most prestigious annual photography competitions. 23rd edition. Eleven categories including Fine Art, Documentary, Nature, Portrait, and Photojournalism. $60,000 total prize pool. Sister organization of the Lucie Foundation.
jury: Michael Pritchard, Director-General, Royal Photographic Society
calls.summary: One of the most prestigious annual competitions. 23rd edition. $60,000 prize pool across eleven categories.
prose: The International Photography Awards (IPA) was founded in 2003 and is now in its 23rd edition — one of the longer-running international photography competitions. The IPA is the sister organization of the Lucie Foundation, which administers the Lucie Awards.

Submissions are split between Professional and Non-Professional tracks across 11 categories: Advertising, Analog/Film, Architectural, Editorial, Event, Fine Art, Nature, People, Sports, Photography Book, and Special Category. Total prize pool is $60,000 across the program.

Top awards: International Photographer of the Year (Professional, $10,000) and Discovery of the Year (Non-Professional, $5,000). Each Professional Category winner receives $1,000 cash plus a $500 travel allowance; each Non-Professional Category winner receives $500 plus $500 travel. Beyond cash, IPA category winners receive an IPA Trophy, two tickets to the IPA Awards Gala, inclusion in the Best of Show exhibition, screening at House of Lucie Galleries worldwide, publication in the IPA Annual Book, and press coverage to the program's 130,000+ member network.

The 2026 jury includes Anne Morin (curator at diChroma Photography), Caroline Metcalfe (Photography Director), Giovanna Calvenzi (photo editor and curator), Kirk McKoy (photojournalist), Michael Pritchard (Director-General of the Royal Photographic Society), Paris Chong (Leica Gallery LA), and others. Entry fees are tiered between $20 and $40 depending on category and submission tier. The 2026 deadline is June 30; results announced October 2026.

prose: The Photo Journalism Prize is an international award honoring editorial and documentary photography. It was founded by Hossein Farmani, the same publisher who created the Lucie Awards.

The 2026 edition runs across 11 categories including Conflict, Daily Life, Documentary, Human Rights, and News. Total prize fund is €9,000: first €5,000, second €3,000, third €1,000. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the prize website with 1–10 images per entry. Fee is tiered €20–€25. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced June 15, 2026.

calls.description: International black-and-white photography competition for project-based work. Submit 8–24 B&W images from any medium. All genres welcome. Winners published in a dedicated book. 3rd edition.
calls.summary: Project-based B&W competition. Submit 8-24 images. Winners published in a dedicated book. 3rd edition.
prose: Gomma Publishing is an independent photobook publisher specializing in black-and-white photography. The Gomma Black and White Photo Award is the publisher's annual project-based competition. The 2026 edition is the award's third cycle.

The brief is process-restricted but genre-open: project-based black-and-white photography of any kind, sourced from any medium (film, digital, hybrid). All genres welcome — documentary, fine art, conceptual. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Each application includes 8–24 black-and-white images forming a coherent project. Single-image submissions are not eligible — the award is structured around bodies of work.
Winners are published in a dedicated Gomma book. Cash prize is €500.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Submittable. Fee is €29. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced December 2026.

calls.title: Landskrona Foto & Breadfield Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International photobook dummy competition. Submit an unpublished photobook dummy as PDF. Winner receives full publication by Breadfield Press and Landskrona Foto in 2027 including design, printing, and distribution.
jury: Raquel Villar-Pérez, Independent Curator of Photography
Tommaso Parrillo, Publisher & Art Director, Witty Books
calls.summary: Photobook dummy competition. Winner receives full publication by Breadfield Press in 2027.
prose: Landskrona Foto is a Swedish photography institution that runs an annual festival in Landskrona — a small port town on the Öresund. Breadfield Press is a Malmö-based independent photobook publisher. The Dummy Award is a joint project — a photobook dummy competition with a full publication outcome.

The brief is straightforward: submit an unpublished photobook dummy. The winning project is published in 2027 as a Breadfield Press / Landskrona Foto co-edition, with design, printing, and distribution all covered by the partnership. The publication is the prize — there's no cash component.

The 2026 jury is Raquel Villar-Pérez (independent curator of photography), Greger Ulf Nilson (creative director), Jenny Lindhe (curator and artist), Mandy Barker (photographer), and Tommaso Parrillo (publisher and art director, Witty Books).
Eligibility is open globally to artists 18+. Submission is through Picter as a single PDF dummy. Fee is €30. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced September 4, 2026.

calls.title: International Aerial Photographer of the Year 2026
calls.org: International Aerial Photographer of the Year
calls.description: Competition celebrating aerial photography from all platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, hot air balloons, mountains, and skyscrapers. Images must be aerial perspective, shot since January 2021.
calls.summary: Celebrating aerial photography from all platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, mountains, and skyscrapers.
prose: International Aerial Photographer of the Year (ILPOTY) is a competition focused on aerial photography across all capture platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, hot air balloons, and even high-vantage-point work from mountains and skyscrapers. The eligibility criterion is the perspective of the image, not the equipment used to make it.
Submitted work must be aerial perspective and shot since January 2021 — recency restricted. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Top prize is $10,000. Submission is unlimited — entrants can submit as many images as they want for a single $22 entry fee, which is unusual for the competition format.
The 2026 jury is chaired by Peter Eastway, with Tom Hegen (the German photographer best known for aerial views of industrial landscapes), Isabella Tabacchi, and drone photographer Joanna Steidle.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the awards' Secure Platform portal. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: ReA! Art Fair 2026
calls.description: Open call for emerging visual artists including photographers for a contemporary art fair at Fabbrica del Vapore, Milan, October 22–25, 2026. All visual art accepted. 50 artists selected; no additional exhibiting costs.
calls.summary: Contemporary art fair at Fabbrica del Vapore, Milan. 50 emerging artists selected. No exhibiting costs.
prose: ReA! Art Fair is a Milan contemporary art fair focused on emerging artists. The 2026 edition runs October 22–25 at Fabbrica del Vapore, the city's converted industrial cultural complex.

Fifty artists are selected through the open call. The fair is multidisciplinary — all visual art is accepted, including photography. Selected artists exhibit without additional booth or production costs beyond the application fee.

Eligibility is restricted to emerging artists. The €1,500 prize is awarded to one of the selected artists. The 2026 jury is five curators: Milena Zanetti, Valeria Conti, Vittoria Martinotti, Erica Massaccesi, and Maria Myasnikova.
Application is via the fair's website with a portfolio PDF. The fee is €55. The 2026 deadline was May 6; results announced June 15, 2026.

calls.title: Prix Virginia 2026
calls.description: International photography prize exclusively for professional women photographers. Submit 12–18 cohesive photographs plus CV and artistic statement. Photos must not have been previously exhibited in France. Winner announced November 2026.
jury: Anna Planas, Artistic Director, Paris Photo
calls.summary: International photography prize exclusively for professional women photographers. Submit 12-18 cohesive photographs.
prose: Prix Virginia is a French international photography prize awarded to professional women photographers. It is organized by Association Sylvia S., based in Paris, with a single €10,000 grant going to the winner.

The 2026 jury is built from major European photography institutions: Damarice Amao (Centre Pompidou), Anna Planas (Artistic Director, Paris Photo), Fiona Rogers (Curator, V&A), and Pauline Vermare (Curator, Brooklyn Museum).
Eligibility is restricted to professional women photographers internationally. Submitted photographs must not have been previously exhibited in France.
The application requires 12–18 cohesive photographs from a single body of work, plus CV and artistic statement. Submission is through Award Force. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was May 7; the winner was announced in November 2026.

calls.title: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International black-and-white photography competition across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, and Street. Open to all skill levels.
calls.summary: International B&W competition across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, and Street.
prose: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards is run by MonoVisions Magazine, an online photography publication operating since 2016 with a focus on black-and-white work. The 2026 cycle is one of multiple international monochrome competitions, distinguished by its deeper category-tiered structure and large jury panel.

Submissions are accepted in two sections — Single photos or Series (maximum 8 photos per series) — across twelve subject categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature and Wildlife, Nude, People, Photojournalism, Portrait, Street Photography, and Travel.

The cash prize pool is $5,000, distributed across two top awards: Series of the Year ($3,000) and Photo of the Year ($2,000). Category winners and honorable mentions receive downloadable badges and certificates of achievement — recognition rather than additional cash.

The 2026 jury comprises 14 international judges: Cyrille Druart, Vera Saldivar de Lira, Arkadiusz Kubisiak, David Rathbone, Dr Nenad Nikolic, Agata Benhacoun, Michael Koster, Tatiana Kurnosova, Zhou HanShun, Monika K. Adler, Timurtas Onan, Keivan Cadinouche, and Philip Flip Collier — bringing together photographers and artists across multiple geographies.

Entry fees: $30 per series submission, $25 per single photo. Eligibility is open to professionals and amateurs at any skill level worldwide; both traditional and digital black-and-white photography are accepted. The 2026 deadline is May 17; winners announced July 26.

calls.title: Nature Photographer of the Year 2026
calls.description: International nature photography competition with 12 categories for individual images, a young photographers category (ages 10–17, free entry), and the Fred Hazelhoff Award for portfolios (€17.50). Award ceremony November 14, 2026.
calls.summary: International nature competition with 12 categories plus young photographers and portfolio awards.
prose: Nature Photographer of the Year (NPOTY) is an international nature photography competition organized by the Nature Talks Foundation (Stichting Nature Talks) in the Netherlands. The 2026 cycle is the contest's 11th consecutive year. Winners are announced at the Nature Talks Photo Festival on November 14, 2026.

The total prize pool is €25,000. The overall winner receives €3,000 in cash plus an additional €1,000 portfolio cash prize. Most category winners receive €500. The C11 category winner receives a photography weekend in Drenthe (Netherlands), and the C13 Youth winner (under 18) receives €250 in products.

Submissions are accepted across 13 categories total, including a free Youth category for photographers under 18 and a separate portfolio award. Photos can be from the current year or previous years — there is no recency restriction on submissions.
The 2025 contest received 24,781 entries from 96 countries, giving a sense of scale.

Eligibility is open to professional and non-professional photographers of all ages worldwide. AI-generated work is not accepted. Registration is free, but most categories carry a paid entry fee (€34 for the main contest, €17.50 for the Fred Hazelhoff portfolio award; the Youth category is free). The 2026 contest opens April 7 and closes June 2 at 23:59 CEST.

calls.title: HIPA Photography Award 2026
calls.org: Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
calls.description: Major international photography award with 2026 theme 'Family.' Categories include Family, Dreams Through AI, Sports Photography, Portfolio, and General. Free entry, open to all photographers 18+.
calls.summary: Major international award. 2026 theme: Family. Free entry. Categories include Dreams Through AI and Sports.
prose: The Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum International Photography Award (HIPA) is one of the largest photography prizes in the world by total prize pool. Named after Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, the 2026 cycle is HIPA's 15th season. Total prize pool: $1,000,000 USD across all categories.

The 2026 main theme is "Family." Submissions are accepted across multiple categories: Family ($40K/$30K/$20K for 1st/2nd/3rd), Dreams Through AI ($40K/$30K/$20K), Sports Photography ($40K/$30K/$20K), Portfolio/Story-Telling ($50K/$40K/$30K), General Color ($40K/$30K/$20K), and General Black & White ($40K/$30K/$20K). The Grand Prize Winner from any category receives an additional $200,000.

Special Awards add further prize money: Photography Appreciation ($100,000), Content Creator ($50,000), and Photographer of the Year ($80,000). AI-generated images are only accepted in the dedicated Dreams Through AI category and are excluded from all other categories.

There is no entry fee. Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. The judging process runs in four stages with typically nine judges; jurors remain anonymous until the season concludes — an unusual policy intended to keep selection insulated from external pressure.
Winners grant HIPA perpetual worldwide publication and promotional rights to winning photographs. The 2026 deadline is May 31 at 11:59 PM UAE local time.

calls.title: Natural Landscape Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Competition celebrating realistic landscape and nature photography. No AI or compositing allowed. RAW file checks for finalists. Multiple categories from grand scenics to intimate abstracts.
calls.summary: Celebrating realistic landscape photography. No AI or compositing. RAW file checks for finalists.
prose: The Natural Landscape Photography Awards (NLPA) was founded in 2021 by photographers Tim Parkin, Matt Payne, Rajesh Jyothiswaran, and Alex Nail. The 2026 cycle is the 6th edition. The competition was set up specifically as a response to the increasing prevalence of compositing and heavy manipulation in landscape photography contests — NLPA positions itself as the prize for landscape work that represents the natural world truthfully.

Post-processing rules are unusually strict. Editing tools like Photoshop are permitted "when used sensitively" to enhance the viewer's experience, but compositing and substantive manipulations that mislead viewers about the natural scene are excluded. AI-generated images are not accepted. Finalists must provide RAW files for verification — a check that has become a defining feature of the award.

The 2026 cycle is judged by Anna Morgan, Albert Dros, Wayne Suggs, Mark Littlejohn, and Eric Bennett. The judging panel rotates each year. Categories cover grand scenic landscapes, intimate landscapes, abstracts, and other formats specific to the natural world.

Submissions accept 1 to 18 images. Eligibility is open globally to photographers worldwide. The 2026 deadline is May 31, with results announced September 15. Total prize pool is approximately $5,000 across categories; specific entry fees are tiered and listed on the awards site.

calls.title: Queer Nature Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Free-entry photography award celebrating LGBTQ+ diversity through nature photography. Theme: Queer Nature (non-human). Submit via WeTransfer. Prizes include exhibitions and publication.
calls.summary: Free-entry award celebrating LGBTQ+ diversity through nature photography. Prizes include exhibitions.
jury: Christine Wilkinson, Wildlife Ecologist & Science Communicator
Charlotte Vermeulen, Storyteller & Emeritus Biologist, ARTIS Amsterdam Zoo
Noah Baars, Founder, Narwhal Rainbow Alliance
prose: The Queer Nature Photography Awards is administered by the Narwhal Rainbow Alliance, an Amsterdam-based organization at the intersection of LGBTQ+ advocacy and natural science communication. The 2026 cycle is the second edition. The brief is unusual: photographs of non-human nature documenting same-sex behaviors, gender fluidity, rainbow families, and other forms of biological diversity that challenge binary norms.

The premise is grounded in scientific literature: same-sex pairings, gender plasticity, and non-binary reproduction are documented across hundreds of species, from clownfish to bonobos, and the awards aim to surface that visual evidence in popular form rather than only academic publication.
First place receives €1,500. The top 10 photos are exhibited at the awards event, with the top 3 announced during the ceremony. There is no entry fee.

The 2026 jury comprises Christine Wilkinson (wildlife ecologist and National Geographic Explorer), Charlotte Vermeulen (emeritus biologist at ARTIS Amsterdam Zoo), Erin Ranney (wildlife cinematographer with credits at Nat Geo, Disney+, BBC), Noah Baars (Narwhal Rainbow Alliance founder), Nova West (filmmaker/photographer), and Laura Pennafort (BBC/Nat Geo cinematographer).

Eligibility is open to everyone — professional photographers, passionate amateurs, students. There is no LGBTQ+ identity requirement for the photographer. Each participant submits a maximum of 3 photos via WeTransfer to info@narwhalrainbowalliance.com, with an explanatory paragraph describing the work's relevance to queer nature. The 2026 deadline was extended to June 10; results announced late July.

calls.title: The Shape of a Moment
calls.description: International call exploring photography's ability to capture fleeting moments. Gold Award winner receives a solo exhibition. Exhibitions in Argentina and Los Angeles. Juror: Gary Hershorn (Reuters).
calls.ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted
calls.summary: Capturing fleeting moments. Gold Award winner receives solo exhibition. Juror: Gary Hershorn (Reuters).
prose: Exposure Photo Gallery is a photography gallery operating across two continents — its primary venue at Urquiza 739 in Río Tercero, Córdoba, Argentina, with a secondary venue in Buena Park, California (Exposure Los Angeles). "The Shape of a Moment" is the gallery's open call exploring photography's capacity to capture instants that reveal something essential through light, emotion, and time.

The Gold Award winner receives $500 cash and a solo exhibition at the Argentina gallery. Silver and Bronze awards recognize artistic quality without cash; ten Honorable Mentions appear as printed works in the physical exhibition; further selections are shown digitally. Special recognitions are reserved for photographers based in Córdoba Province. All recognized artists receive digital diplomas, and selected works are reproduced in an official exhibition book (print-on-demand).
The 2026 cycle is juried by Gary Hershorn, a 29-year Reuters editor and Getty Images contributor who has covered 17 Olympic Games and is the author of New York Celestial.

Entry fees are tiered by image count: $5 for 1 photo, $10 for 3, $15 for 6, $20 for 12. Unlimited submissions are permitted per applicant. AI-edited work is accepted; fully AI-generated work is not. Submissions are JPEG, max 2,000 pixels on the longest side. The 2026 deadline is June 30 at 11:59 PM PST; results announced August 3.

calls.title: Chromatic Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International color photography competition across 20 categories including Aerial, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Portrait, and Street. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
calls.summary: International color competition across 20 categories. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
prose: Chromatic Photography Awards is the color counterpart to several long-running monochrome competitions — entries must be in color, and black-and-white work is explicitly excluded. The 2026 cycle is the awards' 8th edition. Submissions are open to professionals and amateurs worldwide, with no age restriction stated on the official information page.

Entries can be made in 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Cityscapes, Conceptual, Culture, Environmental, Fashion and Beauty, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Nudes, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Sports, Still Life, Street, Travel, and Wildlife and Animal. Category winners receive Gold, Silver, or Bronze medals. The Professional and Amateur top winners receive $2,000 and $1,000 respectively, plus inclusion in the awards' Official Book. Honorable mentions receive certificates and badges.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: $17 amateur / $22 professional per entry at the early deadline (July 19, 2026), rising to $22 amateur / $27 professional at final deadline (October 25, 2026). Winners are announced December 20, 2026.

The jury is composed of magazine editors, gallery curators, professional agents, and other industry-side professionals — names rotate per edition and are listed on the awards site. The competition does not state an AI policy on its information page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.title: PX3 Prix de la Photographie Paris 2026
calls.description: One of Europe's most prestigious photography awards. Categories include Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. Winners exhibited in Paris and internationally.
calls.summary: One of Europe's most prestigious awards. Categories from Analog to Advertising. Exhibited in Paris.
prose: PX3 (Prix de la Photographie Paris) is an international photography competition based in Paris, awarding work across eight categories: Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. The structure separates traditional editorial categories (Press, Portraiture) from medium-specific tracks (Analog, Book), giving applicants flexibility in how they position a series.
The main prize is €5,000, with category and subcategory recognitions stacking on top. Winners are exhibited at PX3's annual Paris showcase and featured in the prize's annual book and online archive.

The 2026 jury includes James Wellford (National Geographic), Steve McCurry (photographer), and Samuel Nja Kwa (Forbes Afrique), with the full jury list published on px3.fr. Entry fees range from €20 to €50 depending on category and submission tier. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide. The deadline is June 17, 2026; AI policy is not stated on the public submission page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.description: Award dedicated exclusively to photographers using large-format cameras. Rewards unpublished work presented as a coherent series of 10 images. Winner receives prize money plus exhibition production.

calls.summary: Exclusively for large-format camera photographers. Unpublished series of 10 images. Prize money + exhibition.

prose: Camera Clara is a French photography prize dedicated specifically to large-format photography. Founded in 2012 by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno, it rewards an unpublished body of work made with a large-format camera, presented as a coherent series of 10 images. The €8,000 prize is paid by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno and includes exhibition production support for the winner.

Submissions are free of charge. The award accepts only large-format work and excludes AI-generated images. Selection criteria emphasize coherence both in form and content, treating the series as the unit of evaluation rather than individual images — applicants are reviewed on whether the body of work holds together, not on whether any single image stands out.

The 2026 jury is unusually senior for a niche prize: Dominique de Font-Reaulx (Jury President), Aurélie Chauffert-Yvart (Artistic Director), Héloïse Conésa (Curator at the National Library of France), Marc Donnadieu (art critic and independent curator), Anne Lacoste (Director of the Institute for Photography of Hauts-de-France), Chantal Nedjib (communications consultant), Guillaume Piens (art historian and founder of Culture Squad Communication), Michel Poivert (Professor of Art History at Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne), and Fabien Simode (art critic and director of Maisons-Alfort Media Libraries), alongside founder Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno.
The 2026 deadline is midnight July 31; the jury meets during September 2026 to designate the winner. Applications are made through prixcameraclara.plateformecandidature.com.

calls.title: Tokyo International Foto Award 2026
calls.description: International photography competition introducing photographers to the creative community in Tokyo. Ten categories including Advertising, Analog/Film, Architecture, Book, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, Portfolio and Special. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
jury: Prof. William Snyder, Rochester Institute of Technology
calls.summary: International competition introducing photographers to Tokyo's creative community. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
prose: Tokyo International Foto Awards (TIFA) is an annual photography competition that culminates in a winners' exhibition in Tokyo. The 2026 cycle is open to photographers aged 18 and over worldwide, across ten main categories - Advertising, Analog/Film, Architecture, Book, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, Portfolio and Special - each subdivided further. Series entries accept 2 to 10 images sharing a common theme, and all work must be no older than five years.

TIFA Photographer of the Year receives €3,000 and a TIFA trophy, New Talent of the Year €2,000 and a trophy, and first-place category winners in both the professional and non-professional streams receive €200 each. Winning work is exhibited in Tokyo and shown in an online gallery exhibition; the organisers state that all winners' services are covered by the entry fee, with no further charges.

Work is reviewed by a jury of international photo editors, curators, professors and gallerists that includes Hideko Kataoka (photo editor and curator), Mariama Attah (curator), Kenro Izu (photographer), Susan Baraz (Lucie Foundation Co-Chair), Professor William Snyder (Rochester Institute of Technology), and Alfie Goodrich (Japanorama).

Entry fees are tiered by experience: €30 per single image and €40 per series for professionals, €20 and €25 for non-professionals, €15 and €20 for students, and €50 for the Portfolio category, with 30% off each additional category the same entry is submitted to. AI-generated work is accepted in a dedicated AI-Generated Images subcategory under Special. The extended deadline is September 1, 2026, and winners are announced 30 to 45 days afterwards.

prose: Milano Photo Awards is an Italian photography contest and exhibition run by TheStreetSoup, with Nikon Italia as official sponsor. The 2026 edition runs September 25–27 at Via Maurizio Gonzaga 7 in Milan, scheduled to coincide with Milano Fashion Week. The exhibition format is a 4×3 meter Samsung LED wall for digital display of selected work, with the top three winners in each category also receiving printed and framed prints. The 2026 edition includes a tribute to Sebastião Salgado.

The total prize pool is €30,000 in cash plus Nikon hardware. There are eight competition categories: Street Photography, Portrait & Identity, Wildlife & Nature, Movement & Sport, Human Landscape, Documentary & Social Vision, Conceptual & Fine Art, and Fashion & Style. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Entry follows a tiered structure with separate access levels: Exhibition Open (€20, 2 photos, €500 first prize plus a Nikon backpack and printing), Exhibition Room 1 (€50, 5 photos, €1,000 first prize plus printing and gala access), Exhibition Room 2 (€80, 8–10 photos, €1,500 first prize plus printing and gala access), and the Oriol Vision Award (€50, 5 photos), curated separately by guest judge Estevan Oriol. The submission deadline is August 15, 2026.

calls.summary: Contemporary art prize. Winners exhibited at major public gallery and published in Aesthetica Magazine.
prose: The Aesthetica Art Prize is run by Aesthetica Magazine, the UK contemporary art publication based in York. Founded in 2007, the prize has run annually for nearly two decades and is open across all media — Painting and Drawing; Video, Installation, and Performance; Photography, Digital Art and Installation; and Artists' Film. Photography submissions are evaluated alongside other categories rather than in a separate track.

The main prize is £10,000, with additional support including exhibition at a major UK public gallery, publication in Aesthetica Magazine, and inclusion in the prize's annual anthology. The prize runs an associated Future Now Symposium and publishes Future Now: 125 Contemporary Artists, a book featuring shortlisted and exhibited work from past cycles.

The 2026 jury draws from senior curators across major UK institutions: Carrie Chan (V&A), Charlotte Hale (V&A Dundee), Taous Dahmani (The Photographers' Gallery), Sarah Coulson (Yorkshire Sculpture Park), Poppy Bowers (The Whitworth), Dr James Finch (Royal Academy of Arts), Farah Dailami (The Hepworth Wakefield), artist Jason Bruges (Jason Bruges Studio), and producer Nephertiti Oboshie Schandorf.

Entry fee is £25 (regular) or £35 (late entry from 12–18 October). The 2026 entry window runs December 1, 2025 to October 11, 2026, with late entries open October 12–18. Judging takes place winter 2026 and results are announced spring 2027. The prize accepts work from artists at any career stage, with no nationality restriction.

The 2026 jury is large — over 20 photographers, art directors, and creative professionals from multiple countries.

calls.title: International Color Awards 2026

jury: James A. Ganz, Senior Curator of Photographs, The J. Paul Getty Museum
calls.summary: 19th annual international color photography competition. 235+ title awards across 35 categories.
prose: International Color Awards is the color-photography sibling to the Black & White Spider Awards. The 2026 edition is the award's 19th cycle. The structure runs over 235 title awards across 35 categories — winners are announced not only as overall prizes but as title-holders within sub-genres.
Total prize pool is $2,750. Winners are announced at an online Photoshow on May 30, 2026.

AI-generated work is not accepted. The 2026 jury draws from museum and creative-industry institutions: James A. Ganz (Senior Curator of Photographs, The J. Paul Getty Museum), Venti Hristova (Creative Director, Netflix), and Lorenzo Balbi (Director, MAMbo Bologna).
Eligibility is open globally to professional and amateur photographers. Submission is through the awards website with unlimited images. The 2026 deadline was March 27.

calls.title: PX3 State of the World 2026
calls.description: Special PX3 contest for photographers to submit series of up to 10 images reflecting unfiltered global stories. 30 photographers selected for a curated exhibition at Paris Photo Prize, which travels internationally. Curated by Hossein Farmani.
calls.summary: Series reflecting unfiltered global stories. 30 photographers selected for curated exhibition at Paris Photo Prize.
prose: PX3 State of the World is a special PX3 (Prix de la Photographie Paris) competition focused on documentary and journalistic work. The framing is direct: "important global stories, eyewitness accounts" and "uncensored news, directly from photographers witnessing events." The brief invites series rather than single images, with the structure foregrounding sustained reportage over individual standout photographs.

Submissions are organized by continent at the entry stage: Europe, Americas, Asia, Africa, Oceania, Arctic, and Antarctic — an unusual geographic categorization that ensures regional coverage in the final selection.

Thirty photographers are selected by curator Hossein Farmani. Each receives €200 cash plus inclusion in the Paris Photo Prize annual exhibition. The exhibition travels internationally, extending the platform's reach beyond Paris.
Each submission is a series of up to 10 images sharing a common theme and a single project title. Entry fee is €35 per series. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide.
The 2026 deadline is May 13.

calls.summary: Candid, spontaneous street photography capturing city life. Free to submit. Exhibition in Athens.
prose: Blank Wall Gallery is an Athens-based photography gallery that runs themed open calls on a recurring schedule. Street Photography is the gallery's call for candid, spontaneous work capturing city life — work made in public space without staging or interference.
Selected work is shown at Blank Wall Gallery in Athens, April 24 – May 6, 2026. The exhibition format is physical only.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email with up to 5 images. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was March 26.

Eligibility is open to photographers 18+ globally. Submission is by email with up to 5 images. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was April 23; results announced April 27, 2026.

calls.summary: One photographer wins a two-week solo exhibition with 40 prints and international promotion. Valued at €2,200+.
prose: Blank Wall Gallery is an Athens, Greece photography gallery (55 Fokionos Negri Street, 11361 Athens). The Best Portfolio competition is the gallery's annual international portfolio prize — structured to identify a single photographer whose body of work merits a solo exhibition.

One winner is selected. The prize is a two-week solo exhibition with 40 professionally produced prints — production and financing of the prints handled by Blank Wall Gallery — plus international promotion through the gallery's website and social channels. The total prize package is valued at over €2,200.
Submissions are made by email and require a portfolio of 10 to 20 images. The format favors a coherent body of work rather than a sampler of strong individual images. Entry fee is €50.
Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. The 2026 deadline is May 31; results announced June 2.

calls.title: Color/less — Cambridge Photography Gallery
calls.description: Open call dedicated to color and its absence. Any approach to constructing the color space of the image is welcome — soft pastels, aggressive red, B&W silhouettes. Color (or its absence) must be a key element. Online exhibition April 10–25, 2026.
calls.summary: Dedicated to color and its absence. Any approach to constructing the color space of the image welcome.
prose: Cambridge Photography Gallery is an online photography gallery that runs themed juried calls. Color/less is the gallery's open call dedicated to color and its absence — work where the chromatic register itself is the subject.

The brief is open in approach: soft pastels, aggressive red, B&W silhouettes, anywhere on the color spectrum. The unifying criterion is that color (or its absence) must be a key compositional or expressive element rather than incidental.
AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running April 10–25, 2026. The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a £15 fee charged only if work is accepted.
Submission is by email. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was March 30.

calls.title: Daylight Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: Photography competition recognizing outstanding photographic work. Top prize includes cash award and creation of a digital portfolio. Juror picks receive international marketing promotion and the opportunity to collaborate with Daylight on a monograph. Winners announced August 2026.
calls.summary: Competition recognizing outstanding work. Top prize includes cash and digital portfolio. Monograph opportunity.
prose: Daylight Photo Awards is the annual juried prize from Daylight Books, the North Carolina-based photography publisher. Daylight has published photo monographs since 2002, and the awards function as both prize and pipeline — with one juror's pick receiving the opportunity to collaborate with Daylight on a future monograph.

The 2026 jury is built from photo editors and curators at major institutions: Mike Kamber (Bronx Documentary Center), Hideko Kataoka (Newsweek Japan), Tif Ng (Magnum Foundation), Momo Takahashi (The New Yorker), and James Wellford (National Geographic).

Top prize is $2,500 plus a digital portfolio created with the photographer. Juror's Picks receive international marketing promotion through Daylight's channels and the chance to develop a monograph project with the publisher.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the Daylight Photo Awards website with 15–20 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was May 1; results announced August 2026.

calls.title: Fotografiska HOME — Global Open Call
calls.description: Global open call exploring home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. Selected works exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Guest curator: James Nachtwey. Submit up to 3 images. Lens-based photography only, no AI.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction & Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
calls.summary: Global open call exploring home. Exhibition at UN Headquarters. Guest curator: James Nachtwey. No AI.
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction & Exhibitions) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026.

prose: Galleri Format is a contemporary art gallery in Malmö, Sweden — focused on photography, video, and film. The Window Exhibition is the gallery's open-call series adapted to its large street-facing windows on Stora Nygatan, beside Gustav Adolfs Torg in central Malmö. The 2026 edition is the sixth cycle.

The exhibition runs June 12 – August 9, 2026. The format is unusual: rather than gallery interior, the work is installed in the windows and viewable from the street. Proposals must be adapted for that context — built for passing foot traffic at all hours rather than for a typical gallery visit.

The gallery covers all production costs and pays an exhibition fee per the Swedish MU agreement (the standard exhibition compensation framework for visual artists in Sweden). Eligibility is restricted to professional artists.
Submission is by email — a single PDF proposal. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced late April 2026.

prose: The Handmade Photobook Exhibition is the Griffin Museum of Photography's annual call for handcrafted photobooks — books where the artist's hand shapes the object itself rather than relying on commercial production. The 2026 edition is the second cycle.

The brief distinguishes the show from the museum's Self Published Photobook Exhibition: this one foregrounds the physical making of the book. Hand-bound, hand-sewn, hand-stamped, hand-pasted — the structural focus is artisanal book objects.
Selection is by Caleb Cain Marcus of Luminosity Lab.
Selected handmade photobooks are exhibited at the Griffin Gallery in Winchester, Massachusetts.

calls.summary: Photography zine inspired by the Japanese Provoke movement — destabilizing certainty, revealing a world beyond language.
prose: Provoke USA is a photography zine published by Domino Film Photo Magazine in Chicago. The brief is explicitly historicized: the zine takes its name and approach from the Japanese Provoke movement of the late 1960s — Daido Moriyama, Takuma Nakahira, Yutaka Takanashi, and the others associated with destabilizing certainty and revealing a world beyond conventional language.
The zine accepts work that engages with that lineage: rough, blurred, contrasted, are-bure-boke, or other approaches that resist clean documentary description.
AI-generated images are not accepted.

International submissions welcome. Submission is by email with the photographer's Instagram handle. Files must be named with the photographer's name (e.g., JohnDoe 1). Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 28.

calls.title: Hariban Award 2026
calls.description: International collotype competition combining 170-year-old analogue printing with contemporary photography. Submit 12 black-and-white photographs. Grand Prize: funded two-week residency in Kyoto collaborating with master collotype printers, solo exhibition, and publication in official catalogue. Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and free Collotype Academy course.
jury: Diane Dufour, Founder & Artistic Director, LE BAL Paris
Erin O'Toole, Curator & Head of Photography, SFMOMA
KIM Jeong Eun, Founder, THE REFERENCE Seoul
calls.summary: International collotype competition. Grand Prize: two-week residency in Kyoto with master collotype printers.
prose: The Hariban Award is run by Benrido, a Kyoto-based collotype atelier founded in 1887 — over 130 years of continuous practice. Collotype is a 19th-century printing technique that achieves an unusually rich tonal range without screens or halftones; it was widely used through the mid-1900s before color printing replaced it commercially. Benrido has preserved the process since around 2000, making it one of the few remaining collotype workshops in the world.
The 2026 cycle is the 13th edition of the award. Approximately 3,700 entries have been submitted across all editions to date.

The Grand Prize is a fully funded two-week artist residency in Kyoto collaborating directly with Benrido's master collotype printers, plus a solo exhibition the following year and publication in the official catalogue. The Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and a free Collotype Academy course at Benrido.

Submissions are 8 to 12 black-and-white photographs at a $40 to $50 entry fee. AI-generated work is accepted. The 2026 jury comprises Diane Dufour (Founder & Artistic Director, LE BAL Paris), Erin O'Toole (Curator & Head of Photography, SFMOMA), KIM Jeong Eun (Founder, THE REFERENCE Seoul), and Leo Rongone (photographer and CEO of Moncler). The 2026 cycle is open April 1 through June 30 (deadline extended); results announced September 15.

Selected work is shown at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, July 10 – August 7, 2026. Open to all media including photography.

calls.title: Artadia Awards 2026 — New York City

calls.summary: Unrestricted $15,000 grants for contemporary visual artists in NYC. Two-round jury process with studio visits.
prose: Artadia is a US grantmaking organization that runs unrestricted merit-based grants for contemporary visual artists in seven cities across the year — New York (April), San Francisco (May–June), Boston (August–September), Atlanta (September–October), and Houston (October–November), among others. The 2026 New York City cycle awards three grants of $15,000 each.

The structural premise: grants are unrestricted — recipients can use the funds for any purpose. Photography is eligible alongside other visual art disciplines. AI-generated work is accepted but must be disclosed.

The selection process is two-round. First, curators review written applications. Six finalists then have 45-minute virtual studio visits with the curatorial panel. Non-selected finalists receive honorariums — the studio visit itself is treated as worth compensating.
Past awardees have gone on to be featured in the Whitney Biennial and Prospect New Orleans. Eligibility is restricted to artists based in the relevant city for each cycle.

The prize runs across three categories: Portrait (spontaneous or posed), Travel (landscapes, cultures, traditions), and Migration & Borders (human movement, territorial and cultural limits). Each entrant submits one photograph per category — single-image rather than series-based.

Technical rules are strict: AI-generated work is not accepted, heavy retouching is disqualifying, and the organizers may request RAW files to verify capture. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+.
The total prize fund is €1,500, distributed across category winners. Submission is free, through the prize's website. The 2026 deadline was May 4; results announced June 25, 2026.

calls.title: Bethany Arts Community — Fall Multidisciplinary Residency 2026

calls.summary: Two-week residency in Ossining, NY. $450 stipend, private studio, room and board. 12 artists across all disciplines.

What's included: a private studio, a private room, three meals daily, and a $450 stipend. Application is free.

There's a community program component built into the residency — each resident facilitates one program for the local Ossining community during their stay. This shapes selection: applicants submit not only their work but a proposal for the community workshop or event they'd run.

Eligibility is open to artists 21+. Application requires one letter of recommendation and one reference. Funding comes from the National Endowment for the Arts and the New York State Council on the Arts. The 2026 deadline was May 6; results announced June 26, 2026.

calls.summary: Fellowship for socially engaged photographers partnering with a Chicago-based community organization.
prose: The Diane Dammeyer Fellowship in Photographic Arts and Social Issues is administered by Columbia College Chicago in partnership with the Museum of Contemporary Photography (MoCP). Founded in 2015 with Fereshteh Toosi as its first fellow, the fellowship supports socially engaged photographers producing new work in collaboration with a Chicago-based community partner organization.

The fellowship runs from September through June with flexible hours, structured to allow the fellow to maintain other professional commitments while embedded with their community partner. The work culminates in a public exhibition and/or publication at MoCP — the partnership between fellow and community organization is treated as the core of the fellowship rather than a transactional output.

Past fellows have addressed human rights, social, economic, and cultural issues across a wide range of communities: Ervin A. Johnson (2016–17), Anahid Ghorbani (2017–18), Sasha Phyars-Burgess (2018–19), Jonathan Michael Castillo (2019–21), Melissa Ann Pinney (2021–22), Dylan Yarbrough (2022–23), the joint Oscar B. Castillo & Wil Sands fellowship (2023–24), and Alessandro Bo (2024–25).

Eligibility requires either an MFA in photography or related field, or a BA plus five years of post-degree creative practice. Preference is given to Chicago-based projects. Two professional references are required. There is no application fee. Applications go through JotForm; the 2026/27 deadline is June 12, 2026.

calls.summary: Annual prize for student photographers. $2,000 first prize plus mentorship with Aline Smithson.
prose: The Lenscratch Student Prize is the photography blog's annual prize for emerging student photographers, founded in 2013 and run by Lenscratch editor Aline Smithson. The prize is restricted to students currently enrolled in bachelor's or master's degree photography programs.

The first prize is unusually layered. The winner receives $2,000 in cash plus a year-long mentorship with Aline Smithson, portfolio review sessions with curators, seats at portfolio review events, museum memberships, a mini-exhibition on Lenscratch, a $500 gift certificate to Freestyle Photo, multiple book collections, and merchandise. The mentorship and review components are worth more than the cash for many recipients.
Second prize: $1,000 plus Lenscratch feature, mini-exhibition, and merchandise. Third: $750 with the same package. Four Honorable Mentions: $500 each.

Past winners include Jordan Tovin (2025), Mosfiqur Rahman Johan (2024), Christian K. Lee (2023), Drew Leventhal (2022), Allie Tsubota (2021), Raymond Thompson Jr. (2020), Guanyu Xu (2019), Zora J. Murff (2018), Shawn Bush (2017), Drew Nikonowicz (2016), and others — many have gone on to significant careers in editorial, museum, and gallery photography.

The 19-juror panel for 2026 includes Aline Smithson, Daniel George, Karen Haas (Lane Curator of Photographs at MFA Boston), Kris Graves (Kris Graves Projects), Hamidah Glasgow (former Director, Center for Fine Art Photography), Alexa Dilworth (former Publishing Director at CDS at Duke), Yorgos Efthymiadis (The Curated Fridge), and most of the past winners themselves. There is no entry fee. Submissions go through Google Form; the 2026 deadline is June 1; results announced July 13.

calls.title: Lenscratch Motherhood Exhibition

calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring all dimensions of motherhood — chosen families, caregiving, absence, and resilience.

The brief deliberately broadens the theme beyond traditional mother-child portraiture. Lenscratch is asking for work engaging with chosen families, caregiving relationships, absence, loss, resilience, and inheritance — all dimensions of mothering as a verb rather than a fixed identity.
Selection runs as a single group online exhibition published on the Lenscratch site, where features remain in the archive long-term.
Submission is single-image: one photograph via Google Form, 72dpi at 1000px long side. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was May 1; results announced May 10, 2026.

calls.title: Lenscratch Fatherhood Exhibition

calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring fatherhood as an evolving role shaped by culture, responsibility, and tenderness.
prose: Lenscratch is one of the longest-running photography blogs and online platforms, with a regular schedule of online exhibitions accompanying its daily editorial coverage. The Fatherhood Exhibition is the platform's open call for photography that engages with the role of fathers — the brief frames fatherhood as an evolving role shaped by culture, responsibility, tenderness, and family expectations.

Lenscratch's open calls have a consistent format: a single themed exhibition publishes online by a fixed date, with one image accepted per photographer. The Fatherhood exhibition publishes June 21, 2026 — typically scheduled to coincide with U.S. Father's Day weekend.

calls.summary: Online exhibition examining tensions and transformations across America. Timed for July 4th.
prose: Lenscratch is one of the longest-running photography blogs and online platforms, edited by photographer Aline Smithson, with a regular schedule of online exhibitions accompanying its daily editorial coverage. "Fault Lines: America" is the platform's open call for photography examining tensions, fractures, and transformations across the United States — resistance, social change, protest, activism, justice, identity, power, and freedom.

The 2026 cycle is timed for the Fourth of July, with the online exhibition publishing on July 4. The call invites work that engages with civic engagement and the challenges facing democratic institutions. Selection is by Norm Diamond and Marcy Palmer; Diamond's stated framing for the call is direct: "What occupies my thoughts is the state of our country and its descent into fascism. This is the most important story of the 21st century."

Submissions are free, with one entry per photographer. Images are sized to 72dpi at 1000 pixels on the long side and submitted via Google Form. Caption format follows Lenscratch's standard: copyright, name, image title, Instagram handle, and website.

Selected work appears in the online group exhibition on Lenscratch — the platform itself functions as the prize, given Lenscratch's substantial readership in the photography community. The 2026 deadline is June 19; exhibition publishes July 4.

calls.title: SE Center for Photography — Magic of Light

calls.summary: Virtual exhibition exploring light and shadow. Juror: Wendi Schneider. 35-40 images selected. 0% commission.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) runs a year-round program of themed virtual juried exhibitions from its Greenville, South Carolina facility. "Magic of Light" is the gallery's open call exploring light and shadow as the foundation of photography — work that engages with light's structural role in image-making, whether literal or metaphorical.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Wendi Schneider, a Denver-based visual artist known for her hand-gilded photographs and the long-running "States of Grace" series. Schneider's own practice sits within the call's frame: light handled as material substance.

Selection takes 35 to 40 images for an approximately one-month virtual gallery, with social media promotion across SEC4P's channels and an archived online slideshow plus video walkthrough. There is no sales commission — artists retain 100% of sale proceeds and all copyrights.

Entry fees: $35 for non-members for up to 5 images ($6 each additional, max 15), or $28 / $5 for SEC4P members. Eligibility is open globally to photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. All formats are welcome — analog, digital, monochrome, color, and antique processes.
The 2026 application window opens March 7 and closes May 15. Selections announced May 30; exhibition runs June 15 through July 30, 2026.

calls.summary: Fine art projects investigating home, being away, or the tension between. Published in print edition.
