calls.summary: Five $8,000 unrestricted grants for photographers in NY State outside NYC. Traditional and experimental photography.
prose: The JGS Fellowship for Photography is administered by the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA), one of the largest artist-service organizations in the United States. The fellowship is funded by JGS — the Joy of Giving Something Foundation, a private foundation supporting photography. The geographic scope is unusual: the fellowship is reserved for photographers working in New York State outside of New York City, addressing the relative concentration of photo-funding inside Manhattan and Brooklyn.
Five fellowships of $8,000 each are awarded annually. The funds are unrestricted, supporting whatever expense advances the artist's practice — materials, equipment, studio rent, travel, or time off.

Eligible work spans traditional and experimental photography, including light-based work, alternative processes, and any form in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal. The breadth of accepted media reflects the fellowship's commitment to photography as a contemporary practice rather than a single tradition.

Eligibility requires applicants to be 25 years or older, current full-time residents of eligible New York State regions for at least 12 months, and not enrolled in a degree-seeking program. Previous JGS recipients are not eligible to reapply.
Applications are free and submitted through Submittable. Each applicant submits 5 to 10 images. The 2026 deadline is May 19, with results announced in summer 2026.

calls.title: Light Work Artist-in-Residence 2027
calls.description: One-month creative residency in Syracuse, New York. Selected artists receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished artist apartment, 24-hour access to state-of-the-art facilities, and staff support. Work published in a special edition of Contact Sheet: The Light Work Annual with a commissioned essay. Open to all artists working in photography or image-based media from any country. 12–15 artists selected annually. Notifications by December 2026.
calls.summary: One-month residency with $7,500 stipend and furnished apartment. Published in Contact Sheet. Open worldwide.
prose: Light Work is a non-profit photography center in Syracuse, New York, founded in 1973. Its Artist-in-Residence program — running for over five decades and counting more than 400 alumni — is one of the longest-running photography residencies in the United States. Past residents have included photographers who went on to MacArthur Fellowships, museum acquisitions, and major editorial careers; the alumni list is treated as part of the program's identity.

Each cycle, twelve to fifteen artists are selected for a one-month residency at Light Work's facility (316 Waverly Avenue, Syracuse). Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment near campus, 24-hour access to Light Work's digital lab and darkroom, and on-staff support. Each resident's work is published in Contact Sheet, Light Work's annual publication, with a commissioned essay.

Eligibility is open globally to artists working in photography or image-based media. There is no application fee. The program is in partnership with Autograph ABP and the Darryl Chappell Foundation, which jointly support specific residency lines for British photographers and Black photographers respectively.

Applications are submitted through SlideRoom (with a physical mail option for those who require it). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026. The selection committee reviews applications in late fall, with notifications sent in December.

calls.title: Doug Pensinger Photography Fund 2026
calls.description: Seven $5,000 grants plus yearlong mentorships from industry professionals for emerging sports photographers. The only nonprofit dedicated to providing career development opportunities to emerging sports photographers. Past grantees range from high school students to recent graduates working as freelancers or interns. Applications close May 1.
calls.summary: Seven $5,000 grants plus mentorships for emerging sports photographers. Only nonprofit dedicated to sports photography careers.
prose: The Doug Pensinger Photography Fund (DPPF) was established to support emerging and early-career sports photographers. The fund's annual grants program is one of the few dedicated funding mechanisms specifically for sports photography rather than documentary or fine-art categories.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers with fewer than three years of cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection structure has two grant tiers. The main grants: seven photographers each receive $5,000 for career development plus an expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). The Gathering is the fund's annual professional convening — selected grantees attend at no personal cost. Up to three of the seven main grantees are eligible for an additional year-long mentorship with members of the fund's Advisory Board.
Development Grants: up to three additional applicants receive $2,500 each as a smaller-scale grant track.

The 2026–27 mentors are Jean Fruth, Bob Martin, and Jamie Schwaberow — all working sports photographers. Submission is through Picter, with 20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was May 1; results announced July 1, 2026.

calls.title: The Paula Riff Award 2026
calls.description: Annual award honoring artist Paula Riff's legacy, recognizing artists who challenge conventional photography through lensless photography, historical/alternative photographic processes, or physical intervention such as cutting, sewing, and collage. Created in 2021 by the Center for Photographic Art and Lenscratch. $1,000 prize plus featured on Lenscratch and the CPA website. Related group exhibition Changing the Narrative: the First 5 Years of Paula Riff Award Winners opens June 20 at CPA in Carmel. Open internationally to artists working at any career stage.
jury: Tarrah von Lintel, Von Lintel Gallery
calls.summary: Award for alternative/experimental photography — lensless, historical processes, physical intervention. $1,000 + Lenscratch feature.
prose: The Paula Riff Award honors the legacy of Los Angeles-based artist Paula Riff, who specialized in camera-less photographic works using cyanotype and gum bichromate processes — her practice emphasized bold colors, form, and design, often abstract or drawn from the natural world. The award was created in 2021 by the Center for Photographic Art (Carmel, California) and Lenscratch as an annual prize.

The award celebrates artists whose work "reflects the artist's hand" — challenging conventional photography through lensless processes, historical or alternative photographic processes, or physical intervention such as cutting, sewing, layering, and collage. The criteria favor work where the photograph is materially altered or constructed rather than only captured.

The winner receives $1,000 in cash plus featured presentation on the Lenscratch website and the Center for Photographic Art website. The 2026 cycle includes potential inclusion in a group exhibition titled "Changing the Narrative: the First 5 Years of Paula Riff Award Winners," opening June 20 at CPA in Carmel.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Tarrah von Lintel, founder of Von Lintel Gallery in Los Angeles. There is no application fee. Submissions are made as a single PDF (5–10 images, image list with medium and process details, artist bio, and statement) via Dropbox. Open internationally to artists at any career stage. The 2026 deadline is June 1; results announced in July.

calls.title: Dek Unu Magazine — June & July 2026 Issue
calls.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome. One artist selected for the combined June/July double issue. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent.
calls.summary: Not-for-profit journal publishing one artist per issue in print and online. June/July double issue. Free, email submissions.
prose: Dek Unu Magazine is an international not-for-profit photography journal that publishes monthly. The structural premise is unusual: each issue features one accomplished artist rather than a multi-photographer group format. Issues are published as both print and online paperback.

Eligibility is open across all fine art photography genres and techniques. Selection criteria pair technical excellence with artistic vision and conceptual intent — the magazine is looking for resolved, mature bodies of work.
The 2026 June/July cycle is a combined double issue — one selected artist for two months of feature.
Submission is by email with 11 images. Application is free. The 2026 June/July deadline was April 20; selection announced around May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Shutter Hub Editions Photobook Award 2026
calls.description: Photobook award from Shutter Hub Editions celebrating bold storytelling and compelling visual narratives. Particularly welcomes photographers creating their first book. Selected by Karen Harvey MBE, Founder and Creative Director of Shutter Hub. A shortlist of six photographers will be celebrated with a dedicated feature, and selected photographers are invited to contribute a Close Up feature, reaching an audience of over 500,000 people. Winning book published by Shutter Hub Editions with 40% commission on profits paid to the photographer. Submit a written proposal and a PDF with 20+ images.
jury: Karen Harvey MBE, Founder & Creative Director, Shutter Hub
calls.summary: Photobook award from Shutter Hub Editions. First-book photographers welcome. Publication + Close Up feature to 500K audience.
prose: Shutter Hub is a Cambridge-based UK photography platform with a global membership and a publishing arm, Shutter Hub Editions. The Photobook Award is the publishing arm's annual prize — selected by Karen Harvey MBE, Shutter Hub's Founder and Creative Director.

The brief is open in subject but specific in intent: bold storytelling and compelling visual narratives, particularly welcoming photographers creating their first book. Photographers without prior book publications are explicitly encouraged.

Selection structure has two tiers. A shortlist of six photographers receives a dedicated feature on Shutter Hub's platforms. From the shortlist, selected photographers are invited to contribute a Close Up feature, which reaches an audience of over 500,000 people through the platform's distribution.
The winning book is published by Shutter Hub Editions. The financial structure is profit-share: 40% commission on profits is paid to the photographer.
Each application includes a written proposal and a PDF with 20+ images. Submission is through the Shutter Hub website. Fee is £25. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results expected around July 2026.

calls.title: VCCA Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation Fellowship in Photography
calls.org: Virginia Center for the Creative Arts
calls.description: Two-week fully-funded residency at Mt. San Angelo in Amherst, Virginia for US citizens or permanent residents. Supported by the Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation, established in 2009 to support photographic education and documentary photography. Includes private bedroom with en-suite bath, individual studio space plus darkroom access, and three meals daily in a cross-disciplinary community. Residency dates available May 1 – August 31, 2027. Applications open June 1, 2026. Fee waivers available on request by September 10, 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: Two-week fully-funded photography residency at Mt. San Angelo, Virginia. Private studio + darkroom. Meals and housing included.
prose: The Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation Fellowship is a fully-funded two-week photography residency at Mt. San Angelo, the Virginia Center for the Creative Arts (VCCA) campus in Amherst, Virginia. The fellowship is supported by the Leonian Foundation, established in 2009 to fund photographic education and documentary photography. Recent fellows include Bing Guan and Sha Luo.

Each fellow receives a private bedroom with en-suite bathroom, an individual studio plus access to VCCA's darkroom, and three meals daily prepared by the campus kitchen. The residency runs in a cross-disciplinary cohort — photographers stay alongside writers, composers, and visual artists working in other media — which VCCA treats as part of the program rather than incidental to it.

The fellowship is restricted to U.S. citizens and permanent residents whose primary discipline is photography. Residency dates available for the 2027 cycle run May 1 through August 31. Applications open June 1, 2026 and close September 15, 2026; fellows are notified December 31, 2026.

calls.title: VISUAL Carlow 2027 Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: Open call for exhibition proposals at VISUAL Centre for Contemporary Art in Carlow, Ireland, for a new commission in September 2027. Open to artists of all career stages working in any media, locally, in Ireland, or internationally — duos and groups welcome. Winning applicant receives a generous artist fee, significant production budget, and curatorial, production, technical, and marketing support. Shortlisted artists receive expansion fees to develop extended proposals. Four gallery spaces available (Main, Link, Studio, Digital). New commission only — existing work ineligible. Shortlist announced end of June 2026; expanded proposals due end of August 2026; winner announced September 2026.
jury: Aileen Nolan, Carlow County Arts Officer
Benjamin Stafford, Visual Arts Curator, VISUAL
Sepake Angiama, Artistic Director, Institute of International Visual Arts
calls.summary: Major new commission for 2027 exhibition at VISUAL Carlow. Any medium. Artist fee + significant production budget.
prose: VISUAL Centre for Contemporary Art is a contemporary art venue in Carlow, Ireland with four distinct gallery spaces — Main, Link, Studio, and Digital — that allow concurrent exhibitions across different formats. The 2027 Open Call is run in partnership with Carlow Arts Office, marking 40 years of county arts officers supporting artists across Ireland.

The call is for a newly conceived or unrealised commission to be exhibited at VISUAL in September 2027. Existing work is not eligible; the program funds new production rather than touring or restaging earlier projects. Eligibility is unusually broad: professional visual artists working in any medium, in any location, at any career stage. Duos and groups are welcome.

What the winning applicant receives: a generous artist fee, a significant production budget, and curatorial, production, technical, and marketing support. Specific fee figures are not published on the public landing page — applicants negotiate within VISUAL's program structure. Shortlisted artists also receive expansion fees to develop extended proposals.
After exhibition, work returns to the artist or an agreed party — VISUAL does not acquire commissioned work into a permanent collection.

Selection is by a five-member jury panel: Aileen Nolan (Carlow County Arts Officer), Aisling Prior (independent curator), Benjamin Stafford (Visual Arts Curator at VISUAL), artist Daphne Wright, and Sepake Angiama (Artistic Director of the Institute of International Visual Arts).
Submission is free. The 2026 deadline is May 22, 2026 at 5pm GMT. Shortlist announced end of June; expanded proposals due end of August; winner announced September 2026.

calls.title: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale 2027 Residency
calls.description: Two-to-four-month residency in 2027 at NKD, a non-profit centre funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality in the village of Dale, Fjaler on Norway's west coast. Established 1998. Residents receive a monthly grant of NOK 11,000, up to NOK 5,000 in travel reimbursement, and free accommodation in a private residence house plus a 50m² studio with 6-metre ceilings and north-lit panorama windows. Open to professional visual artists, designers, and architects (photographers welcome). Not available to students or practitioners in music, writing, dance, or theatre. Residents give a presentation and participate in an open studio day.
calls.summary: 2–4 month residency in Dale, Norway. Monthly grant NOK 11,000, travel covered, free private house and 50m² studio.
prose: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale (NKD) is a non-profit residency centre established in 1998 in the village of Dale, Fjaler — on the west coast of Norway, in a fjord landscape several hours from Bergen. Funding comes from the Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality.

Residencies run two to four months. Residents receive a monthly grant of NOK 11,000, travel reimbursement up to NOK 5,000, free accommodation in a private residence house, and a 50m² studio with 6-metre ceilings and north-lit panorama windows.

Eligibility is restricted by discipline. Open to professional visual artists, designers, and architects — photographers welcome. Explicitly not available to students or practitioners in music, writing, dance, or theatre.

Residents are expected to give a public presentation and participate in an open studio day during their stay. The residency is structured as research and production rather than performance — most output is studio-based with the public components as endpoints.
Application is free, submitted through Rimbert with a portfolio. The 2027-cycle deadline was April 30, 2026.

calls.title: Cavendish Arts Science Fellowship 2026–27
calls.description: Annual fellowship in partnership with Girton College, Cambridge, supporting artists to engage with physicists and others at the Cavendish Laboratory. Runs October 2026 – October 2027 with a Cambridge residency of 6–12 months (can be split across visits). Includes £10,000 stipend, £10,000 production budget, up to £3,000 travel support, rent-free accommodation and meals at Girton College, and a studio/creative workspace plus flexible working spaces at the Cavendish Laboratory. Open internationally to artists of any medium or nationality — no prior science experience required. Must be 18+ and out of full-time education by October 2026. Joint applications accepted.
calls.summary: Year-long art-science fellowship at Girton College, Cambridge. £23,000 total funding + accommodation. All media.
prose: The Cavendish Arts Science Fellowship is an annual art-science residency in Cambridge, run jointly by Girton College and the Cavendish Laboratory — the Department of Physics at the University of Cambridge. The fellowship is structured to allow artists to engage with physicists and other researchers at one of the world's most significant physics institutions, where Watson and Crick worked, where the electron was discovered, and where 30+ Nobel Prizes have been awarded.

The 2026–27 fellowship runs October 2026 through October 2027. The Cambridge residency itself is flexible — minimum 6 months and up to 12 months total, which can be split across multiple visits. The remainder of the year-long appointment can be conducted remotely. The fellowship is not expected to be a full-time engagement.

Financial support: £10,000 stipend (covering living costs), £10,000 production budget for new work, up to £3,000 travel allowance, plus rent-free accommodation and meals at Girton College during the residency. The fellow has access to a studio/creative workspace at Girton plus flexible working spaces at the Cavendish Laboratory.
Past fellows include Logan Dandridge, Ain Bailey, Robert Ssempijja, and Akeelah Bertram (current: Thulani Rachia).

Eligibility is open internationally to artists working in any medium. Applicants must be 18 or over and out of full-time education by October 2026. No prior science experience required. The fellowship explicitly welcomes joint applications. There is no application fee. Applications go through JotForm; the 2026 deadline is May 16 at 11:00 AM British Summer Time. Zoom interviews scheduled for July 22, 2026.

calls.title: Chester Photo Festival 2026 — Making Voices Heard
calls.description: Second edition of the annual Chester Photo Festival, running 16–29 October 2026 across University of Chester, Picturehouse, churches, and a museum. Theme: Making Voices Heard — exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Free entry of up to 5 works; selection fees only apply if chosen (£45/work early deadline 15 May, £60/work late deadline 15 July, covering printing and standard framing). Open to photographers of all experience levels internationally. Accepts photography, moving image (online link + still), and artist books (PDF). Selected works included in the exhibition book and displayed across Chester venues. Late entries close when 300 works are selected. Organised by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen.
calls.summary: 2nd edition photo festival across Chester venues. Free entry; selection fee only. Exhibition + festival book.
jury: Erik Knudsen, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
Alexandru Modoi, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
Cian Quayle, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
Ian Clegg, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
Ana-Cristina Irian, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
Ceyiz Makal Fairclough, Committee, Chester Photo Festival
prose: Chester Photo Festival is a UK photography festival held in Chester, England, with the second edition running October 16–29, 2026 across six city center venues: University of Chester, Chester Picturehouse, St Werburgh's Church, St John's Church, the Grosvenor Museum, and one additional space. The festival was founded in 2023 with its inaugural edition in May 2025.

The 2026 theme is "Making Voices Heard," exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Submissions are accepted across photography (up to 5 JPEGs per artist), moving images and short films (online link plus still), and artist books or zines (as PDF).

The fee structure is unusual: submission is free for up to 5 works, with fees charged only if the work is selected. Selected work pays £45 at the early deadline (May 15) or £60 (£45 for students) at the late deadline (July 15), at which point selection closes once 300 works have been accepted.

Selected work is exhibited across the Chester venues with standard framing provided in three sizes (50×40, 40×30, 30×30 cm), published in the festival book, and the artist receives a participation certificate plus invitations to networking events and artist talks. AI-generated work is accepted.

The festival is open to photographers at all experience levels with international submissions welcome. Selection is overseen by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen.

calls.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Fall 2026
calls.description: Dedicated photography residency at Monson Arts in Maine, with access to the photography studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in nearby Blanchard — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. Darkroom accommodates silver gelatin printing up to 40"×50" from 35mm to 8×10 negatives, plus alternative analog processes. Digital studio with PC workstations, 34" monitors, Adobe Creative Cloud, and a 44" Epson printer. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, and a stipend ($250 for 2-week, $500 for 4-week). Fall 2026 sessions: September 14–24 (2-week) and October 28 – November 19 (4-week). Residents must supply their own materials and have a car (8-minute drive to studio). Open to photographers at any career stage worldwide.
calls.summary: Photography residency in Maine with full darkroom (up to 40×50 silver gelatin) and digital studio. Housing, meals, and stipend included.
prose: The Abbott Watts Photography Residency is hosted by Monson Arts in Monson, Maine, with the photography studio itself located in nearby Blanchard — an 8-minute drive from the Monson Arts main campus, adjacent to the former home of pioneering documentary photographer Berenice Abbott. The residency was launched in fall 2021 and is named after Abbott and longtime collaborator Todd Watts.

The Blanchard studio is unusually well-equipped. The darkroom supports silver gelatin printing up to 40×50 inches from negatives ranging from 35mm to 8×10, plus alternative analog processes. The digital studio includes PC workstations with 34-inch monitors and Adobe Creative Cloud, a 44-inch Epson printer, scanners, trimmers, and a dry-mount press.

Fall 2026 offers two session lengths. The two-week session runs September 14–24 with a $250 stipend; the four-week session runs October 28 through November 19 with a $500 stipend. Both sessions include a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, and full studio access. Residents must supply their own materials and have a car for the daily commute to the Blanchard studio.
Eligibility is open to photographers at any career stage worldwide. Applications go through SlideRoom. Both fall 2026 sessions share the same May 15, 2026 deadline.

calls.title: Peyton Evans Artist Residency (PEAR) 2026–2027
calls.description: One-month residency program on Key West, Florida. Photographers apply under Media Arts. Residencies run the 2nd day of the month to the last day, between October 2026 and August 2027. Residents receive accommodation at the PEAR House (live/work space), a bike to get around the island, and access to shared kitchen facilities. No residency fee once accepted; artists cover their own travel, living expenses, and materials. Founded in 2006, The Studios has hosted hundreds of writers and artists; selection committees are comprised of working artists and professionals across Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Media Arts, Musical Arts, and Performing Arts. Apply via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: One-month live/work residency on Key West. PEAR House accommodation, bike, and shared kitchen. No residency fee once accepted.
prose: The Peyton Evans Artist Residency (PEAR) is administered by The Studios of Key West (TSKW), a Florida arts non-profit based at 533 Eaton Street in Key West. The program supports residencies across Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Media Arts, Musical Arts, and Performing Arts — photographers apply under the Media Arts track.

Residencies run the 2nd day of the month through the last day, with placements available between October 2026 and August 2027. Each resident receives accommodation at the PEAR House — a live/work space — plus a bike for getting around the island and access to shared kitchen facilities.
There is no residency fee once accepted. Artists cover their own travel, living expenses, and materials.

TSKW was founded in 2006 and has hosted nearly 500 multidisciplinary artists across its history. Selection committees are composed of working artists and professionals across the five disciplinary tracks. Eligibility is open to emerging and established artists and writers worldwide.
Applications go through SlideRoom. The 2026 deadline is May 15.

calls.title: Eco-Process Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month summer residency at Blue Cabin Floating Artist Residency in Metro Vancouver (August 2026) for emerging lens-based artists. Program focuses on eco-processing and alternative photographic techniques such as phytogram, lumen printing, cyanotype, and other sustainable photographic processes. Up to 3 mentorship sessions with interdisciplinary artist Morgan Sears-Williams. Blue Cabin is situated on the traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. Priority given to LGBTQ+ 2S emerging artists with some photo/lens-based experience. Open to emerging artists in Metro Vancouver and Indigenous territories/reserves connected to the region. Produced by grunt gallery in collaboration with Blue Cabin Cooperative.
calls.summary: One-month Blue Cabin residency for emerging lens-based artists. Alt process mentorship (cyanotype, lumen, phytogram). LGBTQ+ 2S priority.
prose: The Eco-Process Artist Residency is a one-month summer residency program produced by grunt gallery in collaboration with Blue Cabin Cooperative. Blue Cabin is a floating artist residency in Metro Vancouver, on the traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.

The residency runs August 2026 and is technique-specific. The program focuses on eco-processing and alternative photographic techniques: phytogram, lumen printing, cyanotype, and other sustainable photographic processes that minimize chemistry and material waste.
Mentorship is part of the structure: up to three sessions with interdisciplinary artist Morgan Sears-Williams during the residency period. The selected artist receives a $3,500 fee for the month.

Eligibility is layered. Open to emerging artists with some photo or lens-based experience. Geographic restriction: Metro Vancouver and Indigenous territories/reserves connected to the region. Priority is given to LGBTQ+ 2S (Two-Spirit) emerging artists.
Submission is through Google Form with a portfolio. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was May 1; results announced mid-May 2026.

calls.title: 2026 National Juried Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition at the Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia. Open to U.S. residents aged 18+. Photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021, not previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. Juror Kiera Hight, photographer and filmmaker from Asheville, NC, selects work after installation. Exhibition runs September 4–25, 2026 with an opening reception on September 4. Digital submissions accepted via email or flash drive; JPEG, 300 DPI, minimum 4×6".
calls.summary: National juried exhibition at Academy Center of the Arts, Lynchburg VA. $1,000 Best in Show. Juror: Kiera Hight.
prose: The Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia (600 Main Street) runs an annual National Juried Photography Exhibition open to photographers across the United States. The 2026 cycle is juried by Kiera Hight, a photographer and filmmaker based in Asheville, North Carolina, who specializes in editorial, documentary, and creative work.

Cash prizes include the Best in Show award of $1,000, with additional cash awards given at the juror's discretion based on the installed exhibition. Selection is unusual: rather than judging from digital files alone, the juror selects work after installation — the physical hang influences the awards.

Selected work is exhibited September 4 through 25, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4. The Academy Center provides insurance coverage during the exhibition period and includes selected work in a full-color exhibition catalog. Sales are processed through the gallery, which retains a 35% commission.

Eligibility is restricted to U.S. residents aged 18 or over. Submitted photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021 and cannot have been previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. The entry fee is $45 per artist for up to three submissions. Submissions are JPEG at 300 DPI, minimum 4×6 inches, accepted via email or flash drive. The 2026 deadline is June 30; results announced July 14.

calls.title: Recology San Francisco Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
calls.description: Four-month Artist-in-Residence program at the Recology San Francisco Recycling and Transfer Center, where artists source materials from the Public Reuse and Recycling Area to make work from discarded items. Three sessions run February–May, June–September, and October–January, with six artists awarded residencies annually beginning February 2027. Residents receive a monthly stipend, 24/7 access to a dedicated on-site studio, and support from Recology's Sustainability Education Program. Artists interact with visiting school and adult groups throughout their residency and exhibit at the end. Open to emerging, mid-career, and established artists in all disciplines including photography, new media, video, painting, performance, sculpture, and installation. Applicants must currently live within a one-hour drive of the San Francisco Transfer Station (401 Tunnel Ave) — no housing provided. A mandatory on-site tour is required before applying.
calls.summary: Four-month residency at SF's recycling center — artists make work from discarded materials. Monthly stipend, studio access. Bay Area only.
prose: The Recology Artist-in-Residence Program is a four-month residency at the San Francisco Recycling and Transfer Center — a 47-acre site on Tunnel Avenue where the city's discarded materials are sorted and processed. Founded in 1990 by Jo Hanson and described as the first program of its kind in the United States, the AIR program lets artists source materials directly from the Public Reuse and Recycling Area on site, producing work that engages with discarded objects and waste streams.

Six artists are awarded residencies each year, split across three sessions: February–May, June–September, and October–January. Each resident receives a monthly stipend, 24/7 access to a dedicated on-site studio, and support from Recology's Sustainability Education Program. Artists give regular talks to school groups and adult visitors during facility tours, integrating studio practice with public education. Each residency concludes with a public exhibition and artist talk; selected works enter Recology AIR's permanent collection.

Eligibility is restricted to artists who currently live within a one-hour drive of the San Francisco Transfer Station (401 Tunnel Ave); housing is not provided. The program is open to emerging, mid-career, and established artists across all disciplines — photography, new media, video, painting, performance, sculpture, installation. A mandatory on-site tour is required before applying.

Over its 35-year history the program has hosted more than 190 professional artists and 60 college and university student artists. The advisory board for selection includes Michael Arcega, Charmin Roundtree-Baaqee, JD Beltran, Terry Berlier, Kevin B. Chen, Elena Gross, Jamil Hellu, and Jonathan Carver Moore. The 2027 cycle deadline is September 1, 2026.
