calls.title: Photoworks Artist Venturing Labs — EASE: Crete 2026–2027
calls.description: Open call for a UK-based artist to join an art–science fieldwork lab in Crete in autumn 2026, exploring climate, landscape, and deep time alongside scientific teams. £1,000 stipend for the week on site; travel, accommodation, and meals fully covered. 24-month online engagement with EASE partners and Photoworks platform features.
jury: Mark Kasumovic, Artist & Academic, De Montfort University
calls.summary: UK-based artist joins art–science fieldwork lab in Crete. £1,000 stipend, all expenses covered. Climate, landscape, deep time.
prose: Photoworks is the UK's national photography commissioning agency, based in Brighton. Artist Venturing Labs is a programme produced with EASE (Entrepreneurship, Art & Science for Environmental Sustainability), an interdisciplinary research initiative funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) in collaboration with Nottingham Trent University, De Montfort University, and PicturingClimate.org.

The 2026–2027 lab takes place in Crete, with fieldwork across diverse Cretan locations exploring climate, landscape, and deep time alongside the scientific teams resident on the island. The selected artist commits to one week on site (autumn 2026) plus 24 months of online engagement with the EASE network. No academic background, entrepreneurship experience, or prior interdisciplinary practice is required — Photoworks explicitly invites applicants without an EASE-style track record.

The selected artist receives a £1,000 stipend for the week on site. All travel, accommodation, and meals are covered. The artist gets access to scientific teams, fellow artists in the EASE cohort, and Photoworks' venture-building support, with potential features on Photoworks' digital and editorial platforms.

Eligibility is restricted to UK-based artists, per the UKRI funding requirement. Application is via online form with either a 5-page PDF (expression of interest, bio, project examples, available lab dates) or a 3-minute audio or video recording. The deadline is June 29, 2026 at 23:59 BST.

calls.title: Portal: At the Edge of Becoming
calls.description: Photographs that hold the viewer at the edge of something — work where a shift is imminent but not yet complete. Online curated exhibition with catalog inclusion and Instagram feature. First place receives $500 plus a solo webpage exhibition; second $300; third $200. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes welcome.
calls.summary: Online photography exhibition on tension and threshold. Juror Douglas Stockdale. $1,000 total + solo webpage.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "Portal: At the Edge of Becoming" is the gallery's call for photographs that hold a viewer at the edge of something — where a shift is imminent but not yet complete. The brief asks for work that embodies tension and resists easy resolution, functioning as a threshold rather than a literal representation.

The selection structure is online-first. Selected photographers are featured in a curated online exhibition with a published catalog distributed through Decagon's mailing list and social channels. All accepted artists receive an exhibition page, an Instagram feature, and catalog inclusion. The first-place winner additionally receives a solo webpage exhibition on the gallery site.

Cash awards: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third. The 2026 cycle is juried by Douglas Stockdale — visual artist, editor, photobook publisher, and founder of PhotoBook Journal. Eligibility is open worldwide; all photographic styles and processes are welcome.
Entry fee is $25 per submission of up to 8 images (JPG, 2100 pixels on long side, no watermarks or borders). The 2026 deadline is June 3, with the exhibition running June 20 through August 20, 2026.

calls.title: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography
calls.description: Open call celebrating the creativity, diversity, and evolving practice of photography today. Aligned with World Photography Day. Up to 35 images selected for the physical Middlebury, Vermont gallery and 40 for the online gallery, with all selected work appearing in the exhibition catalog and remaining permanently on the website. Open worldwide, all subjects, styles, and processes welcome.
calls.summary: PhotoPlace's most inclusive call. World Photography Day exhibition in Middlebury, VT + online + catalog.
prose: PhotoPlace Gallery is a photography gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, that programs juried thematic exhibitions on a rolling schedule. "A Celebration of Contemporary Photography" is one of the gallery's most open and inclusive calls of the year — explicitly framed as a celebration of the creativity, diversity, and evolving practice of photography today.

The exhibition is timed to World Photography Day (August 19) and welcomes all photographic subjects, styles, and processes — from traditional landscape and portraiture to experimental and alternative approaches.

Selection structure is layered: up to 35 images are selected for the physical exhibition in the Middlebury gallery, and up to 40 for the online gallery. All selected work appears in the exhibition catalog, remains permanently on the PhotoPlace website, and receives social media promotion with photographer URL links.
Selection is by Paula Tognarelli (former director of the Griffin Museum of Photography) and Zach Hoffman (Gallery Owner/Director).

AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website. Fee is $39 for up to 5 images plus $6 per additional image. The 2026 deadline is June 8, with the exhibition running August 7 through August 29, 2026.

calls.title: America 250 — Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Ninth national juried photography exhibition celebrating the U.S. Semiquincentennial. Open to USA artists 18+. Photography defined as digital or film camera work, unaltered except minor enhancements. AI-generated work not accepted. $800 in awards: $300 best capture of theme, $200 best traditional, $200 best non-traditional, $100 Award of Merit. Exhibition June 19 – August 1, 2026 at Gallery One in Ellensburg, WA. Jurors: Gail Gibson and C. Meier (Blue Sky Oregon Center for Photographic Arts).
jury: C. Meier, Exhibitions Director, Blue Sky Oregon Center for Photographic Arts
calls.summary: National juried photography show on US 250th anniversary. $800 in awards. Gallery One in Ellensburg, WA.
prose: Gallery One Visual Arts Center is a nonprofit gallery at 408 N Pearl Street in downtown Ellensburg, Washington. The annual America 250 exhibition is the gallery's ninth national juried photography show, the 2026 edition timed for the United States Semiquincentennial — the 250th anniversary of American independence. The brief invites work that engages with the country at this milestone moment.

Photography is defined strictly: work created using a digital or film camera, unaltered except for slight enhancements to lighting, coloration, or contrast. AI-generated work is not accepted. The 2026 jurors are Gail Gibson, gallery director and curator, alongside C. Meier, Exhibitions Director at Blue Sky, the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts in Portland.

Awards total $800 across four categories: $300 for best at capturing the exhibit theme, $200 for best traditional approach to photography, $200 for best non-traditional approach, and $100 Award of Merit. Selected work is shown at Gallery One from June 19 through August 1, 2026, with the artist receiving 60% commission on sales.

Eligibility is restricted to artists 18+ residing in the United States. Submission is through CallForEntry.org (CaFE). Fees are $20 for the first entry and $10 for each additional, with a maximum of 6 entries. The deadline is May 17, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST; acceptance notifications are sent May 27, 2026.

calls.title: Mrinalini Mukherjee Creative Arts Grant 2026
calls.description: Annual grant from the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation supporting innovative and experimental projects by established Indian artists. INR 10 lakhs (approximately USD 12,000) disbursed in two equal installments. Eligible disciplines span the visual arts including painting, sculpture, mural, textile, printmaking, performance art, and lens and media-based art. Open to Indian citizens currently residing in India with a minimum of 15 years of professional practice. Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and Persons of Indian Origin are not eligible. Individual artists and collectives may both apply.
calls.summary: INR 10 lakhs (~USD 12,000) grant from the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation for established Indian artists including lens-based practitioners.
prose: The Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation honours the legacy of sculptor Mrinalini Mukherjee (1949–2015), one of India's most significant artists, by supporting the work of contemporary Indian artists. The Creative Arts Grant is the foundation's flagship annual award, structured to fund a single ambitious project rather than supplement an existing practice.

The grant amount is INR 10 lakhs — roughly USD 12,000 — disbursed in two equal installments. Eligible disciplines span the visual arts broadly: painting, sculpture, mural, textile, printmaking, performance art, and lens and media-based art, including projects working at the intersection of these forms.

Eligibility is tightly defined. Applicants must be Indian citizens currently residing in India, with a minimum of fifteen years of professional practice after graduate or postgraduate study. Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and Persons of Indian Origin are not eligible. Both individual artists and collectives may apply.

The brief emphasises innovation and experimentation. The foundation is looking for projects that mark a shift, a new direction, or a willingness to test fresh ideas, materials, and methods rather than continuations of established work. Applications require a project proposal with budget and timeline (up to 1,000 words), a portfolio, and a detailed CV. Submission is free, through the foundation's website. The deadline is May 15, 2026.

calls.title: Guest Room: Annet Dekker & Margriet Schavemaker
calls.description: Open call curated by Annet Dekker (Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis at the University of Amsterdam and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Networked Image at London South Bank University) with Margriet Schavemaker (Director, Kunstmuseum Den Haag), exploring "The Brilliance of the Mundane." Invites reflections on the unnoticed and the unremarkable — images rooted in everyday life, shaped by happenstance, hasty habits, glitched files, accidental photos, and repetitive imagery — asking how to restore dignity to overlooked visual material and considering how these fragments operate as digital folklore fuelling contemporary image practices. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with a face-to-face feedback session from the curators. €250 Guest Room scholarship. Works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.
calls.summary: Theme: "The Brilliance of the Mundane" — everyday, accidental, and overlooked imagery as digital folklore.
jury: Annet Dekker, Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis, University of Amsterdam
Margriet Schavemaker, Director, Kunstmuseum Den Haag
prose: Guest Room is Der Greif's recurring curator-led open call format. Each edition is shaped by an external curator or curatorial duo who set the theme and selection criteria. This Guest Room is curated jointly by Annet Dekker and Margriet Schavemaker.

Dekker is Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis and MA Coordinator of Archival and Information Studies at the University of Amsterdam, and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Networked Image at London South Bank University. Schavemaker is Director of Kunstmuseum Den Haag and specialises in modern and contemporary culture, museum practice, and digital art.

The theme is "The Brilliance of the Mundane." The brief asks for reflection on the unnoticed and unremarkable: everyday images shaped by happenstance, hasty habits, glitched files, accidental photos, repetitive imagery. The curators frame these fragments as a form of digital folklore fuelling contemporary image practices, and ask how to restore dignity to images that are typically dismissed.

Selected work is published on Der Greif's platform. Selected artists also receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators. One artist receives a €250 Guest Room scholarship. Eligibility is open globally; works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (PWYC) — €10 suggested but not required, with 50–100% hardship vouchers available by emailing voucher-guestroom@dergreif.org. The deadline is June 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET; the resulting online exhibition launches July 2026 on dergreif.org.

calls.title: Der Greif Issue 19 — I Am Because of You, Mother Earth
calls.description: Open call for Der Greif's 19th print issue, guest-edited by Zanele Muholi — the South African visual activist and 2026 Hasselblad Award laureate, known for documenting Black LGBTQIA+ communities and reimagining Blackness. Theme: "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth" — examining environment as inseparable from bodies, histories, and relationships, with Muholi framing the body as a landscape, the face as geography, and breath as atmosphere. Accepts photography, writing, poetry, and essays from contributors worldwide; collaborative submissions encouraged. Selected work is reviewed by Muholi, published in Issue 19 with a free copy plus discounted additional copies, considered for an Artist Feature on dergreif.org, and may participate in Der Greif's Paris Photo 2026 events.
calls.summary: Print issue guest-edited by Zanele Muholi. Theme: "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth" — environment as inseparable from body and breath.
prose: Der Greif is the Munich-based photography magazine and platform founded in 2008, supported by the Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung foundation. The magazine's print issues are guest-edited by a single curator or artist who sets the theme and reviews submissions, with Issue 19 guest-edited by Zanele Muholi.

Muholi is a South African visual activist and photographer based in Cape Town, internationally recognised for documenting Black LGBTQIA+ communities, the Faces and Phases project, and a long-running self-portrait practice that reimagines representations of Blackness. They were named the 2026 Hasselblad Award laureate.

The theme is "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth." Muholi reframes environment as inseparable from the self: the body as a landscape, the face as geography, breath as atmosphere, with water in the blood, minerals in the bones, and soil that feeds the body all positioned as part of the same continuous ecology. The brief invites artists and writers to respond to this framing.

Accepted media include photography, writing, poetry, and essays. Collaborative submissions are encouraged. Selected work is reviewed by Muholi, published in Issue 19 with a complimentary copy plus discounts on additional copies, and considered for an Artist Feature on dergreif.org. Selected contributors may also participate in Der Greif's Paris Photo 2026 programme and related events.
Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (PWYC) — €13 until June 7, then €15, with financial assistance available on request. The deadline was extended to July 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET.

calls.title: Jean Giono Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: Free photography contest from the Friends of Jean Giono association, organised in partnership with Regards Alpins (a member association that runs photographic events tied to literature). Photographs — single image or coherent series — inspired by an excerpt from Giono's novel Noé, meditating on extraordinary landscapes and the act of seeing them through a lens. The 2026 Rencontres Giono festival is themed "Giono and Photography," running July 29–August 2 in Manosque; winners are announced at the festival on August 1, 2026. Open to amateurs and professionals of any age and country.
calls.summary: Free contest by Les Amis de Jean Giono and Regards Alpins. Photos inspired by Giono's Noé. Awards at Rencontres Giono, Manosque.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Materiality
calls.description: Themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. The Materiality call, guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho (@frangccom), seeks works that embrace a connection with the process and create a bridge between photography and other media — such as printmaking — to expand the capacities of the photographic form through alternative techniques, materials, and interventions. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with project description (max 500 words). Upload work to a public Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments are deleted. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.

The journal runs themed issues with rotating guest curators. The Materiality call asks photographers to engage with the material side of the medium — surface, texture, substance — and the bridges photography forms with adjacent practices like printmaking.

The call is guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho (@frangccom). The brief explicitly invites alternative techniques, materials, and interventions — works that treat the photograph as more than a transparent image and engage process as part of the meaning.

Emails with attachments are deleted unread.
Submission is free of charge. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline is June 15.

calls.title: THAT ONE PHOTOGRAPH
calls.description: Juried single-image call from Decagon Gallery for a photograph carrying emotional weight tied to memory, attachment, intimacy, grief, distance, tenderness, longing, or time. The brief favors images 'never fully left behind' over technical perfection. $1,000 total cash awards across five placements ($500 first plus solo website exhibition, $250 second, $150 third, two $50 honorable mentions). All selected photographers receive a dedicated exhibition page, Instagram feature, and catalog placement. Online exhibition July 1 – September 1, 2026. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes.
calls.summary: Single-image call on memory, intimacy, longing. $1,000 awards. Online exhibition + catalog from Decagon Gallery.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "That One Photograph" is the gallery's single-image call for the photograph that carries weight tied to memory, attachment, intimacy, grief, distance, tenderness, longing, or time. The brief explicitly de-prioritizes portfolio-best work — the gallery wants images that 'continue to live inside' the photographer rather than technically perfect frames.

Cash awards total $1,000 across five placements: $500 first place plus a solo website exhibition, $250 second, $150 third, and two $50 honorable mentions. A separate Human Presence Nomination offers free entry to a future open call. All selected photographers receive a dedicated exhibition page, Instagram feature, and catalog placement. The 2026 exhibition runs July 1 through September 1.
Selection is by the Decagon Gallery team. All photographic styles and processes are welcome.

Submissions are JPG at 2100 pixels on the long side — no text, watermarks, or borders — plus one short sentence describing what 'continues to live inside' the image. One photograph per entry. Entry fee is $15. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over. The 2026 deadline is June 20 at 11:59 PM Eastern; results announced June 28.

calls.title: RED Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Photographs exploring red in any style — documentary, fine art, abstract, or experimental. 26 images selected for exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, NM, August 7–28, 2026. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Luster paper and 24×24 black museum-quality framing. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Red in any style — documentary, fine art, abstract, experimental. Free pro printing & framing. Santa Fe, NM.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also founded Decode Gallery in Tucson — Dusk operates as Hart's New Mexico project space alongside the larger Tucson program. "RED" is the gallery's themed call asking photographers to explore the color in any photographic style — documentary, fine art, abstract, or experimental approaches all welcome.

Twenty-six photographs are selected for the exhibition at Dusk Gallery, running August 7 through 28, 2026 with an opening reception. Selected work appears in the gallery's published catalog and across social media.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Luster paper, gallery-quality 24×24 inch black museum frames, and white matting from the gallery's collection. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG; the gallery resizes without cropping the original composition.
Sales terms split commission 50/50. Photographer retains all rights.

Entry fees: $40 for 5 images, $45 for up to 10. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Submissions require JPEGs at 500KB to 5MB, 4,500 pixels on the longest side. The 2026 deadline is June 25, with notifications within 2 weeks.

calls.title: BBA One Shot Award - Spring 2026
calls.description: Single-image photography prize. 20 images selected for print exhibition at BBA Gallery in Berlin, plus 30 additional images on digital display. First prize: €300 + exhibition + Artsy listing + social media promotion. All production and shipping costs covered.
calls.summary: Single-image photo prize. 20 images exhibited at BBA Gallery Berlin. €300 + Artsy listing. Production covered.
jury: Vishal Shah, Managing & Creative Director, BBA Gallery
Jo Schwab, Photographer & Lecturer, Camera Work Gallery
prose: BBA Gallery is a Berlin-based contemporary art gallery that runs several international prizes across photography, painting, and sculpture. The One Shot Award is the gallery's single-image photography call, running multiple editions per year — the Spring 2026 edition closes May 25.

The format is intentionally minimal: one image, one entry, €19 fee. Twenty selected images are printed and exhibited at BBA Gallery in Berlin; thirty additional images are shown on digital display. The first-place winner receives €300 cash, the exhibition, social media promotion, and an Artsy profile listing — Artsy being the major online art marketplace.

BBA covers all production and shipping costs for selected work. Eligibility is open globally to any artist 18+, any photographic medium or genre. Submission is through the BBA Prizes platform: JPG, PNG, or HEIC up to 3MB, with name, country, image title, and year of creation.

calls.title: FILE NOT FOUND — Archive Residencies 2026
calls.description: International open call selecting ten artists for residencies at cultural archives worldwide, run by Goethe-Institut in collaboration with Gerador. Each residency lasts 2 weeks to 2 months between August 2026 and May 2027, on-site at one of ten participating archives: Acervo Bajubá (São Paulo), The ArQuives (Toronto), China Modern Art Archive (Beijing), documenta archiv (Kassel), Arsenal Filminstitut (Berlin), Kurdistan Center for Arts & Culture (Erbil), Imagine IC & The Need for Legacy (Amsterdam), VEHA Archive (Podlasie), Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea (Lisbon), and South African History Archive (Johannesburg). Each selected artist receives €2,000 artist fee, €2,000 production budget, and up to €2,000 for travel and accommodation. Final works exhibited at BLMK (Brandenburgisches Landesmuseum für moderne Kunst) in Cottbus, Germany, in Fall 2027. Open to artists worldwide, all disciplines including photography. Working language English.
calls.summary: Ten artist residencies at archives worldwide. €4,000 + travel + final exhibition at BLMK Cottbus 2027. With Gerador.
jury: One representative each from the host archive (deciding vote), BLMK, Gerador, and the Goethe-Institut FILE NOT FOUND project team

calls.title: Men Asleep — 2026 Book & Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: Book and exhibition expansion of the 2025 'Men Asleep' zine compiled by Jordanna Kalman and published by Memory Version. Submit one photograph of a man sleeping. JPEG, 300 dpi, 3000 px on the long side, named Firstname_Lastname.jpeg. Email subject 'Men Asleep Submission' with name, website, and Instagram handle in the body. Entries not following these instructions will not be considered.
calls.summary: Book and exhibition expansion of Jordanna Kalman's 2025 'Men Asleep' zine. One photograph of a man sleeping. Free, open to all.
prose: Men Asleep began as a 2025 zine compiled by Jordanna Kalman and published by Memory Version. Kalman invited fifty women photographers to send a photograph of a man sleeping; nineteen responded, and the resulting 40-page black-and-white zine was inflected by the Gisèle Pelicot case and the contrast between sleep as safety and as vulnerability.

The 2026 open call expands the project into a book and an exhibition. The brief remains spare: one photograph of a man sleeping. The work selected for the 2025 zine ranged from intimate and dreamy to charged with implied threat — the call leaves interpretation to the photographer.

Submission is by email. The image must be JPEG, 300 dpi, with the long side at 3000 pixels, named Firstname_Lastname.jpeg. The email subject must read 'Men Asleep Submission' and the body must include name, website, and Instagram handle. Entries that do not follow these instructions will not be considered.
Entry is free. The deadline is August 1, 2026. The project is run directly by Memory Version; no jury list or selection schedule is published on the call page.

calls.title: PURE ABSTRACTION
calls.description: Online juried exhibit celebrating pure abstraction — shape, color, line, texture, and the rhythm of form. Open to all fine art mediums including photography. Artists receive 100% of sale price with no commission.
jury: Amy Matteson Neill, Creative Director, Art Fluent
calls.summary: Online juried exhibit for pure abstraction across all mediums including photography. 100% commission-free sales. $1,250 in prizes.
prose: Art Fluent is a Boston-based curatorial platform (1 Washington Mall #1218, Boston, MA 02108) that runs themed online juried exhibitions across fine art mediums. "PURE ABSTRACTION" is the platform's open call for work that lets shape, color, line, texture, and form stand on their own — work that is not bound by representation.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. Beyond cash, all accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com, with sales going through the platform at 100% commission to the artist. The selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to 20 submissions per artist. Open globally to amateur and professional artists; AI-generated work is not accepted, and work made under instructor guidance or copied from other sources is excluded. Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account.
Art Fluent does not provide individualized rejection feedback. The 2026 deadline is August 28 (midnight MST), with notification on September 25, 2026.

calls.title: VAiF26 — Photobook Open Call 2026
calls.description: Free international open call from the Visual Arts International Festival (VAiF) in Thessaloniki, Greece, dedicated to photography in book form. Accepts self-published photobooks, publisher collaborations, zines, and dummy books with no thematic restrictions; works with clear visual identity, coherent narrative structure, and contemporary photographic language are valued. Selected works are presented in a group exhibition at VAiF26 in November 2026 and enter the VAiF Photobook Collection for future non-commercial presentations. Jury: Elena Karathanasi (museologist, photographer, graphic designer; Teloglion Foundation), Alexandra Moschovi (photography professor and art historian, University of Sunderland), and Alexander Supartono (art historian and curator, Edinburgh Napier University). Submission via online form with PDF (full book or layout), flip-through video (max 2 min on YouTube/Vimeo/WeTransfer, link valid 15+ days), and photographs of cover, spreads, and details. Open to photographers, artists, publishers, and creative studios aged 18 or over worldwide. Multiple submissions allowed (one form per book). Selected artists send one physical copy for exhibition; copies are not returned and remain in the VAiF Photobook Collection.

calls.summary: Free photobook open call at Visual Arts International Festival in Thessaloniki. Group exhibition in November 2026. No thematic restriction.
prose: The Visual Arts International Festival (VAiF) is an annual festival of contemporary visual arts held in Thessaloniki, Greece, organised by the esp+ photography school. The 2026 Photobook Open Call sits alongside the festival's Photography Portfolio call as a dedicated track for photography in book form — accepting self-published photobooks, publisher collaborations, zines, and dummy books with no thematic restrictions.

Selected works are exhibited as a group at VAiF26 in Thessaloniki in November 2026 and enter the VAiF Photobook Collection for future non-commercial presentations. Entries are free and open to photographers, artists, publishers, and creative studios aged 18 or over worldwide. The jury values projects with clear visual identity, coherent narrative structure, and contemporary photographic language.

The 2026 jury combines curatorial, academic, and design voices: Elena Karathanasi (museologist, photographer, and graphic designer at the Teloglion Foundation), Alexandra Moschovi (photography professor and art historian, University of Sunderland), and Alexander Supartono (art historian and curator specialising in Southeast Asian contemporary art, Edinburgh Napier University).

Submission is via an online form with a PDF of the full book or complete layout, a flip-through video up to two minutes hosted on YouTube/Vimeo or shared via WeTransfer with at least 15 days' validity, and photographs of cover, spreads, and details. Multiple submissions are allowed with one form per book. Selected artists send one physical copy for exhibition; copies are not returned and remain in the VAiF Photobook Collection. Deadline: June 15, 2026 at 23:59 GMT (extended from May 31).

calls.title: Les Photographiques 2027 — Open Call
calls.description: Free open call from Les Photographiques, the annual photography festival in Le Mans, France, for its 2027 edition. The bicentenary of photography's invention is marked by two parallel strands: a non-thematic strand open to all photographic proposals, and a landscape strand integrated into the Réseau LUX network's 200LUX bicentennial project. Festival runs March 13 – April 11, 2027 across Le Mans and partner cities (dates pending confirmation). Selected artists receive €500 exhibition rights compensation plus travel reimbursement up to €400 against receipts. The festival does not cover production costs. Open to artists of any age and nationality; one series per applicant. Digital submission via email; complete application file (regulations and registration combined as a single PDF) is downloaded from the festival website. Non-compliant submissions are not reviewed. Organised by the Festival de l'image association; member of Réseau LUX.
calls.summary: Free open call for the 2027 Les Photographiques festival in Le Mans. €500 artist fee + travel. General + landscape strands (200LUX bicentennial).
prose: Les Photographiques is an annual photography festival held in Le Mans and partner cities in the Sarthe region of France, organised by the Festival de l'image association. The festival is a member of Réseau LUX — the French photography festival network — and the 2027 edition coincides with the bicentenary of photography's invention.

The 2027 programming runs two strands. A non-thematic strand remains open to all photographic propositions, while a second strand is dedicated to landscape as part of Réseau LUX's 200LUX bicentennial project. Applicants submit to either strand through the same call. The festival proper takes place March 13 to April 11, 2027 across Le Mans and partner towns (dates pending confirmation).

Participation is free for the 2027 edition — the festival removed its previous entry fee. Selected artists receive €500 as exhibition rights compensation and up to €400 in travel reimbursement against receipts. Production costs are not covered. The call is open to artists of any age and nationality, with one series per applicant.

Submission is via email only. Applicants must download the regulations and registration form (combined as a single PDF) from photographiques.org and submit complete, conforming dossiers — non-compliant submissions are not reviewed. The deadline is Friday, July 31, 2026 (inclusive).

calls.summary: International photobook award. Yogurt Editions publishes winner in 500 copies; one shortlisted artist gets Artphilein solo show in Lugano.
prose: Charta is a biennial photobook festival based in Lugano, Switzerland, run by independent publisher Yogurt Editions in collaboration with Artphilein, a Lugano contemporary photography organisation. The brief is open in subject but strict in originality: projects must never have appeared in printed book or fanzine format. Self-published works are accepted only if fewer than 15 copies exist without ISBN registration. The award is open to international artists incorporating photography in their practice, with no age restriction.

The winning project is produced by Yogurt Editions in a run of 500 copies. The selected artist receives 30 free copies and 10% royalties on sold copies, reported every six months. Submission requires at least 30 images from a single coherent project, a PDF with project title, artist name, email and synopsis, a signed publishing contract, and the payment receipt. An additional edited PDF showing the work as a sequence is welcome but optional. Early-bird entry is €15 until April 30, 2026; regular entry is €25 thereafter. The deadline is July 25, 2026 at 6:00 PM CET.

calls.title: Verzasca Foto Festival 2027 — Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: Free international exhibition open call for the 2027 edition of Verzasca Foto Festival, marking the festival's shift to a biennial format. Held in Sonogno and surrounding villages of the Verzasca Valley in Ticino, Switzerland, the festival positions photography as a tool for observation, relation, and cultural exchange with peripheral, rural, and marginal places. The 2027 edition seeks work that reveals the everyday gestures sustaining landscapes, economies, languages, and relationships in such territories — without romanticising them. Selected artists receive a participation fee; the festival covers all exhibition production costs. Submission accepts a coherent photo series from any time or location aligned with the brief, plus an optional slide or video for projection (does not influence selection). Open to all photographers worldwide regardless of background. Selected artists are notified by email at the end of June 2026; the festival does not provide feedback on unselected applications.
calls.summary: Free call for Verzasca Foto's 2027 biennial in Ticino. Photography of peripheral and rural places. Fee + production covered for selected.
prose: Verzasca Foto Festival is a photography festival held in Sonogno and surrounding villages of the Verzasca Valley, a remote Alpine area in Ticino, Switzerland. Founded as an annual event, the festival is transitioning to a biennial format with its 2027 edition, positioning itself as a meeting space between artistic practice and territory.

The 2027 open call is built around a clear curatorial line: photography that engages directly with peripheral, rural, and marginal places. The brief asks for work that surfaces the everyday gestures sustaining landscapes, economies, languages, and relationships in such territories — explicitly avoiding romanticisation. Works exhibited in 2027 will be installed in natural and rural settings across the valley.

Selected artists receive a participation fee, and the festival covers all exhibition production costs. The call is free to enter and open to photographers worldwide regardless of background. Submissions can include a photo series from any time or location, provided it aligns with the exhibition concept, with an optional slide or video for projection that does not influence selection.

Selected artists are notified by email at the end of June 2026; the festival does not provide feedback to unselected applicants. Submission is via the festival's website. The deadline is June 10, 2026.

calls.title: Near. Prize 2026
calls.description: Annual prize from Near., a Swiss association for contemporary photography founded in Lausanne in 2009, awarded jointly with Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi in Zürich. The 2026 cycle culminates in an exhibition at the gallery and at Fotofestival Lenzburg, whose 2026 theme is 'Forever Happy' — happiness that means everything and nothing in the present moment. The winner receives a CHF 1,000 grant (intended to support exhibition production or further work), a solo exhibition at Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi, and a one-year free Near. membership. Jury: gallerists Stephan Witschi and Barbara Liebster (Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi); Georgina Casparis, Head and Curator of Art Vontobel; and the Near. committee (one collective vote). Open exclusively to Near. members, Swiss or Swiss-based photographers of any age. Submission is a PDF containing a series of 7–15 images produced since 2023, a project description of roughly 300 words, and the completed application form (downloaded from near.li). Winner announced July 2026.
jury: Stephan Witschi, Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi
Barbara Liebster, Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi
Georgina Casparis, Head & Curator, Art Vontobel
calls.summary: Swiss prize from Near. + Galerie Stephan Witschi. CHF 1,000 + solo show + festival exhibition at Fotofestival Lenzburg. Near. members only.
prose: Near. is a Swiss association for contemporary photography founded in Lausanne in 2009, with a remit to disseminate work, foster critical discourse, and connect Swiss-based photographers with national and international photography professionals. The Near. Prize is the association's annual award, run in partnership with Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi in Zürich.

The 2026 cycle is built around an exhibition at the gallery and a presentation in the 2026 edition of Fotofestival Lenzburg, whose theme is 'Forever Happy' — a reading of happiness that means everything and nothing in the present moment. The winner receives a CHF 1,000 grant to support exhibition production or future work, a solo exhibition at Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi, and a one-year free Near. membership.

The 2026 jury combines gallery, institutional, and association voices: gallerists Stephan Witschi and Barbara Liebster from Galerie & Edition Stephan Witschi; Georgina Casparis, Head and Curator of Art Vontobel; and the Near. committee, which counts as one collective vote.

Participation is reserved for Near. members — in practice, Swiss or Swiss-based photographers of any age. Submission is a PDF containing a series of 7 to 15 images produced since 2023, a project description of approximately 300 words, and the completed application form downloaded from the Near. website. Applications are sent to info@near.li. The call opened April 27, 2026; the deadline is June 7, 2026, with the winner announced in July 2026.

calls.title: Lanesboro Early Career Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Place-based residency in rural Lanesboro, Minnesota (pop. 754), supported by the Jerome Foundation. Two- or four-week residencies for early career artists whose work engages community. Eligibility is restricted to legal residents of Minnesota or one of the five boroughs of New York City who have lived there at least one year, with 2–10 years of practice as a presenting artist (not first-time creators, not yet established). All disciplines accepted including photography. Two-round application: Round One due 11:59 pm CST May 30, 2026; selected applicants advance to Round Two due August 1, 2026. Round Two applicants receive a $75 honorarium. Selected residents receive $1,000/week stipend plus housing and studio; materials and travel are paid from the stipend.
calls.summary: Place-based residency in rural Minnesota. $1,000/week + housing/studio. MN or NYC residents only, 2–10 years of practice. Free.
prose: Lanesboro Arts runs an artist residency in Lanesboro, Minnesota — a town of about 754 people in the bluff country of the state's southeastern corner. The Early Career Artist Residency Program is supported through 2027 by the Jerome Foundation and awards two or three residencies per year. The 2027 cycle is open for Round One applications through May 30, 2026.

The program is built around place and community rather than studio isolation. Residencies run two or four weeks and ask the artist to either apply their work to the people and places of Lanesboro or let the rural context inform their practice. All disciplines are welcome, with photography listed alongside drawing, fiber, glass, media arts, music, painting, performance, printmaking, sculpture, wood, interdisciplinary, and writing.

Eligibility is narrow geographically. Applicants must be legal residents of Minnesota or one of the five boroughs of New York City and must have lived there for at least a year before applying. The 'early career' definition is precise: at least two years of presenting one's own projects but no more than ten years of such experience. First-time creators and established artists are both out of scope.

Applications run in two rounds. Round One asks for basic biographical and project information and closes May 30, 2026; Round Two, due August 1, asks for fuller project plans and pays a $75 honorarium on completion. Notification of Round One results comes June 9. Selected residents receive a $1,000/week stipend, housing, and studio space; materials and transportation come out of the stipend. Application is free.

calls.title: Lanesboro BIPOC Artist Residency 2026/27
calls.description: One- or two-week residency in Lanesboro, Minnesota for Black, Indigenous, and Persons of Color (BIPOC) artists who reside in Minnesota. All mediums accepted, including photography. Studio use is optional. Each artist receives a $1,250/week stipend, an additional $500 art supplies budget per residency, and housing. Residencies scheduled between September 2026 and April 2027. Selection by lottery from eligible applications, followed by individual confirmation meetings with staff. One community share-back (workshop, school visit, gathering, or blog post) is required during the residency. Applications close 11:59 pm Monday August 10, 2026; lottery results communicated by August 14.
calls.summary: 1–2 week residency in rural Minnesota for MN-based BIPOC artists. $1,250/week + $500 supplies + housing. Lottery-based, free.
prose: Lanesboro Arts runs a residency program reserved for Black, Indigenous, and Persons of Color (BIPOC) artists based in Minnesota. The 2026/27 cycle is open to artists of all stages and all mediums — photography is named alongside dance, design, digital media, documentary, fiber arts, film, illustration, installation, music, writing, and the rest of the list. Studio space is available but optional; the program is built around residency time as much as production.

The cycle runs between September 2026 and April 2027. Each residency is one or two weeks long, chosen by the artist. Selected residents receive a stipend of $1,250 per week to cover food and living costs and an additional $500 per residency budget for art supplies, plus housing. One community share-back — a workshop, school visit, gathering, or blog post — is required during the residency.

Selection is by lottery from the pool of eligible applications rather than juried review. After the lottery, staff meet individually with each selected artist to confirm dates and shape the residency. Applications close at 11:59 pm on Monday, August 10, 2026; lottery results are communicated by August 14, 2026. Application is free.

calls.title: 18th Annual NUDE — Manifest Gallery
calls.description: 18th edition of Manifest's annual themed exhibition on the uncovered human form, open to all media including photography. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional image. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium. $9,000 in Grand Jury Awards distributed across nine Season 22 exhibitions ($1,000 per show). Artists receive 70% on sales. Exhibition at Manifest Creative Research Gallery in Cincinnati, Ohio, August 14 – September 11, 2026. Open globally to all artists; original works only addressing the human form theme.
calls.summary: 18-year annual themed exhibition on the human form. Open to photography. $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Cincinnati.

calls.title: AOP Emerging Talent Award 2026
calls.description: AOP Project Award celebrating the new wave of photographers and image-makers who have been practicing professionally — full or part-time — for under three years. No subject restrictions: enter in three formats — Stills (a single image or a 2–5 image series), Moving Image (up to 7 minutes), or Innovation (creative use of AR, VR, CGI or other techniques). Open to AOP members and non-members alike, of any age or background. Judged by established professionals and industry representatives. calls.summary: AOP award for image-makers working professionally under 3 years. Gold prize: membership package, mentorship + £8,520 London billboard.

calls.title: AOP OPEN 2026
calls.description: 16th edition of the Association of Photographers' international open award. No categories, no themes — open to professional, emerging, and amateur photographers. Single image, series (2–5 images), and moving image entries accepted. Innovative work using AR, VR, CGI or other techniques is eligible if created by a person. Best in Show wins £1,250 plus a Fujifilm X Series kit (worth £1,500) and a 1-year Capture One Studio subscription. All images must have been created on or after 1 January 2024.
calls.summary: 16th AOP Open Award — no themes, no categories. Best in Show: £1,250 + Fujifilm kit + Fujifilm House of Photography exhibition.

calls.title: Making Strange
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on the theme of rendering the everyday unfamiliar. Looking for photographs that transform the ordinary through framing, timing, light, distance, or construction — work where the iconic, the ironic, and the overlooked are constructed through deliberate acts of seeing. Thirty images are selected for the in-person exhibition at Praxis Gallery, July 18 – August 8, 2026, with a Juror's Choice award, two Honorable Mentions, and a Directors Choice award (for the most cohesive series). Open internationally to all photographers.
calls.summary: Praxis Gallery (Minneapolis) juried photography exhibition on the everyday made strange. Up to 38 images selected, July–August 2026.

calls.title: Water ~ Sky
calls.description: Landscape photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring the relationship between water and sky as elemental forms in landscape practice. The call seeks work that engages surface and depth, presence and distance, observation and sensation — sea, river, ocean, puddle, sky, cloud, weather, motion, horizon. All approaches welcome from documentary to conceptual. Thirty images selected for in-person exhibition at Praxis Gallery, July 18 – August 8, 2026. Open internationally.
calls.summary: Praxis Gallery (Minneapolis) landscape photo exhibition on water and sky. Up to 74 images selected, July–August 2026.

calls.description: Second annual juried exhibition by The Image Flow (Mill Valley, CA) showcasing photographic artists in the extended San Francisco Bay Area. Open theme — all subject matter and media explorations eligible including digital, alternative processes, and analog. AI-generated images excluded. calls.title: RED Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition celebrating red commanding the frame — documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental styles welcome. 26 images selected for in-person exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, August 7–28, 2026. calls.summary: Dusk Gallery (Santa Fe) photography exhibition on red commanding the frame. Gallery covers printing & framing. 26 images selected.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery — a sister gallery to Decode Gallery in Tucson, both founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart. RED is the gallery's call for photography where red commands the frame: documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental approaches are equally welcome.

What's unusual is the production model. The gallery covers all professional printing on Luster paper, custom matting, and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing — artists submit only the high-resolution JPEG. Files: 500KB–5MB, longest side 4,500 pixels. Twenty-six images are selected.

Selection is by Holly Hart. The exhibition runs August 7–28, 2026 at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe. Prints are archived in the gallery's flat files for six months after the exhibition closes for ongoing promotion. The gallery operates on a 50/50 commission split for any sales; photographers retain all rights.

Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images ($40 or $45). The 2026 deadline is June 25; notifications are sent within two weeks.

calls.title: The Abstract Vision
calls.description: Virtual juried exhibition by SEC4P seeking non-representational photography — work that doesn't attempt to represent external reality but engages with shape, form, color, and texture. Source material may be nature, man-made, or figurative, but the resulting image must read as abstract. Black-and-white or color, analog, digital, and antique processes all welcome. Juror: Catherine Fairchild (Houston-based fine art photographer specializing in abstract work). 35–40 images selected for the virtual gallery; one-month online exhibition with social media promotion, archived slideshow, and video walkthrough. 0% commission — artists retain 100% of sale proceeds and copyrights. Open globally to photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level.
calls.summary: SEC4P virtual exhibition seeking non-representational photography — shape, form, color, texture. Juror: Catherine Fairchild. 0% commission.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) runs a year-round program of themed virtual juried exhibitions from its Greenville, South Carolina facility. "The Abstract Vision" is the gallery's open call for non-representational photography — work that doesn't attempt to depict external reality but engages with shape, form, color, and texture as its own subject.

The brief accepts source material from any direction: nature, man-made objects, or figurative scenes can all be starting points, provided the resulting image reads as abstract rather than descriptive. Black-and-white and color are both welcome, as are analog, digital, and antique processes.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Catherine Fairchild, a Houston-based fine art photographer whose own practice centers on abstract work — particularly photographs of paper in various forms. The juror's perspective sits within the call's frame: abstraction approached through close formal attention to material.

Selection takes 35 to 40 images for an approximately one-month virtual gallery, with social media promotion across SEC4P's channels and an archived online slideshow plus video walkthrough. There is no sales commission — artists retain 100% of proceeds and all copyrights.

Entry fees: $35 for non-members for up to 5 images ($6 each additional, max 15), or $28 / $5 for SEC4P members. Eligibility is open globally to photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. The 2026 submission deadline is July 15; the exhibition opens August 15, 2026.

calls.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 72: The Liminality of Time
calls.description: UK-based independent art zine seeking visual art (photography, painting, video, installation, collage, digital media) and writing (poetry, prose, essays) on the theme 'The Liminality of Time' — temporal thresholds where past, present, and future blur, overlap, or dissolve. Edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers. Free to submit, open globally, no monetary prize. Selected works published online and promoted through the zine's Instagram gallery (@haus_a_rest, 6k+ followers). Issue launches mid-June 2026. Instagram handle is required for submission.
calls.summary: UK indie art/lit zine, theme 'The Liminality of Time'. Photography accepted alongside other media. Free, publication only.
prose: Haus-a-rest is a UK-based independent art zine run by editors Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers. The publication's editorial line is bluntly stated: a space for the bold, curious, and uncompromising — work that resists the obvious. Each themed issue brings together visual art, photography, and writing from artists at any career stage, with emerging and underrepresented voices especially encouraged to apply.

Issue 72's theme is 'The Liminality of Time' — temporal thresholds where past, present, and future blur, overlap, or dissolve. The editors are looking for works that engage with temporal dislocation, memory, ritual, grief, and states of becoming. Photography sits alongside painting, video, installation, sound art, and writing in the issue.

Visual submissions require a single high-quality photograph of the work, a 300-word description connecting it to the theme, and the applicant's Instagram handle (mandatory). Writers may submit up to 1,000 words of prose or three poems with a 50-word synopsis. There is no submission or selection fee.

Selected works appear in the online issue (launching mid-June 2026) and are promoted across the zine's Instagram gallery, which has 6,000+ followers. The deadline is June 1, 2026. Submissions go through CuratorSpace.

calls.title: URBAN Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: 17th edition of the international urban photography contest paired with Trieste Photo Days festival. Categories include Single Photos (Streets, People, Spaces, Creative), Projects & Portfolios, and an Under-35 track (free). Single Photos: first image free, up to 3 images €20, each additional €10. Projects & Portfolios: €40 per project. Category winners receive Giorgio Celiberti trophies (~€1,500 value), exhibits at Trieste Photo Days (October 23–25, 2026), 2-night Trieste stay for two with gala dinner, and partner photography prizes. 2026 jury presidents: Mark Power (Magnum) chairs Projects & Portfolios; Christopher Morris (VII Photo Agency) chairs Single Photos.
calls.summary: Trieste Photo Days' 17th urban photo contest. Mark Power & Christopher Morris jury. Single image free; project €40. Festival exhibition.
prose: URBAN Photo Awards is the international photography competition paired with Trieste Photo Days, the Italian photography festival held each autumn. The 2026 edition is the contest's 17th, with winners exhibited at Trieste Photo Days from October 23 to 25, 2026, alongside the festival's main programming.

Submissions are accepted across three groups. Single Photos covers four thematic categories: Streets (the urban thoroughfare and its life), People (urban figures and portraiture), Spaces (the city as architectural and photographic subject), and Creative (images that challenge perceptions of the urban). Projects & Portfolios is for series-based work. A dedicated free track is open to photographers under 35.

Fees are tiered. For Single Photos, the first image is free, up to three images cost €20 (including the free one), and each additional image is €10. Projects & Portfolios costs €40 per project, with special categories at €50. The under-35 track is free to enter. Submissions are made through the official site.

The 2026 jury presidents are Mark Power, a Magnum Photos member chairing the Projects & Portfolios section, and Christopher Morris, a founding member of VII Photo Agency chairing the Single Photos section. They are joined by photography curators, editors, and journalists from international publications. Winners receive trophies and medals designed by Venice Biennale artist Giorgio Celiberti (valued around €1,500), photography prizes from partners, Amazon vouchers, a two-night stay for two in Trieste, and the URBAN 2026 gala dinner at Trieste Photo Days. The deadline is June 14, 2026.
jury: Mark Power, Magnum Photos (Projects & Portfolios chair)
Christopher Morris, VII Photo Agency (Single Photos chair)
Salwan Georges, Pulitzer Prize-winning visual journalist

calls.title: PLAYA Art/Sci Awarded Residency 2027
calls.description: Awarded residencies at PLAYA, a residency program in Lake County, Oregon, on traditional Klamath, Modoc, and Yahooskin Paiute lands. Photographers are welcome under the visual arts track. The 2027 cycle offers four jury-selected session options: January 21–February 15 (25 nights), February 18–March 1 (11 nights), July 15–August 2 (18 nights), and October 28–November 15 (18 nights). Residents receive free housing in 1- or 2-bedroom cabins with kitchens and bathrooms, studio/workspace access, and one shared group meal per week. No artist stipend; residents cover their own travel, meals beyond the group dinner, and materials. The program brings together artists and scientists across disciplines for cross-disciplinary exchange — selection criteria emphasize connection to science, especially related to Lake County's natural assets, and alignment with PLAYA's mission. Open globally to applicants 18+. Application fee $40 with full waivers available upon request. Decisions announced by October 1, 2026. Reference forms due July 19, 2026.
calls.summary: Jury-selected residency on high desert in Oregon. Free cabin housing, studio access, weekly group meal. Open globally.
prose: PLAYA is a residency program in Lake County, Oregon, set on traditional Klamath, Modoc, and Yahooskin Paiute lands in the high desert near Summer Lake. The program is structured around cross-disciplinary exchange between artists and scientists, framed around the natural landscape — selection criteria explicitly weigh an applicant's connection to science, especially as it relates to Lake County's natural assets, alongside the quality of their work.

The 2027 Awarded cycle offers four jury-selected session options: January 21 to February 15 (25 nights), February 18 to March 1 (11 nights), July 15 to August 2 (18 nights), and October 28 to November 15 (18 nights). Cohorts run 6 to 10 residents at a time, drawn from visual arts (including photography), literary arts, performing arts, new media, interdisciplinary practice, and science.

Residents receive free housing in 1- or 2-bedroom cabins with kitchens and bathrooms, studio/workspace access, and one shared group meal per week. There is no artist stipend, no travel stipend, and no materials stipend — residents cover their own travel, groceries beyond the weekly group dinner, and art supplies.

Applications run through SlideRoom and require 10 to 15 work samples (for visual artists), five short essay responses of roughly 250 words each, two professional references (forms due July 19, 2026), and a description of studio space needs. The application fee is $40, with full waivers available on request. The deadline is June 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT, with decisions announced by October 1, 2026.

calls.title: Innovate Grants - Spring $1,800 Grants
calls.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers. Eighteen honorable mentions also featured on the Innovate platform (nine in art, nine in photo). No artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation required.
calls.summary: Two $1,800 quarterly grants — one for a photographer, one for a visual artist. Eighteen honorable mentions.
prose: Innovate Artist Grants runs a recurring quarterly grant program for visual artists and photographers. Each cycle awards two $1,800 grants — one to a visual artist and one to a photographer. The Spring 2026 cycle is the second of four cycles in the year.

Eighteen honorable mentions are also featured on the Innovate platform alongside the two main grantees — nine in art and nine in photo. Winners and honorable mentions receive feature profiles, interview pages, and promotion on the Innovate Instagram account.

The application is deliberately minimal: name, email, grant category, 3 to 10 images of recent work, and the application fee. No artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation are required.

Eligibility is open globally to visual artists and photographers aged 18 or over; all media and genres are accepted. Submission is through Paperform. Fee is $35. The Spring 2026 deadline is June 18 at 11:59 PM PT.

calls.title: Commonwealth Youth Photography Competition 2026
calls.description: Annual free competition for young photographers aged 18–30 who are citizens or residents of a Commonwealth nation. calls.title: Exposure: Identity and the Evolving Image
calls.org: Global Village Museum of Arts and Cultures
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition at the Global Village Museum of Arts and Cultures in Fort Collins, Colorado, inviting photographers to explore identity through self-portraiture and photographic imagery — asking how we see ourselves and what it means to be seen. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide; work must have been created between 2016 and 2026. Selected works are exhibited and professionally printed at 16×20 inches. Exhibition runs October 2, 2026 – January 22, 2027.

calls.title: 2026 Honeywell Photography Competition
calls.description: Juried photography competition and exhibition at the Clark Gallery in the Honeywell Center, Wabash, Indiana. Open to U.S. residents of all ages — amateurs, professionals, and students — in three categories: Color, Black & White (including sepia), and Altered Images. Artwork must be original and completed within five years of the deadline, and ready to hang. Jurors are not announced in advance to protect the integrity of the show. Awards include Best of Show plus first, second, and third place in each category and ten honorable mentions. Exhibition August 18 – September 23, 2026.
calls.summary: Honeywell Center's juried photo competition in Wabash, Indiana. US residents, all ages. Cash prizes + gallery exhibition.

jury: Natalie Saprykina, Founder, White on White Gallery
calls.summary: Intl juried photo show at the Art Bias gallery, San Carlos CA. Four categories incl youth & film. Cash prizes per category.

calls.title: Queer|Art|Mentorship 2027
calls.description: Year-long mentorship pairing early-career LGBTQIA+ artists one-on-one with an established queer mentor in their field, across Film, Literature, Performance, and Visual Art (photography falls under Visual Art). The 10-month program (January–October 2027) includes a $2,500 stipend, travel funding for a spring retreat, one-on-one coaching from staff, professional networking outreach, and access to the Queer|Art alumni network. Open to self-identified queer, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, non-binary, and/or intersex artists based in the United States who are early-career with an existing body of work, not currently enrolled in school, and have a specific project to develop. Two-stage application: Part One via Google Form due June 15, 2026; invited applicants complete a detailed SlideRoom submission by July 31. Fellows selected by mentors in September; acceptances announced mid-October 2026.
calls.summary: Year-long mentorship pairing LGBTQ+ photographers and artists 1:1 with an established queer mentor. $2,500 stipend, US-based, free.

Apply by emailing written responses on practice, motivation, impact, documentation and sustainable travel plans (max 300 words each), completing the linked Google Form, and submitting a single PDF with 6 images of recent work. Cars are not permitted on the island; environmental sustainability is a selection consideration.
calls.summary: Week-long off-grid residency at Sweeney's Bothy on the Isle of Eigg. Accommodation, £720 artist fee and £250 travel. VAS members.

calls.title: Fidra Fine Art Professional Members Exhibition
calls.description: Collaborative sales exhibition between Visual Arts Scotland and Fidra Fine Art, a contemporary gallery in Gullane, East Lothian, running October 17 – November 29, 2026. All mediums welcome. Selected artists show up to two works; a £15 hang fee is payable to VAS on selection and the gallery takes 40% commission on sales. Applicants must be VAS professional members for the duration of the exhibition. Apply by emailing a PDF with images of 6 works (titles, mediums, sizes, prices), a 200-word artist statement and CV, plus the accompanying Google Form.

calls.title: Larnaca Biennale 2027 Open Call
calls.description: Fifth edition of the Larnaca Biennale in Cyprus, October 13 – November 26, 2027, under the theme Metatopies: Geographies in Motion — place as an event in constant transformation, shaped by geological, anthropological, social, political and historical shifts. Curated by Niki Papaspirou and Marios Fournaris. Open worldwide to artists, photographers, designers and art students 18+, individually or in groups; material, technique and medium are open. Thirteen awards at the opening ceremony, including the Grand Prix, three awards of excellence and six awards of distinction. €50 fee per proposal for individuals (€75 for duos, €100 for groups of 3–5); submit up to three images per work with an optional 200-word statement.

calls.title: PRC Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: The Photographic Resource Center's Artist-in-Residence program gives two artists working in photography and lens-based media four weeks of dedicated studio space inside the PRC gallery, October 21 – November 22, 2026. Each resident gets exclusive use of half the gallery (about 400 sq ft), access to the darkroom, alternative process lab, and digital lab at Lesley University, a $500 stipend, weekly feedback meetings with the PRC Executive Director, and the opportunity to lead one public program. The residency culminates in a dual exhibition November 14–23 with a shared opening reception, artist talks, and professional documentation. Non-live-in: artists arrange their own housing, and there is no location requirement; collaborators may apply to share one slot. Fee $30 ($20 for PRC members).

calls.title: Jentel Artist Residency — Winter/Spring 2027
calls.description: Residency at Jentel, a working cattle ranch 20 miles southeast of Sheridan in Banner, Wyoming, for the Winter/Spring session running January 15 – May 7, 2027. Residents receive private accommodation, a separate individual studio, and a $300 stipend distributed in weekly increments to offset living expenses. Open to visual artists in all media — photography included — plus writers and composers. Applicants must be US residents (citizenship not required) aged 25 or over; full-time students are not eligible, and Wyoming residents have a streamlined application. Applications close September 15 at 12:00 noon MST.
jury: Rotating panel of visual art, literary and music professionals

calls.title: Künstler*dorf Schöppingen Fellowship 2027
calls.description: Residency fellowships at the Künstler*dorf (artists' village) in Schöppingen, Münsterland, Germany. Applications for the 2027 fellowships are open June 27 – August 31, 2026. Fellows live and work on site for two to six months, arranged by agreement and availability. Individual fellows receive €1,500 per month (minus roughly €100–200 for rent and operating costs); collectives — accepted since 2023 — receive €1,000 per person up to €3,000 total. Open worldwide to professional visual artists, authors, and composers with no restrictions on nationality or age. Juries assess the quality of previous work, the feasibility of the proposed project in Schöppingen, and contributions to the residency community. Not a production fellowship: there are no presentation obligations, though fellows may use the exhibition spaces.

calls.title: OD Photo Prize 2026

Open-themed and international — from documentary and street photography to collage, mixed media, and experimental lens-based work; collectives and duos welcome. At least 20 shortlisted artists join a group exhibition in London in November–December 2026 (venue TBC), with works produced by the gallery and sold on a profit-share basis. Additional awards include Judges' Picks, the InCadaqués Award — a solo presentation at the festival in Spain — and the AJ Page People's Choice Award.

calls.description: Third edition of the underwater imaging competition run by DivePhotoGuide, Underwater Australasia, and UW Images. Nine categories — Sydney, Conservation, Australian, International Waters, Tough TG, Portfolio, Smartphone/Action Cam, the new Only Water, and a Reels video showcase — with around AU$70,000 in prizes spanning dive resort packages, underwater imaging equipment, and a photography drone. Open worldwide; images must be shot in the Australasian region, with exceptions for the International Waters and select categories. Winners are announced at the Go Diving Show ANZ in Sydney in September 2026, where finalist images are displayed as metal prints; honours include a Scuba Diver magazine cover story and publication in the 2027 Australian Marine Conservation Society calendar. Proceeds support environmental partners.
calls.summary: Underwater imaging competition with ~AU$70,000 in prizes across 9 categories, for images shot in Australasia. Winners shown at Go Diving Show ANZ, Sydney.

calls.title: ADEX Dugong Photo of the Year 2027
calls.description: Conservation photography campaign from Asia Dive Expo (ADEX) and Asian Geographic spotlighting dugongs and their threatened seagrass habitats. Submit your best images of dugongs in the wild or the underwater and coastal environments linked to them, each with a short story of 80–150 words; entrants also post their submission on Instagram with @AsiaDiveExpo added as collaborator. Free to enter. The grand prize winner is hosted at ADEX 2027 in Singapore with accommodation covered, receives a feature showcase, and is presented at the Blue Legacy Awards on April 11, 2027; shortlisted photographers are exhibited at ADEX 2027, featured online, and receive digital recognition. Public voting begins January 11, 2027.
calls.summary: Free dugong-conservation photo campaign. Winner hosted at ADEX 2027 Singapore; shortlist exhibited at the expo.

calls.title: 2027 Solo and Group Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: The Rehoboth Art League's Exhibitions Committee invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in its 2027 gallery season at the League's campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach, Delaware. Open to members and non-members working in any media, including photography; artists who exhibited at RAL in 2024, 2025, or 2026 are not eligible. Solo applicants submit 5 works and groups 10, created no earlier than 2024, with an artist statement and CV. A limited number of proposals are accepted each year; selected artists are notified by August 31, 2026, and receive 65% of sales.
calls.summary: Propose a 2027 solo or group show at Rehoboth Art League, Delaware. Any media including photography; 5–10 works.

Open internationally to all photographers; visitors can view and purchase photographs through the feature page (50% commission).

calls.title: Mini Maxi Print 2026
calls.description: Open call for professional graphic artists worldwide from Galleri Heike Arndt DK's Berlin space in Friedrichshain, for an exhibition of small and large-format print editions opening October/November 2026. Eligible techniques are editioned printmaking — lithograph, screen print, woodcut, etching, drypoint, linocut, photogravure and similar — in editions of at least 3; monoprints, inkjet and digital prints, and photo-based images without a physically worked plate are excluded. Submit 3–6 prints per section. Free to apply; selected artists pay a €40 exhibition fee plus shipping both ways, and works must remain available for the exhibition period plus 12 months. The gallery produces flyers and a poster featuring each artist.
calls.summary: Print-edition open call at Heike Arndt DK Berlin — etching to photogravure. Free entry, €40 if selected; show opens Oct/Nov.

calls.title: Images of the Shrub-Steppe 2026
calls.description: Annual juried exhibit presented by Boxx Gallery and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy celebrating the shrub-steppe lands of Central Washington — the tenth Conservancy show at the Tieton gallery. Work in any medium made within the past five years and inspired by the shrub-steppe landscape is eligible, as long as it hasn't appeared in a previous edition; there are no location restrictions on entrants, but all work must be delivered to and picked up from the Tieton gallery. Accepted work may be shipped to arrive by August 27 or hand-delivered September 1, and must be for sale (35% gallery commission). Juried by photographer and 2022 Guggenheim Fellow Nancy Floyd. On view September 5–27, 2026, with Juror's, People's Choice, and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy awards of $100 each.
calls.summary: Any-medium juried show on Central Washington's shrub-steppe at Boxx Gallery, Tieton. Juror Nancy Floyd; on view Sep 2026.

calls.title: FL3TCH3R Exhibit 2026 — Socially & Politically Engaged Art
calls.description: Thirteenth annual international juried exhibition of socially and politically engaged art, founded in memory of designer Fletcher H. Dyer and newly at home at Fischman Gallery in downtown Johnson City, Tennessee. All 2D, 3D, video, sound, and performance documentation is eligible, with photography as its own category; open worldwide to artists 18+. Juried by Jessica “JB” Burke of UNC Charlotte, with Best of Show, two Awards of Excellence, and a slate of named awards presented at the September 4 reception. On view August 7 – September 27, 2026; late entries accepted June 24–30 at a $45 fee.
calls.summary: 13th international juried show of socially & politically engaged art at Fischman Gallery, TN. Juror Jessica “JB” Burke.
jury: Jessica “JB” Burke, Associate Professor of Art, University of North Carolina Charlotte
