calls.description: Eighty-second edition of the Swope Art Museum's annual juried exhibition in downtown Terre Haute, running since 1944. Open to current or former residents of Indiana, Illinois, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee with original work in any medium completed 2024–2026 and not previously shown at the Swope. Juried by Mark Pascale, curator in the Department of Prints and Drawings at the Art Institute of Chicago. More than $10,000 in awards, from $100 Awards of Recognition to the Grand Prize, announced at the October 2 opening reception. On view October 2, 2026 – January 10, 2027.
calls.summary: Swope Art Museum's 82-year-old juried annual for six-state region artists; $10,000+ in awards, juror Mark Pascale.
jury: Mark Pascale, Curator, Art Institute of Chicago

calls.title: Baltic Open Submission 2026
calls.description: BALTIC's all-comers exhibition returns for its third edition, with up to 100 works selected for a major group show at the Gateshead gallery from September 19, 2026 to May 2027. Open to anyone based in North East England — professional, self-taught, or hobbyist, individuals and collectives alike, working in any medium, with no exhibiting experience required. One work per artist, submitted as images via Submittable by 10am on June 16. Selection panel includes artists Laura Lancaster and Rachel Lancaster; selected artists notified August 6 and announced publicly August 20.
calls.summary: Free open submission for North East England artists; up to 100 works shown at BALTIC Gateshead, Sep 2026 – May 2027.

calls.title: The Shadow Aspect
calls.description: Open-theme exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis examining shadow as pure visual form and as psychological and cultural symbol — from formal studies of cast light to conceptual and metaphoric readings of the shadow self. All genres and processes welcome, traditional and non-traditional, analog and digital. Juried by Ann Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art. Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry into three future calls), Directors' Choice, and eight honorable mentions shown in the exhibition and online gallery. Images exhibited at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Exhibition August 22 – September 12, 2026; Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5.
jury: Ann Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art
calls.summary: Praxis Gallery (Minneapolis) explores shadow as form, symbol, and psyche. Juried by Ann Jastrab; exhibition Aug–Sep 2026.

calls.title: Photo-Solo Exhibition Proposals — Season 23
calls.description: Manifest Gallery invites proposals for photography-related solo exhibitions to be held during its Season 23 opening period, September 25 – October 23, 2026, as part of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial. Open to all artists working in photo-based media, including experimental and mixed-media approaches. Submit a proposal form, up to 12 images, and a resume; extended deadline June 21, 2026. Solo exhibitors receive a $100 honorarium, a free copy of the season publication, and automatic entry into the $1,000 Grand Jury Award pool; gallery commission on sales is 30%. A parallel all-media call for solo proposals across the full 2026–27 season shares the same deadline. Notifications by early August.
calls.summary: Propose a photography solo show at Manifest (Cincinnati) for the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial period. $100 honorarium.

calls.title: 21c Artadia Award 2026 — Northwest Arkansas
calls.description: Sixth annual partnership award between Artadia and 21c Museum Hotels, providing $15,000 in unrestricted funds to one visual artist. The 2026 edition goes to Northwest Arkansas: applicants must be living and working in Bentonville or Washington Counties, Arkansas, and describe themselves as being at a pivotal moment in their career. The open call is free to apply and runs June 15 – July 15, 2026 via Submittable. Like all Artadia awards, funds are unrestricted — artists use them however they choose.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $15,000 for one visual artist in Bentonville/Washington Counties, AR — Artadia × 21c Museum Hotels. Free.

calls.title: Southwest Artist
calls.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating the spirit of the American Southwest — desert landscapes, indigenous cultures, borderlands, urban environments, and the region's singular light across Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Colorado, Utah, Nevada, and California. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images. The gallery covers professional printing on Luster paper, matting, and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px longest side). Exhibition September 4–25, 2026 with opening reception; post-exhibition sales split 50/50. $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Dusk Gallery (Santa Fe) show on the American Southwest. Pro printing and framing covered; exhibition Sep 2026.

calls.title: Wild
calls.description: Global online exhibit celebrating the natural world — wildlife, landscape, conservation, macro, documentary, fine art, aerial, and experimental nature photography all welcome. Open internationally to photographers of all experience levels. Entrants must demonstrate ethical photographic practice and respect for the well-being of animals and their habitats. Cash prizes of $500, $350, and $150. $20 for the first image plus media fees for additional entries; no AI-generated imagery. Acceptance notifications by August 19, 2026.
calls.summary: Photo Artfolio's nature cycle — wildlife to experimental. $1,000 in cash prizes across three awards; online exhibit; no AI.

calls.title: POOLSIDE 2026
calls.description: Swimming pools as subject matter — Key West's Jag Gallery invites work in any medium, including photography, that dives into pool culture, pool light, and poolside life. Open internationally to artists 18+; up to 5 entries, maximum 40 inches in any dimension, no AI-generated work. Exhibition August 5–30, 2026 at the gallery with an opening reception August 8 and a simultaneous online gallery. Judge's Choice, three honorable mentions, and People's Choice awards; winners are invited to a dedicated 2027 group show. Sales split 50/50.
calls.summary: Key West's Jag Gallery wants pools — any medium incl. photography. Show Aug 2026 with reception; winners get a 2027 group show.

Exhibition October 2026 at The Peale; works are available for purchase with artists receiving 60% of the sale price. $25 entry plus $10 media fee.

calls.title: Zion National Park Artist-in-Residence 2027
calls.description: Four-week residency living in the historic Grotto House in the main canyon of Zion National Park, Utah, run by the National Park Service with the Zion Forever Project. Three sessions are available across 2027. Includes rent-free furnished housing, waived park entrance fees, and a $500 stipend on completion of residency requirements. Open to artists 18+ in all mediums and skill levels; residents present two public programs, spend about 20 hours weekly on public engagement, and donate an original artwork to the park. Travel, meals, and supplies are self-funded; international applicants are not currently accepted.

jury: Zion Forever Project, NPS staff & Zion Arts and Humanities Council

calls.title: 2027 Grand Canyon Artist in Residence
calls.description: Four- to eight-week residency on the South Rim of Grand Canyon National Park, run by Grand Canyon Conservancy. Three artists are selected annually and receive an $800 weekly stipend, $500 travel subsidy, up to $300 for project supplies, free accommodation, special park access, and staff support, in exchange for roughly two public interactions per week. Open internationally to artists 18+ who are legally able to work in the US; priority for underrepresented perspectives and well-researched, Grand Canyon–specific projects. The application fee is waived for Indigenous artists from the canyon's 11 associated Tribal Nations.
calls.summary: 4–8 week South Rim residency with $800/week stipend, housing, and travel subsidy. Three artists chosen for 2027.

calls.title: Villa Barr Art Park Artist in Residency 2027
calls.description: Three-month residencies (Spring, Summer, or Fall 2027) at Villa Barr Art Park, a four-acre former sculptor's estate run by the City of Novi, Michigan. Each session hosts a Visiting Artist living in the four-bedroom house plus a Local Artist with studio access; private and shared studios include woodworking and metalworking tools. All residents receive a $500 materials stipend, and Visiting Artists an additional $500 travel stipend. Open internationally to artists 18+; strong proposals engage the public through workshops, exhibitions, or installations responding to the grounds.
calls.summary: Three-month live-in residency at a Michigan art park with house, studios, and $500 stipends. Open internationally.

calls.title: Max Thelen Studio Residency
calls.description: Twelve-month free studio residency (September 2026 – August 2027) at Art Works Downtown in San Rafael, California, for an emerging visual artist with a committed early-to-mid-stage practice. Covers a 92 sq ft street-level studio with utilities, plus a solo exhibition, waived membership fees, social media promotion, and scholarship funding for Marin Open Studios participation. Applicants should live within commuting distance of San Rafael and work regularly in the studio.
calls.summary: Free 12-month studio plus solo show at Art Works Downtown, San Rafael, for an emerging Bay Area visual artist.

calls.title: Hard Water, Soft Stone
calls.description: September group exhibition at Duplex AIR, an artist-run studio, residency, and gallery space in Lisbon. The theme riffs on the Portuguese proverb about soft water breaking hard stone, inviting work on mutability, persistence, and slow transformation — misreadings and reinterpretations welcome. All mediums accepted; up to 4 completed works per artist, open internationally. Selected artists receive professional exhibition photography, a curatorial text, and installation support; 25% commission on sales, and the fee helps keep Duplex's studio rents below market for local artists. Exhibition September 16–23, 2026.
calls.summary: Lisbon artist-run space Duplex seeks work on mutability and slow transformation for its September group show.

calls.title: FineArt Igualada 2027 — Open Call
calls.description: Open call to select the exhibition projects for the 15th edition of FineArt Igualada, the Catalan photography festival that turns the city near Barcelona into a large space dedicated to photography each spring. Photographers, collectives, and visual artists worldwide can propose a photographic project with a singular gaze — work that moves, provokes reflection, and opens new conversations through the image. Proposals are submitted by email; the festival runs February 19 – March 14, 2027 across venues in Igualada.
calls.summary: Propose an exhibition project for the 15th FineArt Igualada photography festival (Feb–Mar 2027, Catalonia).

calls.title: Skyway 2027: A Contemporary Collaboration
calls.description: Triennial exhibition centering artists shaping contemporary art in the Tampa Bay region, co-organized by five museums: the Museum of Fine Arts St. Petersburg, The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art, Sarasota Art Museum of Ringling College, Tampa Museum of Art, and USF Contemporary Art Museum. Open to artists and collectives working in all media — photography included — who live in Hillsborough, Manatee, Pasco, Pinellas, or Sarasota counties. Selected artists exhibit at one of the five venues between March and fall 2027 and are featured in a full-color catalog with curatorial essays. Free to apply with up to 10 images (plus optional video).
jury: Lacie Barbour, Associate Curator, Sarasota Art Museum
Noah Cox, Assistant Curator, MFA St. Petersburg
Christopher Jones, Curator of Photography and Media Art, The Ringling
Joanna Robotham, Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, Tampa Museum of Art
Christian Viveros-Fauné, Curator-at-Large, USF Contemporary Art Museum
Ola Wlusek, Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, The Ringling

calls.title: Fashion Regenerated 2026
calls.description: Photography and filmmaking competition from Textile Exchange, the global nonprofit driving sustainable fiber and material production, in partnership with Atmos. Visual storytellers are invited to document regeneration across the fashion, textile, and apparel industry — from fiber cultivation to circular design. The overall winner receives a $10,000 paid commission to create new work documenting regeneration, publication through Atmos and Textile Exchange, and an exhibition at the 2026 Textile Exchange Conference; two runners-up receive $2,000 each plus promotion and conference display. Open to photographers and filmmakers 18+ of any nationality; winners must be available to travel autumn 2026 – summer 2027 for the commission. Submit up to 25 photographs, a short film, or both.

One original work per artist, not previously exhibited. Open to US residents 18+; winners announced October 2026.

calls.title: EPF 2026 Photobook Exhibition
calls.description: Open call for a dedicated photobook exhibition at the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo (October 17–27), following the 118-title showcase Ephemere staged during KG+ in Kyoto. Seeking complete, bound photobooks — self-published or publisher-released, A4 or smaller — with bold visual narratives, intentional sequencing, and strong physical presence; theme is open. Two-phase system: the initial digital review is free (submit a PDF, flip-through video, or sequenced JPEGs of the book), then artists selected in July pay a $25 exhibition fee and ship one copy to Japan. Exhibited books are not returned — they join Ephemere's permanent traveling photo library and may be shown again at future international pop-ups.
calls.summary: Bound photobooks for a dedicated exhibition at Ephemere Photo Fest in Tokyo — free digital review; selected books join the archive.

calls.title: Dek Unu Magazine — September 2026 Issue
calls.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the September issue runs July 1–20, 2026; email submissions.
calls.summary: Not-for-profit journal publishing one artist per issue in print and online. September issue window July 1–20. Free, email entry.

calls.title: Dek Unu Magazine — Tuŝis: Altered States (Annual Contest 2026)
calls.description: Dek Unu Magazine's annual juried contest for adventurous, hand-made, light-and-lens-based fine art photography — photo-montage, alternative processes, hybrids, and experimental departures. Photo-hybrids that combine digital painting, original photography, and AI components are welcome as long as the work stays light-and-lens based; exclusively algorithmic or machine-made images are excluded. The jurors' top selection wins $250; all other winners have their entry fees refunded. Winners are published in the August 2026 paperback and e-reader edition of Dek Unu Magazine, showcased online for 31 days with promotion, and given a permanent permalinked catalog page. Submit 5 images. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Dek Unu's annual contest for experimental, alt-process, light-and-lens photography. $250 top prize plus August magazine publication.
prose: Dek Unu Magazine is a small not-for-profit fine-art photography journal that runs monthly single-artist issues and one annual juried contest. Tuŝis: Altered States is the 2026 annual contest, themed around adventurous, manipulated, and hand-made photography.

The brief embraces photo-montage, alternative processes, hybrids, and experimental departures that show the diversity and power of light-and-lens-based fine art photography. Photo-hybrids that combine digital painting, original photography, and AI components are eligible as long as the work remains light-and-lens based; exclusively algorithmic or machine-made images are not accepted.

The jurors' top selection receives a $250 cash award, and all other winners have their entry fees refunded. Winners are published in the August 2026 paperback and e-reader edition of Dek Unu Magazine, showcased online for 31 days with three promotional posts to the magazine's network, and given a permanent permalinked catalog page useful for résumés and grant applications.

Entry fee is $35 for a submission of 5 images (300ppi, 20cm on the longer side). Submissions are made by email to dekunuarts@gmail.com with a short bio, project notes, and payment details. Open worldwide; the 2026 deadline is July 15.

calls.title: Photo Folio Review 2026
calls.description: Official portfolio review programme of Les Rencontres d'Arles, held July 6–10, 2026 during the festival's opening week at the Maison de la vie associative. One-on-one 20-minute sessions with international experts — curators, editors, publishers, and festival directors. Packages run from 5 appointments (€200) to 20 (€550). Each year the experts vote for their favorite portfolio and select a Photo Folio Review Award winner, whose work is presented at the following edition — the 2024 winner Patrick Wack exhibited at Arles 2025. Online reservations only, open until midnight June 18 (Paris time), subject to availability.
calls.summary: One-on-one reviews with international experts at Arles, July 6–10. Experts vote an annual award winner. Register by June 18.

calls.title: TOKAS Research Residency Program 2027
calls.description: Research-focused residency at Tokyo Arts and Space for international and local creators — visual artists (photographers welcome), designers, architects, curators, critics, and writers. Five places for 6–12 week stays within one of three periods between May 2027 and March 2028, for conducting research on arts and culture in Tokyo. TOKAS provides a single-room living space at TOKAS Residency in Koto-ku; no studio or workspace is included. No age limit; applicants must not be students at the time of participation; duos may apply. Application package PDF plus online form with two letters of recommendation and a portfolio. Deadline June 16, 2026, 18:00 JST.
calls.summary: Five 6–12 week research residencies in Tokyo between May 2027 and March 2028. Accommodation provided, free to apply.

calls.title: agriCultural: A Biennial Exhibition
calls.description: Juried biennial presented by the Southeastern Massachusetts Agricultural Partnership (SEMAP) and the New Bedford Art Museum, investigating the complex and undertold stories of agriculture, farming, and the contemporary stories held in the land. Seeks work from artists who are farmers, farmers who are artists, and artists deeply engaged with agricultural themes — 2D and 3D media welcome, including photography. Open to artists residing in Massachusetts or Rhode Island. On view September 10 – November 29, 2026 at the New Bedford Art Museum.
jury: Suzanne de Vegh, Executive Director, New Bedford Art Museum
calls.summary: Juried biennial on agriculture and the land at New Bedford Art Museum, Sep–Nov 2026. MA/RI artists, $25 for up to 3 works.

calls.title: Space: Negative, Outer, Living
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut inviting artists to explore the many meanings of space — physical, emotional, imagined, and infinite. From the vast mystery of outer space to the quiet structure of negative space in composition and the personal environments we inhabit every day: distance, atmosphere, architecture, isolation, balance, discovery, and the relationships between objects and the spaces around them. All media and artistic perspectives welcome, including photography; open to artists 18+. Entry $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising per additional piece up to five. Shown in the Marmer Gallery, August 8 – September 12, 2026.
jury: Andrae Green, Assistant Professor of Painting and Drawing, University of Hartford
calls.summary: Themed juried show on negative, outer, and living space at Arts Center East, CT. All media, from $35. On view Aug 8 – Sep 12, 2026.

calls.title: Vision 250: America in Harmony
calls.description: WHAM Art Center in Surprise, Arizona invites artists to celebrate America's 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence with a special exhibition exploring freedom, harmony, and vision. In a time of division and polarization, the show asks: what would a unified, creative, and harmonious America look like — an America where differences are met with curiosity and connection? All media welcome, including photography; the show will highlight artwork by veterans. Entry $40 for up to five entries (a related series counts as one); exhibition runs July 2–30, 2026.
calls.summary: Themed show for America's 250th at WHAM Art Center, AZ — imagining a unified, harmonious America. $40 for 5 entries, Jul 2–30.

calls.title: Pop Art Exhibition
calls.description: Sparks Gallery in San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter is hosting a Pop Art exhibition showcasing bold, contemporary works inspired by popular culture and modern life. Submissions should reflect Pop Art's playful, colorful, or critical style, exploring themes like consumerism, celebrity culture, comics, and nostalgia — both traditional and innovative approaches welcome, including photography. Open to U.S.-based artists; work must be original and for sale. $20 entry plus $10 per additional media.
calls.summary: Pop-culture-inspired works at Sparks Gallery, San Diego. US artists, original work for sale, from $20. Deadline June 15.

calls.title: Artist in Focus
calls.description: Open call from Fotografiska Emerging and Fotografiska Berlin inspired by Anton Corbijn, running alongside the Berlin museum's Corbijn retrospective. Submit a cover-worthy portrait of an artist or creative voice whose character shines through in a single frame — portraits that go beyond appearance and reveal something honest and memorable about the subject. Lens-based photography only; AI-generated images excluded. One image per submission, up to three submissions per photographer. Three selected artists each receive a signed copy of the 'Corbijn, Anton' photobook, Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3 headphones, and Instagram features on the Fotografiska Berlin and Emerging accounts.
calls.summary: Corbijn-inspired call for a single cover-worthy portrait of a creative voice. Free; three winners get books, headphones, features.

calls.title: Vehicles & Voyages
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the many ways we move through the world — cars, trucks, bicycles, motorcycles, boats, trains, aircraft, and the journeys they make possible. Historic vehicles, scenes of travel, personal road trips, maritime exploration, or imagined voyages into the future: movement, connection, freedom, and discovery. All media and artistic styles welcome, including photography; open to artists 18+. Entry $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), $5 each additional piece up to five. Shown August 8 – September 12, 2026, with reception and awards August 22.
calls.summary: Transportation-themed juried show at Arts Center East, CT — vehicles and journeys in all media. From $35, Aug 8 – Sep 12.

calls.title: Dog Days of Summer
calls.description: WHAM Art Center in Surprise, Arizona invites artists to respond to the hottest, stillest stretch of the season — the dog days, named for the rise of Sirius, the Dog Star, at the peak of summer heat. Sought: work that captures what summer at its peak feels like — heat, stillness, nostalgia, exhaustion, memory, and atmosphere — through color, landscape, abstraction, or personal storytelling. All media welcome, including photography; works may be literal, abstract, symbolic, or conceptual. Entry $40 for up to five entries (a related series counts as one); all work must be for sale, 25% gallery commission. Exhibition runs August 4–29, 2026.
calls.summary: Summer-at-its-peak themed show at WHAM Art Center, AZ — heat, stillness, nostalgia in any medium. $40 for 5 entries, Aug 4–29.

calls.title: TSHOW.2
calls.description: Second edition of TSHOW, the international juried exhibition from Texas nonprofit Tyler Art Lift. Open to painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking and photography up to 80×80 inches — a chance for photographers to show alongside other media with serious cash on the line: $3,000 Best in Show, $1,500 runner-up and a $500 People's Choice award chosen by visitors. Exhibition at Gallery Main Street in downtown Tyler, Texas, September 23 – October 10, 2026, with opening reception October 3. Open internationally to artists 18+; $45 for the first entry, $5 each additional; 30% sales commission supports the show.
jury: Caleb Bell, Executive Director, Tyler Museum of Art
calls.summary: Tyler Art Lift's international all-media juried show, photography welcome. $5,000 in cash prizes at Gallery Main Street, TX.

calls.title: Chew on This
calls.org: Ludington Area Center for the Arts
calls.description: Food-themed juried exhibition at the Ludington Area Center for the Arts on the Lake Michigan shore, inviting artists to explore the creative, cultural and visual power of food — from realistic depictions to conceptual pieces about consumption and community. calls.title: The Keller Prize 2026
calls.description: Annual international all-media art competition founded in 2022 by artist Shelly Hamill in honor of her grandmother, Texas landscape painter Jane Keller. Open to painting, photography, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, textile art, installation and mixed media; juried in 2026 by Aspen gallerist Mia Valley of Valley Fine Art. Cash prizes of $5,000 grand prize, $2,500 first runner-up and $1,500 second runner-up; past grand prize winners include painter Andrea Kowch (2025). All submissions are featured in the online gallery across the website, Instagram and Facebook. Open internationally to artists 18+; $55 for five images, $7 each additional up to 15. The organiser reserves the right to modify, postpone or cancel the competition if fewer than 300 eligible paid submissions are received by the deadline, in which case refunds are limited to the entry fee less non-refundable CaFÉ and payment-processor charges; the advertised awards are stated to be contingent on sufficient participation. Winners are announced in November 2026.

calls.title: The Essence of a Woman 2026
calls.description: National all-media call from MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, exploring the essence of a woman — her physical, psychological, and spiritual characteristics, from a simple portrait in tranquil repose to complex images of women performing personal and professional roles. Environmental portraits showing an individual in her surroundings are welcome. Photography is explicitly included alongside painting, printmaking, digital, sculpture, and more. Exhibition at MVA Gallery October 10 – November 7, 2026. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award carrying a future exhibition, and an annual Grand Prize NYC exhibition opportunity. $35 for 3 images, $5 each additional up to 9. Open to US artists 18+.
calls.summary: All-media national call on the essence of a woman — portraits of strength and vulnerability. Gallery show in Bethlehem, PA.
prose: MVA Gallery — Modern Visual Arts — is a gallery at 35 E. Elizabeth Avenue in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, showing painting, printmaking, photography, sculpture, and more. The Essence of a Woman is its national themed exhibition for fall 2026.

The brief asks artists to explore in art the essence of a woman — her physical, psychological, and spiritual characteristics. That can mean a simple portrait of a woman in tranquil repose or a complex image of her actively performing personal and professional roles; she can reveal vulnerability or strength. Environmental portraits showing an individual in her surroundings are explicitly welcomed.
Accepted media span painting, watercolor, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, sculpture, fiber, drawing, and photography.

The exhibition runs October 10 through November 7, 2026 at the gallery. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award carrying a special future exhibition, an annual Grand Prize with a New York City exhibition opportunity, and an honorable mention granting a free future submission. Selection is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, reviewers, publishers, and academics.

Entry is $35 for 3 images, $5 each additional up to 9 total. Open to current US residents aged 18 and over. Submission is via CaFE. The deadline is June 14, 2026 at 11:59 PM MDT; notifications go out on or about August 17, and accepted work is due at the gallery by October 6.

calls.title: Cyanotype: A Celebration of Process and Possibility
calls.description: Juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont celebrating cyanotype in any form — traditional contact prints, camera-made cyanotypes, photograms, digital negatives, toned and wet cyanotypes, mixed media and experimental approaches, as long as cyanotype is the primary component of the finished work. Juried by Sam Wang. Up to 35 images selected for the gallery exhibition and 40 more for the online gallery; all selected work appears in the exhibition catalog and remains on the gallery website. Exhibition September 4–26, 2026, closing with World Cyanotype Day workshops and artist talks on September 26. Prints due August 21.
jury: Sam Wang, Alumni Distinguished Professor, Clemson University
calls.summary: Cyanotype in all its forms — contact prints, photograms, toned and experimental — juried by Sam Wang for a Vermont gallery show.

calls.title: World Nature Photography Awards 2027
calls.description: The seventh edition of the World Nature Photography Awards (WNPA), an international nature and wildlife photography competition. Fourteen categories spanning Animals in their habitat, Animal portraits, behaviour categories (Bird, Mammal, Amphibian/Reptile, Invertebrate), Plants and fungi, Urban wildlife, Landscapes, Underwater, Black and white, Nature art, Photojournalism and People and nature. Gold, silver and bronze winners in every category; the top-scoring gold image wins the World Nature Photographer of the Year title plus $1,000. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide aged 18+; images of captive or restrained animals are not permitted. Standard entry is £30 for up to six images, with no limit on the number of entries. Submissions accepted online only as JPEGs (1,000–3,000px, under 3MB). Deadline midnight GMT, 30 June 2026.
calls.summary: 7th edition international nature & wildlife awards — 14 categories, $1,000 + Photographer of the Year title. £30 for 6 images, worldwide 18+. Deadline Jun 30.

calls.title: Grand Prix de la Photographie Paris Match 2026
calls.description: For the Bicentenary of Photography, Paris Match launches its first national photography Grand Prix on the theme 'Un regard sur notre époque' (A Look at Our Time). Open to everyone across France, amateurs and enthusiasts alike, it invites photographers to capture contemporary France in all its diversity and contradictions. Entrants submit a series of four original photographs across thematic categories — among them creativity, daring, family and transmission, each backed by a partner (Google France, Bpifrance, VistaPrint, CCF | KOREGE). A jury selects the finalists, revealed in autumn 2026, with an exhibition and awards ceremony on 16 December 2026. Each grand-public category winner receives a prize from Paris Match and its partners plus featured visibility to the magazine's readers. Submissions run 11 June – 19 July 2026.
jury: Jérôme Huffer, Photo Editor-in-Chief, Paris Match
Tania Lucio, Deputy Photo Editor, Paris Match
Stéphane Albouy, Editorial Director, Paris Match
calls.summary: Paris Match's first national photo Grand Prix for the Bicentenary of Photography — submit a 4-image series capturing contemporary France.

calls.title: Eurazeo Photo Prize 2026
calls.description: Eurazeo, a leading European private asset manager, relaunches its long-running photography patronage as the Eurazeo Photo Prize — now a project-development grant anchored in the company's Endowment Fund. Open to professional photographers of all nationalities, based in France or abroad, it invites applicants to submit a project for development; the laureate has six months to create a body of work on the theme 'Stories of Europe', in partnership with the Rencontres d'Arles. Each year one laureate receives a €20,000 grant to deliver an ambitious long-term body of work, plus dedicated artistic and strategic guidance and connections with galleries, festivals, media and leading industry professionals. Building on the Eurazeo Photo Prize that ran annually from 2010 to 2025, the new grant supports creation earlier in the process. Marking the bicentenary of photography, applications are open 26 May – 13 September 2026; free to enter.
jury: Dimitri Beck, Director of Photography, Polka Magazine
Thierry Grillet, Creative Director, Bibliothèque nationale de France
Aurélie de Lanlay, Deputy Director, Les Rencontres d'Arles
Anne Lesage, Head of Images, Centre des Monuments Nationaux
Coralie Savin, Director of Communications, Eurazeo
calls.summary: Eurazeo's relaunched grant: €20,000 plus mentorship to create a body of work on 'Stories of Europe', partnered with the Rencontres d'Arles.

calls.title: Art Through The Lens 2026
calls.description: The Yeiser Art Center's long-running annual international juried photography exhibition, held in the historic 1905 Market House building in downtown Paducah, Kentucky. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over working in photo-based imagery created through photographic processes — including non-lens-made images — completed within the last three years. A juror selects 50–70 images for the gallery exhibition. $1,000 in cash awards: First Place $500, Second Place $300, Third Place $200. Up to 20 images may be entered at $10 each (Yeiser members receive $10 off). Exhibition August 25 – October 11, 2026; the gallery takes a 40% commission on sales.
calls.summary: Yeiser Art Center's annual international juried photography show in Paducah, KY. $1,000 in cash awards; juror Ginny Harris.

calls.title: HCP Annual Fellowship Awards 2026
calls.description: Houston Center for Photography's annual fellowship awards two photographers from anywhere in the world $3,000 each plus a solo exhibition at HCP, opening November 2026. A single juror selects two distinct awards: the Carol Crow Fellowship, for photographers advocating for the environment and celebrating natural landscapes, and the HCP Fellowship, which carries no assigned theme and recognizes work offering insight into current themes, technologies, and practices in photography. Open to all photographic, film, video, and lens-based installation work. The 2026 juror is Natasha Egan, Executive Director of the Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia College Chicago. There is no entry fee, but applicants must hold an HCP Fellowship membership ($35). HCP covers ground shipping for selected artists.
jury: Natasha Egan, Executive Director, MoCP Columbia College Chicago
calls.summary: HCP's annual fellowship: two photographers worldwide each win $3,000 plus a solo show. 2026 juror Natasha Egan (MoCP Chicago).

calls.title: Bath Open Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Now in its 14th year, the Bath Open Art Prize is an international open call run by the volunteer-led non-profit Fringe Arts Bath. Open to visual artists at any stage of their career from across the globe, it accepts work across all genres and mediums — including photography, video, painting, textile, digital, print and 3D, plus small installations and performance. Works selected by 2026 judges Simbah Pilé and Jemma Hickman are shown at 44AD artspace in Bath, UK, 16–31 October 2026. Prizes: £750 first, £250 second, £50 People's Choice art vouchers, and a 44AD solo exhibition opportunity. Entry fees (£22 for one work, £33 for up to three) help fund FaB's free annual visual arts festival.
calls.summary: Fringe Arts Bath's 14th international open art prize at 44AD artspace. All media incl. photography; £750 + solo show.

calls.title: CitiesToBe Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Third edition of the urban photography award organised by Barcelona innovation studio Anteverti — and the first to be thematic and to reward photographic series rather than single images. The 2026 theme is 'Third Places': the informal, shared spaces beyond home and work where city life unfolds. Open worldwide to anyone 18 or over, individuals or collectives, working in lens-based photography only; each participant submits one project of 10 to 20 images shot after 1 January 2024. Jury: Roger Grasas, Arianna Rinaldo, Cristina Garrido, Pilar Conesa and Sergio García i Rodríguez. AI-generated or synthetic images are not eligible. Call opens 22 June, closes 30 September 2026, winners announced November 2026.

calls.org: Barcelona Human Rights International Photo Festival
calls.description: Sixth edition of the international photography festival on human rights and global justice organised in Barcelona by the Más Retina association. calls.title: Lenscratch Still Life Exhibition
calls.description: Online juried exhibition dedicated to the art of still life, juried by photographer Kimberly Witham. Open to work across the genre — constructed tableaux, studies of everyday objects, and contemporary images exploring memory, symbolism, identity, and place through the language of still life. Submit one image (72dpi, 1000px long side).
calls.summary: Lenscratch's free juried online exhibition on the art of still life, selected by photographer Kimberly Witham. One image, no fee.
prose: Lenscratch is one of the longest-running photography blogs and online platforms, with a regular schedule of juried online exhibitions accompanying its daily editorial coverage. The Still Life Exhibition is the platform's open call for photography working within the still life tradition — from constructed tableaux and studies of everyday objects to contemporary work that uses the language of still life to explore memory, symbolism, identity, and place.

The exhibition is juried by Kimberly Witham, a New Jersey-based photographer and educator known for still life work drawing on botanicals, found objects, and the natural world. Selected images publish in an online group exhibition on Lenscratch on July 31, 2026.

Submissions are free, with one image accepted per photographer, sized to 72dpi at 1000 pixels on the long side. Caption format follows Lenscratch's standard: copyright, name, image title, Instagram handle, and website. The deadline is July 19, 2026.

calls.title: Looking In — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by Jessica Alazraki, opening September 11, 2026. Looking In explores what it means to observe from a distance — through windows, thresholds, memories, cultures, and personal experiences — and the spaces between public and private, insider and outsider, visibility and mystery. Inspired by life in a city where glimpses into a neighbor’s world are unavoidable, it reflects on how looking creates curiosity, empathy, and connection. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after August 10, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists’ work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.
calls.summary: NYC billboard show curated by Jessica Alazraki. Theme: observing from a distance — windows, thresholds, belonging. Open to all mediums.

calls.title: Dignity Not For Sale — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Lizzie Suarez, opening September 18, 2026. A call to celebrate the belonging, dignity, and resilience of Miami’s working class as the city is reshaped by wealth and real estate — an invitation to remember what makes Miami special and that our dignity is not for sale. Welcoming submissions of all mediums, including photography, that address these themes, from artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on Miami ad space for at least one month. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists’ work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.
calls.summary: Miami bus shelter show curated by Lizzie Suarez celebrating the dignity and resilience of the city's working class. Open to all mediums.

calls.title: Prix Photoforum 2026
calls.fee: CHF 65 (CHF 35 students/apprentices with proof; free for members)
calls.description: Annual open call from Photoforum Pasquart, a leading Swiss photography institution in Biel/Bienne. The jury selects between 10 and 15 photographers and artists working in photographic media to present their work in a group exhibition at Photoforum Pasquart in December 2026. All photographic practices are welcome, including documentary photography, experimental processes, installation, video and digital media. There is no set theme — applicants explore the possibilities of the photographic medium and demonstrate a distinctive approach to their practice, and submitted work must have been created within the last two years. One participant receives the Prix Photoforum of CHF 5,000, and all selected participants receive CHF 500 toward production and transport costs.
calls.summary: Swiss photography institution's annual juried group show in Biel; CHF 5,000 prize plus CHF 500 production grants for 10–15 selected artists.

calls.title: Kyoto Retreat 2026
calls.description: A fully-funded four-week retreat in Kyoto, Japan, conceived as a time for rest, research and reflection rather than production. Open to visual artists, curators and writers aged 21+ at all career stages and working in any discipline, including photography, moving image and the written word. Selected participants receive round-trip airfare to Kansai/Osaka, private accommodation in a shared house for the duration, and an $800 USD stipend for meals and local transportation. The 2026 retreat runs November 1–30, 2026.
calls.summary: Fully-funded four-week November retreat in Kyoto for artists, curators and writers — airfare, private accommodation and an $800 stipend.

calls.title: Liu Shiming Artist Grants 2026
calls.description: The fourth annual round of grants from the Liu Shiming Art Foundation supporting early-career visual artists, including photographers, in the first decade of their practice. Up to five artists are each awarded a $5,000 grant to support a current or new project that explores the interplay between traditional, cultural or historical influences and contemporary artistic practice. The application period runs June 1 – August 31, 2026, and is open to artists from any country (application materials must be in English).

calls.title: PhMuseum 2026 Women Photographers Grant
calls.description: Now in its 10th edition, the PhMuseum Women Photographers Grant supports the work and careers of female and non-binary photographers of all ages and from all countries, working across documentary, fine art and conceptual photography. The open call awards a total of $11,000 in cash prizes plus €5,000 in MPB gear vouchers: $5,500 (1st), $2,200 (2nd), $1,100 (3rd), a $2,200 New Generation prize for entrants aged 30 or under, and two MPB Special Mentions of €2,500 in vouchers each. Selected work is shown in a solo exhibition at PhMuseum Lab, screened at the PhotoVogue Festival, and featured via a Vogue Italia interview; every entrant also receives a 30-minute portfolio review with a PhMuseum Education mentor. The grant promotes stories told from a female and non-binary perspective and advances gender equality across the photography industry.
calls.summary: 10th-edition grant for women and non-binary photographers: $11,000 cash, MPB vouchers, solo show at PhMuseum Lab. Entries open 8 September.

calls.title: CPA International Juried Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Annual international juried exhibition at the Center for Photographic Art's historic gallery in Carmel-by-the-Sea, California. Open to all photographers 18+ worldwide working in still photographic media; any subject. Submission period July 1 – October 1, 2026.

calls.title: Through the Lens: Presence and Absence
calls.description: Third photography-dedicated juried exhibition at ArtWorks Gallery, run by Workshop13, a nonprofit cultural arts and learning center in Ware, Massachusetts. The theme explores how what we see in a photograph is shaped by what is missing — visibility versus implication, spaces that suggest human presence, objects that stand in for memory. Selected works are shown in the gallery. AI-generated work is not accepted.
calls.summary: Workshop13's third photography exhibition in Ware, MA. Theme: presence and absence — what's missing in an image. AI not accepted.

calls.title: KinoSaito Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Four-week fall residency (November 8 – December 6, 2026) at KinoSaito, an arts center in a renovated former Catholic school in Verplanck, New York. Two professional artists each receive a 900 sq ft studio with loft living quarters (kitchenette and private bathroom) and a $1,500 stipend for living costs and supplies. All media are accepted, including photography and lens-based work; currently enrolled students are not eligible.
calls.summary: Four-week fall residency at KinoSaito arts center in Verplanck, NY. $1,500 stipend, studio + housing. All media incl. photography.

calls.title: .ART Award 2026
calls.description: Inaugural global award marking the 10th anniversary of the .ART domain registry, open to artists worldwide across all disciplines including photography and lens-based work. A single overarching prize combines a $15,000 cash Grand Prize, one-month residencies at Château du Fresne near Paris and Anfitrion in Marbella, Spain (both with round-trip travel), editorial coverage in international art media, and a premium .ART domain valued at $10,000. Jury includes critic Jerry Saltz alongside curators and gallerists. Free to enter, but applicants must register and link a .ART domain to their portfolio; multiple entries are allowed, each needing its own domain. Submit an artist biography, artwork documentation, and a short narrative explaining the concept. Winners announced December 3, 2026 during Art Basel Miami.

calls.fee: $10 per image (up to 5); free for Evendale residents and students 18 and under
calls.description: A juried photography exhibition presented by the Evendale Cultural Arts Center as part of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial, marking the Village of Evendale's 75th anniversary. The theme 'Reflections Through Time' invites work exploring memory, history, change, identity and the stories that connect past, present and future, interpreted personally or universally, documentary or conceptual. Open to amateur and professional photographers residing within a 50-mile radius of Evendale, Ohio (students 18 and under may enter a Student Division). Selected photographs are reproduced on large-scale 4-by-4-foot weatherproof panels and installed outdoors along the Village pool fence as a free public art installation (September 13 – December 31, 2026). Juried by Carolyn Teepen, Assistant Professor of Photography and Filmmaking at Thomas More University.
jury: Carolyn Teepen, Assistant Professor of Photography & Filmmaking, Thomas More University
calls.summary: Evendale Cultural Arts Center juried photo show for the FotoFocus Biennial. Outdoor panels, $1,000+ prizes; Cincinnati-area photographers.

calls.title: Flowing & Flying: A National Exhibit of Waterbirds and Waterscapes
calls.description: A national juried exhibition at d'Art Center, the nonprofit art center in Norfolk, Virginia's NEON District, dedicated to waterscapes — ocean, lakes, ponds, rivers, wetlands and swamps — and the birds that inhabit them. All mediums and styles are welcome, 2D or 3D, making it a natural fit for nature and wildlife photographers. Open to US artists 18+ with original work made in the last 8 years; up to 10 works. Juried by Val Parnell, with $950 in cash awards; exhibition August 22 – September 19, 2026.
calls.summary: National juried show of waterbirds and waterscapes at Norfolk's d'Art Center — all mediums, $950 in awards, show Aug 22–Sep 19.

Judged by photo editors and creative directors from The New York Times, Robb Report, Financial Times HTSI, Condé Nast Traveller UK and Rizzoli. calls.description: The Royal Society's publishing arm runs this annual competition celebrating photography by working scientists — treating the research image as visual culture in its own right, across Astronomy, Behaviour, Earth Science and Climatology, Ecology and Environmental Science, and Microimaging. The overall winner receives £1,000; category winners receive £500 plus Royal Photographic Society certificates and one-year memberships. Open to anyone studying or working in science at graduate level or above; up to 20 entries per person. Free to enter.
jury: Duncan Mackay, University of St Andrews
Ulrike Muller, California State University Fresno
calls.summary: £1,000 top prize for photography by working scientists — free entry, five science categories, open at graduate level and above.

calls.title: The Nature Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: International online nature photography competition across ten categories — Natural Landscapes, Wildlife, Macro, Underwater, Birds, Plant Life, Night World, Environmental Impact, Sharing the Planet and Funny Nature — with conservation built into the entry model: every participant funds a tree through One Tree Planted, and winners choose where planting happens. Photography of the Year wins €1,000, with €100 for each category winner; finalists must supply original RAW/DNG files for verification, and digital art is not accepted. Open worldwide to photographers 18+.
calls.summary: Ten-category nature competition — €1,000 top prize, a tree planted per entrant, originals verified. Open worldwide, 18+.

calls.title: 12th International Phone-ography Competition
calls.description: FotoFoto Gallery, a cooperative photography gallery in Huntington, New York, holds its 12th annual international competition exclusively for images shot on phone cameras — 'Image capture must have been made with the camera on your phone. Any phone!' Around 30 photographs are selected by juror Karen Klinedinst for the gallery exhibition, August 27 – September 19, 2026, with cash awards of $300, $200 and $100. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide (gallery members excluded); 5–15 images.
calls.summary: Phone-camera images only: ~30 works exhibited at this Long Island cooperative photo gallery, with $600 in cash awards.

calls.description: The Placerville Arts Association's National Mother Lode Art Exhibition reaches its 60th edition — a six-decade Northern California institution — showing November 5–21, 2026 at the Mills Station Arts and Culture Center (The MACC) in Rancho Cordova. All media except installations are considered, with photography explicitly listed; photography and digital art are the only media permitted as editions. Juried and judged by mixed-media artist Debra Kreck-Harnish, with over $4,250 in awards including a $700 Best of Show. Open to US-based artists; original work created 2023 or later.

calls.title: CITIZENS — PHOTO IS:RAEL Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open call for the 13th International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv (October 2026), themed around citizenship and photography as active civic practice — grassroots perspectives, democratic engagement, and belonging beyond legal status. Open to artists worldwide at all career stages, with existing or new projects. Photography, film, video, performance documentation, animation, and hybrid/digital forms are accepted; up to 12 images per submission. Selected artists are shown in the festival's Main Exhibition, included in the 2026 catalog, and featured on the festival website.

calls.title: European Month of Photography Berlin 2027
calls.description: Open call for the 2027 edition of EMOP Berlin, one of Europe's largest photography festivals, organised by Kulturprojekte Berlin and staged across the city from 4 March to 4 April 2027. Museums, galleries, archives, libraries, cultural institutes, universities, and individual photographers or collectives may propose a photography or lens-based exhibition; individual artists must have or secure a Berlin exhibition space, and organisations based outside Berlin must partner with a Berlin venue. Selected projects join the official festival programme and receive promotion across the festival's website, social media, and printed guide. Participation is free with no fee, but EMOP does not fund project costs — applicants arrange their own venue and funding. Proposals may respond to the 2027 leitmotif 'Common Ground. Letters from Europe,' though this is optional. Applications are submitted through an online form and reviewed confidentially by a jury including the festival's Artistic Director, with decisions announced in September 2026.
calls.summary: Propose a photography exhibition for the 2027 EMOP Berlin festival programme. Free entry; requires a Berlin venue. Runs March–April 2027.

calls.summary: Travel photography competition. $2,700 prize pool, London exhibition and feature to 1.2M+ followers. Tiered $15–$45 entry.
prose: The Independent Photographer (TIP) is a London-based online photography platform that runs themed monthly competitions and publishes editorial work, interviews, and book reviews. The 2026 Travel Award is the platform's travel-themed cycle, open to work that captures the essence of a place — its people, traditions, and the rhythm of daily life, from bustling markets to serene vistas.

Total prize pool is $2,700: first place receives $1,000, second $600, third $400, and seven runners-up receive $100 each. Winners are exhibited in London and featured across The Independent Photographer's Instagram (970k+ followers). All entrants receive a free online portfolio on the platform.

Eligibility is open globally. Submissions are tiered: €15 for one image, €30 for three, €45 for six, with an early-bird 50% discount available before the early deadline. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200 pixels on one side, maximum 10MB per file. AI-generated work is not accepted — photography-based submissions only, with film, digital, smartphone, tintype, and camera-less photography all welcome. The final deadline is August 31, 2026.

calls.title: Innovate Grants - Summer $1,800 Grants
calls.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers — one grant to a photographer and one to a visual artist. Eighteen honorable mentions are also featured on the Innovate platform (nine in art, nine in photo). The application is deliberately minimal: no artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation required — just name, email, grant category, and 3–10 images of recent work. Open globally to artists 18 or over in all media and genres. Winners and honorable mentions receive feature profiles, interview pages, and promotion on the Innovate Instagram.
calls.summary: Two $1,800 grants — one for a photographer, one for a visual artist, plus eighteen honorable mentions. Open worldwide, minimal application.
prose: Innovate Artist Grants runs a recurring quarterly grant program for visual artists and photographers. Each cycle awards two $1,800 grants — one to a visual artist and one to a photographer. The Summer 2026 cycle is the third of the year's four cycles.

Eighteen honorable mentions are also featured on the Innovate platform alongside the two main grantees — nine in art and nine in photo. Winners and honorable mentions receive feature profiles, interview pages, and promotion on the Innovate Instagram account.

The application is deliberately minimal: name, email, grant category, 3 to 10 images of recent work, and the application fee. No artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation are required.
Eligibility is open globally to visual artists and photographers aged 18 or over; all media and genres are accepted. Fee is $35. The Summer 2026 deadline is September 17 at 11:59 PM PT.

calls.title: Copenhagen Photo Festival — Call for Solo Artists 2027
calls.description: Competitive open call for full solo exhibitions at Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027, the Nordic region's largest annual photography festival. The submission window runs 8 July – 1 September 2026 on the theme 'Frie hænder / Free Hands'. Ten projects are shortlisted; from these, three to five are chosen for solo exhibitions in the festival's exhibition park in the heart of Copenhagen. Solo artists receive a €537 festival participation fee, up to €400 in travel and accommodation support for international photographers, €134 toward food and local transport, a solo exhibition, targeted PR, a permanent website feature, and on-site programming (talks, workshops, guided tours). Remaining shortlisted 'Selectees' receive a €200 fee and a digital screening of their project. Submit a biography, CV, a project description (max 3,000 characters), and a minimum of 10 images; projects previously exhibited in Denmark or shortlisted in prior years are not eligible. Application in English or Danish.
jury: Søren Pagter, Head of Photojournalism, Danish School of Media and Journalism
Patricia Breinholm Bertram, Curator, Martin Asbæk Gallery
Stinus Duch, Founder, Disko Bay Book
Maja Dyrehauge Gregersen, Managing Director, Copenhagen Photo Festival
calls.summary: Solo-exhibition call for Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027 — theme 'Free Hands'. €537 fee, travel support, PR. Window July 8 – Sept 1.
prose: Copenhagen Photo Festival is the Nordic region's largest annual photography festival. Its Call for Solo Artists is the festival's competitive open call for full solo exhibitions — distinct from the public Open Exhibition — with the 2027 theme 'Frie hænder' (Free Hands).

The submission window runs 8 July – 1 September 2026. Ten projects are shortlisted; from these, three to five are chosen for solo exhibitions staged in the festival's exhibition park in the heart of Copenhagen. Shortlisted artists take part in interviews in autumn 2026 before the final jury decision.

Solo artists receive a €537 festival participation fee, up to €400 toward travel and accommodation for international photographers, and €134 toward food and local transport. The festival also provides the solo exhibition, targeted PR and marketing, a permanent website feature, and on-site programming including talks, workshops, and guided tours. The remaining shortlisted 'Selectees' receive a €200 fee and a digital screening of their project during the festival.

Applicants submit a biography, CV, a project description of up to 3,000 characters, and a minimum of 10 images (1500px minimum, sRGB). Projects previously exhibited in Denmark, or shortlisted in previous years, are not eligible; artists selected as a solo artist within the last three years must wait a year to reapply. Applications are accepted in English or Danish, and the deadline is 1 September 2026.

calls.title: Composed
calls.description: A juried exhibition presented by the Texas Photographic Society with PhotoPlace Gallery, exploring composition — framing, perspective, light, colour, geometry, gesture, visual rhythm, negative space and layering — across all genres and processes. Juror Brian Finke, a documentary photographer known for his cultural commentary, selects roughly 35 photographs for the physical show at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont (October 2–31, 2026) and about 40 for the online exhibition on the PhotoPlace and TPS websites. Awards include a $500 Juror's Award, a $300 Director's Award, and two $100 Honorable Mentions. Open to photographers across the United States and worldwide; entry covers five images, with additional media $5 each.

calls.title: LensCulture Photobook Prize 2026
calls.description: LensCulture's photobook award: submit a photo project of 20–30 images ready to become a book — no book dummy required. The winning project, selected by Nazraeli Press, is published as a full monograph valued at over $25,000, with a Los Angeles exhibition and a solo LensCulture feature. Five shortlisted photographers each receive a $500 grant, a solo feature article, a 30-minute portfolio consultation and inclusion in the LA exhibition; ten finalists share a group feature. Judged by a panel of publishers from Nazraeli Press, L'Artiere, Stanley/Barker and Deadbeat Club.
jury: Clint Woodside, Founder & Director, Deadbeat Club
Laura Sackett, Co-Founder & Creative Director, LensCulture

calls.title: Vincent van Gogh Photo Award 2027
calls.description: An international photography competition run by the Rotary Club Nuenen charity in the Dutch village where Vincent van Gogh lived and worked. The 2027 edition's theme is 'Spirit of Light' — inviting photographers to interpret light through van Gogh's eyes. Entrants may submit up to three images, with a separate Student Award running in parallel. Winners share cash prizes of €1,000, €500 and €250 (with a matching student tier) and are exhibited in Nuenen. The winner is announced on 3 September 2027.
calls.summary: International themed award ('Spirit of Light') in van Gogh's Dutch village. Up to 3 images; €1,000 top prize, student tier & Nuenen show.

calls.title: DEAR DAVE, Fellowships 2026
calls.description: Annual fellowship competition from DEAR DAVE, the New York tri-annual print magazine of photography and writing published since 2007. Open to photographers worldwide with no limitation of genre or topic — submit a cohesive body of work of 10 to 20 images. Three selected photographers have their portfolios featured in an upcoming issue of the magazine, and the 40 highest-ranked entrants join the Fellowship Archive on the magazine's website. The jury spans curators, editors and gallerists including Peter Barberie (Philadelphia Museum of Art), Tim Clark (1000 Words), Kristen Lubben (Magnum Foundation) and Domenico de Chirico (Unseen Photo). Previous publication or exhibition does not disqualify applicants.

calls.title: Quiet Hours: Nighttime and Grief
calls.description: Open call from Der Greif inviting lens-based artists to examine nighttime's emotional landscape — how darkness changes the way we see the world and how we feel. Timed around National Grief Awareness Day, the call centres on grief in its many manifestations: bereavement, relationship loss, displacement, or life transitions, and asks how darkness and light can convey narratives of memory and healing. Selected work is featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's Pulse platform, with facilitated peer critique sessions and exposure within Der Greif's international network, plus potential invitations to submit portfolios for sales and commission opportunities. Entry is free with a suggested optional €5 or €10 donation, and 50–100% discount vouchers are available for artists facing financial barriers.
calls.summary: Der Greif call on nighttime and grief — how darkness and light carry memory and healing. Online exhibition on the Pulse platform.

Chosen artists are invited to a preliminary meeting toward a publication.

calls.title: UNSTAGED — How Are Things?
calls.description: Open call from UNSTAGED, the independent photography journal of narrative-led inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity, initiated with the How Are Things Collective founded by Professor Amanda Crawley Jackson (University of the Arts London). The call explores how creative practice — photography in particular — can hold space for urgent dialogue and reflection in a time of polycrisis: projects examining our entanglement with human, non-human and more-than-human entities, bodies, and structures, through material & affective, political & (infra)structural, or speculative lenses. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPGs (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with a project description (max 500 words) via a public Google Drive link emailed to opencall@un-staged.com — email attachments are not considered. Free entry with no contribution fee; selected work is curated for print.
jury: Amanda Crawley Jackson (@occursus1), How Are Things Collective founder
calls.summary: Free call from indie journal UNSTAGED w/ How Are Things Collective: witnessing entanglement in polycrisis. Curated for print.

calls.title: Art That Matters to the Planet: Dark Skies
calls.description: Sixth annual juried exhibition at the Roger Tory Peterson Institute in Jamestown, NY (January 29 – May 30, 2027), themed on the night skies after Peterson's A Field Guide to the Stars and Planets — nocturnal creatures, constellations, light pollution and space junk. All media welcome, including photography; recent works (since 2020) preferred. Guest juror Jon Lomberg, Carl Sagan's principal artistic collaborator and Design Director of NASA's Voyager Golden Record. For the first time RTPI awards cash prizes of $1,000, $500 and $250, announced at the opening reception. International; up to 4 works. Entries open August 1 and close November 7, 2026 via CaFÉ.
jury: Jon Lomberg, astronomical artist and Design Director of NASA's Voyager Golden Record

calls.title: Tracks & Trails: Marks Left Behind
calls.description: Winter juried exhibition in the largest galleries of View Arts Center in Old Forge, NY, in the Adirondacks (December 11, 2026 – March 6, 2027). The theme investigates stories written upon the land — animal tracks, footprints, ski and snowshoe trails, railroads, bridges and winter logging — the marks that become part of the landscape's memory. All media welcome, including photography. Open to US artists; work must be original, created within the past 3 years and not previously shown at View. Up to 3 works ($35 first, $10 each additional) via CaFÉ; artists receive 65% of sales.

The season concludes with a curated exhibition and sales showcase at the Palm Springs Cultural Center. Apply with 3–10 images via CaFÉ.

calls.title: Photobook Dummy Exhibition — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair

Dummies are displayed for consultation throughout the fair, where past editions (72 projects by 65 authors in 2026) have drawn the attention of attending publishers and booksellers — a real chance to move a book project forward. Pre-register with up to 6 photographs of the dummy (72 dpi, max 2 MB each) via the Google Form by October 12, 21:00 GMT; confirmations October 23, dummies delivered by November 16. Participation is free. The fair also runs parallel calls for self-publisher/small-press tables and presentations of authorial projects.

calls.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2027
calls.description: Second edition of the international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2027, with all nominees also shown in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Fee tiered by number of works: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 works per registration with unlimited registrations. Images created solely with generative AI are excluded.

calls.title: Prix LNP 2026 — Les Nuits Photo
calls.description: The annual call for photographic films from Les Nuits Photo, the Paris festival devoted to the photo-film form, organised by the photographers' association Freelens in partnership with SAIF. Open internationally to all authors — established, emerging, students and amateurs alike, whether photographers, directors, editors, artists or journalists. The Grand Prix LNP carries a €1,000 award from SAIF plus diffusion on Fisheye Magazine and 9 Lives Magazine and screenings at partner festivals; the Prix LNP Diapéro, chosen by the Diapéro team, adds €500 and paid distribution on Mediapart. Submissions run 20 June – 15 September 2026 via Google Form; prizes are presented at the festival in Paris in November.

calls.title: Bourse Transverse 2026
calls.description: Joint grant from photographers' association Freelens and ADAGP, the French visual-arts authors' society, supporting a duo — a photographer and an artist from another visual discipline — in creating a work together and publishing it as a book. €12,000 in total: €7,000 to the winning duo and €5,000 towards the book's edition, with the work made within a year and the book published within two. Open to duos from the French scene (working or residing in France for at least five years, or French nationals living abroad) with professional track records of exhibitions or publications; a publisher may already be attached. Applications in French via the ADAGP candidature portal by 3 September 2026, 2pm; the winning duo is announced at Salon Polycopies in Paris on 12 November 2026.
calls.summary: Freelens × ADAGP duo grant — €7,000 for a photographer + visual artist co-creation, plus €5,000 for the book edition. French scene.

calls.title: Head On Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: The flagship international awards of Sydney's Head On Photo Festival, judged completely anonymously — jurors see the photograph, never the photographer's name, CV or following. Three categories: Portrait, Landscape and Exposure (anything that is not portrait or landscape), sharing an AUD 80,000 prize pool that includes AUD 5,000 cash for each category winner plus OM System camera kits. Around 40 finalists per category (20–30 for Exposure) are exhibited in print and online during the festival, 6–29 November 2026. Open internationally to photographers at every level, from phone snapshots to studio and documentary work. Entries are AUD 30 per image, half price for under-25s; final deadline 16 August 2026, 11:59pm Sydney time.
calls.summary: Sydney's blind-judged festival awards — AUD 80,000 pool across Portrait, Landscape and Exposure; finalists exhibited in November.

calls.title: The Shape of a Life
calls.description: Online juried photography exhibition from Decagon Gallery on the idea that a life is not defined by its milestones alone. The brief welcomes portraits, landscapes, interiors, gestures, and quiet everyday moments that reveal human experience with honesty and depth rather than surface description. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition with dedicated pages and published in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, alongside digital badges and certificates. Open to photographers worldwide; up to 4 images. First place receives $500, second $250, third $150, and two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total in cash awards — plus a Human Presence Award granting free entry to a future exhibition.

calls.title: ALT
calls.description: Juried show at Photo Opp, a nonprofit community darkroom and visual workspace housed in the former Moses Montefiore Synagogue in downtown Appleton, Wisconsin. ALT celebrates photography as a medium without limits and asks what happens when artists step outside the expected: cyanotypes and salt prints, film soup, unconventional printing surfaces, digital manipulation, sculptural photography, emulsion lifting, collage and anything that challenges convention or expands the definition of a photograph. The brief prizes curiosity over perfection, process over predictability, risk over routine. Open to Wisconsin residents (work may have been made anywhere, anytime); up to three pieces per artist, free to enter. Selected work hangs in the Community Gallery from October 2026, with an opening reception and awards announcement on October 16, and is featured in a promotional zine sold as a fundraiser. The gallery takes no commission on sales.
calls.summary: Free alt-process juried show at Appleton's community darkroom — cyanotypes, film soup, collage. Wisconsin residents; gallery show + zine.

calls.title: This Land Is Your Land
calls.description: Community photography exhibit at the Library Arts Center gallery in Newport, New Hampshire, marking America's 250th anniversary. The call asks photographers to share images of the places, faces, traditions and stories that make up the fabric of America — sweeping landscapes and quiet hometown streets, everyday moments and the people who shape communities, natural beauty alongside resilience and heritage. Open to photographers of all experience levels who live in New Hampshire or Vermont, or who have a distinct connection to the area; up to two pieces per photographer. Entry is free for Library Arts Center members and $5 otherwise. Accepted artists are notified by July 28 and deliver framed, ready-to-hang work to the gallery on August 5–6. The exhibit runs August 15 – October 9, 2026, with an opening reception on August 14.
calls.summary: Community photo exhibit for America's 250th at a New Hampshire arts centre. NH/VT photographers, all levels; $5, free for members.

calls.org: Kansas City Society for Contemporary Photography
calls.description: The annual juried exhibition of the Kansas City Society for Contemporary Photography, a long-running nonprofit devoted to contemporary photographic practice in the Midwest. Current Works sets out to show what photographic artists are doing now, and the call explicitly welcomes a broad range of styles and processes — digital, film, alternative process, black and white or colour — representing the diversity of photographic excellence in the region. Open to residents of Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, Nebraska, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Texas; work must have been produced between 2024 and 2026 and be built on the entrant's own original photography, with no AI-generated imagery. KCSCP members receive 20% off the entry fee, and students can request a discount code. The 2026 juror is John W. Hans, a Kansas City photographer of nearly fifty years and Director of Production at Dolphin Archival Printing inside Haw Contemporary, whose own abstract, landscape-rooted work is held in the H&R Block and Kansas City International Airport collections. Selected work is exhibited November 12 – December 31, 2026.
jury: John W. Hans, Photographer & Director of Production, Dolphin Archival Printing

calls.title: The Proximity of Harm — Visions of a Compromised Everyday Life
calls.description: First edition of an international photography competition run by the Ippocrate Foundation, an independent Italian organisation working on health, environment and social transformation, as part of a cultural research project into contemporary forms of harm. The brief treats harm in an extended, layered sense — not only environmental damage but a diffuse condition running through relationships, social systems and the construction of individual and collective identity, and equally emotional and perceptual. The project positions photography as a tool of critical observation, looking for personal ways of seeing what is close and everyday yet stays invisible; the aim is not to document harm didactically but to offer an authentic, contemporary perspective. Open to photographers, artists and authors of any nationality aged 18 or over; one to three images, as single pictures or a coherent series, no AI-generated work. The jury is chaired by World Press Photo winner Pablo Ernesto Piovano and includes photographers Pierpaolo Mittica, Ilaria Di Biagio and Ilenia Baldina, and director Silvia Chiodin. Selected photographs are screened on September 18 at Palazzetto Widmann during the Ippocrate Convention in Bagnoli di Sopra, and the three winners are invited to a masterclass with Piovano at the Teatro Carlo Goldoni on September 19 (travel and accommodation at the participant's own expense).
calls.summary: Foundation-run research competition on harm as a diffuse everyday condition. Worldwide, 1–3 images, €10; jury chaired by Pablo Piovano.

calls.title: The Space Between Is What Remains
calls.description: A national juried exhibition at Rolo Gallery, a contemporary space that opened in May 2026 on Denver's Art District on Santa Fe. The call asks for work that holds something — a mark, a quality of light, a feeling that doesn't leave — and is deliberately loose about interpretation: abstract, figurative or anywhere between, with no requirement that work announce its connection to the theme. Photography is welcome alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, mixed media, fibre, ceramics, works on paper and book arts. Open to US-based artists 18 and over at all career stages, with no exhibition history required. calls.title: Beyond The Surface: Exploring Above and Below
calls.description: Hera Gallery — an artist-run cooperative in Wakefield, Rhode Island, founded in 1974 — invites work that makes the invisible visible, navigating the space between inner and outer worlds, the terrestrial and the cosmic. Seen from space, earth is a small blue dot where boundaries dissolve; the call asks where each artist's work sits within that spectrum, whether through a personal, public, spiritual or cosmic lens. All media welcome, 2D, 3D and video. Juror Lydia Jasper is Assistant Curator at MASS MoCA. Submission fees run on a sliding scale, honour system; the gallery takes no commission, so 100% of sales go to the artist. Exhibition runs October 17 – November 14, 2026.
jury: Lydia Jasper, Assistant Curator, MASS MoCA

calls.title: Artist in Residence 2027
calls.description: Twelve-week residencies in the foothills west of Denver, offered three times across 2027 (February 1 – April 30, May 10 – August 6, and August 16 – November 12). Residents get housing in a private one-bedroom cottage, a private studio with 24-hour secure access, paid teaching and workshop opportunities, exhibition space, an artist page on the CAE website and a $250 monthly stipend paid on completion ($750 total), plus chances to sell work at CAE events. In return each artist develops and facilitates one community programme tied to their residency plan. Open to artists 18 and over living and working in the US; photography, film, video, new media and interdisciplinary practice are all eligible, though digital artists must bring their own equipment.
calls.summary: 12-week Colorado residency with cottage, private studio, teaching work and a $750 stipend. Photography and film eligible.
