calls.title: Torn
calls.description: Drawing Rooms, a nonprofit art space in Jersey City, wants to expand what the word 'torn' can mean. The show seeks work that results wholly or partly from the act of tearing — collage, fibre, painting, assemblage — or that documents the residue of that act, a photograph of what tearing left behind, or that composes competing elements and narratives which refuse to resolve. Photography, prints, drawing, painting and sculpture are all accepted; AI-generated and reproduced works are not. Up to three unframed images may be submitted. Exhibited work must be for sale, split 60/40 in the artist's favour. The exhibition runs September 10 – October 11, 2026, with notification on August 16.
calls.summary: Tearing as material and metaphor at Jersey City's Drawing Rooms — photography of what the act leaves behind welcome.

calls.description: A celebration of immigrant artists who enrich the cultural fabric of the United States, hosted by Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit art organisation and community artist space in Frederick, Maryland. Artists born outside the US and now living in the continental US are invited to submit original work in any visual medium — photography, painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art among them — reflecting their own voice and experience. Cuban-American artist, curator and critic F. Lennox Campello serves as juror and curator. Up to three works may be entered; 2D work must be framed and wired. The exhibition runs January 1–31, 2027 in the Artspiration Frederick Gallery.

calls.title: Sum Sum Summ-A-Time
calls.description: Drawing Rooms, a nonprofit art space in Jersey City, gathers work about summertime for an online-only show on Artsy — scenes and places, summer food, leisure, flora and fauna, and the colours and sensations of the season. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, fibre and sculpture, with no size limitation and no AI-generated or reproduced work accepted. Three images are covered by the entry fee and further images may be added for $5 each. The exhibition runs August 6–30, 2026 on Artsy.net, with exhibited work offered for sale at a 60/40 split in the artist's favour.
calls.summary: Jersey City's Drawing Rooms takes summer online — an Artsy-hosted show of the season's places, food, leisure, flora and fauna.

calls.title: Solo Project Space #8
calls.description: Drawing Rooms hands over its Project Space and up to four further gallery areas to artists with a cohesive body of work or an installation — any theme, any concept, any size or medium, photography included. One artist takes the main Project Space and up to four more are given solo areas in the Jersey City galleries for the autumn slot, September 10 – October 11, 2026, with an opening reception on September 12 and a closing reception on October 11. Selected artists may also be picked up for other Drawing Rooms programmes, including The Art Project and the gallery's Artsy.net exhibits. calls.title: A Show of Heads 2026
calls.description: SlowArt Productions' long-running annual exhibition at Limner Gallery in Hudson, New York, devoted to every reading of the human head — traditional portraiture, abstraction, caricature, the conceptual and the surreal. calls.title: Spotlight Awards 2026
calls.description: Production Paradise's annual commercial and advertising photography awards, now in their ninth edition. The real draw is the jury: more than fifty picture editors, art buyers, creative directors and brand leads from IKEA, The Economist, Volvo Cars, Unilever, Louis Vuitton, Cartier, Ogilvy, Droga5, UNICEF, The Guardian and Mattel. Entrants opt in to having their work shown to every judge, and the organisers pitch it as a hiring channel as much as a competition — winner or not. Fifteen categories, one of them for AI-developed imagery. Each submission is a single image, commissioned or personal work, open to photographers in all countries over 18. The Grand Prize winner takes $1,000 cash plus a portfolio review ticket and strategy sessions; category winners receive sponsor packages, with a total prize pool over $40,000. Shortlists are announced from 1 September, winners on 22 September 2026.

calls.title: Global Reporting Grants
calls.description: The Pulitzer Center's open, catch-all reporting grant — no restriction on topic or region — funding in-depth journalism on systemic issues that get too little coverage. Photographers are explicitly eligible alongside reporters, audio and video journalists and documentary filmmakers; staff and freelancers of any nationality can apply. Grants cover reporting costs against a reasonable, detailed budget; most awards for international travel fall between $5,000 and $10,000. It does not fund staff salaries, equipment purchases, books, feature-length films, routine breaking news or data projects aimed solely at academic research. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline; half the grant is paid once paperwork is complete and the remainder on submission of the finished work. Grantees join the Center's reporting network and its education and outreach programs.
calls.summary: Rolling, no-deadline reporting grants of $5,000–$10,000 for photojournalists — travel and hard costs for a specific story.

calls.title: Open Call for Exhibitions — Prospekto and Vilnius Photography Galleries

Applications are accepted year-round with no fixed deadline; selections are made once a year, in August. Submit an exhibition proposal of up to 500 words naming the preferred gallery and exhibition period, a bio of up to 100 words, and a portfolio with supporting visual material such as documentation of previous installations. calls.fee: $35 up to 2, $45 up to 4, $55 up to 6

All works must be for sale; the gallery takes 50% commission. Opening reception August 22.

calls.title: South Florida Cultural Consortium Fellowship 2026
calls.description: The arts councils of Broward, Martin, Miami-Dade, Monroe and Palm Beach counties jointly award grants of $7,500 or $15,000 to visual and media artists who have lived and worked in the five-county South Florida region for at least a year — among the largest regional artist awards in the US. Established in 1988, the consortium has granted over $4 million to more than 300 artists, with recipients' work presented in exhibitions. Photography and media work are eligible (samples from the past three years); degree-seeking students are not. Attendance at one of the remaining online workshops (August 4 or August 22) is required to apply. Funded in part by the National Endowment for the Arts and the State of Florida.

calls.title: Nancy Ingersoll Foster Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: An endowment-funded two-week retreat (September 5–19, 2026) presented by the Elizabeth Lane Oliver Center for the Arts, the nonprofit community art center on the Lake Michigan shore in Frankfort, Benzie County. Named for painter Nancy Ingersoll Foster, a longtime teacher and exhibitor at the center, the residency is housed at the Parsons Center for Arts and Sciences in Lake Ann — Eastern Michigan University's 86-acre arts-and-nature campus — with exhibits and workshops at the Oliver Art Center near the Sleeping Bear Dunes coastline. Open to an artist working in any visual media; applications are a short online form, due July 27.
calls.summary: Two-week endowment-funded September retreat at a nonprofit art center on Lake Michigan; any visual media, free to apply.

calls.title: Crowded Table
calls.description: Juried exhibition at OVERLAP Art Space, a contemporary gallery in Newport, Rhode Island, on food and community — the cultivation, preparation, display and consumption of food, and the habits and traditions of nourishment and gathering. A range of mediums and subject matter is welcome, from topical work to functional 'tools for gathering'; the atmosphere is celebratory yet thoughtful. Jurors are Lesley Baker (Ceramics Department Head, RISD), Bob Dilworth (2025 Joan Mitchell Fellow, Professor Emeritus at University of Rhode Island), and Harry Philbrick (Executive Director, Newport Art Museum). Submit 1–3 images of 1–3 artworks with a short statement (max 250 words) on how the work relates to the theme. Exhibition November 14 – December 19, 2026; the holiday-season show is a fundraiser supporting OVERLAP and the Rhode Island Community Food Bank. The title comes from The Highwomen's 2019 song.
jury: Lesley Baker, Ceramics Department Head, RISD
Bob Dilworth, Artist and 2025 Joan Mitchell Fellow
Harry Philbrick, Executive Director, Newport Art Museum

calls.title: Tomorrow Will Be Yesterday
calls.description: A photo slam presented by the German Photographic Society (DGPh) — a non-profit founded in 1951 with around 1,200 members — at Fotografiska Berlin to mark the society's 75th anniversary. Photographers worldwide, aged 18 and over, submit an existing photographic series of 10–20 images on the theme 'Tomorrow Will Be Yesterday': work that reads the present as raw material for tomorrow's memory — transition, emergence, transformation. Submissions include a short project description (max 600 characters) and a brief artist bio; files as JPEG, sRGB, 3000 px on the long side. Selected works are shown as a sequenced slideshow on the large LED wall at Fotografiska Berlin on 19 September 2026, and in an online slideshow the following day. Non-competitive — there is no cash prize. €15 per project; DGPh members submit free of charge via voucher code.
jury: Kathy Ryan, Photo Director & Curator (former New York Times Magazine)

calls.title: Thinking Photography & Writing Photography 2026
calls.description: Biennial prizes for writing about photography, awarded jointly for the fourth time by the German Photographic Society (DGPh) and the Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation. The €3,000 'Thinking Photography' research prize honours scholarly work in photo theory and history — master's theses, dissertations, and independent publications alike, published or unpublished, created from November 2024. The €1,000 'Writing Photography' prize for innovative publicism recognises journalistic and essayistic publications on photography, with particular interest in blogs, columns, reviews, net-based formats, and work that creatively combines text and photographic material. Texts in German or English. Apply with an English summary (c. 3,500 characters), full manuscript, CV, and publication list via the upload links on the announcement page. An international jury decides; the awards are presented at a public event in 2027.

calls.title: In The Practice of Seeing — High School Section
calls.description: Free national juried photography exhibition for high school students, running as the teen section of Jacksonville State University's In the Practice of Seeing and shown in the Roundhouse Gallery at Hammond Hall alongside the main exhibition, 27 August – 24 September 2026. The brief treats photography as an active process of perception rather than a neutral record — seeing shaped by attention, context, memory and cultural framework. Open to all photographic processes including digital, film, alternative processes, mixed media incorporating photography, and photographic installations; every entry must originate from a camera-based capture or a cameraless photographic method such as photograms, cyanotypes or wet plate. Open to students aged 13–17. Up to 3 images, free to enter; framed work no larger than 16 × 20 inches, with artists responsible for shipping or delivery. Winners receive an Adorama Photo sponsored gift card.

Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging — no sawtooth hangers.

calls.title: Americana
calls.description: Juried exhibition in the East and West Carnegie Galleries at Crooked Tree Arts Center in Traverse City, Michigan, asking what America looks like through your eyes. Beyond the familiar shorthand of rolling farmland, front porches, Main Streets, county fairs and open roads, the call invites work that celebrates, questions, reinterprets or expands American identity — drawing on place, community, music, labour, history, culture, memory, migration, celebration, resilience and everyday life. Works may be literal or abstract, traditional or experimental; all media are welcome, photography included, and artists at every career stage are encouraged. Open to artists 18+ resident in the US Great Lakes region — if your state has a Great Lakes shoreline, you are eligible. Up to three works made in the last three years, $30 entry. Exhibition 4 September – 3 October 2026.
calls.summary: Great Lakes juried show at Crooked Tree Arts Center on the many meanings of Americana — photography welcome.

calls.title: The Unexpected Portrait
calls.description: Juried exhibition at ArtWorks Gallery, run by Workshop13, a nonprofit cultural arts and learning centre in Ware, Massachusetts. Artists are asked to deviate from formal posing and realistic representation, focusing instead on emotion, identity, memory, action or unconventional subject matter through modern techniques, stylised depiction or abstract interpretation of the sitter. Open to most physical media, photography included — electronic media cannot be accommodated, and AI-generated work, work created under instruction and work previously juried into an ArtWorks Gallery show are ineligible. Up to three original pieces per artist; the gallery may cap acceptances at two per artist depending on space. Juried by printmaker and teaching artist Julie Lapping Rivera. Accepted 2-D work must be framed and wired, hand-delivered or shipped with a prepaid return label. Exhibition runs 19 September – 17 October 2026, with an opening reception on 19 September. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales.
calls.summary: Workshop13's juried portrait show in Ware, MA — emotion, memory and abstraction over formal posing. Photography welcome.

calls.title: West Coast Biennial 2027
calls.description: Ninth edition of Turtle Bay Exploration Park's juried West Coast Biennial, held in the museum galleries in Redding, California. Juror Karlo Henry Velazquez Fernandez — artist, curator, founder of The Art Hunger and Arts Director for Viva Downtown Redding — will select between 30 and 50 works for the exhibition. Painting, printmaking, drawing, photography, sculpture and mixed media are all accepted. Open to artists living in California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska, who may enter up to three works made within three years of the deadline. Cash awards are presented at the opening: Best of Show $3,000, First Prize $1,750, Second $900, Third $650, plus Honorable Mention and People's Choice awards of $325 each. The exhibition runs 29 January – 18 April 2027, opening with an artists' reception and juror talk.
jury: Karlo Henry Velazquez Fernandez, Founder, The Art Hunger & Arts Director, Viva Downtown Redding

calls.title: Artist Grant — November 2026 Cycle
calls.description: An unrestricted $1,200 USD grant awarded to one visual artist three times a year, running since 2017. There is no proposal to write: applicants email a link to their website or three to five images of recent work along with a CV, resume or short bio. Open to visual artists aged 18 and over anywhere in the world working in painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation and new or alternative visual art forms; film, video, music, theatre and dance are excluded, and past winners may not reapply. Grantees are featured on the Artist Grant website and social channels. Results are sent within six to eight weeks of the deadline.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $1,200 grant for one visual artist, awarded three times a year. No proposal — just images and a bio.

calls.title: Reverie Magazine — Issue VI
calls.description: Open submissions for the sixth issue of Reverie, an international independent literary and arts magazine whose stated mission is to promote education and amplify the voices of marginalised communities through literature and fine arts. Alongside poetry, prose and short fiction, the magazine reads visual art in all forms — contemporary photography, digital illustration, scans of painting and documentation of physical craft. Artists may send up to five high-resolution pieces as PNG, PDF or JPG to the editors by email, with a 50-word bio in the body of the message. Submissions are free and open worldwide. Previously published work is accepted if the prior publication is credited, and simultaneous submissions are welcome. Reverie asks for first publishing and archival rights; all rights revert to the maker on publication. Editors respond in about a month.
calls.summary: Free open call for Issue VI of an indie international literary and arts magazine — contemporary photography welcome.

calls.title: She Speaks
calls.description: Juried exhibition at the Tolleson Art Gallery — a free exhibition space inside Tolleson Public Library, west of Phoenix — celebrating the creativity and artistic voices of Arizona women. Artists who are women or who identify as female are invited to share work reflecting their experiences, ideas and creative vision across all styles and themes; photography is explicitly welcome alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, digital and textile work. Entry is free and open to Arizona artists of all backgrounds and experience levels. Each selected artist receives a $100 stipend to exhibit, rising to $575 for artists who also present a public program of at least an hour — a workshop, artist talk or demo (optional, not required to submit). The gallery also runs a visitor drawing during the exhibition in which one attendee receives an exhibited artwork purchased for up to $500. Submissions include a brief artist statement of up to 250 words connecting the work to the theme. On view October 23 – December 10, 2026.

calls.title: Open Call: Main Gallery 2027/2028
calls.description: The Firehouse Art Center in Longmont, Colorado is accepting proposals for its 2027/28 exhibition calendar. Housed in a National Historic Landmark building with two exhibition spaces and over 1,000 square feet, the free-admission contemporary art centre draws more than 10,000 visitors a year and has been voted Best Art Gallery in East Boulder County ten years running. Solo exhibition proposals from established and emerging artists in all mediums are welcome, as are group exhibitions and curatorial proposals. An exhibitions committee of artists, arts administrators, business professionals, curators and collectors reviews submissions; preference goes to culturally relevant work with a unique perspective that offers a diverse art experience, and cutting-edge contemporary and multi-disciplinary practices are strongly encouraged. Open to all artists in the continental US, with a stated commitment to artists across race, gender, gender variance, sexual orientation, national origin, age, religion, political affiliation and disability. Teams submit one résumé of no more than one page per member.
calls.summary: Solo, group and curatorial proposals for a Colorado contemporary art centre's 2027/28 season — all media, continental US.

calls.title: 2027 Call for Exhibit Proposals
calls.description: The Museum of Northern California Art (monca) in Chico invites Northern California artists to propose a solo or small group exhibition for its Phillips Gallery, a 32 by 27 foot space. Four slots are offered across 2027, running six to eight weeks each between March 2027 and January 2028, with opening receptions on the Friday of the first week. Artwork must have been produced primarily in Northern California and the artist must currently live in one of the eligible counties; work previously exhibited at monca is not eligible and AI-generated work is excluded. Applications are reviewed by monca's exhibition committee of six artists and collectors, and ask for 8 to 12 images of proposed or representative works, an artist statement, a proposal narrative setting out the vision and thematic focus of the show (including any equipment or electrical needs), and a CV. Artists install and deinstall their own work. The museum does not actively market artwork but keeps a price list at reception and takes 50% commission on any sales.
calls.summary: Solo or small group show at a Chico museum's Phillips Gallery — four 2027 slots for Northern California artists.

calls.title: Echoes of Valor
calls.description: Artspiration Frederick's first veteran art exhibition, on view in the Artspiration Gallery in Frederick, Maryland from November 6 to 29, 2026, honouring the creative voices and lived experiences of military veterans, military families, and artists exploring themes of military service. Original work in any visual medium is welcome, including photography, printmaking, painting, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, and the exhibition seeks a diverse range of voices, perspectives and techniques. Eligible artists must be a US military veteran of any branch, active duty, reserve or National Guard, a military family member, or a civilian artist whose work addresses military or veteran themes; entrants must reside in the continental US. Up to three pieces may be submitted and all three may be selected. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Accepted work is dropped off October 26–27 or shipped to arrive by October 26, with an artists' reception on November 14. Accepted images are also shown in a concurrent online exhibit.
calls.summary: First veteran art exhibition at a Frederick, MD non-profit gallery — open to veterans, military families and service-themed work.

calls.title: 35 Under 35 — 2nd Annual Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Second annual 35 Under 35 exhibition from the Blacksburg Regional Art Association, a 150-member group founded in 1950, in collaboration with community galleries and the Center for the Arts at Virginia Tech. The show exists to put emerging artists on the walls of established gallery and museum spaces and to help them find their way into the wider art community of curators, gallery owners and collectors. Thirty-five works are selected and shown November 2 to 20, 2026 at the Center for the Arts on the Virginia Tech campus, with an artist and awards reception on November 20. Juror Laura K. Higgins, Curator of the Permanent Collection and Special Projects Officer at the Taubman Museum of Art — previously at Tanya Bonakdar Gallery, Gladstone Gallery and Petzel in New York — presents Best in Show ($300), 2nd Place ($200), 3rd Place ($100) and honourable mentions at her discretion. Open to artists living in Virginia who have not turned 35 by November 2, 2026; any medium except AI-generated work. The $5 fee covers up to three works. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 40 inches in either direction.
jury: Laura K. Higgins, Curator of the Permanent Collection and Special Projects Officer, Taubman Museum of Art
calls.summary: Virginia artists under 35 juried into the Center for the Arts at Virginia Tech by a Taubman Museum curator. $5 entry.

calls.title: 51st Juried Annual Exhibition
calls.description: The Miller Art Museum in Sturgeon Bay opens its 51st Juried Annual, the Door County institution’s long-running survey of two-dimensional work by artists living in Wisconsin. It is open to artists 18 and over at every career stage, from emerging to established professional, and accepts original hangable 2D work in any media made within the past two years — photography very much included; the 2026 prospectus cover pairs Nika McKagen’s silver gelatin print with an oil painting. A panel of jurors reviews projected digital entries, and $1,950 in cash awards is presented at the opening reception on September 18: the Gerhard Miller Award of Excellence ($500), three Special Merit Awards ($250 each), three Juror’s Choice Awards ($200 each) and the Bonnie Hartmann Award for Outstanding Creativity ($100). Work may not exceed 48 x 48 x 5 inches including framing, must be a single unit (no diptychs or triptychs) and cannot have been shown previously in Door County; giclée and other reproductions are not eligible, nor is work made under a teacher’s direction in a class or workshop. The exhibition runs September 18 to November 7, 2026. Work may or may not be offered for sale; the museum retains a 40% commission on sales.
calls.summary: Wisconsin artists at any career stage juried into a Door County museum’s 51st annual. $1,950 in awards, $30 for two works.

calls.title: Día de Muertos 2026 — Remembering Is Resistance
calls.description: For its 2026 Día de Muertos exhibition, Recordar es Resistir / Remembering Is Resistance, Longmont’s Firehouse Art Center pairs artists with community members affected by US immigration policy so that each work carries a real story, told safely and anonymously. Selected artists are then paired with a community member and translate that person’s words and experience into a piece for the Main Gallery, where the show sits as both reflection and provocation. Accepted mediums include photography, digital art, painting, drawing, collage, mixed media, text-based work, sculpture, installation, fibre and touchable or interactive work. The centre asks for practices that confront, reflect on or challenge political realities, global or deeply personal, and states plainly that credentials matter less than passion and messaging. Applicants send a single PDF holding a 200-word bio, a 200-word statement and five images. There is no entry fee. The call is addressed to artists in the Longmont area aged 18 and over, and work is hand-delivered on October 5 and 6. Community members need no paperwork and are compensated for their time; translators are provided for anyone who prefers to apply or work in another language. The Firehouse waives its commission entirely and splits any sale equally between artist and community member. The exhibition runs October 9 to November 1, 2026, opening with a reception on October 9.
calls.summary: Longmont art centre pairs artists with community members affected by immigration policy. Free to enter, sales split 50/50.

calls.title: PLAYFUL
calls.description: Arc Gallery's 2027 national juried exhibition, built around the playful spirit — light-hearted, lively, spontaneous work full of fun, amusement and wit, taking its cue from Claes Oldenburg. The gallery is looking for creative play and grown-up mischief: bright colour, whimsical typography, funny imagery, sly innuendo, interactive works that invite audience participation, work that captures street art or spontaneous street photography, and work that expresses child-like wonder and game-play. Photography is among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art and artist books; jewellery, video, film, performance and works needing an external power source are not accepted. Juried by Jennifer Farris, owner of STUDIO Gallery in San Francisco. Three works judged the most imaginative interpretations of the theme each receive $250, a juror's award ribbon, a recognition certificate and the show catalogue; all selected work, gallery and online, appears in the exhibition catalogue. Entry is $35 for one to three images, maximum two entries per artist. Open to artists residing in the United States. Exhibition runs June 19 – July 17, 2027 at Arc Gallery, 1246 Folsom Street, San Francisco.
jury: Jennifer Farris, Owner, STUDIO Gallery, San Francisco

calls.title: Call for Solo or Group Exhibits 2027
calls.description: Huron Valley Arts, a 501(c)(3) arts council serving Michigan's Huron Valley communities for over 25 years, is taking proposals for its 2027 gallery year in Steeple Hall, the exhibition space inside the historic Highland Station House. The call is open to all artists, groups and curators working in any traditional or non-traditional visual arts medium — photography is explicitly among the accepted media — with no restriction on genre, subject matter or content. Artists may apply individually or as a cohesive group through a designated leader. Those selected exhibit for roughly one to two months, and HVA provides advertising plus a 'Meet the Artist' wine and appetizer reception planned in collaboration with the artist. Applicants submit 8–20 images; up to four entries per artist. Hanging works are limited to 25 lbs and 48 inches in any direction, work must be hand-delivered, and unsold pieces collected in person; the gallery suggests pricing in the $100–$500 range, which sells best at the venue. The jury fee is $30, with scholarships available to waive it on request. Applying early is encouraged — HVA reserves the option of contracting with artists before the published notification date.
calls.summary: One-to-two-month solo or group shows in Michigan's historic Steeple Hall Gallery, with reception and advertising. $30, waivers available.

calls.title: Small Works Members Show
calls.description: Woman Made Gallery's end-of-year small-works exhibition, open to all current WMG members of any gender working in any medium — photography included. Each artist submits JPEGs of three works, one of which is guaranteed a place in the show. Work must measure 20 inches or under on its longest side, be priced at $400 or less and listed for sale, and must not have been previously shown at WMG; recent work is encouraged but not required, and a general artist's statement is needed. Selected by the WMG Program Committee. The exhibition runs November 21 – December 19, 2026 at the gallery on South Halsted Street in Chicago. Entry is free with membership; WMG has presented hundreds of exhibitions since 1992 and remains one of the longest-running feminist art spaces in the United States.

calls.title: Photography Now 2027
calls.fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work
calls.description: International photography exhibition at CICA Museum, the contemporary art museum in Gimpo, South Korea, open to artists worldwide. The call spans traditional and digital photography through experimental practice, framed around photography's role as representation, medium, expression and communication. Submission is free by email — up to five JPEGs and/or three video links plus a bio. Selected digital works are printed on A3 foam board and installed by the museum's curators; artists sending physical prints or installation pieces ship at their own cost and are asked to keep 2D work under 1 m on the longest side. Accepted artists contribute $78 USD (110,000 KRW) per work toward show processing and maintenance. The exhibition runs April 7–25, 2027 at the museum.
calls.summary: Free-to-enter international show at Korea's CICA Museum; accepted artists pay $78 per work. Exhibition April 7–25, 2027.

calls.title: Mythos Negra — Dark Myths
calls.description: Juried exhibition at ShadowBoxX Gallery in Waukegan, north of Chicago, for artists working in analog media. Mythos Negra explores the shadowed realms of myth, superstition and folklore that emerge from humanity's deepest fears — the femme fatale whose allure brings ruin, the tragic figure complicit in their own downfall, the wrathful deity dispensing arbitrary punishment. Personal myths and ritual are equally welcome. Eligible work includes film-based and darkroom photography alongside painting, printmaking, sculpture, collage, textile and other physically produced processes; digital artwork, digital manipulation and AI-generated work are not considered. Founded by artist Michael E. Voss, the gallery runs monthly group and solo shows and says it works to keep artists' shipping and display costs down.
calls.summary: Chicago-area gallery show on dark myth and folklore — analog media only; film and darkroom photography welcome, no digital or AI.

calls.title: America the Bountiful — Photography Show 2026
calls.description: Annual juried photography show at the Coastal Arts League's public gallery on Main Street in Half Moon Bay, a volunteer-run nonprofit that has served the Coastside for over forty years. This year's theme is America the Bountiful; prints on any surface are welcome, up to three entries per artist. Open to Bay Area artists 18 and over, with work hand-delivered September 28 and collected November 2. Three merit awards of $150, $100 and $50 are given. All exhibited work must be for sale and must not have been shown recently at the gallery; the League retains a 30% commission. The show runs October 1 – November 2, 2026 with a reception on October 3.

calls.title: Lines & Layers
calls.description: Fall juried show in the light-filled second-floor galleries of Falkirk Cultural Center, an 1888 Queen Anne estate on eleven acres in San Rafael, listed on the National Historic Register and run by the City of San Rafael since 1974. Lines guide the eye and define form; layers add depth, texture and history — artists are invited to explore either or the relationship between the two, from patterns in nature to bold geometric composition and richly textured surfaces. Photography is welcome alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, fiber and mixed media. Open to artists living in the nine Bay Area counties, with up to three works made in the past two years and not previously shown at Falkirk. The exhibition runs September 11 – October 23, 2026, opening during San Rafael's Art Walk.
calls.summary: Bay Area juried show in a historic 1888 San Rafael mansion; photography welcome. Exhibition September 11 – October 23.

calls.title: That's Absurd.
calls.description: Absurdist open call from the Alliance for the Arts, the nonprofit visual and performing arts centre on McGregor Boulevard in Fort Myers, running since 1975. The show invites work that treads the line between meaning and meaninglessness — collapsing expectations, twisting logic, turning the familiar unrecognisable. Surreal imagery, exaggerated forms, inconclusive narratives and playful disruptions of reality are all fair game, in serious humour and methodical chaos. Open to all artists everywhere, one to three works, with photography among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, glass, printmaking, fiber and digital media. Absurdest in Show takes a $200 cash award, with four Most Absurd prizes across figurative, food-related, 2D and 3D work. On display November 6–28, 2026.
calls.summary: Absurdist juried show at Fort Myers' Alliance for the Arts — photography welcome, $200 Absurdest in Show. On view Nov 6–28.

calls.description: Long-running juried show and sale from the Aurora Artists Guild, a volunteer nonprofit of photographers and 2-D artists in Aurora, Colorado. Photography has its own dedicated category — traditional, digital or computer-enhanced — judged alongside separate 2-D and Miniatures categories, with up to three works per category and nine in total. Janet Schreiner jurors all three. Awards for photography are Best of Show, 1st, 2nd, 3rd and honourable mentions, with monetary awards and gifts set by entry numbers and sponsor contributions. Accepted work is hand-delivered to Aurora Central Library on October 31; only Miniatures may be mailed. The show runs November 6 – December 4, 2026, with the reception and awards ceremony on November 7.
calls.summary: Colorado juried show with its own photography category, at Aurora Central Library November 6 – December 4.

calls.title: Quinn Emanuel Silicon Valley Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Silicon Valley office in Redwood Shores for emerging and mid-career artists working in any medium, including photography. Two artists are selected per cycle and each receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus a materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency begins November 2026; a one-month exhibition follows, mounted with curator Alexis Hyde in a venue agreed with the artists, and work may be offered for sale. The studio is an office inside the Silicon Valley location, in a 24/7 keycard-access building with parking if needed. Open only to artists living in the greater Bay Area, as regular in-person studio use is expected; international artists may apply but must secure their own visas. Preference goes to underrepresented artists in the early or middle stages of their career. No education requirement, and the firm will make accommodations for disabled artists. Apply by email with a 500-word proposal, a CV and an 8–10 image portfolio as a single PDF under 20MB.
jury: John Quinn, Founding Partner, Quinn Emanuel
calls.summary: $20,000 + $1,500 materials for a 4-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Silicon Valley office. Bay Area artists only.

calls.title: Opulent Mobility 2026
calls.description: Opulent Mobility is an international annual exhibit that asks artists to re-imagine disability as opulent and powerful rather than merely functional. The 2026 focus is disabled joy — as the call puts it, at a time when rights are being dismantled and images erased, deliberate acts of joy are powerful and essential. Curated by founder A. Laura Brody with disability arts activist and photographer Anthony Tusler, and supported by the Numotion Foundation. Two-dimensional and sculptural work, music files and performances on digital media are all accepted; photographers may submit digital files rather than shipping prints, which makes the show genuinely open to international entrants. A flat $20 fee covers gallery rental and insurance for up to ten works, and is waived on request if it causes hardship. The exhibit runs December 6–20, 2026 in person in Los Angeles and online; the gallery takes 30% of any sale. Accessibility is built in: artwork descriptions in text and audio, and ASL interpreters at the opening and the online artist talk.
jury: Anthony Tusler, Disability Arts Activist & Photographer
calls.summary: Disabled joy: international exhibit re-imagining disability as opulent. $20 for 10 works, waived on request; digital files welcome.

calls.title: Women United ART PRIZE 2026 — Photography & Printmaking
calls.description: Annual international prize for women-identifying artists, with a dedicated Photography & Printmaking category covering all types of photography and printmaking including cyanotype. First place in each category receives USD 500 cash, an in-depth interview in Women United Art Magazine Special Edition 2026, a podcast interview, a virtual solo exhibition with 3D gallery tour, an artist directory profile, a USD 250 printing gift card, and free entries to 2027 opportunities. Second and third place receive interviews, an online group exhibit and virtual 3D tour. Places 4–10 are featured in the magazine and group exhibit. Regular entries close 31 August; a last-minute phase runs 1–15 September at higher fees. Fee waivers available for artists in countries affected by war, natural disaster, or the suppression of women’s rights.
jury: Mona Lerch, Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Women United ART MOVEMENT
Victoria J. Fry, Founder, Visionary Art Collective & New Visionary Magazine

calls.title: Around, Above, Below
calls.description: Group exhibition at Van Der Plas Gallery on Manhattan’s Lower East Side exploring perception and the experience of daily life as we move through urban environments, rural landscapes and the spaces in between. Artists working in all media are encouraged to submit, including photography. On view 15–28 October 2026 with an opening reception on 15 October, 6–8pm. Submissions form part of the gallery’s year-round Open Call Program and remain in consideration for future exhibitions beyond this cycle.

All rights to the photographs remain with the photographer and files are used only for the book printing. Photographers are notified 7–10 days after the deadline. Apply by paying the entry fee via PayPal and emailing your entry.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery

calls.title: Emerging Berlin
calls.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, dedicated to supporting and showcasing image-makers with a distinctive visual language whose photographic practice embodies, represents and shapes a part of Berlin. Selected artists are given a platform at Fotografiska Berlin through solo or group exhibitions. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — the definition is not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and includes self-taught artists and those working outside traditional pathways. The call has run on an ongoing basis since 12 March 2026; submissions are reviewed by the jury every six months, followed by a curation period of up to two weeks. Open to anyone 18 or over — the Berlin connection is a criterion for the work, not a residency requirement.
calls.summary: Rolling Fotografiska open call for image-makers whose practice shapes a part of Berlin. Free, leads to museum exhibitions.

calls.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, running since 2023 and dedicated to supporting and showcasing early-career image-makers from across Sweden. Roughly three artists a year are invited to present their work within Fotografiska Stockholm’s exhibition programme, alongside opportunities for professional dialogue and development. Material is reviewed on an ongoing basis throughout the year, and only artists whose work moves forward in the internal review are contacted. Applicants must be 18 or over and based in Sweden. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and including self-taught artists.
calls.summary: Rolling Fotografiska open call for emerging image-makers based in Sweden. Free, leads to Fotografiska Stockholm exhibitions.

calls.title: Fire
calls.description: Fire as an elemental force but also as an idea. The gallery invites photographic work that engages with fire as metaphor, condition and experience rather than simply as subject matter — images that consider the elemental through the psychological, the social, the environmental or the poetic. Work that reveals fire through gesture, light, atmosphere, colour, landscape, portraiture, abstraction or narrative is welcome, where the photograph evokes rather than describes. Not every fire burns. Open to photographers of all levels, in colour or black and white. Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space in Raleigh from September 4 to 30, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4, and is then presented on the gallery website year-round. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed in-house on the gallery's Canon imagePROGRAF Pro-1100.
calls.summary: Raleigh gallery show on fire as metaphor and condition, not subject. Juror Robbie Bailey. September exhibition in Gallery X.

Reduced rates of €15 (early bird) or €20 apply for students, unwaged applicants and those from low-income economies. Early bird deadline September 7, final deadline September 14. calls.title: Guildford Festival of the Arts 2026
calls.description: Open call for the 2026 edition of this Surrey arts festival, accepting any visual art of any medium that can be displayed in a gallery or on a screen — photography included. There is no set theme. Two tracks run in parallel: an Open Call for artists aged 18 and over, and a separate Student Open Call. The 2026 judging panel is Sally Varah MBE DL, Councillor Jane Tyson (Mayor of Guildford), artist Monica Popham and photographer Andy Newbold. Everyone's first submission is free; further artworks go through a separate paid form. Alongside the £1,000 first prize there is a £500 runner-up prize, a £150 gift voucher for the student winner and an exhibition at New House Art Space for the Public Vote winner. Selected artists are notified by email in late August or early September and may sell work through the festival team during the festival, on which a 15% commission is retained to fund the following year's edition. Artists should submit once; a series, diptych or triptych should be sent as a single image encompassing the whole piece. The inaugural 2025 festival drew over 2,400 visits across 20 venues.
jury: Councillor Jane Tyson, Mayor of Guildford

calls.title: Pretty Ugly — Student Photography Competition 2026/27
calls.description: A darkroom print competition asking students to explore the idea that ugliness is often just a matter of perspective. A rough texture, an unusual face, a forgotten space — under the right conditions the overlooked becomes extraordinary, and perceived imperfections such as scars, wear and age can tell powerful stories of resilience and character. Entrants are challenged to question first impressions and capture their own interpretation of 'pretty ugly'. All images must be shot on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white film and hand-printed by the student in the darkroom on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white papers; digital submissions are not accepted and prints must be posted with an entry label firmly attached to the back of each. Minimum print size is 8x10 inches, and images that have won other competitions or been published by a third party are not eligible. Multiple entries are encouraged, and lecturers may bundle a class's prints in one package. Open to students of any age anywhere in the world taking a full or part-time course at a school, college or university; prints go to HARMAN technology in Mobberley, Cheshire, or to its Seattle address. ILFORD points students without darkroom access to its Pop-Up Darkrooms and community darkroom locator.
calls.summary: Free worldwide student darkroom competition on beauty in the overlooked. ILFORD/Kentmere film and paper, prints posted in.

calls.title: Let Our Hearts Speak
calls.description: Open call for a collective publication from Rethinking Eastern Europe, an artist collective founded in 2024 by Polish visual artist Zula Rabikowska that now gathers around 50 artists from Central and Eastern Europe, the Balkans and the diaspora. Taking its title from bell hooks — 'when we love we can let our hearts speak' — the call invites work that engages with 'Eastern Europe' as a lived, shifting and often contested space: not only geography, but memory, inheritance, migration and emotional landscape. The publication brings together visual and written works reflecting on intimacy, love, identity, displacement and belonging, and understands the region as plural and expansive, shaped by diasporas, post-socialist realities and personal archives. Open to artists of any age, nationality, location and career stage, including those working outside institutions. Published in collective print and digital formats with careful artist attribution; fee waivers are available on request.
jury: Diane Smyth, Editor, British Journal of Photography
Max Gorbatskyi, Curator, Open Eye Gallery
Zula Rabikowska, Artist & Founder, Rethinking Eastern Europe
calls.summary: Collective publication on Eastern Europe as memory, migration and belonging. £150 first prize, portfolio review, fee waivers.

calls.title: James Balog Earth Vision Awards
calls.description: Juried prizes supporting photographers responding to today's complex environmental issues, organised and produced by the Denver Art Museum with funds endowed by James Balog and other donors, and awarded every two years. The awards recognise sustained commitment and significant accomplishment in photography that bears witness to the relationship between humans and the environment and challenges people to build healthier, more sustainable relationships with nature. A three-member jury of expert photo professionals reviews all entries and may contact entrants for clarification before final decisions; fabricated photographs, cloning, excessive colour manipulation and AI-generated content are not considered. First prize is $40,000 ($30,000 on award, $10,000 twelve to eighteen months later) and the finalist receives $25,000 ($19,000 on award, $6,000 later). Applicants submit a portfolio of 10 to 20 photographs — falling outside that range is grounds for disqualification — with an artist statement describing firsthand experience and the environmental significance of the work, an explanation of the intended project and its anticipated impact, and a resume or exhibition history. Open to photographers worldwide aged 21 or over; previous winners and finalists are not eligible. The call opens September 1, 2026, winners are announced in January 2027, and awards are presented at the Denver Art Museum in March 2027.
calls.summary: $40,000 biennial award from the Denver Art Museum for photographers responding to environmental issues. Opens September 1.

calls.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, for artists who have declared their independence from portraying reality — abstract work built on line, shape, colour, form and gestural mark, from drip paintings and colour fields to geometric designs and abstract patterns found in nature, architecture and human activity. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027.

Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media and fully experimental work. Studio ACE is an arts-education nonprofit founded in 2016 that runs free art programmes for neurodivergent children, teens and adults; ACE Gallery, its exhibition space, opened in early 2024 and shows both emerging and established artists. Submit 3 to 20 works. Accepted work is notified August 21, with drop-off September 11–12. Exhibition runs September 19 – October 22, 2026, with an opening reception on September 19.

What distinguishes it from a typical juried show is the award structure: ADC puts the total at over $450,000, though most of that is its own services valued in-house rather than cash — ten gallery representation contracts valued at $8,500 each, two solo shows, six group shows, print and digital magazine features and SmartSell memberships, alongside $74,100 in juror awards and $175,000 in purchase awards. The jury is drawn from ADC's own staff — president Litsa Spanos, gallery director Annie Kautz, marketing director Amy Scalia and assistant gallery director Chance Smith — with more jurors to be announced. Entry is $25 per work, with the last entry free on applications of four or more. Results are announced October 2, work arrives at the gallery by October 16, and the opening night and awards ceremony fall on November 7.

calls.title: Changing Asia 2026
calls.description: The Changing Asia photo exhibition, organised by China Daily with the Asia News Network, returns with the theme "Moments of Connection: Smiles and Hands of the Asia-Pacific" — a phrase drawn from the 2026 APEC leaders' meeting slogan, and a brief that asks for real interactions: collaboration, trade, mutual assistance, cultural exchange. Within that frame the call keeps its long-standing threads — the social, economic, environmental and cultural shifts reshaping the continent, stories of resilience told through individual communities, and Asia's diversity documented in its contrasts as much as its connections. Entry is free and open to photographers worldwide; work must have been made since 1 January 2023, and basic colour correction and filters are accepted. Selected images are shown in the exhibition, published in the accompanying photo book and awarded a certificate. Earlier editions launched in Bangkok (2022) and Jakarta (2023) before moving online in 2024, which drew over 1,400 submissions from more than 40 countries. The 2026 exhibition opens on 26 October at the Shenzhen Research Institute of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, ahead of the APEC meeting.
calls.summary: Free worldwide call from China Daily and the Asia News Network on connection across the Asia-Pacific. Exhibition plus a photo book.

calls.title: The In Between
calls.description: Detroit-rooted online gallery Ninety-Seven Modern invites emerging artists to submit black-and-white work exploring the transient nature of the in between — the dual realities most of us live in at any given moment: recollection and the present, anger and love, stagnation and momentum. Black and white is framed as a reminder that both can exist together, with or without a fight for dominance. All mediums are welcome. Entry is a flat $5 for up to three works, submitted by email with a third-person bio; the gallery does not accept AI-generated imagery. Ninety-Seven Modern also lists selected artists' original works for sale through its shop.

calls.title: The Quiet Image II
calls.description: Second edition of The Quiet Image at The Ace Project, a contemporary photography space on Zaagmolendrift in Rotterdam. The call asks photographers based in the Netherlands and Belgium for work exploring the relationship between nature and the human body. Up to five works may be submitted by email for review; submission is free. Selected photographers are invited for a personal conversation at the gallery, and their work must be professionally printed and framed at their own cost — participation also carries a contribution fee towards exhibition costs, which the gallery does not publish in advance. The exhibition runs 25 September to 18 October 2026.

calls.description: Tenth annual national juried exhibition at the Lexis Gallery, Trinity Cathedral in Sacramento, a progressive Episcopal community that runs the show as an open conversation about faith rather than a devotional display. The 2026 theme is 'Living Water' — work that explicitly references faith and work simply in conversation with the spirituality the theme suggests are equally welcome. All media including photography; juried by Ryan M. Reynolds, Chair of Art and Art History at Santa Clara University. $5,000 in cash awards: $3,000 first place, $1,500 second, $500 honorable mention. Open to US artists with original work made in the last five years and not exhibited in Sacramento within the last two. Exhibition runs 3 October – 8 November 2026 with an opening reception on 3 October.
jury: Ryan M. Reynolds, Chair of Art and Art History, Santa Clara University
calls.summary: 'Living Water' at Trinity Cathedral's Lexis Gallery, Sacramento. $5,000 in cash awards, juried by Ryan M. Reynolds. US artists.

calls.title: Confluence of Art Annual 2026
calls.description: Free-to-enter juried annual at the James Hansen Gallery inside Pablo Center at the Confluence, the arts centre where the Chippewa and Eau Claire rivers meet in western Wisconsin. Around 50 pieces are selected across 2D, 3D and multimedia from artists in the Chippewa Valley, the Midwest and beyond, and a judge picks four of them for cash prizes announced at the October awards reception. Up to three pieces per artist, original and made in the last five years, not previously shown at Pablo Center within two years. Submissions go by email with a bio or statement, title, size, medium and price. Work is dropped off 1–8 September; the exhibition runs 28 September – 22 November 2026, awards reception 9 October. Gallery commission is 40%, or 30% for Pablo Center members.
calls.summary: Free juried annual at Pablo Center's Hansen Gallery, Eau Claire WI. ~50 works in all media, cash prizes for four, show Sep 28–Nov 22.

calls.title: 14th Annual Eastern West Virginia Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Annual open-theme juried exhibition at Berkeley Art Works, the Berkeley Arts Council's gallery in downtown Martinsburg. Open to artists 18 and over living in Berkeley, Grant, Hampshire, Hardy, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan or Pendleton County — a deliberately regional show for the eastern panhandle and highlands of West Virginia. Original two- or three-dimensional work in any medium or technique, abstract, representational or non-representational, completed in the last three years and not previously exhibited at Berkeley Art Works. Juried by Sonya Evanisko, Professor of Art and Painting/Drawing Coordinator at Shepherd University, who selects a Best in Show, a Merit Award and an Honorable Mention. On view 24 September – 15 November 2026.
jury: Sonya Evanisko, Professor of Art, Shepherd University
calls.summary: Open-theme juried show at Berkeley Art Works, Martinsburg, for artists in eight eastern West Virginia counties. Juror Sonya Evanisko.

calls.title: Figuratively Speaking
calls.org: Wallkill River Center for the Arts
calls.description: Regional exhibition on the human figure at the Wallkill River Center for the Arts in Montgomery, in New York's Hudson Valley. The call asks how we see ourselves and how we see others: 'With all the special attributes that make each of us an individual, the one truth that we can't get around is that we all share humanity, for better or worse. Tell us a story.' Juried by painter John McGiff (BFA SUNY Purchase, MFA University of Pennsylvania, two Delaware Division of the Arts painting fellowships). One entry of up to four pieces per artist, $25, waived for WRCA artist members. Open to US residents 18 and over; work must be hand delivered by 8 November — no shipping. AI-generated work and reproductions such as giclée prints of paintings are not accepted. 2D works up to 30 inches wide by 40 inches high including the frame, priced by the artist between $200 and $9,000. Gallery takes 30% commission; exhibition runs 14 November – 20 December 2026.
calls.summary: The human figure, juried by painter John McGiff, at the Wallkill River Center for the Arts in the Hudson Valley. $25, hand delivery.

calls.title: Backwards/Forwards
calls.description: Juried exhibition of handmade prints at Light Art Space in Silver City, New Mexico, staged as the juried show of the Southwest Print Fiesta. The brief asks artists to treat time as material — memory, pressure, inheritance, repetition, rupture and possibility — looking backward at the histories that shape us and forward at futures we imagine or fear. All work must be handmade prints made by the artist in the last five years using traditional printmaking and/or photographic processes: silver gelatin, photopolymer and copperplate gravure, cyanotype, vandyke, gum bichromate, palladium, platinum, carbon, salt, chemigram, lumen, argyrotype, oil print, chlorophyll, instant transfers and lifts, alongside etching, woodcut, lithography, screenprint and letterpress. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Digital processes are allowed only where meaningfully integrated with handmade methods; AI-generated and purely digital prints are ineligible. Juror Terran J. Last Gun, Piikani artist based in Santa Fe and an Art in America 2026 New Talent. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over. $35 for three works, $10 per additional piece up to ten, $20 for full-time students. Work must arrive ready to hang but framing is not required. Exhibition runs 8 October – 7 November 2026 with a reception and juror talk on 9 October; gallery takes 50% on sales and artists cover shipping both ways.
calls.summary: Handmade prints as a record of time — cyanotype to letterpress — juried by Terran J. Last Gun at New Mexico’s alt-process gallery.

calls.title: PhEST Portfolio Reviews 2026
calls.description: Free portfolio reviews at PhEST – See Beyond the Sea, the international photography and contemporary art festival in Monopoli, Puglia. Reviews run 8 August (3–6pm) and 9 August (10am–1pm) at the Saint Leonardo Monastery, in 20-minute one-to-one sessions; each photographer can book up to three reviews, one per reviewer. Completed projects and work in progress are both welcome, presented as prints or on a device. The 2026 reviewers are Josh Lustig, picture editor at FT Weekend Magazine; Erik Vroons, writer and editor at Over Magazine; Veronica Daltri, photo editor at Il Manifesto; Krzysztof Candrowicz, curator and co-founder of Łódź Fotofestiwal; artist and curator Francesca Seravalle; and Hannah Watson, director of Trolley Books. Sessions with Lustig, Vroons, Candrowicz and Watson are held in English only. Registration is free and online until 2 August, with limited on-site places from 10 minutes before each session.

calls.title: Photobook Open Call ZUM/IMS 2026
calls.description: Annual photobook call from ZUM magazine, the contemporary art department and the Photography Library of the Instituto Moreira Salles in São Paulo, running since 2017 to deepen the institute’s links with contemporary photography publishing. Open to publications released from October 2025 onwards, from any country, from publishers of any size or self-published — dummies and prototypes are not accepted. Entry is free and open to any nationality. Selected publications each receive R$300 towards costs, are presented during Festival ZUM in November 2026 and stay on display in the IMS Photography Library; a panel of external guests and IMS staff then awards the three best publications R$2,000 each. Enter through the online form and post or hand-deliver a copy to IMS Paulista — books must arrive by 26 September 2026. All submitted publications are accessioned into the IMS Photography Library and catalogued for public consultation unless the author asks for the copy back within 30 days of the shortlist.
calls.summary: Free photobook call from ZUM and Instituto Moreira Salles — R$2,000 each to three winners, shown at Festival ZUM in São Paulo.

calls.title: Duets: A Collab Show
calls.description: Collaboration-only show at the Avondale Arts Center, the volunteer-run gallery of the Avondale Arts Alliance just east of Atlanta. Every work in the September–October exhibition must be made by exactly two artists together; entrants can submit up to six pieces and may pair with a different collaborator on each one. Work that does not meet the two-artist rule is disqualified. Only one of the two collaborators submits the entry. Entry is $15 for up to three pieces and $30 for up to six, paid by Square link; artists 18 and under enter free with a voucher code, and the alliance asks anyone facing financial hardship to get in touch. Open to Atlanta and surrounding artists, and work must be hand delivered on 5–6 September — no shipping. Status emails by 29 August; exhibition runs 12 September – 24 October 2026 with a closing reception. All work must be for sale and the alliance retains 30%.
calls.summary: Atlanta-area show where every piece must be made by two artists together. Up to six collaborations, hand delivery only.

calls.title: Wild & Domestic 2026
calls.description: All-media juried exhibition about animals — wild and domestic — at the Medford Arts Center, a 501(c)(3) community arts centre on North Main Street in Medford, New Jersey, funded in part by the New Jersey State Council on the Arts. Juror of awards is Terri Amig; chairs are Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Open to artists 18 and over, up to three original pieces each, none previously shown at MAC. calls.title: Circuito OFF 2026
calls.description: The free and independent section of NARNIMMAGINARIA, the photography festival staged in the historic centre of Narni, Umbria, and run by the Associazione culturale SATOR. Now in its 11th edition, the 2026 theme is "Through human landscapes": the traces people leave in the places they inhabit and reshape, and the invisible territories of their stories and emotions. Documentary, narrative, conceptual, artistic and experimental readings are all admitted, and entry is open to photographers of any age, nationality or background. Three categories: Single Shot, a single photograph, with fine-art printing and installation handled entirely by the organisers; Triptych, three photographs or a single panel supplied already printed and hung in the bars, restaurants, shops and other businesses of the centre rather than in galleries, with installation optionally delegated to the organisers for €35; and Stories, a printed sequence of 8 to 18 images at 30×40 cm, framed by the organisers. Entrants can apply to one, two or all three categories and submit more than one work in each, paying a €15 contribution per category. Everything goes by email as a single ZIP folder. The exhibition runs 17 October to 2 November 2026; printed works are due 8 October.
calls.summary: Narni's independent festival section: single shots, triptychs or series shown across the historic centre in October.

calls.title: ROOTS
calls.description: Second open call from Fototeka, a Romanian analog photography hub and publisher, for a new collective printed volume following its first book Sequence 01, which brought together 93 photographers. The theme is ROOTS — origin, belonging, memory and connection, read literally or metaphorically: natural elements, portraits, archives, rituals, personal and collective histories. Roots usually remain hidden, yet they shape what becomes visible. Only film-based photography is eligible; digital and AI-generated images are excluded. Up to ten analog photographs per submission, minimum 3000 pixels on the long side. The 50 RON (about €10) fee supports the editorial, design, printing and presentation work and does not guarantee inclusion: the curatorial team sequences the book, so a submission may end up represented by no photographs, one, or several. Selected work may also be featured on Fototeka's online platforms. The album is planned for October–November 2026.
calls.summary: Film-only open call for Fototeka's second collective printed volume on origin, belonging and memory. ~€10.

calls.title: Under Many Moons: Asian and Pacific Islander Art, Identity, and Community
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Sebastopol Center for the Arts presented with AAPIC North Bay and the Many Moons Festival, the annual autumn gathering in Sebastopol that uplifts Asian American and Pacific Islander culture, creativity and community. The show explores identity, heritage, belonging and cultural expression. While it centres AAPI voices and perspectives, artists of all backgrounds engaging thoughtfully with the themes are invited to submit work reflecting personal and collective narratives shaped by culture, place and lived experience. All media, photography included. Entry is $35 for one application of up to three images, with $10 for each additional application. Work must fit through a 7' by 7' gallery door and on an 8-foot wall; the centre's installation team can hang selected pieces. Juror Patricia Wakida is a community historian, linoleum block carver and letterpress printer who apprenticed as a papermaker in Gifu, Japan. Work must have been made in the last five years and not shown at SebArts before. Notifications 14 August; exhibition runs 26 September – 11 October 2026 with an opening reception on 26 September.
calls.summary: AAPI-centred juried show with AAPIC North Bay and the Many Moons Festival. Open to all backgrounds, all media.

calls.title: CCAN 2026 — 10th Annual National Juried Art Competition
calls.description: Tenth edition of the Center for Contemporary Arts' national juried competition in downtown Abilene, Texas. Over $7,000 is awarded annually across 11 media categories — including a dedicated 2D Photography (Film & Digital) category, each with a $500 first prize — plus a $750 juror's award and a $1,000 best of show. Juror Carlyn Ray is a Dallas-based glass artist known for large-scale installations. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original, made within the last three years, and the image submitted must be the piece delivered. Wall-mounted 2D work is capped at 48 inches framed on its longest dimension, wall-mounted 3D at 36 by 36 inches and freestanding 3D at 36 inches in any dimension, with a 50 lb weight limit. No video or mural work. Entry is $35 for one image and $20 for each additional, limit three. Notifications 1 September; exhibition runs 10 October – 21 November 2026, with the opening reception and awards on 10 October.

calls.title: Contemporary Figures: A National Juried Exhibition
calls.description: National juried exhibition of contemporary figurative work at LHUCA, the Louise Hopkins Underwood Center for the Arts in Lubbock, Texas. The call asks how the body is understood in relation to environment, society and technology: scientific advances have made us more aware of the composition and processes of the human body while blurring the boundaries between the human and the nonhuman, and the body remains intimately tied to identity and to how we move in space and in relation to others. Figurative work addressing a range of themes and presenting the body in unique ways is welcome. Open to painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, photography, digital art, ceramics, books and textiles; all works must hang on the wall and are capped at 36 by 36 inches, with plexiglass glazing required on anything shipped. Open to artists 18 or over living in the United States. Entry is $25 for up to two images. Cash prizes of $300, $200 and $100 plus a $50 honorable mention. Notifications 11 September 2026; the exhibition runs 2 October – 28 November 2026, with opening receptions on 2 October and 6 November during the First Friday Art Trail, which draws an estimated 5,000 visitors a month to LHUCA's galleries.
calls.summary: Figurative work — bodies, identity, technology — juried into LHUCA's Lubbock galleries. $300/$200/$100 prizes.

calls.title: Call for Proposals 2027
calls.description: LHUCA invites exhibition proposals for its 2027–2028 gallery season in Lubbock, Texas. Four galleries are available and each exhibition runs two consecutive months. All visual art media are accepted, including photography. Free to apply: submit a PDF with 5–10 digital images, an artist statement of up to 500 words, contact details and preferred dates. An artist stipend is available for travelling artists, and work can be for sale or not. Proposals are encouraged but not required to respond to the character of a particular gallery; floor plans are published alongside the call. Artists who have exhibited with LHUCA before can only reapply every five years. The galleries draw an estimated 5,000-plus visitors a month during the First Friday Art Trail.
calls.summary: Proposals for two-month solo or group shows across LHUCA's four Lubbock galleries. Free, with travel stipend.

calls.title: Chaos: An Exploration of Disorder, Meaning, and Possibility
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Bitfactory Gallery & Studios in Denver seeking two-dimensional, wall-hanging work that responds to chaos — visible or invisible, personal or collective, destructive or generative. It may appear as a fractured system, an unsettled world, a difficult relationship, a crowded mind, or the moment when certainty gives way; it may be imposed on us, created by us, or necessary before change can occur. Literal, emotional, psychological, social, symbolic and abstract approaches are all welcome. All 2D mediums qualify, including photography, painting, collage, fiber and textile, pastel, graphite and print works. Open to Colorado residents aged 18 and over; 3–10 images, $25 entry with $5 per additional image. Juror W. Max Thomason. Notifications 10 August; exhibition runs 21 August – 12 September 2026 with an opening reception on 21 August, 6–9pm.
calls.summary: Denver gallery show on chaos as system, state of mind or world. 2D wall work, photography welcome. Colorado only.

calls.title: Common Ground in the Heartland: Reflecting on America at 250
calls.description: Free-to-enter juried exhibition at the Visual Arts Center of the Washington Pavilion in Sioux Falls, marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. The centre invites artists from across the Midwest to reflect on the people, places and experiences that shape a shared story — from small towns and family farms to growing cities and tribal communities — in a region long a crossroads of cultures, traditions, industries and ideas. The exhibition explores the values, traditions and relationships that bring people together while recognising the diverse experiences that define communities, with suggested themes including community and belonging, cultural heritage, land and stewardship. All mediums are welcome, photography included, and up to five images may be submitted. Artists from the Midwest or with a connection to the region are encouraged to apply, though entry is not formally restricted, and artists at every career stage are invited. Work must not exceed 60 inches or 50 lbs and arrives ready to install; the centre insures it and splits sales 70/30 in the artist's favour. Notifications 5 August, with work due 20 August — the show then runs an unusually long 28 August 2026 – 21 February 2027.
calls.summary: Free juried show at Sioux Falls' Washington Pavilion on the Midwest at America's 250th. All media, up to 5 works.

calls.title: REBUILDING: Art as Renewal, Possibility, and Purpose
calls.description: Juried exhibition at the Art League Rhode Island Gallery and Tiernan Hallway Gallery in Pawtucket, asking how art can restore what has been fractured — making whole what has been broken, empowering what has been silenced and reclaiming what connects us. The theme is not about loss but about what gets built next: how art can reassemble meaning, mend relationships and model balance in a world seeking repair. Open to any artist 18 or over, in all 2D and 3D media; 1–5 images plus an optional video, $35 entry with $10 per additional media file. Work must be original and previously unexhibited with ALRI, and anything conceived or created with generative AI is ineligible. Jurors are Kerry Phillips, a Miami-based installation artist working with found objects and site-responsive materials, and Meaghan Kent, independent curator, founder of the nonprofit Site95 and former Deputy Director at MOCA North Miami. Awards are $500 first, $300 second and $150 third, plus two honorable mentions and a People's Choice. Notification by 4 November; exhibition runs 5 December 2026 – 17 January 2027.
calls.summary: Pawtucket juried show on repair and renewal, juried by Kerry Phillips and Meaghan Kent. $500 top award.

calls.title: Fresh Squeezed 2026 Annual Juried Show
calls.description: The Suffolk Art League's annual juried exhibition at the Suffolk Art Gallery in Suffolk, Virginia, marking the league's 50th anniversary and asking for artists' latest, never-before-seen work. Open to artists over 18 in all mediums: the gallery's own listing rules out only video and audio, though the CaFÉ entry also excludes digital, so anyone printing digitally is worth checking with first. Work must not have been previously exhibited at the gallery and must have been completed within the last two years. Members submit up to three works for $30; non-members pay $55 and full-time student non-members $50, both of which include an individual membership. First place is $500 plus the opportunity to present a one-person show at the Suffolk Art Gallery in 2027, with $300 second and $200 third. 2D work must be framed, wired or gallery-wrapped — no sawtooth hangers — and 3D work is displayed on pedestals provided by the gallery. Notifications by 25 September; exhibition runs 24 October – 4 December 2026. The league retains a 30% consignment on works sold.
calls.summary: Suffolk Art League's annual juried show. First place wins $500 and a 2027 one-person show at the gallery.

calls.title: Summertime: Long Days, Lazy Days, Gentle Breezes
calls.description: The second Juried Theme Gallery call of 2026 from the Arizona Photography Alliance, a Scottsdale-based non-profit now in its third year of online juried exhibitions. The brief is deliberately broad — summer as long days, lazy days and gentle breezes — and work in any medium is welcome, analogue, digital or alternative process, though AI-generated photography is not accepted. Independent juror Claire A. Warden, an interdisciplinary artist working in still and moving image whose cameraless abstraction has appeared in Harper's Magazine, Der Greif, Strange Fire Collective, Lenscratch and Light Work's Contact Sheet, selects one first-place winner for a $100 cash award plus two honourable mentions featured on AZPA's website and social channels. Every entrant is represented in the resulting virtual gallery — the juror picks one image from each submission — and all entrants may offer their chosen image for sale, handling any transaction directly. Open to members and non-members alike; joining brings the fee down to $25. AZPA board members may not enter. Submissions run August 1–20, 2026 through CaFÉ, with notifications on 3 September and the gallery going live on 4 September.
calls.summary: Broad summer theme, any process. Juror Claire A. Warden picks a $100 first place; every entrant appears in the online gallery.

calls.title: Seen/Unseen at Eric Fischl Gallery
calls.description: A portfolio-based call from the Arizona Photography Alliance for a gallery exhibition at the Eric Fischl Gallery, perched atop Phoenix College's Fine Arts Building with panoramic views of central Phoenix. Seen/Unseen invites the full range of photographic methods and styles — from the tangible world we perceive to the hidden meanings and emotional states we sense — and asks for a cohesive body of work rather than single images. The juror is Emilia Mickevicius, Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography in a curatorial post shared between Phoenix Art Museum and the Center for Creative Photography, previously curatorial assistant in SFMOMA's photography department, where she worked on Sightlines, Kinship: Photography and Connection and Sea Change. Selected applicants exhibit three to five works chosen from their submitted portfolio; all selected work is also presented as an online exhibition. Applicants must be current AZPA members at any level, though you need not live in Arizona — membership can be taken out at the time of applying. Accepted work must arrive exhibition-ready, shipped by 28 September or hand-delivered 29 September; the gallery retains 30% on sales. Exhibition runs 5–22 October 2026 with an opening reception on 5 October.
jury: Emilia Mickevicius, Norton Family Assistant Curator of Photography, Phoenix Art Museum & Center for Creative Photography

calls.title: 2026 Fall Members Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Wayne Art Center's autumn members' show in the Davenport Gallery outside Philadelphia, juried both for entry and for awards. Eligible media run from painting and works on paper through ceramics, glass, fiber and jewellery to photography and 3D printing, so it is one of the few regional all-media shows where lens-based work sits alongside craft. Each member may submit exactly one original work made after 1 January 2024 and not previously shown at WAC — no second CaFÉ accounts, no exceptions. The juror is Peter Van Dyck, a Philadelphia painter who trained at the Florence Academy of Art and has taught at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, with solo shows at John Pence Gallery, Eleanor Ettinger Gallery and The Grenning Gallery. Open to Wayne Art Center 2026/2027 adult members aged 18 and over; membership can be taken out before applying. All accepted work must be hand-delivered to and collected from the centre — nothing shipped. Notifications 22 August, hand delivery 1 September, exhibition 8 September – 3 October 2026, with a reception and awards presentation on 20 September.
