calls.title: Celebrating Color
calls.description: A national juried group exhibition at Edgewater Gallery, an artist-owned collective that has been part of downtown Fort Bragg on California's Mendocino Coast since 2003. The show takes colour in any form or dimension as its subject — atmosphere, emotion, memory, and the way chroma changes what we see — and the gallery says it is especially interested in work with a distinctive relationship to colour, whether through intensity, harmony, contrast, material presence or unexpected combinations. Photography is explicitly among the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, collage, fiber, sculpture and ceramics; AI-generated work, video and installation are not accepted. Open to artists 18 and over living in the United States, up to three works each, all of which must be original, for sale, and available for the full run. Two-dimensional work must be ready to hang without sawtooth hangers, and pieces must fit through a standard door. The four jurors are all working artists: ceramicist Alexis Moyer, mixed-media abstractionist Chris Hagie, painter Gwen Lowery, and Karin Denson, whose glitch-based paintings, photomontages and collages sit between nature and technology. Jury results 7 September, work due by 25 September, exhibition 1 October – 2 November 2026 with an opening reception on 2 October. The gallery takes 40% commission.
calls.summary: National juried show on colour at a Mendocino Coast artist-owned gallery. Photography welcome, no AI, four artist jurors.

calls.title: 24th National Fine Art Show
calls.description: The Peninsula Art League's annual juried show, now in its 24th year, returns to the Gig Harbor Vintage Aero Museum — a hangar of restored vintage aircraft that the League has turned into an exhibition venue. Photography and digital art are judged alongside two- and three-dimensional work, and the two jurors come from Pacific Northwest museums: Jessica Wilks, Director of Curatorial and Interpretation at Tacoma Art Museum, who has led curatorial teams for more than twenty years and shapes TAM's commitment to artists of the region; and Greg Robinson, Chief Curator at the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art, formerly director of the Museum of Northwest Art and a Betty Bowen Award committee member. More than $8,500 in cash prizes will be awarded. Open to artists 18 and over anywhere in the country; work must be original, made in the last two years, and not produced in a class or workshop. AI tools may be used in a supporting role for editing or minor enhancement but may not generate the artwork. Nudes, religious symbols, political themes and extreme violence will not be considered. All work must be for sale with a 15% commission; 2D pieces need D-rings and taut wire, no sawtooth hangers. Shipped work is accepted, at a $20 handling fee per piece. Jurying finishes 27 October and everyone is notified by 29 October. The show runs 14 November – 2 December 2026.
jury: Jessica Wilks, Director of Curatorial and Interpretation, Tacoma Art Museum
Greg Robinson, Chief Curator, Bainbridge Island Museum of Art

calls.title: 2nd Annual Kit Gilbert Juried Showcase
calls.description: An open, themeless juried showcase at the Gilbert Center in downtown Ruston, Louisiana — a legacy project of the Ross Lynn Charitable Foundation that carries forward the work of two local artists, Ross Lynn and Kit Gilbert, the Ruston painter this annual show is named for. There is no set subject: any original work made since 2020 is welcome, and photography is explicitly among the media considered alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, textile, ceramics and short video. The juror is Julie Crews, an oil painter based in Huntsville, Alabama who keeps an open studio and gallery at the 122-year-old Lowe Mill Arts and Entertainment complex and paints the domestic scenes of her own life — backyard fires, children swimming, errands around town. Two cash awards: the Juror's Choice / Best-in-Show at $750, and a People's Choice at $500 voted by visitors on opening night. Open to US artists 18 and over, up to three works, each needing a 250-word artist statement. AI-generated work is not accepted. Photographs must be framed or mounted — unframed works on paper and unmounted prints will be rejected — and artists arrange their own delivery and return shipping. Notifications 19 October, work due 7 November, exhibition 16 November 2026 – 15 January 2027 with a reception on 19 November. The Gilbert Center takes 30% commission.
calls.summary: Themeless juried showcase in Ruston, Louisiana honouring painter Kit Gilbert. Photography welcome, $12 an entry, $1,250 in cash awards.

calls.title: Artifacts
calls.description: A juried exhibition at 6 Bridges Gallery, a fine art and craft gallery on Main Street in Maynard, Massachusetts, built around the marks, remnants and meaningful objects that shape how we understand the world. The gallery is looking for work that uncovers the traces of what remains — hidden histories, personal relics, the quiet evidence of lives lived — and asks artists to think about what we carry forward, whether physical, emotional, cultural or imagined. All media are welcome except video and AI-generated work. The juror is Claudia Fiks, an independent curator and arts administrator of more than twenty years who founded and directs TAG | The Art Gallery at the New England Art Center in Boston's SoWa Art & Design District, directs Newton Open Studios, and writes on contemporary art for Artscope Magazine; she says she values authenticity, risk-taking, and work that communicates beyond the surface, regardless of medium or career stage. Open to artists 16 and over, up to three works made in the last three years, wired and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers) and no larger than 40 inches in any direction. Three awards are given: the Artifact Award, Jurors' Choice and People's Choice. All work must be for sale and artists keep 60%. Work must be hand-delivered — the gallery does not accept shipped artwork. Notifications 9 September, drop-off 30 September – 3 October, exhibition 7 October – 14 November 2026 with a reception on 17 October.
jury: Claudia Fiks, Founder and Director, TAG | The Art Gallery at the New England Art Center

calls.title: 26th Annual Juried Fine Art Show & Sale
calls.fee: $45 for up to 2 entries ($35 members) + $5 each addl
calls.description: A three-day juried show and sale run by the Rockwall Art League in North Texas, open to artists across a five-state region — Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and New Mexico — and now in its 26th year. Photography is one of eight judged categories, alongside oil, watercolour, acrylic, mixed media, mosaic, drawing and sculpture, and up to $6,600 in cash prizes is awarded across them — $1,000 for Best in Show, $500 and $200 for first and second in each category, plus a run of ribbon-only special awards. The two judges are Dana Brock, an abstract and mixed-media painter and Signature Member of the Southwestern Watercolor Society, and Rachel Townsend Cerny, founder of RTown Gallery in historic downtown Grapevine, Texas. The League says it exists to give both established and emerging artists a platform, and the event puts work in front of collectors and business representatives from across the DFW metroplex. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original and made after 1 January 2024, and compositions based on published material, other artists' work, or generated with AI are not eligible. Work made in a class or workshop is out, as is anything containing nudes, conspicuously religious content, drug references or blatant political statements. Up to two works per artist, submitted with two to five images. New for 2026: hand delivery only — shipped work is not accepted — 2D pieces capped at 36 x 36 inches including frame, sculpture under 50 lbs, and a new venue at The Center at Rockwall City Place. Notifications go out 26 September; take-in is the morning of 16 October and the show runs 16–18 October 2026, with awards announced at the 16 October reception and final awards on the 18th.
jury: Rachel Townsend Cerny, Founder, RTown Gallery
calls.summary: 26th-year North Texas juried show, photography one of eight judged categories with a share of $6,600 in cash prizes. Five-state region.

calls.title: Local Testimony 2026
calls.description: The annual Israeli press and documentary photography exhibition, founded in 2003 and shown each year at MUZA — Eretz Israel Museum in Tel Aviv, in parallel with World Press Photo. The 2026 contest opens on 13 August and closes at midnight on 31 August. Single images may be entered in six fields — News (open only to holders of a GPO or Israeli Journalists Union press card), Religion and Faith, Society and Community, Urbanism and Culture, Sport, and Nature and Environment — up to ten photographs per field. Alongside singles there are three other formats: short series (up to four series of four to six photographs each, no press card required), Long Exposure (a documentary story built over more than a year, ten to fifteen photographs, at least three from the past year), and video works up to seven minutes made in 2025–2026. The curator of the 2026 edition is Ilia Yefimovich, a documentary maker and AFP staff photographer. Entry is free. Grants totalling 30,000 NIS are split equally between Photo of the Year (the Roi Idan Prize, given by the Israeli Journalists Union), Series of the Year, and Video Work of the Year — the last a production grant from Shomrim, the Center for Media and Democracy, dedicated to making a new video work with the Shomrim newsroom for the 2027 exhibition. Every photographer in the exhibition receives the catalogue and a certificate of participation.
jury: Ilia Yefimovich, Curator and AFP photographer
Nir Elias, Photo Editor, Reuters Israel
Shiraz Grinbaum, Photographer and editor, Madaf
Ilan Yitzhayek, Head of Journalism, Sapir College
Yaakov Israel, Artist and photography lecturer
Guy Raz, Curator of Photography, MUZA Eretz Israel Museum
Giora Shalmi, Director, School of Geographic Photography
calls.summary: Israel's annual press and documentary photography exhibition at MUZA Tel Aviv. Free to enter, 30,000 NIS in grants across three top prizes.

calls.title: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards 2027
calls.description: The 2027 cycle of MonoVisions Magazine's international monochrome competition is open. Work is entered either as a single photograph or as a series of up to eight images sharing one idea, across twelve categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature and Wildlife, Nude, People, Photojournalism, Portrait, Street Photography and Travel. Both traditional and digital black-and-white photography are accepted, and the competition is open to professionals and amateurs alike. The prize fund is $5,000, split between Black and White Series of the Year ($3,000) and Black and White Photo of the Year ($2,000); category winners and honourable mentions receive badges and certificates rather than additional cash. Fees are tiered by deadline — $20 for a single photo and $25 for a series until the early deadline of 17 January 2027, then $25 and $30 until the final deadline of 16 May 2027. Winners are announced on 25 July 2027 and judged by a panel of thirteen international photographers and artists.
calls.summary: MonoVisions' 2027 monochrome awards across 12 categories, singles or series of 8, with $5,000 split between two top prizes.

calls.title: 13th Annual LA Billboard Exhibition: No Walls
calls.description: For thirteen years The Billboard Creative has turned billboards across Los Angeles into a citywide open-air gallery, buying the same advertising space that usually sells products and giving it to artists instead. Selected artists each receive their own billboard in Los Angeles for four weeks; TBC covers production, installation and the billboard space itself, and photographs each installed board for its exhibition archive. Boards are placed on high-traffic routes near galleries, museums and cultural centres as well as on ordinary commuter roads, so the work is seen by people who would not otherwise walk into a gallery — past exhibitions have been covered by NPR, Hyperallergic, the Los Angeles Times and KCRW. Photography is explicitly welcome alongside painting, sculpture, collage, mixed media and digital work: if the piece can be supplied as a digital file it can go on a billboard. Video and audio works are not accepted for this edition. Entries cost $28 for the first image and $10 for each additional image up to twenty.
jury: Curator selected by The Billboard Creative
calls.summary: Selected artists each get a Los Angeles billboard for four weeks, with production, installation and space covered. Photography welcome.

calls.title: Sea to Shining Sea
calls.description: A national juried exhibition of the American landscape in all media at the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art in Saint Joseph, Missouri, on view from 21 November 2026 to 21 February 2027. Artists may submit up to three works, each juried and scored individually, with a maximum size of 60 by 60 inches and 50 pounds. The juror is Lisa Grossman, a painter and printmaker based in Lawrence, Kansas since 1996 whose work follows the prairies and river valleys of eastern Kansas; she has had more than thirty solo shows across the Midwest and on both coasts and is represented by Haw Contemporary in Kansas City and SNW Gallery in Manhattan, Kansas. Awards are chosen after the exhibition is hung: $500 Best of Show, $250 second, $150 third and a $100 People's Choice. Open to artists 18 and over; AI-generated work is not considered. Work may be shipped (arriving by 10 November with a prepaid return label) or hand-delivered on 16 November. Work need not be for sale, but the museum retains 30% on any sales.
calls.summary: National juried show of the American landscape in all media at a Missouri museum, three months on view and $1,000 in awards.

calls.title: Best in Show
calls.description: Kirkland Arts Center's first annual juried exhibition, built around the animals we live with. Each year the centre picks a different animal and leaves the interpretation entirely open; the 2026 subject is dogs, real or imaginary, abstract or representational. The call is open to Washington-based 2D and 3D artists of all ages working in any medium — photography included — with work no larger than 48 inches in height or width. Selected pieces are shown from 18 September to 9 October 2026 with an opening reception on 18 September, and a $500 prize goes to one winner in each of the 2D and 3D categories. Artists ship or deliver their own work ready to hang or display and include return postage; the centre takes 40% commission on sales. KAC was founded in 1962 and has occupied the historic Peter Kirk Building, built in 1893, for more than sixty years.
calls.summary: First annual juried show at a 1962 Washington arts centre, themed on dogs. Any medium, all ages, $500 prizes in 2D and 3D.

calls.title: Athenaeum Gallery Show Proposals
calls.description: The Athenaeum Gallery, a Greek Revival landmark in Old Town Alexandria run by the Northern Virginia Fine Arts Association, sets aside part of its programme for shows proposed by artists and curators rather than chosen by the gallery director. Artists living or working in Virginia, Maryland or the District of Columbia may propose a solo show; groups of artists from the region may propose a group show; and a curator based anywhere may propose a show of work by artists from the area. Proposals are reviewed by gallery director Twig Murray on what the artist is trying to communicate, what makes the work distinctive, technical quality, and how recently the artist has shown locally. All visual media are welcome, photography included, but every work must be wall-mounted, less than nine inches deep and ready to hang on picture hooks; nothing floor-standing and nothing requiring electricity. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales.

calls.title: CCA Call for Exhibition Proposals 2026
calls.description: Coconino Center for the Arts in Flagstaff, managed by Creative Flagstaff, invites exhibition proposals from artists, curators and cultural organisations for rolling review by its Exhibitions Selection Committee. The building holds a 4,000 square foot Main Gallery, which programmes three to four major exhibitions a year, an adjacent 215 square foot Project Gallery with four to six shows a year, and a 200-seat theatre; it sits on US 180 on the road to the Grand Canyon and serves the arts, science and cultural communities of northern Arizona. Interdisciplinary proposals involving digital media or installation are particularly encouraged. calls.title: Rosewood Arts Center 2027 Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: The Kettering Health Art Gallery at Rosewood Arts Center, run by the City of Kettering just outside Dayton, Ohio, presents six to eight solo exhibitions a year by emerging local, regional and national artists, and is taking proposals for its 2027 season running January to December. Artists working in any media may apply, including video and installation. A proposal consists of a cover letter describing the exhibition, any special installation requirements, possible public programmes and available dates; an artist statement, resume and exhibition record; and ten images with titles, media, dimensions and dates — the selection committee sees only those ten. Rosewood also welcomes proposals for accompanying educational programmes, community projects and artist talks. Three regional arts professionals make the recommendations and everyone is notified by 10 September 2026. Selected artists receive a $300 honorarium; the city insures all work while on exhibition and covers printing and mailing of an announcement for each show. Open to adults living in the United States, though current City of Kettering employees are not eligible for solo exhibitions.

calls.title: Showcase 2027
calls.description: Northwind Art's Showcase programme fills the Jeanette Best Gallery on Water Street in Port Townsend, Washington with roughly thirty-six artists a year, arranged in three cohorts that each hang for about four months: 28 January – 10 May, 13 May – 6 September, and 9 September 2027 – 3 January 2028. Jurors look for a cohesive body of work and pay particular attention to retail pricing, aiming to select artists whose work generally sits under $1,000. The programme is geared towards artists in Jefferson, Clallam, Mason, Kitsap and Island counties but the application is open to artists outside them; Showcase artists may not be represented by another gallery or retail outlet in Port Townsend during their run. Ten images are required, each with dimensions, medium and retail price, and no imagery derived from AI. The selection panel is made up of two Northwind Art exhibits staff, exhibit designer Suzanne Lamon and executive director Martha Worthley. The $35 fee is waived on the honour system for artists from historically underrepresented BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ communities. Everyone is notified by 5 December 2026.
jury: Suzanne Lamon, Exhibit Designer, Northwind Art
Martha Worthley, Executive Director, Northwind Art

calls.title: Art Edu 2026
calls.description: A juried exhibition at Art Center Waco celebrating art educators as practising artists — the work they make beyond the classroom, which so often feeds back into how they teach. Active and retired art educators living in McLennan, Bell, Falls, Coryell, Limestone, Hill and Bosque Counties in central Texas may submit up to three original works made in the last five years. All 2D and 3D media are eligible, photography included; reproductions of original works such as giclée prints are not, though photographic prints are. Work can be up to 72 inches in any direction and wall pieces up to 60 pounds, and artworks previously exhibited at ACW are not eligible. The show hangs in the Beard Gallery from 29 October to 19 December 2026. calls.title: Aurora 2026 Members Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Aurora PhotoCenter, the artist-run photography centre in Indianapolis, opens its main gallery to its own membership for a juried show that treats photography as broadly as possible — all work that incorporates photography, in any subject, style or working method, will be considered. Barbara Tannenbaum, Chair of Prints, Drawings and Photographs and Curator of Photography at the Cleveland Museum of Art, is the juror; she organised over 80 exhibitions across 26 years at the Akron Art Museum before joining Cleveland in 2011, where her shows include Ilse Bing: Queen of the Leica and DIY: Photographers & Books, the first museum exhibition of print-on-demand photobooks. Any member current as of 31 August may send up to five images, noting print size, framing, capture method (35mm, 120, 4x5, DSLR, phone or other) and date. Submitting costs nothing beyond membership, and artists living outside Indiana can join through Aurora's $35 Distance membership. Aurora makes all decisions about printing, matting, framing, layout and pricing, and prints and prepares accepted work for the wall from existing frame stock free of charge. Work is priced at no more than $300; artists keep 70% of any sale or can donate the proceeds to Aurora. The show runs 4 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 with an opening reception on 4 December.
calls.summary: Aurora's members show in Indianapolis, juried by the Cleveland Museum of Art's Barbara Tannenbaum. Free to enter, Aurora prints and frames.

calls.title: periscope:project:space Open Call 2027
calls.description: periscope is an artist-run project space in Salzburg that has been programming exhibitions, performances and site-specific work since 2014, and it is assembling its 2027 season through an open call to Austrian and international visual artists. Three lines of interest are named: solo presentations of an artist's own practice shown as premieres, projects that respond to the space or the site itself, and performance as part of an artistic practice. Depending on the project, periscope covers production costs, pays expenses for transport, travel and accommodation, and pays an exhibition fee — an unusually concrete offer for a small independent space. Submissions are digital only and consist of documentation of the work, a proposal or sketches of up to 400 words, and a CV. There is no entry fee and no theme beyond the three interest areas; past programmes have included lens-based and photographic projects alongside installation and sound work.
calls.summary: Salzburg project space picks its 2027 season: solo shows and site-specific projects, with production costs, travel and artist fee covered.

calls.title: Picture This — 2026 Photography Show
calls.description: The San Marcos Art League gives over its Art Center gallery for the month of August to a show dedicated entirely to the photographic medium, from traditional film work to contemporary digital compositions. Entry is open to all and each entrant may submit one artwork; accepted work must be hand-delivered ready to hang at the San Marcos Art Center on Sunday 2 August between 1pm and 4pm, since shipped work is not accepted. Work must be original, signed and completed in the previous 24 months, and must not have been shown at the Art Center Gallery before. Two-dimensional pieces are capped at 36 inches wide by 68 inches high including framing, and everything must be for sale, with the Art League retaining a 20% commission. The exhibition runs 5–28 August 2026 with a public opening reception on Friday 7 August from 6 to 8pm.
calls.summary: A whole August gallery month given to photography in San Marcos, Texas. Open to all, one work each, $20 to enter.

calls.title: San Marcos Arts Festival Juried Art Exhibition 2026
calls.description: The juried exhibition anchoring the San Marcos Arts Festival, presented by the San Marcos Art League on behalf of the City of San Marcos and open to artists in any fine art media, photography included. The juror is Margo Handwerker, Director of the Glassell School of Art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, previously Dean of its Core Residency Program and Chief Curator and Director of the Texas State Galleries in San Marcos; she holds a PhD from Princeton's School of Architecture and is a practising artist and member of the M12 Studio collective. Up to $500 in cash prizes is awarded at the juror's discretion. Artists may submit up to five entries but no more than two works can appear in the show, and work must have been completed in the last two years. Accepted work must be hand-delivered on 1 November — nothing shipped — framed no larger than 36 by 48 inches and under 35 pounds. The exhibition runs 4–20 November 2026 at the San Marcos Art Center, with an opening reception on 13 November and the festival itself on 14 November. All work must be for sale; the Art League retains a 20% commission.

calls.title: Erbleichen
calls.description: NEU! is an artist-run space on Untere Vogelsangstrasse in Winterthur with a curated programme of a new show every two months. For a group exhibition in November 2026 it is looking for work from a world that flows thick and slow and is losing its colour — spaces where time seems to stand still and the future and its promises go unfulfilled, time loops, system errors, ghosts, doppelgängers of decay. The great bleaching. Proposals are welcome across all mediums and may be unfinished, unproduced, in process or complete, and are sent by email. There is no entry fee. NEU! notes that it is not able to cover shipping or similar costs.

calls.title: diptych/triptych/multiples/collage
calls.description: A Smith Gallery's juried online exhibition for work built from more than one frame — diptychs, triptychs, multiples and collages. The gallery's premise is that diptychs tell stories, triptychs tell larger stories, and multiples and collages tell larger ones still. Juror Manuela Thames is a Saint Paul–based photographic artist, born and raised in Germany, whose largely self-taught, contemplative practice explores loss and grief, generational trauma, belonging and connection; her work has been recognised by the Monovisions Awards and a Julia Margaret Cameron Award, and she teaches for Santa Fe Workshops, SE Center for Photography, Maine Media and LACP. Jurying is blind. Up to 47 images are selected for the online exhibition and catalogue, with 27 chosen for 'The 27', a hardbound fine-art book. The Juror's Award and Directors' Award each carry an online solo exhibition, 'The 27' and a blog feature; a Visitors' Award of $100 goes to the most Instagram likes. Photographers submitting 13 or more images receive a complimentary director review. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide in all photographic mediums; work previously exhibited at A Smith Gallery is ineligible. Online exhibition 1 November – 31 December 2026, reception 28 November.

calls.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Moments of Color
calls.description: Open call on colour — the bold contrast of urban life, the soft pastels of a sunset, the vibrant hues of nature — asking how photographers capture the essence of colour in their work and turn ordinary moments into something extraordinary. Free to submit; selected photographers pay a participation fee only if exhibited (€35 if the photograph is printed, €15 if it is shown on the gallery's 43-inch 4K digital screen). Over 100 printed photographs are shown in each exhibition, with printing on 260 gsm paper, framing, hanging, invitations and the opening night all covered by the gallery, and no commission taken on sales. Selected work is shown at Blank Wall Gallery in Athens, 23 October – 4 November 2026.

calls.title: Patchwork
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Kinhouse Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana, inspired by quilts and the art of piecing things together. Work may respond to the quilt as literal artwork, as technique (piecing, patchwork, appliqué, stitching in any medium), or as visual language — grids, blocks, repeated motifs and pattern-based composition, even outside fiber art. All mediums are accepted, and work engaging pattern, texture, scrap and reuse, and the handmade is especially encouraged. Selected artists receive a $20 shipping stipend and inclusion in the published Patchwork Catalog alongside an extended selection of submitted work. Exhibition October 2–30, 2026, opening during the Arts This Way Broadway Arts Festival; 20% commission on sales.
calls.summary: Quilt-inspired juried show at Fort Wayne's Kinhouse Gallery — any medium engaging pattern and piecing. Exhibition + catalog.

calls.title: GLEAN 2026/27
calls.description: Juried program giving five Portland-area artists five months of access to the Metro Central transfer station — the dump — to glean discarded materials and make work from them. Selected artists receive a $3,000 stipend, studio visits, marketing support and group critiques with GLEAN artists and partners, culminating in a group exhibition. Gleaning runs November 2026 to March 2027, with on-site safety training and orientation on November 2, 2026 and the exhibition in April/May 2027. Each artist must produce at least eight pieces for sale at the exhibition, with 95% of each piece made from gleaned materials, and keeps 80% commission on sales; Recology and Metro each retain one unpurchased piece, and studio space is not provided. For a third year, one of the five places goes to an artist selected for exceptional craft, supported by the Rainmaker Craft Initiative. One residency position is reserved for a student currently enrolled in an art program at a local college or university, considered separately from other applications, and artists working in a variety of media are encouraged to apply. GLEAN is a partnership between Recology Oregon Recovery, Metro — the regional government that manages the Portland area's garbage and recycling system — and the environmental arts nonprofit ReClaim It, and has run since 2010.
jury: Jury of arts and environmental professionals
calls.summary: Five Portland artists get five months of access to the dump, a $3,000 stipend and a group show. Free to apply.

calls.title: Hotel Willa Artist-in-Residence 2027
calls.description: Four-week self-directed residency at Hotel Willa in Taos, New Mexico, activated by The Paseo Project, for the months of February, March, April, July, August, October, November and December 2027. The hotel — a 1940s motel reimagined as an art-forward destination in the historic district, five minutes' walk from Taos Plaza — hosts one artist at a time. Residents get a private one-bedroom suite with kitchenette, a private on-site studio outfitted with work surfaces, easel, sink, desk lamp, rolling cart and cutting mat, a bicycle for the duration, and restaurant discounts and vouchers. There is no stipend: artists cover travel, materials and meals, and a car is recommended. Artists are invited to give an artist talk and open studio on the third Thursday of their stay. Open to artists, makers, writers and creatives in all disciplines who live or work in the Four Corners region or within a 300-mile radius of Taos; Taos County residents are not eligible, and the program cannot accommodate couples or families.
calls.summary: Four weeks in Taos with a private suite, studio and bike at Hotel Willa, for artists within 300 miles of town.

calls.title: Delfina Foundation — Central & West Africa Curators Residency 2027
calls.description: Six- or twelve-week residency in London during Delfina Foundation's winter 2027 'open' season (5 January – 28 March 2027), for curators based in Central and West Africa, supported by Delfina's Network of Patrons for Africa. Support covers a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees, a £40 per day living allowance, a £70 per week materials and research allowance, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom with desk in Delfina's house, which hosts up to eight residents around a shared kitchen, library and dining room. The programme includes guided visits to museums, galleries, non-profits and artist-run spaces, trips to institutions outside London, organised presentations and studio visits, portfolio reviews and mentoring. Applicants must hold nationality of and be based in one of 26 listed countries, have at least five years of professional curatorial practice — independent, institutional or academic — and be proficient in English, as the interview is conducted in English. Curators with an artistic background are welcome, but the residency is not open to applicants whose primary practice is as an artist.
calls.summary: Fully funded 6–12 week London residency for curators based in Central and West Africa, with flights and allowances.

calls.title: RBSA On Tour at Winterbourne House Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Free members' exhibition taking RBSA work out of the gallery and into Winterbourne House, the Edwardian house and botanic garden in Birmingham, for a four-and-a-half month run from October 10, 2026 to February 28, 2027. Open only to RBSA Members, Associates and Honorary Members; work may have been shown at the RBSA Gallery before, and pieces from the recent Members and Associates Small Works Exhibition are especially welcome. All styles and media are eligible including photography and digital work, where digital technology is an essential part of the artistic process — but not giclee or other reproductions of handmade originals, and not AI-generated images. Every print, digital ones included, must be editioned with the edition size clearly stated. Artists may submit up to four works, with at least two each expected to hang and the Winterbourne House curatorial team selecting if the show is oversubscribed. All work must be under 65cm in every dimension including the frame, made in the past three years, priced at no more than £695 and for sale for the full run. There are no entry fees and no display fees.
calls.summary: Free RBSA members' show at Winterbourne House, Birmingham. Photography welcome, up to four works, October–February run.

calls.title: The PASEO 2027 Biennial
calls.description: Twelfth edition of the outdoor festival that turns the streets of the Taos Historic District into a night-time gallery of installation, projection and performance, across the evenings of Friday and Saturday, September 17–18, 2027. The 2027 theme is Convergence — movement toward connection, the dynamic space between individuality and collectivity where difference, contradiction and multiplicity coexist; rivers converge without abandoning their sources, cultures converge while carrying memory forward. Work must be immersive, site-responsive and/or participatory, built for outdoor viewing after dark, and already fully realised: The PASEO does not fund new commissions or undeveloped concepts. Selected artists receive a stipend of $500–$3,000 for standard projects, rising to $5,000–$15,000 for larger works depending on scope and impact, with travel, lodging, shipping, installation assistance and equipment covered and an artist fee set to W.A.G.E. standards. Artists must be present from sunset to 11pm on both nights, and are invited to propose adult and youth workshops, lectures and forums as part of the application. Open to emerging, mid-career and professional artists over 21 from anywhere in the world.
calls.summary: Taos turns its historic streets into a night-time projection and installation festival, with stipends up to $15,000.

calls.title: Hawaiʻi Nei 2026 — 18th Annual Exhibition
calls.description: Annual juried exhibition at the Wailoa Center in Hilo devoted to the native species of Hawai'i Island — organisms that arrived naturally by wind, waves or wings, whether endemic to Hawai'i or indigenous to Hawai'i and elsewhere. Artwork whose main subject is a non-native species, a Polynesian introduction, or a native species found only on other Hawaiian islands is not accepted, and work made from materials taken from an endangered native species is excluded. Any medium is welcome, with separate adult categories for two-dimensional work, three-dimensional work and photography, plus a youth section that is free to enter. Reproductions and AI-generated or AI-assisted work are not accepted; pieces must have been made in the past four years and not previously shown at the Wailoa Center, and because the gallery is a State Parks facility work with nudity or offensive religious, political or violent content may be juried out. Open to residents of Hawai'i Island only. Emily Catey Weiss, program director at the Volcano Art Center and previously a working photographer on Oahu's North Shore, juries the adult divisions; Erzsi Kuba Palko, illustrator of two books on native Hawaiian species, juries the youth divisions. The jurors ask for an artist statement describing your pilina — your relationship to the species, to the island and to the piece itself — and say it may weigh in the selection. calls.title: 2026 Call for Exhibiting Artists
calls.description: Baton Rouge Gallery — center for contemporary art, founded in 1966 and one of America's oldest artist cooperatives — opens its annual application to join a roster of more than 75 Exhibiting Artists working across a wide range of media. Members show in the gallery's 2,800 square foot space, keep 60% of all sales of their work, are represented on the gallery website, get a discount at Mo's Art Supply, and have a genuine voice in how the organisation runs: exhibiting artists vote on which special exhibitions to host and which artists to invite to join. In return, members exhibit at least once every three years in month-long shows, help with receptions, talks and installation, and pay $100 in annual dues, with opportunities to offset that cost; membership is reviewed every five years. Open to artists 18 and over who are at least two years removed from formal art education — no student work or work made under supervision — and who can show Louisiana residency or explain their relationship to Baton Rouge or the state; once accepted, artists may keep their membership if they move away. Applications are juried in two rounds on craftsmanship, originality, quality of presentation and professional experience.

calls.title: HOPE
calls.description: Juried exhibition running September 25 – November 6, 2026 at The Studio Door, the gay-owned and operated gallery in San Diego. The brief is a single question — what gives you hope? — with no prescribed message or point of view: the gallery is looking for authentic work capable of making a lasting connection with the people who see it, work collectors will want to live with. Painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art, artist books and sculpture are all accepted; performance art is not, and video, film, installation or anything requiring an external power source needs gallery approval before submitting. An entry is one to three artworks, all of which must be available for sale and arrive gallery-ready, with black or natural wood frames preferred. Juror Patric Stillman, the gallery's founder, juried the 2025 Oceanside Museum of Art Biennial, writes a monthly arts column for The WORD San Diego and received the 2024 Larry T. Baza Arts & Culture Award from San Diego Pride; he gives three Juror's Awards of $100 each. Gallery space is limited, so not every accepted submission can be hung. Open to Southern California visual artists; artists are notified by September 4 and are responsible for hand delivery on September 19 and pickup in November. Sales are split 50/50 with the gallery.
calls.summary: San Diego's gay-owned Studio Door asks what gives you hope. Photography welcome; three $100 juror's awards.

calls.title: 20/20 Vision: A 20th Anniversary Exhibition
calls.description: Twentieth-anniversary show from Artists of Palm Beach County, presented at Studio 1608 in West Palm Beach, an art destination that has become a gathering place for artists, collectors and enthusiasts across the county. Abstract, representational, contemporary, traditional and experimental work are all welcome. Every piece must be in a 20 x 20 inch format: work on paper should be adhered to a 20 x 20 canvas, photographs may be printed on canvas or metal, and three-dimensional work must fit within a 20 x 20 inch footprint, though height may vary. Artists may submit up to three works, all of which must be for sale at the price given at submission — that price cannot be changed later — with members receiving 75% of the gross. Explicitly sexual or political work is not accepted, and neither is anything created with artificial intelligence. Membership is not required to enter but lowers the fee. Irina Rothenberg, an art collector and advisor at Findlay Galleries, judges, awarding $150 for first place, $100 for second and $50 for third. Artists are notified on or before September 9; work is delivered September 14, the opening reception is September 19 and the closing reception October 17, 2026.
calls.summary: Palm Beach County's 20th-anniversary show at Studio 1608. Everything 20x20 inches; photos on canvas or metal.

calls.title: Lubbock Arts Festival Juried Gallery 2027
calls.description: Juried gallery of the 49th Lubbock Arts Festival, held April 10–11, 2027 in the Lubbock Memorial Civic Center and open to artists working in any fine art medium, photography included. Entries must be original in design and execution, completed within the last two years, and not made in a workshop or under supervision; each artist may enter up to ten works, of which no more than three will be shown. Juror Rob Weingart has taught foundations, 2D and 3D art at West Texas A&M University for the past decade and previously worked in the gallery and museum world in New York, Chicago and London, with a BFA from the University of North Texas and an MFA from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Up to $1,000 in cash prizes is awarded at the juror's discretion. Accepted work must be hand delivered — shipped artwork is not accepted — ready to hang securely on wire with no sawtooth hangers, no larger than 44 x 72 inches framed and under 35 pounds. All work must be for sale at the submitted price with sales tax included; the Lubbock Arts Alliance retains a 33 1/3% commission, and artists must obtain a Texas sales tax number in order to enter.

calls.title: Marco Pesaresi Award for Contemporary Photography 2026
calls.description: 25th edition of the Premio Marco Pesaresi, promoted by the Municipality of Savignano sul Rubicone in partnership with the Municipality of Rimini and organized with Savignano Immagini APS, the association behind SI FEST. Honoring Rimini-born photographer Marco Pesaresi, the award supports photo-reportage marked by research, intentionality and innovation in contemporary photography and visual culture. Photographers of any age and nationality submit a portfolio of up to 20 images, preferably on a single theme, proposing a project they intend to complete with the €5,000 prize; work that has already had a definitive exhibition or book form is not eligible, and early-stage ideas may be entered in project form accompanied by an earlier portfolio. The prize money, paid in two installments, must be used for project expenses such as travel, production, permits and collaborations, and the completed project is exhibited at the following edition of SI FEST in 2027. AI-generated imagery is admitted only if its use is explicitly declared. The winner is notified privately by September 4 and proclaimed during the opening weekend of SI FEST's 35th edition (September 11–13, 2026), then joins the jury that selects the next edition's winner.

calls.title: Fall 2026 New York City Fellowship
calls.description: Twelve-week fellowship for NYC-based early-career photographers and photojournalists, running mid-September to mid-December 2026. Fellows produce an in-depth documentary project based in New York City that speaks to social issues and engages NYC communities, with bi-weekly mentorship and project development support from the Magnum Foundation team. Alongside the project, fellows spend Wednesdays and Thursdays (16 hours a week) working in Magnum Foundation's New York office on research, multimedia production, event production and emerging-platform work — paid arts administration experience treated as an integral part of the team. Compensation is a $5,000 production grant paid at the start plus $25/hour for the in-office hours. Candidates should have expertise in at least one of arts administration, research, writing, video production or graphic design, and at least one completed long-term project; recent graduates and self-taught photographers are encouraged, and the program is open to photographers of all ages. No room, board or transportation is provided. Selection is by an internal committee. Supported by Select Equity Group Foundation and the Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation.
calls.summary: 12 weeks in NYC: $5,000 production grant, paid office days at Magnum Foundation, and mentorship on a documentary project.

calls.title: F/262 Curated Open Call 2026
calls.description: Series-based track of the F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal — a curated open call rather than a competition, inviting a complete project, series or conceptual body of work for review by the festival's curatorial team, guest curators, international advisors and external reviewers from partner institutions. All genres are eligible, including fine art, documentary, experimental, portrait, conceptual and cross-disciplinary work; works-in-progress are accepted if presentable by summer 2026. One selected project is awarded a dedicated solo exhibition at CEF – Centro de Experimentação Fotográfica in Caldas da Rainha after the 2026 festival closes. There is no cap on the number of projects selected: chosen work is shown in indoor cultural venues with wall text developed alongside the curators, listed in the official festival guide, promoted through festival and press channels, and may be considered for photobook features, talks or portfolio reviews. The festival covers exhibition production costs and artists retain full copyright. Open to photographers, artists and collectives of any nationality, age or background; collaborative projects welcome. Submit a single PDF with a project statement, bio and the photographs, plus one JPG cover image. Judged on conceptual clarity, visual quality, originality and exhibition viability.
calls.summary: Curated series call from the F/262 Festival in Portugal. Winner gets a solo show at CEF; production costs covered.

Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing.

calls.title: WSP Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Two-week fully funded residency in New York City for a woman street photographer, March 29 – April 12, 2027. The package (advertised at $10,000) covers a studio apartment at El Barrio's Artspace PS109 in East Harlem, a round-trip ticket from anywhere in the world, visa fee, subway pass and SIM card, and a $50 daily stipend, plus daily reviews and mentorship with Nina Welch-Kling and Lauren Welles. The resident produces a solo exhibition shown during the annual Women Street Photographers group exhibition and takes part in the WSP Festival in NYC (April 9–11, 2027), a panel discussion and an Instagram Live interview. Submit a cohesive series of up to 10 images with an artist statement explaining the project and why the residency matters to you — statement and images are weighted equally. Street photography is preferred; other genres are considered if the statement connects to street work. Up to three series per photographer, each on its own form. Photographers who cannot afford the fee, or who live in countries affected by US sanctions, can request one free entry form by email.
jury: Nina Welch-Kling, WSP Artist Residency Mentor
calls.summary: Fully funded two-week NYC residency for a woman street photographer, with $50/day stipend, mentorship and a solo exhibition.

calls.title: Small Matters
calls.description: Blind-juried open call for work at an intimate scale, shown at Carter Burden Gallery in Chelsea, New York (548 West 28th Street) from November 19 to December 16, 2026. Two-dimensional work including the frame must measure at least 5 inches and no more than 15 inches in any direction; three-dimensional pedestal pieces must stay under 10 inches and 50 lbs. Jurors are artist-curator Beth Barry and reportage artist Veronica Lawlor. The gallery is part of the Carter Burden Network and particularly encourages artists over the age of 60, though the call is open to all US visual artists over 18. Works on paper must be framed under plexiglass, white or natural wood frames preferred. The gallery takes no commission on sales.
calls.summary: Chelsea gallery show of work under 15 inches, jurors Beth Barry and Veronica Lawlor. Artists over 60 especially encouraged.

calls.title: We the People
calls.description: Open call from Studio Montclair, a nationwide non-profit of exhibiting artists in New Jersey, for work that shows fellow citizens living their lives inside the 250-year-old experiment in democracy that is the United States — read through the Preamble's goals of a more perfect union, justice, tranquility, common defense, general welfare and liberty. Artists are encouraged to interpret those goals unconventionally. All mediums are accepted, including video and installation. The exhibition runs September 18 – October 23, 2026 at the Leach Gallery, 641 Bloomfield Avenue, Montclair. Juror Jeremy Moss trained as a photographer in the UK, shot New York Fashion Week and campaigns for McGraw-Hill and the New York Times, and has curated the Iris Gallery at the South Orange Performing Arts Center for a decade. Cash awards will be presented. Studio Montclair retains 30% on sales, and exhibiting artists who live within 25 miles of the Leach Gallery must sit the gallery for at least two hours during the run or pay a $40 fee towards a sitter.
calls.summary: New Jersey non-profit's show on American democratic life, juried by Jeremy Moss. All mediums, cash awards, free for members.

calls.title: Women's Work: Women Artists Making Their Mark 2026
calls.description: The 18th year of O'Hanlon Center for the Arts' annual online show devoted to women artists, part of the Mill Valley non-profit's commitment to gender equity in the art world. Open worldwide to artists who identify as female, aged 16 and over, in any medium except video — the work does not need to reference women or women's issues, though it may. Two jurors, gallerist Donna Seager and artist Irene Bee Kain, each independently select the same maximum number of works and every selection by either juror is included, so the exhibition reflects two distinct curatorial eyes rather than a consensus. Selected work is presented in a curated online show running 17 August – 31 October 2026, promoted through social media, print media and email outreach, with a printable catalogue and permanent archive access after the show closes. A Zoom roundtable with both jurors takes place on 18 August. Work previously shown at O'Hanlon, in the gallery or online, is not eligible.

calls.title: Inspection Pit Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: A month-long, fully funded residency at Inspection Pit, a not-for-profit contemporary art space in a converted garage barn beside a working farm in West Sussex, near the South Downs. The 2027 resident stays on site from 30 January to 27 February 2027 in private accommodation, with a dedicated studio for independent work, a bicycle for getting around locally, and a £500 bursary paid on arrival. Inspection Pit runs three exhibitions a year and reserves one slot for the resident, so the residency can lead to a solo show at the space roughly six months later — the 2025 resident, RCA photography graduate Danilo Zocatelli, showed his photographic and video project VIADO there in May 2026. The residency is aimed at artists who want uninterrupted time and space away from commercial pressure; the call says only "artists" and names no media, but the space's own programming makes clear lens-based work is at home there. Applying is free: complete the downloadable application form and email it in with a 150-word artist statement, up to six images, and two character references. The artist must cover their own food, materials, travel and day-to-day costs.
calls.summary: Month-long West Sussex residency: free private accommodation, studio, £500 bursary and a possible solo show six months on.
prose: Inspection Pit is a not-for-profit contemporary art space in West Sussex, housed in a converted barn that once served as a garage for vintage cars — the sunken inspection pit in its floor gave the organisation its name. It sits beside a working farm near the South Downs and presents three exhibitions a year, one of which is reserved for its artist resident.

The 2027 residency runs from 30 January to 27 February 2027. The selected artist stays on site for up to one month in private accommodation, free of charge, with a dedicated studio for independent work and a bicycle available for use in the local area. A £500 bursary is paid at the start of the residency to help with personal expenses. The artist provides their own food and studio materials and covers travel, transportation and day-to-day living costs.

Approximately six months after the residency ends, the resident may be invited to present a body of work in a solo exhibition at the space. This is a real pathway rather than a nominal one: the 2025 resident Danilo Zocatelli, who completed an MA in Photography at the Royal College of Art, showed his photography and video project VIADO at Inspection Pit in May 2026.

The call is worded openly, for "artists" across the visual and creative arts, without naming individual media. Photographers should read that as an invitation rather than a hedge: the space gave Zocatelli his solo show, and its 2023 exhibition SAHAR was made with Sirkhane Darkroom, the photography workshop working with children in southeast Turkey. No age or residence restriction is published, and there is no application fee.

To apply, download the application form from the residency page and email it, with a 150-word artist statement, a digital portfolio of up to six images, and two character references, to inspectionpit.uk@gmail.com. The deadline is 5 August 2026. Artists selected for interview are notified by 21 August 2026, interviews take place on 1 September, and the 2027 resident is notified by 4 September 2026.

calls.title: Luis Valtueña International Humanitarian Photography Award 2026
calls.description: Médicos del Mundo Spain's 30th annual award for documentary and photojournalistic series on health, humanitarian action, international cooperation, emergencies, social exclusion, migration, refuge, armed conflict, inequality or human rights violations — with particular value given to stories that receive little public coverage. Entry is free and anonymous: photographers submit a series of 5 to 10 images, at least half of them made between 2025 and 2026, with no name in the captions, project text or file names, and the jury assesses the work without knowing who made it. The €12,000 prize fund is split €6,000 to the winner and €2,000 each to second, third and fourth place, plus a €1,500 special prize from the Donostia Human Rights Film Festival awarded to one photograph from the winning series, which becomes the festival's 2027 image. Every selected series enters a touring exhibition and printed catalogue produced by Médicos del Mundo, which commits to promoting the photographers for at least a year; winners receive travel and two nights' accommodation for the award ceremony and exhibition opening in Madrid in January 2027. Only single-frame photographs are accepted, digital work must stay within technical correction, and photographers keep the rights to their images.

calls.title: Sirmione Photo Marathon 2026
calls.description: One-day photo marathon on Lake Garda, run by the Municipality of Sirmione as part of the 17th Sirmione Award for Photography. On Sunday 11 October 2026 a maximum of 250 registered photographers meet at 9am in Piazza Carducci and then have eight hours, from 10am to 6pm, to interpret four themes announced by the jury on the day — one photograph per theme, all of it shot inside the marathon window, delivered digitally by 18 October. Reflex, compact and phone cameras are all admitted, and the jury explicitly rewards spontaneity and a photographer's relationship with the place. First prize is €1,500, second €500, third a two-night stay for two in Sirmione, and the best image in each individual theme takes €250. Registration costs €12 and is online only — it closes on 4 October, cannot be done on the day, and places are limited; accompanied minors take part free. Images may be optimised to the author's taste but not distorted: adding or removing key elements, or using generative AI to enlarge, enhance or insert unreal elements, means exclusion, and originals can be requested.

calls.title: SALTPRINT Volume 01 — From Where You Stand
calls.description: First volume of SALTPRINT, an independent print photography zine and archive founded, edited and designed single-handedly by photographer and designer Petra Zegnal in Zagreb, and published every two months from open calls for photographs made across Europe. The theme From Where You Stand is about point of view — literal, emotional, political, personal or poetic: a window, a street, a daily walk, a workplace, a corner of Europe. The editor is looking for images that feel observed rather than forced, and states plainly that this is not about finding the most dramatic location. Submit one photograph, taken anywhere in Europe though you need not live there; digital or film, black and white or colour, street, documentary, landscape or portrait, shot on a camera or a phone. Selection is on connection to the theme, visual strength, atmosphere and originality rather than technical perfection, and beginners, students, self-taught and previously unpublished photographers are explicitly welcome. Three featured photographers per volume are also invited to a short written interview and receive a print copy; other selected photographers receive a digital copy. Free to enter, no payment for Volume 01, and photographers keep full copyright. Deadline 13 September 23:59 CET, selections by 30 September, publication October 2026.
calls.summary: One photograph taken anywhere in Europe for the first volume of a Zagreb-run indie print zine — free, beginners welcome.

calls.title: HOU @ HCP
calls.description: HCP dedicated its third gallery space in 2024 to photographers from Houston and its metro area, and considers submissions on a rolling basis for one of eight solo exhibition slots a year. The call opens each September and stays open until the end of August; work is reviewed as it arrives and applicants hear by the end of the following month. There are no themes and no limits on the type of work so long as it falls within the discipline of photography, and no experience level is required — Houston-based artists may also apply more than once a year with new work. HCP provides installation, lighting and insurance, and has a limited number of white metal frames, though it does not supply matting. There is no entry fee, but entrants must be HCP members at the time of submission; memberships are non-refundable and the membership number goes on the application. Submit up to 15 edited JPGs at 2000px on the longest side with a bio, statement and CV.
calls.summary: Rolling call for one of eight solo slots in HCP's Houston-only gallery — no fee, no theme, membership required.

calls.title: Artist-in-Residence — January–June 2027
calls.description: Six-month workspace residency at Riverviews Artspace in downtown Lynchburg, Virginia, sponsored by Bank of the James, for the January–June 2027 term. The resident gets free space within a shared artist studio, access to Riverviews' creative community, staff and professional network, individualised professional development including mentorship and portfolio feedback, and a final exhibition or public presentation of the work made during the residency. Monthly public engagement runs through First Fridays and open studios. In exchange the resident keeps regular studio hours, gives curatorial and installation help on every exhibition in the term, engages with visitors, and delivers at least one public artist talk, workshop or presentation. Open to emerging or mid-career artists comfortable in a shared studio, open to collaboration, interested in installation and curation, and able to keep a consistent presence in Lynchburg for six months. Free to apply, but note this is workspace only — no housing and no monetary compensation. Selection announced December 15, residency begins January 1, 2027.

calls.title: Los Vivos y Los Muertos 2026
calls.description: Fourth annual juried exhibition honouring the cultures, heritage and traditions of Mexico and the southwest United States, centred on work inspired by Día de los Muertos. Photography is an explicitly eligible medium alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, ceramics, sculpture, metal, wood and fibre; all genres and styles that fit the theme are considered, 2D and 3D. Open nationwide to established and emerging artists aged 14 and above — the prospectus defines emerging as hobbyists or artists still developing their practice with little public recognition, and established as professionals whose main economic activity is making art. Up to three works may be entered, each with year, size, medium, an artist statement and a 50–80 word note on the inspiration behind the piece. Work previously submitted to the 2023, 2024 or 2025 editions is not eligible, and pieces may not exceed 48 inches in any direction or 20 pounds. The show is curated by visual art professionals and forms part of a month-long, county-wide Día de Muertos celebration mounted with Lake Jackson Historical Association, Freeport Historical Museum, Brazoria County Historical Museum, Brazosport LULAC and the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce of Brazoria County. Selected work hangs at The Center for the Arts & Sciences in Clute, Texas from 6 October to 2 November 2026, with a reception and awards presentation on 9 October. Accepted work is hand delivered or shipped to Clute by 2 October — non-local artists cover shipping both ways and must include a pre-paid, insured return label. Due to the family-friendly venue, nudity and highly controversial subject matter will not be selected.
calls.summary: Fourth annual Día de los Muertos juried show in Clute, Texas. Photography is an eligible category; $1,000 Best in Show, open nationwide.

calls.title: Annual Open Juried Show 2026
calls.description: The Brazosport Art League's annual open juried show, hung in the League's gallery at The Center for the Arts & Sciences in Clute, Texas from 11 August to 13 September 2026. Photography is one of six judged categories — 'photography wall hung printed on any medium' sits alongside a separate class for digital-created art and enhanced photography, plus work on canvas or panel, work on paper or Yupo, wall-hung mixed media, and free-standing 3D. Open to all artists; work must be original, made entirely by the entrant within the past two years, and no copies of published material or of other artworks are accepted. Prints of originals are permitted only in the digital art and photography categories. Up to three pieces may be entered, wired for hanging — saw-tooth hangers are accepted only where a frame cannot be wired. Entry is by physical take-in at the Art League Studio on Saturday 1 August, 12–3 PM, with early drop-off accepted in the gallery vault alongside the paperwork and fee. Juror Carl Dalio is a Bay City painter and signature member of the American Watercolor Society, National Watercolor Society and Rocky Mountain National Watermedia Society; he may jury work out of the show with comments. Beyond the $500 overall award, each category carries a $100 blue award, with $75 red and $50 white awards where a class draws 15 entries, plus unlimited green honourable mentions; categories drawing fewer than five entries may not receive awards at all. A reception and awards presentation follows on Friday 14 August, and work is collected after 2 PM on 13 September.
jury: Carl Dalio, painter and signature member, American Watercolor Society
calls.summary: Texas Gulf Coast art league's annual juried show with two photography categories. In-person take-in on 1 August; $500 overall award.

calls.title: Fotograf Zone Festival — International Open Call
calls.description: Open call for photographic projects to be exhibited on poster panels in the busy concourse of Můstek metro station at Wenceslas Square in central Prague, during the 16th Fotograf Zone Festival, running 1–11 October 2026 under the title Wild Kin. Four projects are selected; the festival covers all costs for production, printing, installation and photodocumentation of the exhibition. Work should relate loosely to the festival theme, which asks how we perceive others — both human and non-human — and where the boundaries between humans, animals, environments and technologies lie. The exhibition space consists of sixteen vitrines measuring 147 × 75 cm, four of which are given to the selected artists. Entry is by email with three PDFs: a CV and short bio of up to 500 characters, a portfolio of previous work up to 10 MB, and a project description of up to 1,500 characters with images, also up to 10 MB, each file labelled Surname_Name plus document type. There is no limit on how many projects one author may submit, but the participation fee applies per project, and it is paid by bank transfer to the organisers rather than by card. The international jury is Lucie Černá, a Czech curator, editor and founder of untitled, an independent publishing house and platform for photography and visual art; Karina Golisová, a Slovak photographer working in documentary practices who studied at AFAD Bratislava and FAMU; Lovro Japundžić, a Zagreb-based curator whose work explores the interplay between performance and visual art; and Amelie Rose Schüle, director of Photoforum Pasquart in Biel/Bienne since 2023. Fotograf Zone has connected photography communities from Prague outward since 2002 as a magazine, gallery and international festival.
jury: Lucie Černá, curator, editor and founder, untitled
Amelie Rose Schüle, Director, Photoforum Pasquart

calls.title: For the Love of Art 2026
calls.description: Juried exhibition at the ArtCentre of Plano, housed in the historic Saigling House in Haggard Park — a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark on the National Register of Historic Places. Photography is named outright in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, fiber, ceramics, glass and sculpture; video, performance, sound-based work, murals and site-specific installations are not eligible. Open to artists aged 18 and over who keep a primary residence in Texas, at all career stages. Up to three works may be entered and each is juried independently; 2D work is capped at 36 inches on the longest side including the frame, and all work must have been completed within the last five years. Work generated primarily through generative artificial intelligence is not eligible, and any use of generative AI in the process must be disclosed. The juror is Deborah Hartigan, a Dallas-based abstract expressionist, sculptor, gallerist and art advisor with more than forty years in practice, who founded DHV Artworks in 2016 and opened its 5,000 square foot Dallas Design District gallery in 2021; her clients include American Airlines, which commissioned her to curate its DFW Flagship Lounge. The exhibition is the centrepiece of the ArtCentre's month-long season-opening celebration and runs 24 October to 21 November 2026, with a VIP preview on 24 October and a ticketed gala on 30 October. Selected work appears in the exhibition, an online gallery and a printed catalogue. All work must be for sale, with a 50/50 split between artist and ArtCentre; artist cheques are issued 4 December 2026. Hand-delivered work is due 19 October, shipped work between 12 and 19 October.
jury: Deborah Hartigan, artist, gallerist and curator, DHV Artworks
calls.summary: Juried show at the ArtCentre of Plano's historic Saigling House. Photography is an eligible medium; open to Texas artists 18+.

calls.title: Sip & Stroll Artists' Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Juried members' exhibition presented by the Woodinville Arts Alliance with The Winemakers Reserve, on display in Washington wine country on 13 and 14 November 2026. Photography is one of eleven named categories, alongside acrylic, ceramic, digital, mixed media, oil, pastel, pencil, watercolour, fibre/textile and 3-D. Judging takes place on 13 November, followed that evening by the Sip and Stroll event from 5 to 8 PM, where visitors meet the artists over wine and live music and the awards are presented; the show stays up for the weekend. Each artist may enter up to three pieces made within two years of the show date. Work generated with artificial intelligence is explicitly excluded, as are giclée prints, art prints and copies. Pieces must measure at least 144 square inches and no more than 2,304 square inches including framing, be wired to hang — no glass clips, easel backs or saw-tooth hangers — and any matted work must be covered with glass or plexiglass. All entries must be priced to sell and remain on display for the run; the Alliance retains 30 per cent commission on sales of original art and pays artists within two weeks of the event. Accepted work is hand-delivered to the venue between 10 and 11 AM on 13 November, or shipped with return postage enclosed, and collected on the Saturday afternoon; the Alliance states that artists must be present at the Friday evening event. Entry is open only to Woodinville Arts Alliance members, but membership can be bought to enter and costs $44 a year. The judge is visual artist Anna Macrae.
calls.summary: Juried members' show at a Woodinville winery with photography as a named category. Cash awards; membership required to enter.

calls.title: 2026 Call for Curators
calls.description: Annual call for curatorial proposals for Crown Gallery at Metro Art Studios in Bridgeport, Connecticut, for an exhibition running 7 November 2026 to 2 January 2027. Open to curators working or residing in Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, New York and New Jersey; all visual art mediums are considered, and the gallery is particularly suited to large installations and conceptual art as well as more traditional forms. The selected curator receives a $350 stipend. Proposals need a curatorial statement explaining the focus and concept, a minimum of three artists, and between ten and twenty images of the work planned for the show — examples of similar work are acceptable. All work in the exhibition must be for sale, and artwork by the proposing curator may not account for more than a third of the pieces shown. Special consideration goes to proposals reflecting a commitment to access, diversity, equity and inclusion. Crown Gallery is roughly 1,250 square feet — 25 by 50 feet with 11-foot ceilings — in a restored mill building; a floor plan is attached to the prospectus and a visit before applying is encouraged. Installation runs 31 October to 4 November, and the opening reception on Saturday 7 November coincides with a weekend-long city-wide open studio event that brings almost 2,000 visitors to Metro Art Studios. The curator handles wall labels, price list and other in-gallery material; the organisation covers neither shipping nor installation costs, though pedestals are available and all work is fully insured while on site in a building with 24-hour security. A 40 per cent commission is retained on sales. Metro Art Studios is a non-profit housing 39 loft studios in a three-storey former corset factory in Bridgeport's South End.

calls.title: REMEDY Photo Festival 2027 — Photography Commission
calls.description: REMEDY Photo Festival and Lincoln Museum & Usher Gallery invite photographers and artists working with photography to propose a new body of work exploring health, care, wellbeing and lived experience. The selected artist receives a £5,000 commission — a £3,500 artist fee plus a £1,500 production budget — to develop work for exhibition at REMEDY Photo Festival 2027 at a venue in Lincolnshire, with curatorial support from the REMEDY team and support from Lincoln Museum & Usher Gallery. The commission asks what role photography can play in changing how we see, understand and talk about health; proposals may explore illness and disability, care and caring relationships, identity and belonging, recovery and resilience, physical and mental wellbeing, and communities and connection. Outline concepts are welcome — the selected artist develops the proposal through research, engagement and collaboration during a November 2026 – May 2027 development period, and collaborative or socially engaged approaches are encouraged. Apply with up to 5 images (JPEG, 1000px longest side), a project statement of up to 300 words and a 100-word bio.
calls.summary: £5,000 commission (£3,500 fee + £1,500 production) for new work on health and care, shown at REMEDY Photo Festival 2027. Free to enter.

calls.title: 16th Arbella International Photography Contest
calls.description: Long-running free international contest, now in its sixteenth year, run by Arbella Pasta (Durum Gıda) as a social-responsibility and arts project bringing Turkish and international photographers together. The 2026 edition marks the 200th anniversary of the invention of photography and runs two categories: the themed "Beauty of Imperfection", which looks for the aesthetics, emotion and story carried by marks, breakages, wear, irregularities and unexpected detail that fall outside the perception of perfection, and "Open", with no subject restriction at all. A separate Future Viewfinder award is applied automatically to entrants aged 18–24 and comes with physical workshop programmes in Istanbul. Entrants may submit up to five photographs per category and may win at most one award per category; work must have been taken on or after 1 January 2021. Collage, HDR, artificial bokeh, and the addition or removal of objects are all disallowed, and images generated from text prompts by AI tools are strictly not accepted. Up to 26 photographs across both categories are selected for an exhibition. Copyright stays with the photographer; awarded, honourable-mention and exhibited work may be used credited for contest promotion and archiving.
jury: Barbara Di Maio, co-founder, Women in Street Italy
Coşkun Aral, war correspondent, documentary and TV producer
Sumru Gözaydın, Marketing Communications Manager, Arbella
calls.summary: Free 16th-year international contest on the beauty of imperfection. $10,500 in prizes, an exhibition, and a separate award for ages 18–24.
