prose: The Arbella International Photography Contest has run for sixteen years, organised by Durum Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. — the company behind Arbella Pasta — as a social-responsibility and arts programme intended to build a platform where Turkish and international photographers meet. It is free to enter and carries a total prize pool of $10,500.

The 2026 edition is framed around the 200th anniversary of the invention of photography and is divided into two categories. "Beauty of Imperfection", the main category, asks for images in which traces, breakages, wear, irregularity, accident and unexpected detail are treated as aesthetic parts of character, reality and sincerity rather than as flaws. The "Open" category carries no subject restriction — people, nature, city, street, portrait, documentary, conceptual or architectural work all qualify.

New for this edition is Future Viewfinder, an award applied automatically to entrants aged 18–24 in each category. It is not a separate application route, and the organisers say it will extend beyond prize money into physical workshop programmes held in Istanbul for selected younger participants.

Entrants may submit up to five photographs per category, with no repetition of content between them, and may receive at most one award per category. Work must have been taken on or after 1 January 2021, and previous exhibition or publication elsewhere is not a barrier. The technical rules are strict: collage, HDR, artificial background blur, and the cloning, moving or addition of objects are all disallowed, with only sensor dust-spot cleaning permitted; EXIF data must be intact; and images generated from text prompts using AI tools such as Midjourney or DALL·E are strictly not accepted.

The selection committee is Barbara Di Maio, Coşkun Aral, Ercan Arslan, İlkay Öztürk and Sumru Gözaydın. Jury evaluation takes place on 12 September 2026 and results are announced on 25 September 2026. A maximum of 26 photographs across both categories are launched as an exhibition, with the award ceremony and opening announced separately. Copyright remains with the photographer; awarded, honourable-mention and exhibited images may be used with credit by the organiser for promotion, communication and archiving, and may not be sold or transferred commercially.

calls.title: Howard Chapnick Grant 2026
calls.description: Grant from the W. Eugene Smith Memorial Fund that recognises programs rather than individuals — initiatives making a significant contribution to the field of documentary photography through education. Funding may support research, direct learning, online resources, publication, archives, exhibition or dissemination through social media; it explicitly does not fund the creation or production of photographs. Applicants must be based anywhere in the world and must have been operating for at least one year. The 2026 award is $7,500, paid as $6,000 on award and $1,500 on submission of the final report. Applications are made by email directly to the Smith Fund with a one-page description of no more than 500 words covering the program's activities, its constituency and its contribution to the community, plus at least three reference links for verification. Entries open 1 July 2026 and recipients are announced 15 December 2026. A $25 donation is invited but voluntary — the Board of Trustees notes that some programs can afford to donate and others cannot.
calls.summary: $7,500 from the Smith Fund for programs advancing documentary photography through education. Free to apply, by email, worldwide.
prose: The Howard Chapnick Grant sits alongside the W. Eugene Smith Grant in Humanistic Photography and the Smith Student Grant, but it works differently from both: it recognises programs, not individuals. The Fund is looking for initiatives that make a significant contribution to the field of documentary photography through education, and applicants must have been operating for at least one year. There is no geographic restriction.

For 2026 the award is $7,500, dispersed as $6,000 on receipt of the grant and $1,500 on submission of a final report. Funding may go toward research, direct learning, online resources, publication, archives, exhibition, or dissemination through social media. It explicitly does not fund the making or production of photographs — this is money for the educational infrastructure around documentary photography rather than for a shooting project.

Unlike the Fund's other grants, applications do not go through Picter. Entries are accepted by the Smith Fund directly by email, with "Chapnick Grant" in the subject line, and consist of a description of no more than 500 words on one page covering the program's activities, its constituency and its contribution to its community, together with at least three reference links so the Fund can verify the work.

A $25 donation accompanies the application, but it is explicitly voluntary: the Board of Trustees states that it understands some programs can afford to donate while others cannot. Entries opened on 1 July 2026, the deadline is 12 October 2026 at 11:59pm EDT, and recipients are announced on 15 December 2026.

calls.title: Hodder Fellowship 2027-28
calls.description: Ten-month visiting fellowship at Princeton University awarding $93,000 to artists and writers of exceptional promise, selected — in the terms of the fellowship — more for promise than for performance. The award is intended to give recipients "studious leisure" to pursue an independent project and undertake significant new work, and carries no formal teaching obligation. The 2027-28 cycle accepts applications from the Program in Dance, the Program in Theater and Music Theater, the Program in Visual Arts and the Department of Music, so photographers and other visual artists are eligible this round. Applications ask for a résumé, a project proposal of 500 words and work samples such as images, writing excerpts or performance video. US citizenship is not required. Previous recipients of the Princeton Arts Fellowship may not apply, and an applicant may apply for the Hodder at most twice in a lifetime.

prose: The Hodder Fellowship is awarded by Princeton University's Lewis Center for the Arts to artists and writers of exceptional promise — composers, choreographers, performance artists, visual artists, writers, translators and humanists with, in the fellowship's own phrase, "much more than ordinary intellectual and literary gifts". Candidates are chosen more for promise than for performance, which makes it one of the rare major fellowships explicitly aimed at where a practice is going rather than what it has already accumulated.

The award is a ten-month appointment carrying a stipend of $93,000. Its stated purpose is to give recipients "studious leisure" — time to pursue an independent project and undertake significant new work. There is no formal teaching requirement, distinguishing it from the Princeton Arts Fellowship, which asks fellows to teach a course each semester.

Eligibility rotates by discipline. For this cycle Princeton is accepting applications from the Program in Dance, the Program in Theater and Music Theater, the Program in Visual Arts, and the Department of Music — so photographers and other lens-based artists working under the Visual Arts umbrella can apply this round. US citizenship is not required.

Applications consist of a résumé, a 500-word project proposal and work samples, which may be images, writing excerpts or performance video depending on the discipline. Previous Princeton Arts Fellowship recipients are not eligible, and an applicant may apply for the Hodder no more than twice in a lifetime. The deadline is 8 September 2026 at 11:59pm EDT, and there is no application fee.

calls.title: SPIE International Day of Light Photo Contest 2026
calls.description: Free annual contest from SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics, run in support of the International Day of Light and open to amateur and professional photographers aged 18 and over worldwide. The contest looks for images showing the transformative impact of light on lives, communities and the planet: the properties of light and how it interacts with the atmosphere, nature and materials; light technology such as lasers and LEDs; images made with telescopes, microscopes and other optical instruments; people interacting with light; and light in the betterment of the human condition. Entrants may submit a maximum of two photographs, each on its own entry form and accompanied by a title and an artist statement covering subject, location, date, equipment and any adjustments made. Images must be at least 3,000 pixels on the longest side at 300dpi, in TIF or JPEG, and must have been taken after 16 May 2024. Only limited optimisation is allowed — no watermarks, and AI may not be used to generate images or composites. Winning photographs are published in SPIE publications and displayed at SPIE conferences and exhibitions with credit. Prize money cannot be paid to entrants in countries under US sanctions, though they may still enter and compete for recognition.
jury: Panel of judges selected by SPIE

prose: SPIE — the international society for optics and photonics, based in Bellingham, Washington — runs this contest each year in support of the International Day of Light, with the stated aim of raising public awareness of the role light and light-based technology play in daily life. It is free to enter and open to amateur and professional photographers alike, aged 18 and over, anywhere in the world.

The theme is broad within its subject: images that depict the properties of light and how it interacts with the atmosphere, nature and materials; light technology such as lasers and LEDs; pictures created with optical instruments like telescopes and microscopes; people interacting with light or light technology; and light in the betterment of the human condition. Judging weighs content, scientific interest, creativity and artistry, execution of photographic technique, and overall appeal for the International Day of Light — a mix that rewards work which is scientifically engaged and visually resolved at once.

Each person may submit a maximum of two entries, one photo per form. Every entry needs a title and an artist statement giving the subject, the location and date, the equipment used, any adjustments made and how the image ties to the theme. Files must be TIF or JPEG, 300dpi or more, at least 3,000 pixels on the longest side and between 5MB and 20MB. New for 2026, photographs must have been taken within the past two years, after 16 May 2024, and re-submissions are not considered.

Only limited enhancement for brightness, contrast and minor cosmetic flaws is allowed; black and white is fine; watermarks are not acceptable; and artificial intelligence may not be used to generate images or create composites, with judges disqualifying anything that appears to have used AI beyond simple adjustments.

Prizes are $2,500 for first place, $1,000 for second, $500 for third, and a $1,000 Judges' Choice for Best of Science. Winning photographs are also published across SPIE publications, online and in print, and displayed at SPIE conferences and exhibitions, with credit to the photographer. One prize per participant. Entries close 16 September 2026 at 11:59pm PST; winners are notified 16 October and announced 30 October 2026. Note that prize money cannot be awarded to individuals located in countries under US sanctions, though entrants from those countries are welcome to compete for recognition.

calls.title: Anderson Center Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Two- to four-week residencies on the historic Tower View estate in rural Red Wing, Minnesota, running May through October 2027 for artists, writers, musicians and performers of exceptional promise and demonstrated accomplishment. The Anderson Center uses "artist" broadly to mean those working in visual, literary and performing arts, including work that does not fit neatly into categories, and hosts roughly five residents at a time and 35–40 a year. There is no charge for the residency itself and all food is provided: each resident has a room in the Tower View residence with weekly housekeeping, and a chef prepares dinner on weeknights with all groceries supplied. Visual artists are given a 15' x 26' studio, and shared facilities on site include a darkroom, a printmaking studio with an etching press, and an open-air forge. No stipend is attached to the general program and residents arrange their own travel. Since 1995 more than 900 residents from 46 states and over 40 countries have worked there. There is one application deadline for the season, and selected artists, the wait-list and runners-up are notified by 2 March 2027.

prose: The Anderson Center at Tower View, founded in 1995 on a historic estate in rural Red Wing, Minnesota, offers residencies of two to four weeks' duration from May through October each year. It hosts around five residents at a time and 35–40 a year, and since its founding more than 900 residents have come from 46 states and over 40 countries. Work made there has gone on to receive Guggenheim Fellowships and NEA funding.

For photographers the practical detail worth knowing is the facilities. Visual artists are provided a 15' x 26' studio, and the shared workspaces on site include a darkroom, a printmaking studio with a Charles Brand-like etching press, and an open-air forge — a rarer combination than most residencies of this scale offer.

There is no charge for the residency and all food is provided. Each resident gets a room in the historic Tower View residence with a desk, a large closet and either a private or shared bathroom, with linens and weekly housekeeping. A residency chef cooks dinner for the cohort at 6pm on weeknights using the commercial kitchen on site, and all groceries are supplied. Outside the Early Career Artist, Deaf Artists and Public Artist programs no additional funding is available, and residents arrange their own transport to the center, to Minneapolis–St. Paul Airport or to the train station in Red Wing.

The Anderson Center uses the word "artist" broadly, meaning those working in visual, literary and performing arts including those whose work doesn't fit neatly into categories and genres, and states that the program supports artists from around the world across a wide range of cultures, races, sexual orientations and genders. The cohort model is central — the organisation's stated belief is that exchange across disciplines is generative.

Applications for the 2027 season are open now, with a $30 application fee. There is only one deadline: 12 p.m. noon Central Standard Time on 12 January 2027. Jury review takes place in late January and February, and the selected artists, wait-list and runners-up are notified by 2 March 2027.

calls.title: Anderson Center Early Career Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Month-long funded residency for a cohort of five early-career artists at the Anderson Center's Tower View estate in Red Wing, Minnesota, supported by the Jerome Foundation. Selected artists each receive a $625 per week stipend, a travel honorarium, a documentation budget, art-making resources, lodging and studio space, and chef-prepared communal dinners. The program is interdisciplinary and open to all disciplines; visual artists are given a studio, and the site's shared facilities include a darkroom and a printmaking studio. Applicants must be legal residents of Minnesota or of the five boroughs of New York City, must not be enrolled in a degree-granting program from application through the residency, must self-identify as early career with two to ten years of generative experience beyond any formal training, and must have an artistic practice centred on creating entirely new work. Artists with more than ten years of experience are generally ineligible, though exceptions are made for those who took time away for caregiving, illness or education. There is no fee to apply, and selected artists, the wait-list and runners-up are notified by 2 March 2027.

prose: The Early Career Artist Residency is the funded strand of the Anderson Center's program, supported by the Jerome Foundation. A month-long cohort of five artists works together at the Tower View estate in Red Wing, Minnesota, in a program built specifically for artists early in their development who have not yet received substantial recognition.

Unlike the general residency, this one pays. Selected artists each receive a $625 per week stipend, a travel honorarium, a documentation budget covering services such as photography, video and audio, art-making resources, lodging and studio space, and chef-prepared communal dinners. There is no fee to apply.

The program is interdisciplinary and open to all disciplines, with the cohort model and cross-disciplinary exchange treated as central to what the residency offers. Visual artists are given a studio, and the shared facilities on the estate include a darkroom and a printmaking studio with an etching press — relevant if you work in analogue or alternative process.

Eligibility is tightly drawn. Applicants must be legal residents of Minnesota or of New York City's five boroughs; must not be enrolled in a degree-granting program from the time of application through the residency; must self-identify as early career, meaning roughly two to ten years of generative experience beyond formal training; and must have a practice centred on creating entirely new work. Artists with more than ten years of experience are generally ineligible, though the Anderson Center makes exceptions for those who stepped away for caregiving, illness or education.

The deadline is 12 p.m. noon Central Standard Time on 12 January 2027. Jury review takes place in late January and early February, and selected artists, the wait-list and runners-up are notified by 2 March 2027.

calls.title: I'M SCARED 2026
calls.description: The third edition of Bethany Arts Community's I'M SCARED series, born out of the questions of what it truly means to be scared, what shadows haunt your thoughts and what we should genuinely fear — and how you make space to show frightening work at all. calls.description: A juried exhibition at the Deines Cultural Center in Russell, Kansas — a three-gallery centre built around the wood engravings of Prairie Printmaker E. Hubert Deines — looking for artists who bring thoughtfulness and unique insight to the magical, mystical and macabre. Awards are $500 for first place, $250 for second and $150 for third, judged in person and announced at the 23 October reception. Notification 19 September, delivery by 7 October, exhibition 16 October – 20 November 2026.

Notification 18 September, drop-off 27–28 September, exhibition 1 October – 1 November 2026, reception with juror award 10 October.

calls.title: Wavelength: Yellow
calls.description: Wavelength is Artlink's colour-specific open call exploring the physical spectrum of visible colour, changing hue with each iteration; this edition is devoted entirely to yellow. Work need not be only yellow but must have a primarily yellow focus, and photography is named explicitly among the welcome media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramic, installation, video and fibre. Juried by Ellen Mensch, the Fort Wayne artist, curator and educator who has run Artlink's exhibitions and education programming for more than six years. Artlink is a nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne. Open to artists 18 and over residing in the United States at $12 per entry; accepted work must arrive ready for installation, shipped work framed with plexiglass rather than glass, and a 35% sales commission applies. Exhibition 22 October – 15 November 2026, accepted work due 11 October.
jury: Ellen Mensch, Exhibitions, Education & Marketing, Artlink

calls.title: 2028 Bear Gallery Exhibition
calls.description: Fairbanks Arts Association's annual portfolio call for its Bear Gallery, which programmes two exhibitions a month year-round by Alaskan artists and groups working across media, for local and international visitors. Artists submit a cohesive portfolio rather than a themed entry and may propose a solo show, a group show of two or more artists without a curator, or a curated exhibition where a curator sets the theme and selects the work; proposals for curated juried exhibitions are not accepted. Open to Alaska residents 18 and over who live in the state at least six months of the year, with an individual or group eligible for a Bear Gallery show once every four years. Submit 7–10 work samples made in the last five years, up to three of which may be video, with signatures and identifying names removed so a panel of professional Alaskan artists can review the applications blind. Entry is $35, or $30 for Fairbanks Arts members at the Artist level and above, and AI-generated imagery may not appear in exhibited work. Applications open 1 August 2026 and applicants are notified in early 2027 for exhibitions in 2028.

calls.title: In the Realm of the Mystic
calls.description: Verum Ultimum, the Portland gallery known for long-running themed series like Chasing Ghosts and Abstract Sanctuary, invites artists to transcend the mundane for an online-only exhibition. The theme is deliberately loose: the gallery is less interested in a literal or didactic reading than in how your work speaks to it — whether your process reveals a subdued or bold manifestation, whether you borrow from myth, fairy tale, legend and cultural influence, whether you are drawn to bestiaries, invented lands or social commentary, or whether the mystic surfaces as a simple abstract field that speaks to life itself. All media and modes of expression are encouraged, including narrative, illustrative, conceptual and abstract work. Open to artists 18 and over, national and international; a minimum of two images to enter, with additional images at $5 each. Work may be listed for sale at a 20% gallery commission or marked not for sale, a first for Verum's virtual shows. calls.title: LatinXperiencia 2026: La Resiliencia
calls.description: Cabrillo Gallery's annual LatinXperiencia series returns for National Hispanic Heritage Month with a call to Latino/a/x artists living anywhere in the US, working in any art media or discipline. The theme is resilience — the capacity that lets us bend without breaking, whether through personal upheaval such as illness, the end of a relationship or the death of someone we love, or through the larger pressures of authoritarianism, threats to immigrant communities and communities of colour, economic crisis, war and environmental disaster. Work does not have to address Latino/a/x themes or culture, though it can; the gallery welcomes any interpretation, imagery or content that captures the idea of resilience. Juried by Alyssarhaye Graciano, Visual Arts Curator at MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana) in San Jose, an author, textile artist and advocate for emerging and established artists of colour. Up to three works per artist; entries must be original and not previously shown at Cabrillo Gallery, and no AI-generated images will be considered. Three Juror's Awards of $300, $250 and $200 are presented. This is a physical exhibition — accepted artists deliver or ship work at their own expense and must include a prepaid return label. Selected artists are notified by 17 August. The show runs 28 September to 27 October 2026 at the gallery in Library 1002 on the Aptos campus, with a reception on 26 September and a curator's talk during it. The submission deadline was extended to 4 August.
jury: Alyssarhaye Graciano, Visual Arts Curator, MACLA

calls.title: New Works 2026
calls.description: A juried exhibition in the Hayloft Gallery at the Floyd Center for the Arts, built around the bold directions, fresh perspectives and evolving techniques of artists working in the Blue Ridge region. The show is looking for the new media, methods and creative journeys artists are embracing — experiments with unfamiliar materials, innovative processes, or fresh interpretations of traditional forms — and restricts entries to work made in the past two years, so it reads as a snapshot of where a practice is right now rather than a survey. All visual media are welcome, including photography; video entries must arrive with both the file and the display equipment plus installation directions, and artists of 3D work supply their own display. Open to artists 18 and over living within a 150-mile radius of the centre in Floyd, Virginia. Up to three works per artist. First ($200), Second ($150) and Third ($100) Place awards are presented along with a People's Choice ($50); the centre retains a 40% commission on sales, with 60% paid to the artist. The juror is being finalised and will be announced. Jurying runs 29 August to 6 September, notifications 8 September, delivery 8–16 September, and the exhibition opens 3 October with a reception 4–6pm, closing 21 November 2026.
calls.summary: Blue Ridge regional juried show for work made in the last two years. All visual media, $500 in awards, Hayloft Gallery.

calls.title: Fotosalongen 2027
calls.description: Sweden's largest photography salon returns for its second edition at the Hasselblad Center in Gothenburg, and the open call is deliberately wide: amateur and professional photographers working across every genre are invited to submit, with no set theme. The foundation welcomes documentary photography and photojournalism alongside nature, family, street, science, politics and art photography, and says the salon is built to create unexpected encounters between established artists, emerging talents and photographers whose work has never been shown publicly. The jury looks for compelling images and photographic narratives with depth, originality and a diversity of expression, so that the selected works together offer a broad snapshot of photography today. Submissions are still photography only — no video — as up to five single images, or an installation without electronic equipment; one project per person or group, and groups may apply jointly. Entry is free. Selected photographers exhibit at the Hasselblad Center, receive compensation of SEK 3,200, appear in the exhibition catalogue and may sell work; participants cover transport of works to and from the Center. The jury is chaired by the foundation's chief curator Dragana Vujanović Östlind and includes Alexandra Ellis of the Sune Jonsson Centre for Documentary Photography at Västerbottens museum, film director Tarik Saleh and photographer Elisabeth Toll. Applications run from 1 August to 18 October 2026 via Picter; the exhibition itself runs 23 April to 26 September 2027, in a venue that draws around 70,000 visitors. Open to anyone who turns 18 during the application year or is older, and who is either a Swedish citizen or has a residential address in Sweden.
jury: Dragana Vujanović Östlind, Chief Curator, Hasselblad Foundation (Chair)
Alexandra Ellis, Curator, Sune Jonsson Centre for Documentary Photography

calls.title: Overshoot
calls.description: The first open call from DOTLOGIC, the Trieste social cooperative behind URBAN Photo Awards, Exhibit Around, dotART and Trieste Photo Days, asking photographers worldwide for their own account of climate change. The title refers to the crossing of the 1.5°C threshold: 2024 was the first full year above it, and the call takes that as the beginning of what science calls an overshoot, where every fraction of a degree brings consequences that are more severe and less reversible. Submissions can approach the theme through landscapes in transformation — coasts, mountains, farmland, cities — or through people: those who work, adapt or resist in the face of climate effects, the everyday gestures a changing climate transforms, and more conceptual readings of the distance between what the numbers say and what bodies feel. Any genre is welcome, from reportage and documentary to street, landscape and fine art, but only single photographs are admitted; no projects or portfolios. AI-generated or AI-manipulated images are strictly prohibited, as are watermarks and signatures. Files must be JPG, RGB/sRGB, at least 2000 pixels on the short side and under 10MB. Twenty selected photographs are exhibited at Magazzino 26 in Porto Vecchio, Trieste from 23 October to 8 November 2026 alongside work by Mark Power and Christopher Morris, the international guest artists of Trieste Photo Days 2026, with full production — printing and setup — covered by the organisers. Selected authors are published in the official Magazzino 26 catalogue, receive a limited-edition commemorative coin, and may be considered for future Exhibit Around exhibitions. Authors keep moral and intellectual property rights; the organisers take non-exclusive promotional rights with author credit. The entry fee is €20, and the number of photographs you may submit depends on your Exhibit Around membership tier, from one image for non-members up to twenty-five at the top level. The call runs 1 to 31 August 2026 and responds to Goal 13 of the UN 2030 Agenda.

calls.title: Art Solano 2026
calls.description: Arts Benicia's county-wide survey of the artists of Solano County, open to any subject and to all 2D and 3D visual media plus video — photography included. Eligibility runs to artists living in Solano County or whose main studio is there, which covers Benicia, Dixon, Fairfield, Suisun City, Rio Vista, Vacaville, Vallejo and the communities of Allendale, Hartley and Green Valley. The juror is Glen Helfand, a writer, critic, curator and professor in the Graduate Fine Arts Program at California College of the Arts, whose writing on art, culture and design has appeared in Artforum, Aperture, The Guardian, Photograph, SFMOMA Open Space and W, and who has organised exhibitions for the de Young Museum, the San Jose Museum of Art, the San Francisco Art Institute, the Mills College Art Museum, Art Toronto and the San Francisco Main Library. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 36 inches wide or 72 inches high including the frame, and 3D work is capped at a 36 by 36 inch footprint; staff should be contacted about installations or unusual sizes. Work previously shown at Arts Benicia is not eligible. Wall works must be wired rather than hung from sawtooth hangers, there is a 35-pound weight limit on hanging work, and the prospectus states that giclées are not accepted, so check with the gallery before submitting inkjet prints. Arts Benicia handles all sales and artists receive 60%. Entries close 2 August 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific, jurying runs 4–15 August and artists are notified 18 August. Hand delivery is 1–2 October and shipped work must arrive by 2 October. The exhibition opens with a members' and artists' preview on 22 October and a public reception on 24 October, and runs to 20 December 2026 at the gallery on Commandant's Lane. The show is supported by a grant from the Solano County Arts Council.
jury: Glen Helfand, writer, critic and curator, California College of the Arts
calls.summary: Solano County survey in all 2D, 3D and video media, juried by critic and curator Glen Helfand for a two-month Benicia show.

calls.description: A small-works call with one governing rule: one dimension of each piece must measure six inches, before framing. Cape Fear Studios in downtown Fayetteville opens it to visual artists in any medium, photography included, with up to three original works per artist — no prints or mass-produced work — and a minimum age of 18. The juror is Silvana Foti, previously executive director of the David McCune International Art Gallery at Methodist University, where she was instrumental in the gallery's opening and the founding of its advisory board. She holds an MFA in printmaking and ceramic sculpture from the Art Institute of Chicago and the University of Notre Dame and a BFA from St Mary's College, and has curated regional, national and international exhibitions including Warhol, Chagall, The Story of the Exodus; Picasso: 25 Years of Edition Ceramics; Rodin: Portraits of a Lifetime; and Impressionism to Modernism: Masterworks of Early Photography, all meeting American Alliance of Museums standards. She taught at college level for more than twenty years and chaired Methodist University's Department of Art. Awards are First Place $450, Second $200, Third $100 and two Honorable Mentions of $50 each. Entries close 10 August 2026 through CaFÉ and the exhibition runs 25 September to 24 November 2026 in the main gallery.

calls.title: Le Salon des Artistes 2026: Represent Your Culture
calls.description: The Denison Arts Council's second annual Salon des Artistes, a juried show in downtown Denison, Texas modelled on the historic Salon de Paris that began in 1667 — the original platform where creative expression, public support and institutional recognition met, and which shaped European art for centuries. This year's theme, inspired by the council's annual Día de los Muertos festival, is 'represent your culture': artists are asked to show how they connect with the people and places they descend from, through beloved recipes, cultural dress, family traditions or anything else that celebrates where they come from. The theme is open to interpretation and every work is considered with nuance, all media judged equally for prizes without regard to category — photography included. The juror is Jose Vargas, an independent exhibition curator and visual artist known for his work with the arts across the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex and founder of the El Corazón and La Virgen de Guadalupe exhibitions in Dallas. The council advertises awards totalling $1,500, itemised in the prospectus as Best in Show $600, Second Place $400, Third Place $250, an Honorable Mention of $100 and a People's Choice of $100 decided by open voting from all guests and announced at the close of the show. Applications close 13 August 2026, electronic acceptance notifications go out 21 August, accepted work is dropped off in Denison on 6 September, and the exhibition opens to the public with an artists' night reception and award presentation on 12 September, with a midway reception on 10 October and a close on 7 November 2026. Note that the council cannot receive or return artwork by mail: accepted artists must arrange drop-off in person and collect work on 8 November. Photography is explicitly listed among the accepted media, wired and ready to hang, and the council retains 20% commission on works sold during the show.
jury: Jose Vargas, independent curator and visual artist
calls.summary: Salon de Paris-inspired juried show on cultural heritage, any medium. $600 Best in Show and a two-month Texas exhibition.

calls.title: 30x30 2026
calls.description: Blue Line Arts' annual challenge asks selected artists to make thirty original artworks in thirty days — a deliberate push to refine a practice, test an unfamiliar direction or simply work faster than deliberation allows. Every finished piece must measure precisely 6 by 6 inches, must hang securely on the wall (no pedestals, and no command strips or temporary hardware for 3D work), and 3D work may not extend more than 6 inches from the wall. Applicants do not submit the thirty pieces up front: the application takes 3–10 samples of existing work reflecting the direction intended for the challenge, and the gallery explicitly asks artists not to make the thirty artworks before being notified. Open to artists everywhere aged 18 and over, in any medium including photography; work must be original, completed within the last two years and never previously exhibited at Blue Line Arts. All pieces must be individually for sale, with the gallery handling sales — non-members receive 50% of gallery sales and members 60%. Entry is free for current Blue Line Arts Artist Members at the $75 level or above with a discount code from the gallery coordinator, and $25 for non-members covering 3 to 10 images. Applications close 4 September 2026 at 5pm Pacific, notifications go out 18 September, and the exhibition runs 24 November to 19 December 2026 in Roseville, with a reception on 19 December.
calls.summary: Make thirty 6x6-inch works in thirty days. Any medium incl. photography, free for members, December show in Roseville.

calls.title: Freedom's Journey
calls.description: Juried exhibition marking the 200th anniversary of Freedom's Journal — America's first Black-owned and Black-operated newspaper, founded in New York in 1827 by Samuel E. Cornish and John B. Russwurm in response to the exclusion and misrepresentation of Black Americans in the mainstream press. The New England Black Artists Collective invites submissions in any medium, and explicitly names photographers alongside sculptors, mixed-media and interdisciplinary artists; the call particularly welcomes creatives with lived experience as members of the African diaspora. Artists are asked what "Freedom's Journey" meant to the paper's original readers, and what it means now — what freedom looks like personally, to a family, to a community, who has led the journey towards it, and what has deferred it. Up to three works may be submitted with a 150–250 word artist statement plus a statement tying the work to the theme; new and existing work are both eligible. Selected work is shown at the Krikorian Gallery at the Worcester Center for Crafts in Worcester, Massachusetts. Three jurors read the entries: Toby Sisson, Associate Professor and Director of the Visual Arts Program at Clark University; Deborah Hall, founder and director of the Worcester Black History Project; and Candace Casey, Gallery Director of the Krikorian Gallery. They name a best of show, which carries a $500 cash prize, and two honorable mentions. Wall pieces must arrive wired and ready to hang (no alligator hooks); textiles may run up to 88 by 90 inches and all other work up to 65 by 60 inches. Artists are notified by 3 January 2027 and jury results are announced by 6 January; work must be in house — delivered or mailed with return postage — by 16 January, and the exhibition runs 1–28 February 2027.
calls.summary: Any-medium juried show on the 200th anniversary of Freedom's Journal, America's first Black-owned newspaper. Krikorian Gallery, Worcester.
jury: Toby Sisson, Associate Professor & Director of the Visual Arts Program, Clark University
Deborah Hall, Founder & Director, Worcester Black History Project
Candace Casey, Gallery Director, Krikorian Gallery

calls.title: Fall into Art 2026
calls.description: The San Marcos Art League's autumn open show at the San Marcos Art Center, asking for work that carries the colours and traditions of the season — from pleasant autumnal memory to the new adventures that arrive as the year turns. Open to all artists across every medium, with photographs, fine art prints and digital art named explicitly alongside sculpture, textiles and pottery. Each artist may enter one original work completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at the Art Center Gallery. Two-dimensional work must be framed or gallery-wrapped with no visible staples, wired for the gallery's hanging system, and no larger than 36 by 68 inches including the frame; three-dimensional work is considered on size and stability. All work must be hand-delivered — the Art Center does not accept shipments — with intake on 30 August, a public reception on 11 September and pickup 1–2 October. Work must be for sale at a price fixed at entry, and the Art League retains a 20% commission. Entry is $10 for Art League members with the code sent to them by email, and $20 otherwise; submissions close 28 August at 5pm or when the show fills.
calls.summary: All-media autumn open show at the San Marcos Art Center; photography named explicitly. Hand delivery, one work, $10 for members.

calls.org: South Haven Center for the Arts
calls.description: National juried exhibition at the South Haven Center for the Arts on Michigan's Lake Michigan shore, built around change as the one constant of human experience — joyous, tragic, sudden or gradual, and above all the way we react to it. Artists are asked to muse on a deviation in their life, work or world and make a piece that reflects their response to a change experienced, anticipated or initiated, with a brief note on how that change informed the work. Open to artists residing in the United States and the Tribal Nations that share these geographies, in any visual medium; work must be original and completed within the last five years, with a maximum of two entries. Two-dimensional work is capped at 72 by 55 inches, three-dimensional work must fit through a standard doorway and stay under 50 pounds, and no installations or ceiling-hung work are accepted. Juried by David Baker, artist and professor emeritus at Southwestern Michigan College and a longtime teacher at Ox-Bow. Awards are $500 for first place and $250 for second; the show runs 26 September to 7 November 2026 with an opening reception on 25 September. Entry is $25 for up to two works, reduced to $10 for students and artists facing unforeseen hardship.
jury: David Baker, Artist and Professor Emeritus, Southwestern Michigan College

prose: The South Haven Center for the Arts sits on the Lake Michigan shore in south-west Michigan, and its annual national juried exhibition is the show it opens to artists from across the country. New/Now: Pondering Change takes as its premise that change is the one fact nobody escapes — losing a first tooth, the birth of a grandchild, a natural disaster, the graying of one's hair — and that the only variable is our reaction to it.

The call asks for a piece made in response to a deviation in your life, your work or your world: a change you have lived through, one you anticipate, or one you set in motion yourself. Applicants write a short note on how that change informed the work, which is part of what the juror reads.

Juror David Baker is a poetic landscape painter working largely en plein air near Lake Michigan and around the Ox-Bow campus, a professor emeritus at Southwestern Michigan College who still teaches at Ox-Bow and at the Center itself. Awards are $500 for first place and $250 for second.

Entries are open to artists residing in the United States and the Tribal Nations that share these geographies, in any visual medium, with a maximum of two works. Two-dimensional pieces top out at 72 by 55 inches; three-dimensional work must pass through a standard doorway and weigh under 50 pounds. Work must be original and made within the last five years. Entry is $25, or $10 for students and artists economically challenged by unforeseen events, and the Center takes a 35 per cent commission on anything sold during the run. Submissions close 31 August at 11.59pm ET, notifications go out by 5 September, and the exhibition runs 26 September to 7 November 2026.

calls.title: In Flux
calls.description: Juried exhibition for members of the Oceanside Museum of Art's Artist Alliance, staged off-site at Covet Art Gallery in the South Oceanside district north of San Diego. The show is loosely rather than strictly themed: artists are invited to read the title however they like, with the call pointing toward physical, emotional or environmental change — work that expresses movement, transformation or uncertainty, whether through shifting materials or shifting ideas. Selection is by Laurie King, who founded Covet Art Gallery in December 2023, and is made with an eye to which pieces build the strongest show in combination. Up to 20 works may be entered and a maximum of two per artist will be selected. Photography is explicitly accepted alongside limited-edition prints in traditional printmaking media and limited-edition digital prints; other reproductions of original works are not. Two-dimensional work is capped at 84 by 84 inches and smaller pieces have a better chance given space limits. Eligibility requires current OMA membership at any level with the $25-per-person Artist Alliance add-on, and entry scholarships are available on request. Entry is $25 for the first submission and $10 for each after; the exhibition runs 3–29 October 2026 with a public reception on 3 October.
jury: Laurie King, Owner and Founder, Covet Art Gallery
calls.summary: OMA Artist Alliance juried show at Covet Art Gallery, Oceanside. Photography accepted, entry scholarships available.
prose: The Oceanside Museum of Art runs an Artist Alliance for artists in the San Diego region — a $25-per-person add-on to any level of OMA membership that brings an online registry listing and access to member exhibitions. In Flux is one of those exhibitions, and it takes the Alliance out of the museum and into Covet Art Gallery on South Coast Highway in South Oceanside.

The theme is deliberately loose. Artists are encouraged to submit their own reading of the title, with the call gesturing toward work that explores physical, emotional or environmental change: movement, transformation, uncertainty, a world in constant motion, whether that shift happens in the materials or in the ideas.

Juror Laurie King founded Covet in December 2023 to show contemporary artists with unusual perspectives and to give artists, collectors and the community somewhere to meet; the gallery also runs an online marketplace carrying work from artists across the country. She selects for the strongest show taken as a whole, so individual merit is not the only criterion.

Up to 20 entries may be submitted and a maximum of two works per artist will be chosen. Photography is named among the accepted media, along with limited-edition printmaking and limited-edition digital prints; giclées and other reproductions of originals are not. Entry is $25 for the first submission and $10 for each additional one, and scholarships are available for artists who ask. Submissions close 10 August at 10.59pm Pacific, notifications go out by 28 August, and the show runs 3–29 October 2026 with a reception on opening night.

calls.title: Virtual 46th Annual Juried Photographic Exhibition
calls.description: Marie Selby Botanical Gardens in Sarasota has run this juried photography exhibition for forty-six years, and the 2026 edition is presented online, with entries submitted digitally and every accepted photograph shown in a virtual gallery. Five categories are open: Living Art, Make a Splash, Plant Portraits, The Birds and the Bees, and Black + White. The headline award is the Richard and Ellen Sandor Photography Prize, $5,000 annually for the best artistic representation of an orchid species from any category, judged by a panel on artistic merit, creativity and visual impact. Images must be original, owned by the entrant, shot within the past year at either of the Gardens' two campuses — Downtown Sarasota or Historic Spanish Point — and not previously published for compensation; volunteers may not enter work made during service. Files may carry no watermarks, words, graphics or clearly identifiable people, and each photographer may enter a maximum of three. Entry is $45 for the first image and $15 for each additional, dropping to $30 and $10 for Selby Gardens members. The submission window is short: 3 to 10 August 2026, closing at 5pm on the tenth. Awards are announced online on 27 August and the exhibition runs through 30 September.
calls.summary: Forty-sixth year of Selby Gardens' juried photo show, online. $5,000 Sandor Prize for the best orchid photograph.
prose: Marie Selby Botanical Gardens has staged an annual juried photographic exhibition since 1980, making this the forty-sixth edition. The Gardens sit on Sarasota Bay in Florida and hold one of the world's major living collections of orchids, bromeliads and gesneriads across two campuses — Downtown Sarasota and Historic Spanish Point. The 2026 show is presented virtually, in partnership with the Observer Media Group: photographs are entered through an online portal, and accepted entries and winners are posted to both selby.org and yourobserver.com.

Five categories are open — Living Art, Make a Splash, Plant Portraits, The Birds and the Bees, and Black + White — and a juried panel selects on artistic merit, creativity and visual impact. Above the categories sits the Richard and Ellen Sandor Photography Prize, a $5,000 annual award for the best artistic representation of an orchid species, drawn from any category.

The eligibility rule is specific: images must have been taken within the past year at one of the two Selby Gardens campuses, must be original and owned by the entrant, and must not have been previously published for compensation. Volunteers cannot enter work made while serving. Files may not carry watermarks, words, graphics or clearly visible people.

Each photographer may enter up to three images. Entry is $45 for the first and $15 for each additional, or $30 and $10 for Selby Gardens members. The submission window opens at 10am on 3 August 2026 and closes at 5pm on 10 August. Awards are announced online on 27 August, and the exhibition is on view from 27 August through 30 September 2026.

calls.title: RADIFORNIA
calls.description: An open call to artists who call California home, staged in person at Covet Art Gallery in South Oceanside north of San Diego. The brief is the spirit of the Golden State rather than its scenery alone: sunshine and rebellion, surf and skate, desert highways and city lights, palm trees, punk shows, lowriders, redwoods, taco stands, sunsets over the Pacific. Work can draw on the coast, the mountains, the desert, the streets, the music or the people, and can be laid-back, loud, nostalgic, rebellious, colourful, contemplative or completely unexpected — the only requirement is that it feels like California. All media are welcome and photography is named explicitly alongside painting, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, fibre, printmaking, glass, wood and installation, traditional or experimental. Up to 20 works may be entered. Selected artists show in the physical exhibition and also receive access to the Covet Art Gallery online marketplace, where they may list further work for sale as part of an online version of the show. All work must be for sale. Entry is $25 plus $5 for each additional image; the exhibition runs 22 August to 26 September 2026 with an opening party on 22 August from 5 to 9pm.
calls.summary: California artists only: the spirit of the Golden State, in person at a South Oceanside gallery. All media, photography included.

prose: Covet Art Gallery opened in December 2023 on South Coast Highway in South Oceanside, a short walk from the beach north of San Diego, showing contemporary artists with distinctive points of view and running an online marketplace alongside the physical space. RADIFORNIA is its open call to artists based in California.

The brief is a state of mind rather than a subject list. The call reels off sunshine and rebellion, surf and skate, desert highways and city lights, palm trees, punk shows, lowriders, redwoods, taco stands and sunsets over the Pacific, then says the work does not have to be about any of them — it can come from the coast, the mountains, the desert, the streets, the music or the people, and the only requirement is that it feels like California.

All media are welcome and photography is listed explicitly, alongside painting, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, fibre art, printmaking, glass, wood and installation, traditional or experimental. Artists may submit up to 20 works, and everything entered must be for sale.

Selected artists appear in the in-person exhibition and are also given access to the gallery's online marketplace, where they can list additional work as part of an online version of the show. Entry is $25 plus $5 per additional image. Submissions close Sunday 2 August 2026, the show runs 22 August to 26 September, and the opening party is on 22 August from 5 to 9pm.

calls.title: Zari Art Prize 2026
calls.description: The Zari Art Prize returns for 2026 from Zari Gallery, a Fitzrovia gallery in London's West End founded in 2016 to show new and established artists united by mixed cultural heritage. The prize is awarded across three categories — painting, sculpture and photography — from a £4,000 prize pool, with Photography taking £550 and Photography Runner-up £350 alongside a £1,000 Best in Show and a £300 People's Choice. There is no set theme. Artists worldwide may submit up to ten works; entry is £20 for a single work, rising on a sliding scale to £87.50 for ten. Judges select an online shortlist between 23 and 31 August, a public vote opens 2 September, and the shortlist is announced 9 September, with shortlisted work delivered 11–17 September for the gallery exhibition in central London. Photographs must arrive framed and fitted with hanging hardware; images are submitted as JPEGs under 10 MB, ideally 300 dpi and at least 1600 pixels wide. Work is offered for sale to the gallery's collector audience.
calls.summary: London West End gallery prize with a dedicated photography category — £550 plus £350 runner-up from a £4,000 pool, and a Fitzrovia show.

calls.title: Weathered & Fired: Barnstormers and Atmospheric Fired Ceramics
calls.description: Artspiration Frederick invites original work inspired by barns, farms, rural landscapes and the passage of time in Frederick County, Maryland — from weathered wood and rusted metal to atmospheric fired ceramics that embrace the elements. All media are accepted and photography is named explicitly alongside 2D, 3D, ceramics, sculpture and mixed media. Artists may submit up to three pieces and up to three may be selected; all work must be original, exhibition-ready and for sale, with 2D work properly framed and wired (no sawtooth hangers). The exhibition runs 2 October to 1 November 2026 with an artists' reception on 10 October, in a gallery that is free to enter, open to the public and wheelchair accessible. Accepted work is dropped off 29–30 September, or shipped to arrive by 29 September at the artist's cost with a prepaid return label. Jurors are potter Tony Clennell, a Royal Canadian Academy of Arts member with an MFA from Utah State who has taught across four continents, and Kimberly Yourick, founder of Lockhouse Gallery in Brunswick, Maryland and an oil painter specialising in plein air landscapes. Notification is emailed the week of 21 September.
jury: Tony Clennell, Potter, Royal Canadian Academy of Arts

calls.description: The School of Art Collection and Galleries at Kent State University opens its fourth Aggregate — a national juried exhibition whose brief is deliberately wide: open to all artists living in the United States working in any medium, gathering the range of what is being made across the country. Entrants may submit up to three pieces for a flat $10 fee, one JPEG per work, and only works submitted online and selected by the judges will be shown. The exhibition runs 6 November 2026 to 9 January 2027 at the KSU Downtown Gallery, 141 East Main Street in downtown Kent, Ohio, with an opening reception on 6 November from 5 to 7 p.m. A $500 first prize and a $300 runner-up prize are awarded. Accepted work must reach the gallery no later than 28 October 2026, must stay up for the run of the show, and cannot be substituted; hanging work needs a professional hanging device (no tape or loosely attached wire), and every piece must be labelled with the artist's name, title, medium, dimensions and price or insurance value. The galleries programme comprises eight exhibition spaces on the Kent campus and in downtown Kent, showing local, regional, national and international artists with new exhibitions every four to six weeks, supported by the Ohio Arts Council.
calls.summary: National juried show in any medium at KSU Downtown Gallery, Ohio. $10 to enter, $500 first prize, Nov–Jan run.

calls.title: Beauty That Remains
calls.description: Kingdom Bound Ministries and Project Lab are gathering work for a one-day community art exhibition in Buffalo's Sheridan Parkside neighbourhood, built around faith, restoration and what endures through hardship. The call is for work that speaks to rebuilding — restoration, redemption, peace, resilience, compassion, healing and the beauty that survives difficult seasons — and especially to community: the ways people come together to support one another and carry hope forward. Work may be symbolic, abstract, deeply personal or narrative-driven. Accepted media are listed explicitly and include photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, mixed media, digital art, printmaking and textile/fibre work; AI-generated art is not accepted. The exhibition is a fundraiser tied to the conversion of a long-closed school building into the Sheridan Parkside Life Center, a space for connection, care and creativity, and proceeds also support the centre's literacy initiatives for local children. Artists may submit one to ten images for a $25 fee; selected work is shown on 19 September 2026 from 11am to 4pm at 169 Sheridan Parkside Drive, Tonawanda, New York, with a raffle of donated pieces running through the day and artists able to sell their work on a 60/40 split. Notification is 26 August 2026.
calls.summary: Faith, restoration and community in Buffalo. Photography named; one-day show and fundraiser for a neighbourhood life centre.

calls.title: When Light Gathers
calls.description: The Pierro Gallery of South Orange opens a group exhibition bringing together local and regional artists with connections to Jewish culture and community. Opening in December during Hanukkah, the show is timed to a season associated with light, gathering and reflection, and it is explicitly not a religious brief: the gallery states that artists are not expected to engage with religious or cultural themes in their work, and that the exhibition exists to let many voices be seen together. Emerging and established artists are both welcome, and up to three works may be submitted with title, medium, dimensions, year and price; a short artist statement and bio are requested only if the work is selected. Founded in 1994 and run by the South Orange Department of Recreation and Cultural Affairs, Pierro is a non-commercial municipal gallery that charges no submission fee and takes no commission on sales, inviting a voluntary donation instead. The gallery accepts photography alongside painting, sculpture and mixed media, and works needing glass or Plexiglass must meet its standard framing guidelines. Artists are notified the week of 12 October 2026, and the exhibition opens 3 December 2026 at the Baird Community Center, 5 Mead Street.
calls.summary: Free, no-commission municipal gallery show for artists with connections to Jewish culture. Hanukkah opening in South Orange, NJ.

calls.title: The Wellspring of 1000 Eyes
calls.description: The Art Department, Paisley marks the first year in its new permanent home — a former Argos store on Causeyside Street — with an open call built on the phrase "Keep your Eye on Paisley", which the organiser attributes to Benjamin Disraeli, and on Argos Panoptes, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth set to watch and never sleep. Artists are invited to respond to Vintage Paisley (any photograph or artwork of the town's past or present) and to the broader themes of Power & Guardianship, The All-Seeing Eye, The Eyes of the Truth, The Third Eye, The Public Eye and Private Eye. Photography is named among the media the exhibition will feature, and the entry guidance is explicit that works may be of any medium or genre. There is no entry fee and no hanging fee — the project is supported by Renfrewshire Council's Culture, Heritage & Events Fund — and up to six works may be submitted per artist, all through the online form. Work is graded by a selection panel using an average-score system; artists are notified on 8 November 2026, hand-in runs 16–30 November, and the exhibition opens 1 December 2026 and closes 30 January 2027. Most work is expected to be for sale, with a 30% commission plus VAT on the commission element supporting the charity, and remittance by 31 March 2027.
calls.summary: Free two-month show in Paisley's new gallery on the theme of eyes and seeing. Any medium, up to six works, no hanging fee.

calls.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Winter 2027
calls.description: Monson Arts' dedicated photography residency, reserved within its general open call, gives one photographer per session access to the private studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in Blanchard, Maine — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. The darkroom takes silver gelatin prints up to 40×50 inches from negatives between 35mm and 8×10 and supports other analog and alternative processes; the digital side has PC workstations with 34-inch monitors and Adobe Creative Cloud, a 44-inch Epson printer, scanners, trimmers and a 48×96-inch dry-mount press. Residents supply their own film, paper, chemistry and ink. The winter 2027 open call runs August 1 to September 15, 2026 and covers three sessions, of which the four-week January 25 – February 18 session is the one that carries the Abbott Watts placement. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, a $500 stipend for the four-week session, and join a cohort of five visual artists and five writers. A car is needed for the eight-minute drive to the Blanchard studio; cell service is very limited in both locations. Applications go through SlideRoom and are open to artists at any career stage, US and non-US citizens with working knowledge of English, who are not currently enrolled in a BFA or MFA program.
calls.summary: Maine photography residency with a 40×50 silver gelatin darkroom, housing, all meals and a $500 stipend. Winter 2027 session.

calls.title: Enigmatic Encounters: The Veil Grows Thin
calls.description: Create Appalachia's autumn show at the Kingsport Center for Art & Technology asks what emerges when the boundary between worlds turns fragile. Drawing on folklore, spirits, dreams, unseen forces and the liminal places between the known and the unknown, the call seeks work that is eerie, ethereal or enchanted — ghostly encounters, ancient legends, supernatural landscapes, forgotten memories, or personal readings of the unseen. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, illustration, sculpture, pottery, mixed media, installation, short film, video, animation, game art, digital illustration, graphic design, 3D print and fibre work. This is a physical gallery show, not an online display: digitally made work is printed and hung, and moving image runs on monitors with a two-minute cap. AI artwork is not accepted. The entry fee covers up to three submissions, with each additional set of one to three files charged again. Selected artists are notified three days after the deadline; work is dropped off in person or shipped with prepaid return labels, and the gallery takes 30% commission on sales. The exhibition opens August 28 with a reception on September 3 and runs to October 30, 2026.
calls.summary: Folklore, spirits and the liminal, hung in a Tennessee gallery. Photography named in the media list; $30 for up to three works.

calls.title: Seasons of Change
calls.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's autumn juried show in Prescott, Arizona takes transformation as its subject — shifting seasons and weather, migration and seasonal wildlife, personal growth, new beginnings and endings, healing and resilience, time and nostalgia, and abstract readings of movement and change. Photography is one of the four judged categories in its own right ("all types of photography mediums"), alongside original paintings, three-dimensional objects and handcrafted jewellery. The call is open to members and non-members alike, with Arizona artists particularly encouraged; up to five works may be entered, the first three covered by the base fee and each further work charged separately. Entries are juried for the gallery show and then judged again in the gallery, with an awards ceremony and reception on September 25. Reproductions of original paintings, giclées and printed merchandise such as tote bags are excluded, as are nudes and work unsuitable for family viewing; canvas or frame size must be at least 154 square inches and no more than 1,728. All artwork must be for sale and delivered in person — no shipping — with gallery intake on August 31. The Guild takes 25% commission from members and 40% from non-members. The exhibition runs September 2 to October 24, 2026, and accepted work also stays in the online Web Gallery for three months.
calls.summary: Arizona guild show on transformation with photography as its own judged category. Members and non-members, in-person delivery.

calls.title: A Charles River Journey
calls.description: Eighty artists, eighty miles: the Dedham Art Association and the Wellesley Society of Artists, working with the Charles River Watershed Association, are assembling an exhibition that follows the Charles River along its full course from Hopkinton to Boston. Artists are asked for visual impressions of the river — its meandering natural landscapes, the communities it connects, and its role as both a recreational and an ecological resource — with the flora, fauna, people and places reimagined as a record of the environmental and social narratives of the moment. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, mixed media and collage, and printmaking; each artist submits one original two-dimensional work. Eighty works will be juried in and are eligible for over $2,500 in cash awards. The call is open to artists living in New England, emerging and established, as well as students enrolled at New England universities. Selected work is announced December 1, 2026, delivered in January, and shown at the Dorothy and Charles Mosesian Center for the Arts in Watertown, Massachusetts from January 22 to March 12, 2027, with an opening reception on January 28.
calls.summary: Eighty New England artists trace the Charles River's eighty miles. Photography accepted, over $2,500 in awards, Mosesian Center show.

calls.title: 78th Regional Exhibition
calls.description: For over seventy-five years the Arnot Art Museum's Regional Exhibition has gathered artists from across the Northeast and Eastern Canada into a museum setting, and the 78th edition is open now. Photography is named outright in the museum's own media list alongside painting and drawing, sculpture, graphics, clay, textiles, jewelry, wood and metal work, and mixed media. The Museum keeps a primary focus on representational art but explicitly welcomes non-objective work for the Regionals, so the door is open to conceptual and abstract lens-based practice too. Up to $10,000 in cash awards is distributed among the juror selections, and selected artists receive two complimentary tickets to the Gala Reception and Awards Ceremony on 19 December. Work is shown in the Museum's West Wing Galleries from 29 September to 19 December 2026. Entry is open to artists 18 and over living in Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island or Vermont, or in Ontario, Canada; work must be no more than five years old and not previously shown at the Museum. Maximum two entries per artist, nothing over 96 inches or 150 pounds, and a 40% commission applies to sales made during the exhibition.
jury: Alisha Sickler Brunelli, artist and lecturer, Department of Art & Design, Binghamton University
Dana Carlisle Kletchka, PhD, Associate Professor of Arts Administration, Education, and Policy, The Ohio State University
Bekah Mertus, Associate Curator, Arnot Art Museum

calls.title: We Are the Ones
calls.description: Willow Street Gallery, the exhibition project of DC Arts Studios in the Takoma neighbourhood, is looking for work about community — what it means to hold and be held by other people, and to build something better together. The theme takes its title from the closing line of June Jordan's Poem for South African Women, and the gallery is explicit that it is a starting point rather than a literal brief: the call frames healing as a communal endeavour and resilience as something rooted in giving of yourself and receiving the care of others. Photography is named directly in the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, mixed media and textile art; the gallery can take 2D work in any physical medium but cannot accommodate video or other digital media this round. Open to artists 18 and over living and working in the greater Washington DC region — DC, Maryland and Virginia. Two cash prizes are awarded, $200 for best in show and $100 for the runner-up, and the show runs 12 September to 3 October 2026, with an opening reception on 12 September and a closing reception on 2 October. DC Arts Studios has served the DMV since 1979 and keeps its gallery commission at 20% rather than the usual half.

calls.title: Reel Pride 2026 Art Show
calls.description: The Reel Pride Art Show is the gallery arm of Winnipeg's Reel Pride International Film Festival — a space for 2SLGBTQI+ artists to show work alongside the festival at The Gas Station Arts Centre. The organisers welcome work in all forms and mediums and are open about what they are after: personal expression, a statement, or a celebration, and the many ways queer and Two-Spirit people experience and build community. There is no entry fee. If work sells the artist keeps the full sale price — the festival takes no commission — and artists retain full copyright, with images used only to promote Reel Pride and its events. Submissions run entirely through the call site, and accepted work is dropped off in Winnipeg during the week of 7–11 September. The show runs 15 September to 2 November 2026 alongside the festival.

calls.title: Artist-in-Residence Program: Winter and Spring 2027
calls.description: The Mosesian Center for the Arts in Watertown runs its second Artist-in-Residence Program with a straightforward proposition: free studio space and professional development support, no fee to participate beyond a refundable key deposit. Photography is named directly in the list of eligible visual-art disciplines, alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking and mixed media, and the programme also takes performing, literary, interdisciplinary and socially engaged artists. Residents get a private or shared 11 by 22 foot studio with 24-hour access for three months, a welcome reception, and $45 an hour (minimum 1.5 hours) for any workshops or classes they teach during the residency. Two to three General Artist Residencies are offered free of charge. One Ignite Artist Fellowship is selected from this cycle, carrying the same free studio space and professional development support for an emerging artist from the global majority or a historically marginalised community, plus a $1,000 stipend towards materials, transport or project costs. The programme is aimed at emerging and mid-career local and regional artists looking for time and space to experiment. Housing, per diem and materials are not otherwise included, and residents are expected to share their work through at least one public-facing event — an open studio, artist talk, workshop or performance. Winter residency runs January to March 2027, spring runs April to June, and selected artists are announced 15 October 2026. Applications ask for eight images or files, a CV, an artist statement and a short bio.
calls.summary: Free three-month studio residency outside Boston. Photography named, Ignite Fellowship for global-majority artists carries a $1,000 stipend.

calls.title: The New Masters 4: Women Artists of Northeast Ohio
calls.description: The Wasmer Gallery on the Ursuline College campus hosts the fourth edition of its juried exhibition for women artists living and working in Northeast Ohio. The gallery enumerates photography explicitly among the accepted media — traditional, digital and computer-enhanced — alongside painting, works on paper, mixed media, sculpture, glass, fiber and jewelry, and giclée reproductions are barred except for signed and numbered limited editions or photography. Open only to women artists 18 and over, emerging and professional, currently residing in the eighteen counties of Northeast Ohio: Ashland, Ashtabula, Columbiana, Cuyahoga, Erie, Geauga, Huron, Lake, Lorain, Mahoning, Medina, Portage, Richland, Stark, Summit, Trumbull, Tuscarawas and Wayne. The guaranteed minimum prize pool is $500, rising with the number of entries, and is split across Best in Show, an Award of Excellence for first prize and an Award of Distinction for second; final amounts are announced on 12 September with acceptance notifications, and cheques are issued by Ursuline College. Up to three works per artist at $10 each, capped at $30. Work must be original, made in the last five years, not made under instruction in a class or workshop, and not previously shown at the Wasmer Gallery. 2D work including mat and frame must be no larger than 30 by 40 inches.
jury: Yana Mikho-Misho, artist, arts advocate and Curator, Museum of Creative Human Art (MoCHA), Cleveland

calls.title: Nostalgia
calls.description: Member show at the New Hampshire Art Association's Portsmouth gallery built around memory and the act of looking back — personal histories, shared experiences, places once known, cherished objects, cultural touchstones, and moments that continue to resonate as they pass on. NHAA welcomes artwork in any medium and names photography outright in its list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, installation, fibre arts and digital work, provided it engages with the theme. This is not a juried show: all member entries are accepted, though the association notes it may have to limit accepted works by size if response outstrips available wall space. Entry is $12 for the first piece and $10 for a second, and NHAA membership is required — artists can join when applying. The exhibition runs 2–27 September 2026 at 136 State Street with an opening reception on 4 September, 5–8pm; work is dropped off 30–31 August and collected 27–28 September. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour.

calls.title: Reflections 180 Years of Manchester NH
calls.description: Manchester, New Hampshire has spent 180 years becoming itself, and Mosaic Art Collective is asking artists to look closely at it — the mills along the Merrimack, the neighbourhoods, industries and people who have reshaped the city again and again, and the city as it exists today. Work can be documentary or interpretive as long as it speaks to reflection on Manchester's history and present; all media are welcome except reproductions and AI-generated work. This is a lightly juried call. The exhibition runs 12 September – 26 October 2026 at Mosaic Studios, 66 Hanover Street, with an opening reception on 12 September, 5–7pm; acceptance notices go out 24 August and accepted work is dropped off 26–28 August. Entry is $10 for up to four works and sales split 75/25 in the artist's favour. Work must arrive ready to hang with d-rings and picture wire, or a $5 wiring fee applies at drop-off.

calls.title: Full Circle — New Beginnings 2026
calls.description: Mosaic Art Collective marks its fourth anniversary and its move to a new street-level gallery in Manchester, New Hampshire with a show about cycles: the seasons we move through, the relationships that anchor us, the personal transformations that bring us back to ourselves in new form. A return to an old practice, a fresh start after loss, the quiet repetition of daily rituals — the collective wants to see how artists interpret what it means to come full circle. All media are welcome except reproductions and AI-generated work. Entry is $10 for the first work and $10 for each additional, up to four. The exhibition runs 7–28 September 2026 at the collective's gallery on Chestnut Street with an opening reception on 12 September, 5–7pm, and acceptance notices on 30 August. Sales split 75/25 in the artist's favour, and work must arrive ready to hang with d-rings and picture wire or a $5 wiring fee applies at drop-off.

calls.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe looking for photographs that get at what it means to be human — not just faces, but the quiet and unguarded moments behind them, the tired eyes at the end of a long day, the burst of laughter that comes out of nowhere, the way we hold each other and hold ourselves together when no one is watching. Portraits and candid work are equally welcome; posed or unposed does not matter, only whether it feels real. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers and juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images for the gallery walls. The gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side). Exhibition runs 4–26 December 2026 with an opening reception on 4 December; prints are archived in the gallery's flat files for six months afterwards, photographers retain all rights, and sales split 50/50. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Dusk Gallery (Santa Fe) show on what it means to be human. Printing and framing covered; exhibition Dec 2026.

calls.title: Holiday Art Competition 2026
calls.description: Juried competition and exhibition presented by the Delaplaine Arts Center with the Holiday Committee of Celebrate Frederick, on a secular theme of "The Holidays in Historic Frederick" — winter, downtown, snow and light, built around recognisable Frederick landmarks such as the Carillon, Schifferstadt, the Clustered Spires, Carroll Creek Linear Park and the streets around Market and Patrick. All two-dimensional work in any medium is accepted and photography is named outright alongside painting, drawing, hand-pulled prints, etchings, collage and digital painting; work must be original, unpublished commercially, and able to reproduce in black and white. Judging runs in two rounds — remote review of digital entries, then in-person judging after installation — and accepted work is announced 7 November. The Judges' Choice award is $1,000, with a Barbara Maghan People's Choice certificate voted at the reception and an optional Judges' Special Award. The reception is 2 December 2026, 5:30–7pm, and selected work stays on view in the Community Outreach Gallery 5–27 December. Entrants should note that the Holiday Committee retains exclusive commercial rights to the winning artwork for two years for poster production and five years for other promotional pieces. Accepted work is hand-delivered or shipped to Frederick, framed and wired ready to hang. Entry is $20 per piece.
calls.summary: Delaplaine + Celebrate Frederick juried show on the holidays in historic Frederick, MD. $1,000 Judges' Choice; photography named.
