calls.title: Life Framer — Travel
calls.description: The October round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly award, judged by Michael Yamashita, the American–Japanese photographer whose four decades with National Geographic have taken him across six continents, from the Tibetan Plateau and the Mekong to remote villages and historic trade routes. The brief opens with Susan Sontag — “I haven't been everywhere, but it's on my list” — and asks for the world's landscapes, people and cultures, whether on your doorstep or ten thousand kilometres away. Landscape, travel, portraiture, reportage, street and aerial work are all welcome, from any type of photographer, with images new or drawn from the archive. Analog and digital devices including phones are accepted, and editing, mixed media, collage and compositing are allowed so long as photography is at the heart of the work; AI-generated imagery is not. The monthly first prize is $2,000, part of a $24,000 annual fund shared between the twelve monthly winners, and the first- and second-prize images each month are exhibited in Life Framer's galleries around the world. Entry is tiered: $20 for one image, $30 for three, $40 for six, or $100 for a twelve-month membership allowing up to ten images in every monthly theme.

calls.title: Atlanta Art Fair 2026
calls.description: Atlanta Photography Group is selecting the work for its own booth at the Atlanta Art Fair, which returns to the historic Pullman Yards campus for its third edition on 1–4 October 2026. There is no theme and all photographic genres and processes are welcome. Up to 24 works will be chosen by Andi McKenzie, PhD, Curator of Works on Paper at the Michael C. Carlos Museum; APG's booth at last year's fair was picked by guest curator Melissa Messina as the best curated booth at the fair. Selected works must be no longer than 30 inches on the long side and presented in white frames — no exceptions, and no saw-tooth hangers — and are delivered to the APG Gallery by 25 September. Entry is $70 for up to six works and is open to current APG members only; membership starts at $25 a year for students and $55 for individuals. Notifications go out on or about 28 August 2026.
jury: Andi McKenzie, PhD, Curator of Works on Paper, Michael C. Carlos Museum

calls.title: Interdisciplinary Craft + Photography Artist Residency 2027–2028
calls.description: A three-month studio residency in Houston for artists whose practice sits at the intersection of contemporary craft and photography, offered by Houston Center for Contemporary Craft together with Houston Center for Photography. Residents get 24/7 access to a 200-square-foot studio at HCCC, a $1,000 monthly stipend that includes a small housing and materials allowance, and — through HCP — printing credits and full access to HCP's Digital Lab. Residents give a joint artist talk and are included in HCCC's annual In Residence exhibition. Applicants must be able to demonstrate how their work engages both craft and photography; HCCC's programme details list the accepted craft media as wood, glass, metal, fiber and clay, but HCP adds that no particular amount of photographic experience is required, only an interest in showing photo-based work. Residents must work in their studios two days a week during HCCC public hours and open the studio to visitors on Saturdays and one other day. Applications for the 2027–2028 cycle are submitted through the same online application as HCCC's general residency programme, which opens on HCCC's apply page on 1 December 2026 and closes 1 February 2027, with acceptances emailed in late May. Neither organiser has published an entry fee yet — HCP's FAQ answers the fee question with "stay tuned". International applicants must provide proof of eligibility to work in the US.

calls.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — September 2026
calls.description: Autumn cycle of the Vienna-based independent art journal's rolling open call, inviting artists and photographers worldwide to submit bold contemporary visual work for publication and features. Submitting is free: up to six works go in through the form on the open-call page, or by email. If your work is selected, the publishing options are charged separately — €35 for publication in the magazine, €65 for publication plus an artist page on the Arty Rat website (biography, statement and photographs of works), and €100 for either a curatorial review or a place in the Vienna group exhibition. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the magazine, photographs of their printed pages and a feature on Arty Rat's Instagram; two artists are chosen for the magazine covers, and one artist is given free participation in Arty Rat's group exhibition at The Names Gallery in Vienna. The call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 or over, and selections are made by Arty Rat's curator Oleksandr Dyvnich.
calls.summary: Vienna indie art journal's autumn call. Free to enter, two cover features and one free place in a Vienna group show.

calls.title: Beecher's 2026 Open Exhibition — Autumn
calls.description: Beecher's is a gallery in the market town of Ross-on-Wye, on the edge of the Wye Valley, running a year-round programme of solo and group shows. Its Autumn Open has no set theme and is open to any artist living in the UK, emerging or established, working in painting, drawing, illustration, printmaking, sculpture, mixed media, photography or digital art — all media are eligible except reproductions, film and video. There is a dedicated photography prize, chosen by juror John Bulmer, the photographer who has documented Britain with a photojournalistic eye since the early 1950s and whose exhibition The North opens at Beecher's in January 2027. First prize is £250 cash plus a year's representation by the gallery, inclusion in its 2027 group exhibitions, a professional portfolio review and career planning session, and promotion across Beecher's website, newsletter and social channels; further prizes in each category include group exhibitions, business mentoring and marketing, and there is a Visitors' Choice Award decided by votes at the gallery. Judging is anonymous from the submitted images. Around 60 works are selected and hung salon style. Work may not exceed 100cm in any direction or 25kg, must have been completed within 36 months, and must arrive framed and ready to hang. Artists may enter up to six works, and all work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining 50% commission and donating a tenth of that to a partner charity. Selections are announced 6 September, the private view is 17 September, the exhibition runs 18 September to 17 October, and unsold work is collected between 17 and 19 October.
calls.summary: UK-wide open at a Ross-on-Wye gallery with its own photography prize picked by John Bulmer. £250 and a year's representation.

calls.title: Got Rhythm
calls.description: A themed group show at Grove Gallery on Grove Street in downtown Evanston, run by the Evanston art school Studio 215, asking how artists respond to rhythm, sound and music. The organisers want two-dimensional work that reverberates with the rhythm of life — heartbeat, breath, the cadence of speech — and are open to everything from abstraction to representation, citing Kandinsky's music-driven paintings and centuries of figure painters conveying the movement of dance. Accepted media are painting, drawing, printmaking, photography and textiles; work must hang on the wall, weigh under five pounds and measure no more than 30 inches on the longest side including the frame. Only original, one-of-a-kind works are accepted and open-edition giclée prints are excluded, so a photographer should be entering a print made as the work itself. This is a regional call, limited to artists living in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Iowa, Kentucky or Minnesota. Entries are judged by Melanie P. Brown, a Chicago painter and teaching artist who has performed live painting with local musicians, and Ross Martens and Darren Oberto, both co-owners of Alley Gallery in Evanston — Martens studied Film and Photography at Northwestern and works as an artist, photographer and framer. The exhibition runs across September and October 2026 with an opening reception in early September, and is promoted across the Midwest in Chicago Gallery News, Newcity and elsewhere. All work must be for sale, split 60% to the artist and 40% to the gallery.
calls.summary: Midwest-only show on rhythm, sound and music at an Evanston gallery. Photography accepted, judged by three working artists.

calls.title: Small Town: Small Works 2026
calls.description: The annual small-format open call at the Reeves House Visual Arts Center, the visual arts wing of Woodstock Arts — a four-acre arts complex north of Atlanta with a performing arts centre, an outdoor music venue, a sculpture garden and a gallery whose shows rotate every eight weeks. Everything in the show is 15 inches or smaller in any direction including the frame, and the call is deliberately hyper-local: entrants must be 18 or over and live within a 15-mile radius of Woodstock, Georgia. Fifteen dollars covers up to five submissions. Photographs and other works on paper must be framed and protected under glass or plexiglass, and hanging hardware is strictly specified — wire, D-rings or a cleat only, no sawtooth hangers, plastic frames or clip frames. Only original work is eligible and pieces previously shown at the Reeves House are not. All work is for sale, split 60% to the artist and 40% to the Reeves House; because the show is hung as a rotating stock, sold pieces go home with the buyer and another work comes out of storage to replace them, so the organisers ask that submissions be similar in size. Notifications go out by 13 October, signed contracts are due 6 November and work is dropped off 2–7 November. The exhibition is on view 13 November 2026 to 2 January 2027, opening with a reception on 13 November from 6 to 8pm.
calls.summary: Small-format open at Woodstock Arts' Reeves House, GA. $15 for five works, open to artists within 15 miles of Woodstock.

calls.title: Natural Harmony
calls.description: LightBox invites photographers worldwide to submit work for Natural Harmony, a show about the land's persistence — a storm overtaking a mountain range, vines reclaiming a forgotten building. The gallery is looking for a modern, expansive reading of "landscape": nature's intersection with humanity, untouched land caught in a moment of change or motion, and enduring yet overlooked corners of the world. The exhibition is juried by Jody Miller, a member of The Guild at LightBox, and runs 10 October – 11 November 2026 at the gallery in Astoria, Oregon, accompanied by live performative work from musicians and writers responding to the images on the walls. Open to any style or medium: traditional, digital and alternative photographic processes are all eligible; fibre-based silver gelatin or archival pigment inkjet for black and white, C-prints accepted. Accepted work must arrive framed and ready to hang, no larger than 20 x 24 inches. Entry is $40 for up to 5 images or $60 for up to 10; artists are notified by 9 September 2026 and accepted work is due 3 October. The gallery retains a 40% commission on sales.
jury: Jody Miller, The Guild at LightBox
calls.summary: Landscape as persistence — juried show at LightBox in Astoria, Oregon, with live performance responding to the work.

calls.title: Human Impact Awards 2026
calls.description: Wex Photo Video's annual documentary award, run in partnership with Sony, asks for a 5–10 image series exploring how people shape, affect and respond to the world around them. The brief is deliberately open — community and belonging, identity and representation, climate and land, urban change, protest and social change, care and resilience, ritual, technology, inequality, displacement or simply everyday humanity. Human impact does not have to mean crisis; the judges are looking for thoughtful visual stories with a clear point of view that hold together as a body of work rather than a set of strong singles. Entry is free with no purchase necessary, and images made on any camera, phone or system are welcome. The open Professional Award pays £5,000 for first place, £3,000 for second and £1,000 for third. The Phil Smith Student Photography Award, named in memory of a member of the Wex business team, awards Sony camera and lens kits to its top three students, who enter with a school or university email address. Entries are reviewed by an independent panel of photographers and industry professionals. Photographers retain full copyright; AI-generated imagery and stock photography are disqualified. Open to UK residents aged 18 or over.
calls.summary: Free-to-enter UK documentary award with Sony — 5–10 image series on human impact, £5,000 top prize plus a student category.

calls.title: Small Wonders 2026
calls.description: The 22nd edition of Maryland Federation of Art's annual small-works exhibition, for artists who dream big but work small. Everything must fit under 11 inches in all directions including the frame and display, but there is no limit on creativity or media. MFA exhibitions are blind juried — names and identifying information are hidden from the juror — and this year's selections are made by Abby Daggett, Gallery Director and Marketing Director at Maine Art Hill in Kennebunk, whose background spans commercial galleries and museums in Boston, Venice and Italy. Selected work is shown at MFA's Circle Gallery in Annapolis and its new second location on Maryland Avenue from 25 November to 22 December 2026, with a virtual awards ceremony on 30 November, an opening reception on 3 December and two further Midnight Madness receptions. The juror presents cash awards totalling $1,000. Entry is open to artists residing in any state or territory of the US, Canada or Mexico; up to 6 original works made in the past three years may be entered, and work previously shown at Circle Gallery is not eligible. Artists are notified 29 October and keep 70% of sales (75% for MFA members). Founded in 1963, MFA is a 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by the Maryland State Arts Council.
jury: Abby Daggett, Gallery Director, Maine Art Hill

calls.title: After Dark 2026
calls.description: Maryland Federation of Art's annual nocturnal exhibition, shown in MFA's Virtual Gallery from 15 October to 14 December 2026. After Dark explores the quiet, mysterious world that emerges once the sun goes down — the flicker of a single lamp in an open window, the starlit silence of a rural field, the way night transforms how we see, feel and imagine. MFA invites limited palettes, subtle contrasts and softened forms that express the stillness and introspection of twilight, and the show is assembled from paintings, photographs, installations and mixed media works. All MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with names and identifying information hidden from the juror; this edition is selected by Kevin Murphy, Eugénie Prendergast Senior Curator of American and European Art at the Williams College Museum of Art. Awards designated by the juror total $500, announced 2 November. Entry is open to artists worldwide with the exception of sanctioned countries, with up to 6 original works made in the past three years; work previously shown in MFA's Virtual Gallery is not eligible. Only artists in the 48 contiguous United States may set a sale price, and MFA reimburses up to $40 of their shipping on online sales; everyone else lists Price on Request and MFA refers enquiries to them. Artists are notified 24 September and retain 80% of sales (85% for members). Founded in 1963, MFA is a 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by the Maryland State Arts Council and runs Circle Gallery in Annapolis.
jury: Kevin Murphy, Eugénie Prendergast Senior Curator of American and European Art, Williams College Museum of Art

calls.title: Colours of Humanity Arts Exhibition 2026
calls.description: A free open call from the European Union Office to Hong Kong and Macao, the Goethe-Institut and Eaton HK for artworks interpreting diversity, equity and inclusion. Work is welcomed across any medium, from painting to digital art to sound art, and finalists join a major curated group exhibition at the Goethe Gallery on the 14th floor of the Hong Kong Arts Centre in Wan Chai, running November to December 2026. The show is curated by Eunice Tsang and Jims Lam. Alongside the artwork call, artists can pitch a Community Action proposal — a one-day participatory experience at EATON such as a workshop, screening, performance or discussion serving underrepresented groups — with up to HK$8,000 in honorarium to realise it; past editions produced communal cooking and zine-making programmes. The grand prize is a two-week residency at EATON. Entries are judged by an independent panel on artistic excellence, interpretation of the theme, and the strength of the message and narrative, with shortlisted artists notified by early October. The call is open to Hong Kong and Macau-based artists only, with a maximum of three submissions per artist and only one work exhibited; Community Action pitches do not count toward that limit. Work must be original and not previously exhibited at Goethe Gallery.
calls.summary: Free EU Office, Goethe-Institut and Eaton HK call on diversity, equity and inclusion. Hong Kong and Macau artists.

calls.title: 200 Years of Photography: Images, Representation and AI
calls.description: An open call to join a week of intensive photography workshops in Hong Kong marking two centuries since the first lasting photographic image, and asking what a photograph means when anyone can fabricate one. The Goethe-Institut Hongkong and the French Consulate of Hong Kong run the project with the School of Creative Media at City University of Hong Kong, supported by the Franco-German Cultural Fund. Successful applicants are assigned to one of three workshops: Gwenola Wagon (France) on image-making in the age of AI, from anarchives to speculative narratives; Andreas Müller-Pohle (Germany) on Machine Images, developing concepts from idea to finished work; and a third on photojournalism in the age of AI, covering fact-checking techniques for identifying AI-generated images and how visual truth is being redefined. The format is two virtual preparation sessions with your mentor in September or October, then three full days in person in Hong Kong on 9–11 October. Work produced during the workshops — experiments, sketches, short films and ideas in progress — goes on public display at the Goethe-Gallery in Wan Chai, opening the evening of 12 October, followed by a public symposium at City University on 13 October. Applications are welcome from students in photography or journalism, early-career practitioners and young professionals working with images, and anyone with a strong interest and some experience in photography, AI and visual culture. Applicants must be 18 or over, apply individually, and commit to the preparation sessions, the full three-day workshop and the exhibition opening.
calls.summary: Selected participants join three-day AI-and-photography workshops in Hong Kong with a public showcase and symposium.

calls.title: Vivid
calls.description: A colour-driven juried exhibition at the Kavanagh Gallery of Fine Line Creative Arts Center in St. Charles, Illinois, in the Fox River Valley about an hour west of Chicago. Work in this show needs unmistakable energy and a lively, dynamic composition that elicits a strong reaction — bold, vibrant, saturated hues. All media are accepted, with a maximum width of 48 inches for wall work. Jurors select on creativity, quality of artistry and originality as represented in the submitted images, and $800 in prizes will be awarded. The show runs 17 December 2026 to 12 February 2027, with an in-person opening reception on 17 December from 6 to 8pm; the gallery is closed to the public from 20 December to 3 January. Entry is open to any artist 18 or over residing in the United States, with up to 3 pieces per application and one image per piece; work previously shown at Fine Line is not eligible. Artists are notified by 14 November. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 30% commission; artists are responsible for shipping to and from the centre, and hand-delivered work is checked in on 12 December.
calls.summary: All-media juried show of bold, saturated colour at Fine Line's Kavanagh Gallery near Chicago. $800 in prizes.

calls.title: Life in the Forest
calls.description: A juried exhibition at the Kavanagh Gallery of Fine Line Creative Arts Center in St. Charles, Illinois, on the forest as an amazing and sometimes mystical place. Light filtering through the canopy reveals the plants and animals that call the forest home, but it can also open the imagination to rarer, mythical dwellers — fantastical creatures, fairies, elves and the occasional unicorn glimpsed out of the corner of your eye. The show will present the wonders, both real and imaginary, of a walk in the forest, and work in all 2D and 3D media will be considered by the jury. $800 in prizes will be awarded, with jurors selecting on creativity, quality of artistry and originality. The exhibition runs 18 February to 2 April 2027, with an in-person opening reception on 18 February from 6 to 8pm. Entry is open to artists 18 and older residing in the United States, with up to 3 pieces per application and one image per piece; work previously shown at Fine Line is not eligible. Artists are notified by 9 January 2027. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 30% commission; artists arrange shipping to and from the centre, and hand-delivered work is checked in on 13 February.
calls.summary: Real and imagined forests, all 2D and 3D media, at Fine Line's Kavanagh Gallery near Chicago. $800 in prizes.

calls.title: Artifacts of the “Now”
calls.org: The Cultural Arts Center at Glen Allen
calls.description: An open call from The Cultural Arts Center at Glen Allen exploring the current moment — physical, geographical and cultural — in all mediums. What objects place one in the current moment? What imagery is reflective of the time, something that could be a touchstone for future generations? What says “this is so 2026”? All artists working in 2D and 3D are invited to apply, and the theme will be interpreted by a range of differing artists in one of the Center's on-site gallery spaces. Galleries are kept family friendly, so work with explicit violence, language or nudity is refused, as is anything the Center reads as inflammatory toward a religious or cultural group. Housed in the old Glen Allen School, the 50,300 square foot multi-use facility opened in 1999 and is home to four galleries — the Gumenick Family, Slantwall, Midway and Glass Door — showing regional and international talent alongside concerts, theatre, dance and arts education. Admission to the Center is free. Entries are taken through the Center's ArtCall portal, where questions go to the gallery team, co-curators Rosalind Koons and Kitty Tillman. Work need not be for sale, but anything sold during the run is split 70/30 in the artist's favour, and CACGA insures work in the gallery at 65% of its stated retail value. The ArtCall listing marks this call regional to Virginia while the call text itself states no residency requirement, so artists outside the state should check with the Center before paying.
calls.summary: What says “this is so 2026”? All-media open call at a 50,000 sq ft Richmond-area arts centre with four galleries.

calls.title: Snapshot America: A Portrait of the United States in 2026
calls.org: Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: The Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts wants a time capsule of America at 250. This is a call to photograph the country as it is right now — your community, your friends, your neighbourhood, local events, landmarks, landscapes and the ordinary activities that make up daily life in the United States. From the grand celebrations to the tragedies that touch everyone, RICPA asks what image defines present-day America for you, what best represents the town you live in, what gives you the strength to get up in the morning and what keeps you up at night. Note the form RICPA wants: street photography, snapshots and other straight-out-of-camera work, with photo editing kept to a minimum. Curation is overseen by David DeMelim, RICPA's managing director, working with a team of educators, members and curators. Selected work hangs in the RICPA galleries at 118 North Main Street in Providence from 19 November to 11 December 2026, with an opening reception on the 19th, and an expanded collection — more work than the walls can hold — is published in book form as the lasting record. Deliberately, there are no individual prizes: to avoid implying that one community or one issue matters more than another, RICPA instead offers every entrant a discount coupon for the book. Entry is open to residents of all 50 states and the 14 territories, 18 and over, through CaFÉ. Current RICPA members get 20% off the entry fee, and membership can be bought at the point of entry. Accepted work must be exhibition-ready and no more than 48 inches including the frame; RICPA runs an optional print-and-frame-rental service from $45 for artists who would rather not ship. The gallery takes a 40% commission on sales, 20% for exhibiting and supporting members.
jury: David DeMelim, Managing Director, Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts

calls.title: Dorothy Antoinette LaSelle Travel Fellowship 2026
calls.description: Two awards of $5,000 for Texas-based visual artists to fund a research trip that pushes their practice forward. The fellowship takes its cue from its namesake: Dorothy Antoinette “Toni” LaSelle (1901–2002), a pioneer of modernism in Texas, travelled to Europe in 1927–28 after finishing her MA at the University of Chicago, studying the art of England, Italy and France — a trip made possible only by a study fund she won for work shown in the First Student Art Exhibition at the Renaissance Society in 1926. She went on to live in Denton and teach art and design for over four decades at what is now Texas Woman's University. The guest juror this year is Lana Meador, Associate Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at the San Antonio Museum of Art, who co-curated Texas Women: A New History of Abstract Art and has juried awards for the City of San Antonio's Department of Arts and Culture and the Texas Sculpture Group. Applicants must currently live in Texas and have done so for at least a year, hold a degree in the arts, and have had at least three solo or group exhibitions in the past three years — BFA and juried shows count. There is no application fee. Applications ask for up to four work thumbnails, a CV, two references, proof of Texas residency and a project proposal of 2,000 characters or less covering why the fellowship matters to your practice, your goals for the trip and when you would travel. Awardees are notified on 2 November 2026 and must complete their travel between 1 December 2026 and 31 December 2027.
jury: Lana Meador, Associate Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, San Antonio Museum of Art

calls.title: Beyond the Surface: A Mixed Media Exhibition
calls.description: The Art Center in Dover, New Hampshire is running a national juried exhibition on what happens when artists combine materials, techniques and ideas in a single piece. Photography is named outright in the organiser's own list of things artists may incorporate, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, fiber, found objects, digital elements, assemblage and sculpture — so lens-based work that is layered, printed onto unusual substrates, cut, stitched or built into an object belongs here. The juror is Dennis Cardalisco, a contemporary artist with more than forty years in the visual arts who studied at the Museum School at Tufts University and holds a BFA from the Massachusetts College of Art and Design. Awards are Best in Show, a Juror's Choice selected by Cardalisco, and a People's Choice voted by exhibition visitors. Entry is open to artists living in the United States aged 18 and over, with up to three original works per artist — works submitted together should come from a series or complement one another, and both the art and the framing must be consistent. Work must have been made in the last five years and not previously shown at The Art Center. Both 2D framed and 3D work are accepted; 3D pieces needing a pedestal must stay under 36 inches high and within a 16-inch footprint, while larger floor-standing work is encouraged and exempt from those limits. The exhibition runs 8 September to 31 October 2026 in the gallery and online, with an artists' reception on 3 October. Accepted work is delivered or shipped by 1 September and must arrive ready to hang, packed for re-use, with a prepaid return label. All work must be for sale; the artist keeps 70% and The Art Center retains 30%. Entry is $30 for up to three submissions and free for current Art Center members.
calls.summary: National juried mixed-media show in Dover, NH. Photography named among eligible materials; free for members, $30 otherwise.

calls.title: The WAE Open 2026
calls.description: Heidi Gallery's annual open, run out of a 2,000-square-foot light-filled space with adaptive walls at JSDD in Livingston, New Jersey. The gallery was established in 2021 and is explicit about showing established, emerging and underrepresented artists together. The WAE Open is not thematic — all mediums are accepted, including installations, across three categories: 2D work, sculpture and floor installation. The 2026 jurors are Sharnita Johnson and Joel Tidey, and there is a $500 Best in Show cash award presented at the opening reception. Every entry, selected or not, is included in a digital exhibition that runs alongside the physical show. Entry is open to artists living or working in New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania or Connecticut, with one to three pieces per artist; work must have been produced in the last three years and no giclée reproductions of original art are accepted. Two-dimensional work is capped at 36 by 42 inches and 30 pounds and must be properly wired — no saw-tooth hangers — with gallery-format framing preferred; sculpture must stay within two feet in any direction and floor installations within a four-foot square and 50 pounds. Accepted artists are asked to write or record an audio description of their work, under 60 seconds, which is made available to gallery and website visitors. Work is hand-delivered on 3 October, the exhibition runs 8 October to 6 December 2026 with an opening reception and award on 8 October and a closing reception with artist insights on 6 December. All work must be for sale and the gallery retains 40% commission. Artists must carry their own insurance.
calls.summary: Non-thematic annual open at a New Jersey gallery, all mediums. $500 Best in Show; every entry also shown digitally.

calls.title: September 2026 All Media Show
calls.description: Crossroads Art Center in Richmond represents more than 225 mid-Atlantic artists and runs a bimonthly juried call with cash awards of $100 for first place, $75 for second and $50 for third. The September edition has no theme — it is an open juried show judged by a guest juror, shown live in the gallery and simultaneously online. Photography sits in the organiser's own eligible-media list alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, digital art, fiber, wood, metal, ceramics and assemblage. The gallery accepts only original work by the entering artist; reproductions and giclée prints are refused unless approved by the owner, though work where the printed process is itself the art — etching, monoprint, silkscreen, lithography — is welcome. AI-generated images, professionally photographed images by another person, another artist's images and instructor's images are all strictly prohibited. Entry is $15 per submission for the general public with a limit of three, or $12 per submission for gallery members who also get a fourth entry free. Submitted work must be taken off the market everywhere else — other galleries, online marketplaces, personal sites and social selling platforms — from the moment of submission until the artist is notified. Artists are notified by 21 August, drop-off runs 9 to 12 September, the open house is 18 September and the exhibition closes 8 November 2026, with unsold work collected from 10 November. All work must be for sale, must stay up for the full run, and all wall-hung and 2D work must be wired — no saw-tooth hangers. Commission on sales is 30%.

calls.title: MICROCOSM: The Universe in the Smallest Things
calls.description: An in-state call from The Lab on Santa Fe, a gallery at 840 Santa Fe Drive in Denver's Art District on Santa Fe whose exhibitions are seen by crowds during the district's First Friday Art Walks. The premise is that if you look closely enough at one small thing you start to see everything: a single mark, a strange little object, the texture of paint, the pattern of a leaf, the surface of a stone, the shifting light across a Colorado landscape. The organisers want work that zeroes in before it zooms out, and are explicit that this is not a nature-themed exhibition — the subject might be a landscape, a face, a room, a memory, an invented object or something that cannot be named at all. They say they love artists who trust the small moments instead of chasing the obvious ones, and ask whether obsession and compulsion can transmute into virtuosic brilliance. If your work rewards a closer look, it belongs in the conversation. The gallery publishes no list of eligible or excluded media, and it has previously hosted a dedicated international street photography exhibition, so lens-based work is in scope. The call is open to Colorado artists only, and applicants must be able to drive their work in for delivery — no shipping is allowed. Work can be turned away at drop-off for improper wiring. All submitted art must be for sale, at the price given on the application, and measurements on the application must be accurate. Entry is $29 for one or two images, one application per artist. The exhibition has been moved and lengthened: the gallery now runs it 1 to 30 January 2027, having upgraded it from its original three-week November slot.
calls.summary: Denver Art District gallery wants work that rewards a closer look. Colorado artists only, $29, January 2027 show.

calls.title: About Time
calls.fee: CA$10 per work (CA$20 more if selected)
calls.description: Metchosin ArtPod is an artist-run gallery on southern Vancouver Island, and About Time is its autumn exhibition on how we experience time — personal, social, political, everyday, generational or historical. Work may dwell in the overall or the nearby, the microcosm or the immeasurable: the abstract mood of time, the urgency of process, a specific hour. All mediums are welcome and photography is spelled out in the submission guidelines — limited-edition photographs and prints, including giclée, inkjet and archival prints, are accepted in editions of 25 or fewer, and photographs must be taken by the artist and may not reproduce another artist's work. On AI the ArtPod says it is still reflecting, but requires submitted work to represent the artist's own creative vision and authorship. Jurying is blind: the juror sees only the image, the medium and substrate, and the artist statement, which is capped at 1,000 characters. Artists may submit up to three original works; diptychs, triptychs and small series count as one work if shown in a single photograph. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 7 feet high by 5 feet wide and there is no minimum size. Work must not have been exhibited in a juried exhibition or commercial gallery on southern Vancouver Island in the past year. Submission is CA$10 per artwork, with a further CA$20 hanging fee per accepted work payable before drop-off; the ArtPod takes 30% commission and all work must be for sale. Exhibiting artists get a social media promotion package and a QR code beside their statement linking to their own site. The exhibition runs 28 August to 18 October 2026.

calls.title: Call for Artists: 12-Month Gallery Representation
calls.description: Art in the Berkshires Gallery and Creative Studio opened at 8 Castle Street in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, and is now assembling the core group of artists it will represent from December 2026 through November 2027. Photography is named explicitly in the call alongside painting, printmaking, drawing and sculpture, and limited-edition photography is permitted; reproductions and AI-generated artwork will not be considered, and work must have been created in 2024 or later. The gallery asks for work that is Berkshires-minded — it offers paintings of Hawaiian beaches as an example of what would not fit — and for a genuinely distinct perspective; all styles are welcome, but artists are expected to have a large enough body of work that sold pieces can be replaced quickly. Up to thirty artists are selected. Rather than a single show, the selected group works together across four to five seasonal exhibitions through 2027, with all represented artists shown year-round and the first group exhibition opening 3 December 2026 and running to 31 January 2027. Selection happens in two parts: a jury reviews submissions and announces first-round results on 27 September, shortlisted artists are interviewed between 1 and 23 October, and final acceptances are issued on 30 October 2026. Representation carries exclusivity in Southern Berkshire County. The call is open to artists who live or work in Berkshire County or within fifty miles of it, which in practice reaches into eastern New York, northwest Connecticut and southern Vermont. Entry is $30 and submissions run 25 July to 20 September 2026; the gallery publishes no commission rate for represented artists, so that is worth asking about before applying. The gallery describes itself as community-focused and also invites represented artists interested in running workshops at its Creative Studio or teaching as paid instructors to get in touch separately.
calls.summary: A year of gallery representation in Great Barrington for up to 30 artists. Photography named; jury plus interview, $30 to apply.

calls.title: Fusion: Strathmore's 35th Annual Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Strathmore is a multi-disciplinary arts centre on a 16-acre site in North Bethesda, Maryland, and its Annual Juried Exhibition reaches its 35th edition with Fusion. The theme is growth through combination: from stars creating the elements that make up the universe to harmonising flavours from different cultures in a dish, fusion represents not only the new but the accomplishment of creation. The call asks for work that mixes multiple mediums, abstract or representational — the organisers say this can include but is not limited to drawing, painting, mixed media, assemblage and sculpture, and work may be of any style and combination of mediums, including pieces that invite the viewer to touch them. Artists from the DMV region and beyond are encouraged to apply. One submission fee of $36 covers up to eight works, is non-refundable and is tax-deductible, and there is no cap on how many works from a single artist's entry may be accepted — each is considered individually on technical mastery, connection to the theme, and original and aesthetic approach. Jurors are still to be announced. All work must be exhibition-ready and available for sale for the full run; the Mansion uses an Arakawa cable hanging system, so hanging works need ¾-inch or larger d-rings or screw eyes with a ¼-inch or larger opening, and cleats, saw-tooth hangers and anything requiring a nail in the wall are refused. Anything previously exhibited or offered for sale at Strathmore is ineligible. Jury results land 1 December 2026, accepted work is dropped off 11 to 13 January 2027, and the exhibition opens to the public on 23 January 2027 with a reception on 4 February, closing 27 February. Artists arrange and pay for their own delivery and pickup.
calls.summary: Strathmore's 35th Annual Juried Exhibition asks for work that mixes mediums. $36 covers up to eight entries; Mansion show in 2027.

calls.title: 2027 Juried Biennial Exhibition
calls.description: Olin Hall Galleries at Roanoke College in Salem, Virginia has run its Juried Biennial every two years since 1990, and the 2027 edition is free to enter. The gallery frames the show as a survey of work by artists within a 200-mile radius of the college, and its media line is unusually explicit: "All fine arts media are accepted for submission, including, but not limited to, painting, drawing, sculpture, graphic design, photography, ceramics, printmaking, mixed media, textiles, video, and film." The juror is Betsy Johnson, Assistant Curator at the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, where she oversees the photography and works-on-paper collections and has curated Feel the Sun in Your Mouth: Recent Acquisitions (2019), Toyin Ojih Odutola: A Countervailing Theory (2021), One with Eternity: Yayoi Kusama in the Hirshhorn Collection (2022), A Window Suddenly Opens: Contemporary Photography in China (2022), Basquiat x Banksy (2024) and the co-curated Revolutions: Art from the Hirshhorn Collection, 1860-1960. Awards total $2,800 — $1,000 first place, $800 second, $600 third and a $400 Community Choice — announced at 7 p.m. during the opening reception on 22 January 2027. Artists may submit up to three works in any medium; everything must be original and completed within the last three years. Olin Hall Galleries is a non-profit and takes no commission on sales from the exhibition, forwarding interested buyers' details straight to the artist. Two-dimensional work needs proper hanging hardware and sculpture must be portable and under 150 lbs. Accepted work is hand-delivered to the gallery 6 to 9 January 2027, the show runs 22 January to 14 March 2027, and pieces are collected 15 to 17 March.

calls.title: President's Art Show 2026
calls.description: Salt Lake Community College's President's Art Show reaches its 32nd edition in 2026, a juried exhibition open to every Utah artist, amateur or professional, with $5,000 in prize money on the table. Photography is named outright in the accepted-media list alongside painting, sculpture, works on paper, textiles and fibre, and decorative work in glass or wearable form. Artists may enter up to two original works completed in the last two years, at $15 per submission, and up to three images may accompany each entry — for a series, one image must show how the whole is meant to hang. The SLCC Art Committee juries on artistic theme and vision, technical execution, and aesthetic value. The prize stack is unusually well spread: Best in Show $1,500, President's Award $1,000 chosen by SLCC President Gregory F. Peterson, a $1,000 Community Award chosen by an honorary art community representative, a $500 Jury's Choice from the Art Committee, and $500 each for second and third place. Work must be exhibition-ready with wire backing on two-dimensional pieces, and three-dimensional work cannot exceed six feet or 150 pounds. Nothing is shipped: the artist or a representative delivers and collects at the South City Campus in Salt Lake City. Sales carry a 25 per cent commission, waived for SLCC students. Notification lands 15 September, drop-off is 23 October, the reception is 29 October with awards at 7 p.m., and the show runs to 19 November 2026 in the South City Campus Multipurpose Room.

calls.title: Seeds 2026
calls.description: Westobou is a non-profit arts organisation in Augusta, Georgia whose gallery on Broad Street programmes national, regional and local artists with a focus on emerging and mid-career contemporary and experimental practice. Seeds is its twelfth annual juried exhibition of small works priced at an affordable $300 or less, timed for the holidays, and the 2026 juror is Vanna Black — an Atlanta illustrator, painter and muralist with a BFA in graphic arts from Georgia State University, represented by Cat Eye Creative, who has made work for ATL DTN, LivingWalls, the City of Atlanta, the Sustainable Forestry Industry, Hermes and Canada Goose of Atlanta. Westobou runs the juror chain as a relay: each year's juror picks the next. Applying is free, through a Google Form, and asks for a brief proposal describing what you plan to exhibit, five to ten images representative of your style, an exhibition history and bio, and a link to a website or social media. No medium is excluded — the prospectus describes the show as featuring a variety of local and regional artists working with various mediums and a variety of styles, and the parameters are about scale and format rather than material: every individual piece must fit inside an 18-inch square (or an 18-inch cube if three-dimensional), work must be framed unless there is good reason otherwise, and it must have been completed in the last 18 months, though it does not have to exist yet when you apply. Ten to twelve artists are selected, each given roughly nine feet of gallery wall to hang gallery- or salon-style with a two to three foot gap from the next artist; Westobou reserves the right to curate the layout. Selected artists must supply at least four pieces, all for sale, with a 40 per cent commission on sales. Notification lands by 28 August 2026, completed work is due in the gallery by 26 October, and the show runs 6 November to 19 December 2026 with a juror talk at 5 p.m. and an opening reception 6 to 8 p.m. on 6 November.
jury: Vanna Black, illustrator, painter and muralist

calls.title: Small Works 2026
calls.description: The Northville Art House is a community gallery in downtown Northville, Michigan, and Small Works is its year-end juried holiday show — over 125 works of art on a diminutive scale, 16 inches or less in any direction including any frame. The call is national: artists 18 and over anywhere in the continental United States may submit up to four original works created in the last ten years and not previously exhibited at the Art House. Photography is named outright in the accepted-media line alongside collage, drawing, painting and printmaking on the two-dimensional side, and ceramics, sculpture, assemblage, mixed media and metalwork on the three-dimensional side; the only exclusions are film, video, electronic and AI-generated artwork. The Northville Art House Exhibition Committee — practising artists, art instructors, staff and community leaders — serves as juror, selecting from the submitted images alone, so image quality matters. Entry is $40, or $30 for Art House members, paid after the online form is completed. Awards run first through fourth place plus honourable mentions, totalling more than $700 in cash and prizes, presented at 6 p.m. during the free public opening reception on Friday 13 November. Every work must be for sale — the show is pitched to visitors looking for original art to give as gifts — and sales split 65 per cent to the artist, 35 per cent to the Art House. Work must arrive installation-ready: works on paper framed, two-dimensional pieces wired for hanging (sawtooth hangers accepted but not recommended), three-dimensional pieces free-standing, pedestal-ready or hung with wire or rod. Jury notification is 29 September 2026 by 5 p.m. EST, delivery is 1 and 2 November, the exhibition runs 13 November to 18 December 2026, and pick-up is 18 and 19 December. Shipping, packing and insurance are the artist's responsibility, and shipped work needs a pre-paid return label.

calls.title: Sublime Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: The Sublime Photo Awards are a small independent international competition established in 2025, built around a single idea taken straight from the dictionary: the sublime is that which inspires awe through elevated quality, whether beauty, nobility or grandeur. The organisers argue a sublime photograph is reached by great technical skill, an incredible composition or a powerful message, or the sum of several of these, and the award is open to everyone from amateur to professional aged 18 and over, worldwide. There are five categories: Black & White (toned images such as sepia or selenium are accepted here), Creative (abstract, conceptual, fine art, still life, experimental), Nature (landscape, wildlife, macro, seascape, trees, underwater, astrophotography), People (adult portrait, children, family and wedding, fashion and beauty, self-portraits, culture, staged) and Street (light and shadow, people, candid and staged moments, silhouettes). Any capture device is allowed in every category — digital, analogue, drone, mobile, tablet, computer, scanner — and panoramas are accepted. Computer-generated images, whether AI or other technologies, are permitted only in the Creative category. Images must carry no watermark, logo, copyright line or signature. One photo per category may be entered at no cost, but free entries are not eligible for the cash prizes; the paid ladder is $18 for two photos, $25 for three, $31 for four and $36 for five. One caveat worth knowing before you enter: because of state competition law, residents of Maryland, Colorado, Nebraska, North Dakota, Vermont, Montana and Arizona may use only the free option, which means entrants in those seven states cannot compete for the cash prizes at all. The jury is Loredana Denicola, a photographer and visual artist, Daria Bonera, director of DB Agency, and the visual artist Joana Dionisio. Grand prizes are $500, $300 and $200 for first, second and third, each with a place in the Sublime winners gallery, Instagram exposure and a certificate with a winner's badge; ten honourable mentions per category receive the gallery placement, social exposure and an honourable-mention badge. Entries close 1 November 2026 and winners are announced on 3 January 2027.
jury: Loredana Denicola, photographer and visual artist

calls.title: Anderson Center Salzburg Exchange Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Since 2008 the Anderson Center at Tower View has run an annual artist exchange with the City of Salzburg, and each July one Minnesota visual artist takes the Stadt:Atelier live-in studio at the Künstlerhaus in Salzburg, Austria — the building that also houses the Salzburger Kunstverein, five minutes' walk from the historic centre. The 2027 residency runs 1–30 July. The studio is a furnished 70 m² combined living and working space over two floors with kitchenette, lounge, bathroom and wi-fi, with linens and cooking and cleaning supplies provided; a €600 stipend for food is included. In return, a Salzburg artist comes to work at the Anderson Center's own artist community in Red Wing. There is no fee to apply. Eligibility is tightly drawn: the programme is open to emerging and mid-career visual artists who are current legal residents of Minnesota and have been for at least a year, and the enumerated media explicitly include photography alongside ceramics, painting, drawing, filmmaking, sculpture, printmaking, fabric, animation and jewellery — writers and performance artists are not eligible. The participating artist pays their own travel to Salzburg and back, and is asked to gift one work made during the residency to the City of Salzburg. Applications close at noon Central time on 13 November 2026 and require a CV or biographical statement of up to three pages, a one- to two-page letter of intent, and at least ten high-resolution images of recent work. Jury review runs through late November and December, with the selected artist, wait-list and runners-up notified by 5 January 2027 at the latest.
calls.summary: One month in a live-in studio at the Künstlerhaus, Salzburg, for a Minnesota visual artist. €600 food stipend; free to apply.

calls.title: Determination Without Limits 2026
calls.org: Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
calls.description: Second edition of the global photography competition run by AccessAbilities Expo in partnership with the Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum International Photography Award (HIPA), documenting the achievements and everyday lives of People of Determination. Five categories: Hope in Inclusion (resilience and human connection), Artistic Inclusion (the creative talents of People of Determination in the visual, performing and literary arts), Assistive Technology & Innovation (prosthetics, apps and devices that enable independence), Sports Inclusion (athletes with disabilities and integrated sport) and Accessible Environments (inclusive urban design, buildings and transport). Each category awards AED 5,000, AED 3,000 and AED 1,000 for first, second and third place — AED 45,000 in total. The competition explicitly sets out to empower photographers who are themselves People of Determination, giving them visibility on an international platform. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide with no entry fee; one photograph per category, up to five entries in total. Images must be JPEG or RAW, high resolution, at least 5 MB, with no watermarks, signatures, borders or timestamps. Submissions run from 20 July to 11:59 PM UAE time on 20 August 2026, online only through the HIPA website. Winners are announced at AccessAbilities Expo in Dubai.
calls.summary: Free global photo competition on People of Determination, run by AccessAbilities Expo with HIPA. AED 45,000 across five categories.

calls.title: Neighborhood Stories
calls.description: Open call juried by Laurie Freitag, founder of L.A. Photo Curator, on the stories that make a neighbourhood, town or city its own — a local celebration, a holiday tradition, a street festival, a family business, a favourite gathering place, or the quiet rituals of everyday life. Portraits, street photography, documentary, travel, fine art, conceptual work, mobile photography and mixed media rooted in photography are all welcome. First place receives a solo online exhibition, a featured Q&A article with the juror's responses, and a month on the L.A. Photo Curator homepage; every entrant's work appears in the online group exhibition with artist statement, bio and website, and every entry is considered for Top 40 Images of the Year and Photographer of the Year. One participating photographer is also invited to serve as guest juror alongside Freitag on a future L.A. Photo Curator competition. 5% of entry fees go to No Kid Hungry and a further 5% to the winner's chosen charity. Submit 3 or 6 images (not 4 or 5) by email after PayPal payment; a limited number of fee waivers is available on request. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide.
jury: Laurie Freitag, Founder of L.A. Photo Curator

calls.title: Fixed Focus Fellowship 2027
calls.description: Year-long fellowship at Aurora PhotoCenter, the artist-run photography centre in Indianapolis, for up to 10 Indiana photographers aged 18 to 26 — with no art-school enrolment required and no limitation on subject, style, working method or academic training. The 2027 cycle runs 29 January to 31 December 2027 and gives each fellow a free one-year Aurora membership with darkroom, scanner and printer access; free places on Aurora's core workshops (developing black-and-white film, developing colour film, making a black-and-white print, scanning basics, digital printing basics), each offered monthly for the length of the fellowship; a $1,000 use-it-or-lose-it credit for darkroom rental, scanning, digital printing and alternative-process workshops charged at the member rate; one-to-one mentoring arranged with founding director Mary Goodwin; professional sessions on pricing work and applying for grants and exhibitions, worked on real applications; a Final Friday feedback dinner with the cohort every month; and a group exhibition of work made in the programme opening 3 December 2027, with all work for sale. Aurora frames it for photographers outside Indianapolis with limited access to facilities, recent graduates who have lost campus darkrooms, self-taught photographers documenting family and community, multidisciplinary artists strengthening the photographic side of their practice, studio and fashion photographers moving toward fine art, and anyone wanting to work seriously in cyanotype, wet plate collodion, platinum-palladium, van dyke, gum printing or photograms. Applicants who work primarily in another medium may apply with a project that incorporates photography. Fellows buy their own film, paper and materials. Applications open 15 August 2026 and are submitted by email: up to 10 images or supporting files, a statement of interest of up to 250 words, a short biography of up to 200 words including your age, and two references. Selection is by Mary Goodwin with a group of local arts leaders.
jury: Mary Goodwin, Founding Director, Aurora PhotoCenter

calls.title: Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: Standing open call for exhibition proposals at Aurora PhotoCenter, the artist-run nonprofit photography centre in Indianapolis's Factory Arts District. Aurora's programme mixes emerging work by local artists with shows by internationally exhibiting, award-winning photographers, and proposals are welcome from individual artists, collaborations and curators. Submissions are by email and free of charge: an exhibition description covering the artists and the major themes of the show in no more than 500 words, a biography of the artist or artists covering previous exhibitions and relevant experience in no more than 500 words, a vision-and-execution statement giving the approximate number and size of works, formatting, framing, installation requirements and any special programming to accompany the exhibition, and no more than 10 JPEGs of work to be included. Proposals are evaluated on a rolling basis as they arrive rather than against a fixed deadline. Aurora asks that hard-copy materials not be sent unless requested, and cannot provide feedback on individual proposals because of the volume received. Applicants needing accommodations to submit can contact director Mary Goodwin directly. Aurora runs three gallery spaces alongside a darkroom, digital lab and residency programme.

calls.title: Dodho Magazine #38
calls.description: International open call for the next print edition of Dodho Magazine, conceived as an artistic and curatorial volume rather than a conventional magazine and distributed to curators, festival directors, galleries and publishers looking for new voices in contemporary photography. Two routes: the Magazine pack, for projects and portfolios published inside the magazine, at €45 for one portfolio, €75 for two or €90 for three; and the Cover pack, for single images considered for the front page, at €45 for three images, €75 for six or €90 for ten. Everything is completed in one registration — details, upload and payment in the same form — with all material sent as a single ZIP named for the author; fragmented submissions are not accepted. Files must be JPG at 72 dpi and at least 1200 pixels on the longest side, and a PDF with a project text may be included for the Magazine option. Work that has already been published or awarded is eligible as long as the photographer holds the rights, and there is no restriction on when the images were made. The displayed price is final, with VAT added automatically for applicants in Europe where it applies. Photographers retain copyright throughout, granting only a promotional licence that can be revoked on 15 days' notice unless the work has already gone to print. Collectives and duos may apply as a single entrant. Every applicant is told the outcome roughly a week after the deadline and is given access to the digital edition afterwards to show the editorial criteria behind the selection. Submissions run from 1 July to 6 September, selection 7 to 11 September, notification 12 to 13 September, and publication on 25 September. Dodho has published 37 print editions over more than 11 years, featuring 222 photographers from 32 countries.
jury: Janine Bean, Gallery Director, Janine Bean Gallery
Maxim Panés, Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Dodho Magazine

calls.title: Quiet Landscape: Beauty, Stillness, and Connection
calls.description: PhotoPlace Gallery's autumn juried call for landscape photographs that reward slowing down. Rather than dramatic spectacle, the gallery is looking for pictures that invite reflection and reveal the subtle relationships between people, place, light and time — sweeping vistas and intimate details, untouched wilderness and cultivated fields. Natural, rural, urban and cultivated landscapes are all welcome, approached through traditional, documentary, conceptual or fine-art methods, and work may turn on solitude, atmosphere, changing seasons or the quiet moments that usually go unnoticed. Juror Kat Kiernan, formerly editor-in-chief of Don't Take Pictures and now Manager of Public Programs at the Morgan Library & Museum, will select up to 35 photographs for the gallery in Middlebury, Vermont and roughly 40 more for the online gallery. All selected work is reproduced in the exhibition catalog, kept permanently on the PhotoPlace website and promoted through the gallery's publications and social channels; online-gallery selections receive the same catalog inclusion and promotion as the wall selections, and all selected artists are eligible for exhibition awards. Entries open 8 August 2026 and close 7 September, with juror selections announced 21 September, prints due 23 October and the show running 6–28 November 2026 with an opening reception on 6 November. There is no limit on the number of images submitted.
jury: Kat Kiernan, Manager of Public Programs, Morgan Library & Museum

calls.title: The Crux of Visibility: Portraits, Vision, and Empathy
calls.description: LACP's next virtual exhibition asks what it means to be seen. Portraits hold a particular kind of power, the call argues, and can speak in many photographic languages — ID cards and institutional archives, museum collections and family albums — sometimes conveying fragmented, complex identities and sometimes arresting all other readings by fixing a single meaning to a face. This open call is curious about the conversations and connections portraiture enables, and invites images that treat the photographic portrait as a possibility for connection and unexpected encounter, whether conceptual, documentary, digital or candid. Juror Shana Lopes, PhD, Assistant Curator of Photography at SFMOMA, whose curatorial credits include Zanele Muholi: Eye Me and Constellations: Photographs in Dialogue, will make a blind selection. First place receives $500 cash; second a $250 LACP gift card plus a one-year membership; third a $250 gift card. Further artists are named honorable mentions and shown in an online gallery running three months. The exhibition is open internationally to all levels and to artists working in any medium with a relationship to photography. Entrants must state explicitly in the image description or artist statement if AI was involved in production beyond simple editing. Submissions close 22 September 2026 at midnight PT, acceptances go out 13 October, and the virtual opening is on Zoom on 19 November, with the show online until 19 February 2027.
jury: Shana Lopes, PhD, Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA
calls.summary: LACP's virtual portrait show, juried by SFMOMA's Shana Lopes. $500 first prize, open internationally to all levels.

calls.title: World ShootOut 2025–2026 — Underwater Photo Grand Prix
calls.description: Now in its twentieth year, an underwater photography competition running since the Eilat Red Sea Shootout in 2005, with 884 winners and more than $284,000 in cash awarded alongside dive travel prizes. Images must be made underwater or half-in, half-out of the water, and taken between 2 November 2024 and 1 November 2026. Nine categories are open: Best 5 Images, Wide Angle, Macro & Super Macro, Amateurs, UW Fashion, Black Water, BigAnimals Behaviour, Video Clips of the World and Best Picture of the Year, the last of which may reuse images entered elsewhere. Fees are charged per category and per set — €25 for a single image in most categories, €15 in Amateurs, €35 for a first set of five in Best 5 Images and €45 for a video clip — with the per-image rate falling as sets are added. Awards include €2,000 and the Andromeda statuette for Best Picture of the Year, chosen by the director of the boot Düsseldorf dive show; €1,000 cash each in Macro, Wide Angle and Amateurs; and a Papua New Guinea dive package for two worth about $18,900 for the Best 5 Images winner, plus resort packages and equipment from the competition's dive-industry sponsors. The Amateurs category is restricted to entrants who have never won a World ShootOut prize and to GoPro, phone and fixed-lens compact cameras. Minor editing is allowed — colour and contrast, backscatter removal, up to 15% cropping, minor flaw fixes — but moving or removing subjects, compositing and any use of AI are prohibited, and semi-finalists must supply original RAW and JPEG files on request. Judging is by an international panel including National Geographic's David Doubilet: semi-finalists are named 25 November 2026, category finalists 25 December, and the winners at the boot Düsseldorf show on 30 January 2027.
jury: Shlomo Cohen, Art Director, World ShootOut
Alex Kassler, Editor in Chief, TAUCHEN magazine
Phil Simha, Diving Author and Photographer (Video Clip)
Andres Claros, Barcelona Underwater Camera Museum (Video Clip)

calls.title: Eerie Expressions
calls.description: The San Marcos Art League's October show at the San Marcos Art Center, asking for work that captures the spirit of the month — spooky, scary, black-light, Goth-inspired, spirits and monsters and goblins, from the whimsical to the wonderfully dark. Entry is open to all and every medium is eligible, with photographs and digital art named explicitly alongside fine art prints, sculpture, textiles and pottery. Each artist may enter one original work completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at the Art Center Gallery. Two-dimensional work must be framed or gallery-wrapped with no visible staples and wired for the gallery's hanging system — no saw-tooth hangers — and no larger than 36 by 68 inches including the frame; three-dimensional work is judged on size and stability and must stand unaided. Subject matter has to suit a family-oriented venue. All work is hand-delivered — the Art Center does not accept shipments — with intake on 4 October between 1pm and 4pm, a public reception on 9 October from 7 to 9pm (an hour later than usual, to find the darkness), and pickup on 29–30 October. Work must be for sale at a price fixed at entry and the Art League retains a 20% commission. Entry is $10 for Art League members using the code emailed to them and $20 otherwise; submissions close 2 October at 5pm or when the show fills.
calls.summary: October-spirited open show in San Marcos, Texas. Every medium, photography included, one work each, $20 to enter.

calls.title: Hounds in the Hulse
calls.description: A free community exhibition in the Hulse Gallery at Art Center Waco built entirely from work about pets and companion animals — furry, feathered, scaled or otherwise. The centre addresses the call to pet lovers throughout McLennan County and the surrounding area, and is explicit that you do not have to be a professional artist to take part: it welcomes submissions from artists at every level, from community members, and from pet owners who commissioned a portrait of their animal. Every medium is eligible and photography is named alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, fibre art, sculpture and ceramics, so long as the work features or is inspired by a pet. Each person may submit up to three artworks through the centre's Google Form, with no entry fee. Work must arrive ready to display safely in a gallery: there is no minimum size, nothing may exceed 72 inches in any direction, wall pieces are capped at 60 pounds, and framed work needs secure hanging hardware. Gallery space is limited, so submitting does not guarantee inclusion — Art Center Waco says it will show as many community submissions as it can while keeping the hang safe and considered. Selected participants are sent drop-off, exhibition and pickup details afterwards. Submissions close 31 August 2026.
calls.summary: Free community show at Art Center Waco for work about pets and companion animals. Photography welcome, up to three pieces.

calls.title: Mosaic Life Care Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Mosaic Life Care and the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art run this judged exhibition together for artists living within 100 miles of St. Joseph, Missouri. Selected work hangs in the Art Experience Galleries at Mosaic Life Care from 2 September 2026 and stays up for roughly six months unless it sells. Work is judged with ribbons awarded across ten categories, photography and digital art among them alongside oil and acrylic, watercolour, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, 2-D mixed media, fibre and textiles, and sculpture and 3-D mixed media; awards are announced at the opening reception. One $30 entry fee covers an unlimited number of works. Entries go to the Albrecht-Kemper Museum by post or email with a signed entry form, a completed W-9 and a separate photograph of each piece — JPEG files under 1MB named artist, entry number, title and medium, or printed photos of at least 4x6 inches labelled on the back — and the fee is paid online through the museum's call-for-artists page. Entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian signature. Work must be original and the artist's sole property, free of others' copyrighted material, and pieces shown in a previous Mosaic exhibition are not eligible; subject matter depicting cemeteries, death, violence, blood, car crashes or nudity is barred, and the venue cannot accommodate video or performance work. Work is priced at entry and the Albrecht-Kemper Museum takes a 30% commission, with the artist supplying a comparable replacement if a piece sells before the six months are up. Entries close 11:59pm CT on Friday 7 August 2026, with artists notified on 14 August and accepted work delivered on 1 September.
calls.summary: Six months on the wall at Mosaic Life Care, juried with the Albrecht-Kemper Museum. $30 covers unlimited works.

calls.title: Booker Creek Arts Festival 2026
calls.description: The inaugural Booker Creek Arts Festival turns St. Petersburg's historic EDGE District into a four-day walkable gallery from 12 to 15 November 2026, with juried work by hundreds of Florida artists hung inside the district's restaurants, cafés, shops, hotels and residential buildings rather than in a single venue. Named after the urban stream that runs through downtown St. Petersburg, the festival wraps the art in live mural painting, glass blowing, dance, music and children's activities, and visitors move between venues with a map, voting by text for the People's Choice Award. Up to $50,000 in prizes is on offer — a $10,000 Booker Creek Best of Show, a $7,500 Award of Excellence, ten $1,500 Merit Awards and two $2,500 People's Choice Awards, presented on Saturday 14 November. The organisers name painting, photography, wall sculpture and mixed media among the competing media, and entries may be paintings, sculptures, ceramic works, textile works, photographs, drawings, mixed-media works, collages or assemblages. Entry is open to artists who have lived in Florida for at least six consecutive months and are 18 or older on 14 August 2026; each artist makes one application only, submitting three separate works with one high-resolution image each, for a $25 non-refundable fee. Every submitted work must have been completed in or after 2023 and must be physically hangable — digital-only works, new media, video and film are not permitted, and a single piece may occupy no more than 6 feet high by 8 feet wide. Work created solely by AI software will not be treated as the artist's own and will be disqualified. Artists do not have to be present during the festival, and visitors can buy work directly from them. Submissions close at 11:59pm EDT on Friday 14 August 2026.
calls.summary: Inaugural St. Petersburg festival turning the EDGE District into a walkable gallery, with up to $50,000 in juried prizes.

calls.title: Freedom: The Spirit Within
calls.description: Marion Cultural Alliance's September 2026 juried exhibition, presented, curated and juried by Lisa Russo (M.F.A., M.Ed.), asks artists what freedom means to them — personal journeys, creative expression, relationships, beliefs, memories and everyday life. Work responding to America's 250th anniversary and the 25th anniversary of September 11 is welcome but the theme is deliberately wider, taking in self-expression, resilience, identity, hope, possibility, remembrance and the enduring human spirit. The call is open to local and regional artists in all media, with photography named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fibre art, mixed media, digital art and fine craft; MCA membership is not required to enter. Each artist may submit up to two original pieces, no giclées or reproductions, suggested size up to 50 inches in any direction, and only work that engages the theme will be accepted. Cash and ribbon awards go to Best of Show, which carries the cash prize, with ribbons for first through fifth place and honourable mention. All exhibited work must be for sale, with proceeds split 70% to the artist and 30% to MCA, whose share funds its arts programming in Ocala and Marion County. Alongside the show, guest curator Lisa Russo runs a hands-on classical drawing workshop, Draw Like the Masters, on Saturday 19 September 2026 — a separate, optional $75 booking. Entries are submitted digitally through ArtCall by midnight on Sunday 16 August 2026; no physical or mailed submissions are accepted.
calls.summary: Lisa Russo curates and juries MCA's September show on freedom — photography included, cash and ribbon awards, $25 to enter.

calls.title: Art & Woman Edition 4
calls.description: The fourth volume of Arts to Hearts Project's Art & Woman series, a storytelling-based publishing project that has published more than 300 women artists since 2024. Guest curator for this edition is Liz Lidgett, founder of Liz Lidgett Gallery and Design in Des Moines and author of Art for Everyone. The edition is intentionally open-themed: rather than responding to a set concept, artists are asked to submit work that reflects their own journey and practice, whether that means identity, memory, belonging, resilience, transformation, family, culture, motherhood, healing, loss or joy. Submissions are welcome across all visual media, with photography named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, ceramics, textile art, mixed media, collage, digital art, installation, illustration and experimental practice, and there is no requirement to make new work — existing, previously exhibited or already sold pieces are eligible so long as the artist holds the rights. The top winner receives a USD $500 cash award, a four-page editorial feature in the book, a written artist interview on the Arts to Hearts site, an engraved crystal trophy and certificate, and newsletter and social promotion to the project's audience; the first runner-up also receives a four-page feature, an interview and a trophy, and the second runner-up a four-page feature and a trophy. A separate optional $22 add-on buys a published virtual studio-visit interview if selected; it is not part of the entry. The book is distributed worldwide through Amazon, Barnes & Noble and the Arts to Hearts shop. Open to women and womxn artists worldwide aged 18 or over at any career stage, including collaborative work where the submitting artist identifies as a woman. Entry is tiered by image count, from $21 for one image to $100 for twenty. Applications close at 11:59pm EST on 30 August 2026.
calls.summary: Fourth volume of the Art & Woman book series, curated by Liz Lidgett — $500, a four-page spread and worldwide distribution.

calls.title: Art in the Atrium 26
calls.description: The 26th installment of the City of Frisco's Art in the Atrium, a free rotating exhibition in the atrium of the George A. Purefoy Municipal Center. The city seeks original two-dimensional work from artists in Frisco and the surrounding area, loaned for display from 30 September 2026 to 1 February 2027. Photographs are explicitly provided for and must be printed on quality paper at a resolution of at least 300 dpi; work must have been made within the past two years, be framed and ready to hang with wire securely attached — unframed canvases with finished edges and wire are also accepted — and measure no more than 60 by 60 inches. Three-dimensional work is not considered. Each artist may submit two images through CaFÉ at no cost, with a description explaining motivation, themes or process, and pieces may be offered for sale. Submissions are reviewed by the Arts and Culture Advisory Board and city staff on criteria including uniqueness and originality, visual impact and demonstrated excellence of technique, and every artist is notified in writing. Work must be delivered and collected in person, with drop-off on 29 September 2026 — shipped work is not accepted and return shipping is not provided. The entry deadline is Wednesday 6 September 2026.
calls.summary: Free civic call: four months of wall space in Frisco's municipal center atrium, with photographic prints expressly provided for.

calls.title: Teeny Tiny BOLD
calls.description: Ripple Artspace — formerly Rountree Gallery, on Main Street in Platteville, Wisconsin — runs Teeny Tiny BOLD as its annual national juried exhibition of small-scale work. Working within a limited scale, the gallery argues, forces artists to distil ideas and refine craft, and the call is open to all subjects and themes in any medium provided the finished piece measures no more than 12 inches in any direction including frame, base or mounting hardware. Photography is named among the eligible media alongside painting, drawing, collage, fibre, metal, ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media and digital media; both two- and three-dimensional work is welcome. The juror is John T. Upchurch, a Chicago-based sculptor working in wood, stone, metal, found objects and salvaged material who earned his BFA from the Kansas City Art Institute in 1990. The exhibition runs 19 November 2026 to 9 January 2027 and is marked by three public events: Small Business Saturday and Holiday Magic on Main on 28 November, an Artist Sunday open house with live music from the Prairie Lights String Band on 29 November, and an artist reception on 11 December. Ripple Artspace retains a 30% commission on all work sold during the exhibition, and sold pieces stay on the wall until it closes. AI-generated work is not eligible and may be disqualified. Open to artists aged 18 or older residing in the United States or its territories; the entry fee is $30 for three to six images.
calls.summary: National juried small-works show at Wisconsin's Ripple Artspace — nothing over 12 inches, photography welcome, AI barred.
