calls.title: Bettie Awards 2027
calls.description: The Elizabeth Barker Delaplaine Award for Young Artists — the Bettie Awards — is the Delaplaine Arts Center's annual free award for high-school artists, run each March for Youth Art Month and named for a lifelong supporter of the arts in Frederick County, Maryland. Artists living in or attending school in Frederick County in grades 9 to 12, whether public, private or homeschooled, may apply at no cost with one work no more than five feet in any direction; all media are eligible, photography named alongside painting, printmaking, ceramics, drawing and sculpture. A first-round jury of Delaplaine instructors and art professionals selects at least ten Bettie Award Winners, and a second-round jury of artists from across the region picks one of them as the Bettie Award Grand Prize Winner. The grand prize is $1,000; every other winner receives $100, and visitors vote through the run of the show for a People's Choice Award worth $250. The grand prize winner is also featured in an article in Delaplaine Arts magazine, distributed across the region, and other winners' work may be published in local print and online media. Judges treat presentation as a real criterion and will not award the grand prize to work that is poorly prepared for installation. Applications close at 11:59pm EST on Monday 1 February 2027, winners are announced on 6 February, selected work is delivered 22–28 February, and the exhibition opens with an awards presentation on Saturday 6 March 2027, running to 25 April.
calls.summary: Free Maryland high-school award: $1,000 grand prize, $100 to every winner, a March exhibition and a magazine feature.

calls.title: Capturing Ecology 2026
calls.description: The British Ecological Society's annual photography competition, run since 2013, looks for images that tell ecological stories — triumph, challenge and survival — rather than pretty wildlife portraits alone. The 2026 edition opens eight categories: Ecologists in Action (yourself or colleagues at work in the field or lab), Animals (in partnership with ZSL), Plants and Fungi (with Plantlife), Species Interactions, Resilient Nature, Doorstep Ecology, Macro Photography, and a new Nature from Above category for drone and aerial work. Entrants may submit up to eight images, each with full camera settings, location, species names and a description of what is happening; no image may be entered in two categories. A panel of wildlife photographers and ecologists — Max Mudie, Ian Price, Gabriela Staebler, Laura Dyer, Matt Doggett, Rathika Ramasamy, Richard Bardgett and Harriet McAra — scores every entry on creativity, impact and technical merit, and the BES makes the final call. The overall winner takes £750 and twelve months of free BES membership; each category winner takes £120, and one person may win at most two categories. Entry is free for BES members and is waived entirely for photographers who are citizens of and resident in a Global South country; everyone else pays £12 per entry. Plantlife members may enter the Plants and Fungi category free. Digital enhancement must be declared and is limited to cleaning and minor colour work — black and white is fine, AI-generated images are not accepted, and animal welfare, honesty and permits are treated as disqualifying rules rather than guidance. Photographers retain copyright; entering grants the BES and its partners the right to reproduce the work, including in its membership magazine Niche. Under-18s are actively encouraged to enter. Submissions close at 23:59 BST on Monday 31 August 2026 and winners are announced in January 2027.
calls.summary: Learned society's ecology photo prize: eight categories, £750 overall, £120 each, free for members and Global South entrants.

calls.title: Art and the Ship Channel
calls.description: The Art League of Baytown's first fall juried exhibition, funded by the Port Houston Community Grant Program and built around the communities, parks and green spaces within three miles of the Houston Ship Channel. Photography is one of three judged categories alongside 2D and 3D work, and the source of inspiration must be a public park, greenspace or publicly accessible community within that three-mile band — private property is off limits, though neither the organiser's page nor the ArtCall prospectus states a residency rule — the three-mile band governs the subject of the work, not where the artist lives. Awards total $2,000: $300 Best of Show and a $200 Honoree Award chosen by a Port Houston representative, plus $175 first, $150 second, $100 third and a $75 honourable mention in each of the three categories. Donna Tennant jurors the show. Work must have been made in the past five years, be entirely the artist's own, and carry a short artist statement that is displayed alongside it; copies of other people's work, images built from published or copyrighted photographs, and AI-generated art are all ineligible, as is work depicting nudes, destruction, cruelty, political statements or violence. Photographs must be framed unless printed on canvas or metal, wired and ready to hang, and no larger than 48 x 48 inches; no sawtooth hangers. Judging weighs visual impact, originality, composition and craftsmanship, with a further criterion for resourceful and sustainable use of materials. Entries run 1 August to 16 September 2026 through ArtCall, acceptance emails go out between 26 and 30 September, and accepted work is delivered in person in Baytown on 8–9 October (other arrangements by email if those dates are impossible). The show runs 10–30 October, Thursdays to Saturdays, closing with an awards reception on 30 October. Sale is preferred but not required; the Art League retains a 20% commission.

calls.title: Her Wild Becoming
calls.description: Virtual exhibition and print catalog celebrating the evolving voices of contemporary women artists worldwide, juried by a five-person panel: Danielle Krysa (The Jealous Curator), Ekaterina Popova (Create! Magazine), Alicia Puig (PxP Contemporary), Marina Granger (The Artist Advisory) and Liza Zhurkovskaya (Kefi Art Gallery). The theme reads becoming as an untamed process — identity, intuition, resilience, transformation, and the many ways women define themselves through creative expression — honouring the courage to trust one's inner voice and keep evolving. Open to women artists of all backgrounds, disciplines and experience levels, 18 and over. All 2D and 3D media are accepted, photography named explicitly among them; film and video are not. Selected work appears in the online exhibition on visionaryartcollective.com and in the print catalog, and a small number of artists receive extra prizes from the jurors (a Substack subscription, Create! Collective membership, a Create! Magazine blog feature and two Instagram spotlights). Tiered fees: $25 for 1–2 images, $30 for 3–4, $35 for 5–6. Artists are notified within four to six weeks of the deadline and the exhibition is presented in October 2026.
jury: Danielle Krysa, Curator & Founder, The Jealous Curator
Alicia Puig, Curator & Co-founder, PxP Contemporary
Marina Granger, Founder, The Artist Advisory
Liza Zhurkovskaya, Curator & Founder, Kefi Art Gallery

calls.title: Solo and Small Group Exhibits
calls.description: The Delaplaine seeks proposals for solo and small group exhibitions on an ongoing basis, for five galleries on two floors of its building in historic downtown Frederick, Maryland; openings are held on most first Saturdays. Proposals go to an Exhibition Selection Panel of artists, art professionals, art consultants and art educators, which asks whether the work is enriching, cohesive and relevant, and whether the installation suits the spaces available — the Delaplaine states plainly that artists are not judged on their backgrounds or writing skills. All media are encouraged and the call is open to anyone: past exhibitors have been local and international, professional and non-professional, self-taught and highly trained. Applicants submit 6–20 work samples with a bio/CV, artist statement and exhibit proposal; no commercially made prints, giclées or reproductions of an original work are considered. Proposals are reviewed every other month (received Jan 15–Mar 14, notified by Apr 8; Mar 15–May 14 by Jun 8; May 15–Jul 14 by Aug 8; Jul 15–Sep 14 by Oct 8; Sep 15–Nov 14 by Dec 8; Nov 15–Jan 14 by Feb 8), and shows are scheduled about two years in advance, which gives artists room to develop the body of work they intend to exhibit. Fees are $7 for Delaplaine members and $37 for non-members — the figure the Delaplaine's own FAQ and the CaFÉ prospectus text both give, though CaFÉ's fee panel prints $35 for non-members, so budget for the higher one.
jury: Exhibition Selection Panel of artists, art professionals, art consultants and art educators

calls.title: Future of Archives: Whose Archive Is It Anyway?
calls.description: Open call for speakers for Whose Archive is it Anyway?, a one-day event at The Photographers' Gallery on Friday 16 April 2027 and the first in a three-part series exploring the future of archives and archiving. The brief asks what makes an archive and who decides: who creates one, what it consists of, who it is for, who has access, and what becomes of the everyday material that sits outside institutional collections, hidden, forgotten or displaced. The Gallery is explicit that it wants submissions of real-life experience rather than academic papers, and the call is aimed particularly at people working outside traditional institutions and archives. Suggested subjects include artists' and photographers' legacies, reclaimed photographic archives, family archives, counter-archives that question dominant historical narratives, grassroots and radical archives, questions of ownership and authority over images and their stories, memory and lost histories made visible again, digitisation and digital preservation, and technologies that reduce barriers to archives while safeguarding material. Selected speakers receive a fee of £200. Applicants must be 18 or over and available to attend the Gallery in person on 16 April 2027. There is no application fee. Applying takes a short Microsoft form: name, email, a talk title (which can be a work in progress) and a 400-word summary, plus confirmation that you can present in person on the day. Applications close 1 November 2026 at 11.59pm BST and selected speakers are notified by 18 January 2027. Supported by TownsWeb Archiving.
calls.summary: Paid speaker call for a one-day event on the future of photographic archives at The Photographers' Gallery, London.

calls.title: F/262 NEXT GEN Award 2026
calls.description: Single-image award for young photographers at the F/262 International Photography Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal, run as its own competition alongside the festival's Photography Awards, Curated Open Call and Photo Book Award. Open worldwide to photographers aged 25 and under at the time of submission, split into two bands: Junior (16 and under) enter free and submit 1–3 images; Emerging (17 to 25) pay €5 per image and submit 1–5 images. Both bands must upload proof of age as a PDF. Any subject is welcome and any device qualifies, including analogue cameras and phones; the festival's 2026 sub-theme 'Shaping Shores / Moldar as Margens' is suggested but not required. A shortlist of up to 10 photographers is selected after the deadline. The overall winner takes the title NEXT GEN Photographer of the Year 2026 and a dedicated solo exhibition at the CEF (Centro de Experimentação Fotográfica) in October–November 2026. Gold, Silver and Bronze each receive a festival exhibition plus a Rotary Prize of €450, €200 and €100 respectively, KOYLAB print vouchers of €250, €150 and €100, BlackRapid straps and SmartAlbums software; Gold also receives an Instax Mini Evo Cinema camera. All shortlisted finalists join the NEXT GEN group exhibition and receive a finalist certificate and festival catalogue feature. Photographers keep full copyright; the festival takes a non-exclusive licence for up to three years. Submissions close 19 August 2026, World Photography Day, with the winner announced in September.

calls.title: Community Gallery Wall Takeover
calls.description: Fotografiska Tallinn invites local and international photographic artists, image-makers, amateur photographers and photography enthusiasts to take over the walls of its Community Gallery on the museum's 1st floor — a space where art, everyday life and lively encounters intersect. The museum is looking for photo series and projects that speak to our time: work that raises timely or socially relevant questions, offers new perspectives and sparks dialogue, and that can enter into conversation with Fotografiska's wider exhibition programme. This first application round closes on 19 August 2026, World Photography Day, and selects work for the autumn 2026 season, when the museum will also present its major Vivian Maier exhibition. After that, submissions remain open year-round, with the next available exhibition slot opening in early 2027. Selected artists present their work in one of Fotografiska Tallinn's most visible and accessible exhibition spaces, supported by the museum's communications, marketing and public programme activities. Both new projects and previously exhibited works are welcome. Production of the works remains the responsibility of the artist, though the museum can recommend trusted production partners. Applications are sent as a single PDF containing 10–15 photographs, a short project description and a short artist bio.
calls.summary: Fotografiska Tallinn opens its 1st-floor Community Gallery to photographers worldwide. Free, first round closes World Photography Day.

calls.title: Identity 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the theme of identity, which the gallery calls "a broad and versatile theme that can be explored through many photographic genres". Portraits can express personal or collective identity, documentary work can reveal the experiences of individuals or groups, and even landscapes or cityscapes can reflect the environments that shape who we are. Identity may be rooted in culture, religion, place, community or countless other influences, and photographers are invited to explore it in all its forms — whether reflecting their own or telling someone else's story. Selected work is shown at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 3 to 20 December 2026, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for consideration as Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £38 participation fee that covers printing, installation and de-installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition on identity in all its forms — personal, collective, cultural. Glasgow show Dec 2026 plus catalogue.
prose: Identity 2026 is one of Glasgow Gallery of Photography's themed open calls — the gallery runs a roughly monthly schedule of themed group exhibitions across the year. The gallery calls identity "a broad and versatile theme that can be explored through many photographic genres": portraits can express personal or collective identity, documentary work can reveal the experiences of individuals or groups, and even landscapes or cityscapes can reflect the environments that shape who we are. Identity may be rooted in culture, religion, place, community, hobbies or countless other influences, and photographers are invited to explore it in all its forms, whether reflecting their own or telling someone else's story.

The exhibition runs December 3 through 20, 2026 in the gallery's Glasgow space, sharing the December program with In Between 2026. The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected — a £38 participation fee covers printing, installation and de-installation, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. The frames used belong to the gallery, and prints are presented at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image.

Selected work also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and is included in the exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for the gallery's Photographer of the Month consideration, which functions as ongoing visibility beyond the show itself. Photographers may collect their prints after the exhibition if they arrange it in advance; work put aside for collection is held for one month.

Eligibility is open globally — emerging and established, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Each photographer submits up to 8 JPEGs at minimum 300ppi and 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, sent in a single batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address. The deadline is August 28, 2026, with acceptance notification by September 2 and payment due September 16; only selected photographers are notified.

calls.title: In Between 2026
calls.description: International photography exhibition on the in-between: "those fleeting moments that sit on the edge of change, right before something happens or just after it unfolds". The gallery is looking for images that hold tension and drama, capturing the charged pause between action and outcome. All photographic genres are welcome and the theme is open to interpretation — whatever the in-between means to you. Selected work is shown at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 3 to 20 December 2026, and also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and in an exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for consideration as Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers selected pay a £38 participation fee that covers printing, installation and de-installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image. A discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on the shortest side) by free file transfer to the gallery's submissions address.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition on fleeting moments at the edge of change. Glasgow show Dec 2026, online gallery and catalogue.
prose: In Between 2026 is one of Glasgow Gallery of Photography's themed open calls — the gallery runs a roughly monthly schedule of themed group exhibitions across the year. This call focuses on "those fleeting moments that sit on the edge of change, right before something happens or just after it unfolds": images that hold tension and drama, capturing the charged pause between action and outcome. All photographic genres are welcome and the theme is explicitly open to interpretation — whatever the in-between means to you.

The exhibition runs December 3 through 20, 2026 in the gallery's Glasgow space, sharing the December program with Identity 2026. The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected — a £38 participation fee covers printing, installation and de-installation, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both December exhibitions. The frames used belong to the gallery, and prints are presented at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image.

Selected work also appears in an online gallery on the gallery's website and is included in the exhibition catalogue. All selected participants receive a digital certificate of participation and are put forward for the gallery's Photographer of the Month consideration, which functions as ongoing visibility beyond the show itself. Photographers may collect their prints after the exhibition if they arrange it in advance; work put aside for collection is held for one month.

Eligibility is open globally — emerging and established, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Each photographer submits up to 8 JPEGs at minimum 300ppi and 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname, sent in a single batch via Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox to the gallery's submissions address. The deadline is August 28, 2026, with acceptance notification by September 2 and payment due September 16; only selected photographers are notified.

calls.title: Altered Horizons — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated in-house by SaveArtSpace, opening October 9, 2026. Altered Horizons asks artists to disrupt the mundane landscape with visions of alternative realities, dream states and mind-expanding wonder — work that reawakens curiosity and sparks moments of lucid awareness for passers-by, whether through hyper-saturated surrealism, cosmic abstraction or visionary portraiture. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of any age, skill level or background; still images only, no video. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after September 7, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.

calls.title: Flatland Feature — Issue 3
calls.description: Online photography feature showcasing a series of a photographer's work in a slide-show format as a virtual gallery experience. Selected photographers' work is featured for six months on the MWCP website, January through June 2027. Each feature consists of 10–20 images with an accompanying artist statement and biography, and visitors can view and purchase photographs online (50% gallery commission). Selection is based on the thematic series submitted rather than on individual images. Open internationally to all subject matter, genre and photographic media — MWCP describes the feature as a platform for photographers making work about the central plains region and about the multitude of other places, ideas and concepts. No shipping is required; work is presented online only.
calls.summary: Online portfolio feature — 10–20 images showcased for six months on the MWCP website. All genres, open internationally.
prose: Midwest Center for Photography (MWCP) is a Wichita, Kansas gallery that runs themed exhibitions alongside two online feature programs. Flatland Feature is the series-portfolio slot — a place for an extended body of work rather than the single-image group shows that fill most of the gallery's calendar.

Selected photographers receive a six-month feature on the MWCP website, January through June 2027. Each feature presents 10–20 images in a slide-show format with an accompanying artist statement and biography, closer to a solo presentation than a group exhibition entry.

Visitors can view and purchase photographs through the feature page. MWCP takes 50% commission on sales, and no shipping is required — the work exists online only, so there are no framing or print costs unless a sale is made.

Eligibility is open to all photographers internationally, with no restriction on subject matter, genre or photographic medium. Selection is based on the thematic series submitted rather than on individual images, and a brief artist statement and bio are required. The fee is $100 for 10 images, $150 for 15 and $200 for 20. The Issue 3 deadline is October 1, 2026.

calls.title: AUTO PHOTO Awards 2026
calls.description: The AUTO PHOTO Awards celebrate 100 global winners in automotive photography, with the Top 100 images printed in the annual AUTO PHOTO photobook published by Shutter Hub Editions. Past editions are held in international archives and collections including the British Library, Cambridge University and Motorsport UK HQ, and sold through selected stockists. There are no categories — entries are open to all photographers whatever their level of experience, with suggested prompts covering cars as art, motorsport, scenes and styling, innovation, and auto portraiture. Alongside the Top 100 there are eight named judges' awards, and a Creative Impact Award whose winner joins the judging panel. Pay-what-you-can entry from £25, 10 images per entry and unlimited entries; free submissions are offered on request to photographers experiencing homelessness, displacement, poverty or social injustice.
jury: Charlie Roughton, Co-Founder and Director, The Maze Group
Charles Gordon-Lennox, Founder, Goodwood Revival and Festival of Speed
Łukasz Dawczyk, Head of Technology & Media, Ultrace and Co-Founder, Driven Stories
Justina Williams, Team Owner, EXCELR8 Motorsport
Mai Ikuzawa, Team Principal, Team Ikuzawa and Creative Director, Bentley Motors
calls.summary: Shutter Hub's automotive photography awards — Top 100 printed in the annual photobook, eight judges' awards. Pay what you can from £25.
prose: AUTO PHOTO is Shutter Hub's automotive photography award, and the book is the point of it. The Top 100 images are printed in the annual AUTO PHOTO photobook published by Shutter Hub Editions, and past editions sit in international archives and collections including the British Library, Cambridge University and Motorsport UK HQ. Shutter Hub describes the book as a promotional tool as much as a collection — a portfolio circulated to the people who buy and commission photography across the automotive and creative industries.

The 2026 edition drops formal categories entirely. Shutter Hub still suggests themes as prompts rather than gates: cars as art, motorsport, scenes and styling, innovation, and auto portraiture — the last of these aimed at the people in the automotive scene rather than the machines. Entries are open to photographers at any level of experience.

Beyond the Top 100 there are eight named judges' awards — seven of them chosen by an individual from the motorsport or automotive world, the WXVE Award by that production team — plus a Creative Impact Award recognising someone who has made a significant impact in the automotive community and creative industries; that winner is invited to join the judging panel. Every winning photographer also receives a digital certificate and social promotion.

Entry is pay-what-you-can with a £25 minimum (the form offers £25, £35 and £45), 10 images per entry, and photographers may enter as many times as they like. Shutter Hub receives no external grants or funding but offers a number of free image submissions to photographers experiencing difficult circumstances including homelessness, displacement, poverty and social injustice — email before entering to be considered.

The submission form asks whether AI was used in the production of each image, so AI-assisted work is accepted with disclosure. The deadline is 15 October 2026 at 5pm UK time, and Shutter Hub says every photographer who entered will be contacted by the end of November 2026.

calls.title: Life Framer — Series Award Edition XII
calls.description: Life Framer's annual series award, running alongside its twelve monthly themed competitions and asking instead for a cohesive body of work — any topic, any genre, any format. Submissions are a series of 5 to 20 photographs with a shared theme or aesthetic rather than a broad portfolio; images may be new or from the archive, and may have been previously published or exhibited. Edition XII is judged by Lisa Woodward and Mia Dalglish, co-curators at Pictura Gallery in Bloomington, Indiana. Three finalists are shortlisted and each receives an online portfolio review session with the curators before the first prize is chosen. The winner receives a three-month, fully funded solo show at Pictura Gallery in summer 2027, curated by Woodward and Dalglish, with printing, framing and curatorial costs covered by Life Framer and Pictura Gallery. Second and third prizes receive the review session plus write-ups on the Life Framer Journal and Pictura Gallery's Curious Photo Blog. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over.
calls.prize: Funded solo exhibition at Pictura Gallery
calls.summary: Annual series award for a cohesive body of work. Winner gets a three-month funded solo show at Pictura Gallery, Bloomington IN.
prose: The Series Award is Life Framer's annual counterweight to its twelve monthly single-image competitions. Where the monthly rounds ask for individual photographs against a theme, this one asks for a body of work: a series of 5 to 20 photographs held together by a cohesive subject, narrative or aesthetic. There is no theme and no category — any topic, any genre, any format, with images new or drawn from the archive, and previously published or exhibited work allowed.

Edition XII is judged by Lisa Woodward and Mia Dalglish, co-curators at Pictura Gallery in Bloomington, Indiana. The two have worked together as jurors, guest critics and portfolio reviewers for thirteen years, at festivals including FotoFest, Photolucida, Filter Photo and Les Rencontres d'Arles.

The judging has an unusual step built in: three finalists are shortlisted and each gets an online portfolio review session with Woodward and Dalglish before the first prize is decided. Shortlisted finalists must be available for that session on a weekday in February 2027. All three prizes therefore include the review; second and third also receive write-ups on the Life Framer Journal and Pictura Gallery's Curious Photo Blog.

First prize is a three-month, fully funded solo show at Pictura Gallery, curated by Woodward and Dalglish in collaboration with the photographer and held in summer 2027. Pictura, established in 2008, is hosted within the FAR Center for Contemporary Art, a building on the National Register of Historic Places. Life Framer and Pictura cover printing, framing and related curatorial and exhibition costs; travel and accommodation are not included.

Entry is $45 for a series of 5 to 20 images, open worldwide to photographers aged 18 or over. Life Framer's rules state that AI-generated imagery is not accepted. The deadline is 31 December 2026 at 23:59 PST, with winners announced publicly in early March 2027.

calls.title: Solo Artist Exhibition Fall 2027
calls.description: Open call for artists from Washington DC, Maryland and Virginia to propose a solo exhibition at Hill Center at the Old Naval Hospital on Capitol Hill. Hill Center Galleries runs a yearly Solo Artist Exhibition in which roughly six artists each get a solo show installed concurrently in one of the galleries, sharing a joint opening reception, an artist panel talk and a holiday reception during the run. The Fall 2027 installation runs August 29, 2027 through January 9, 2028. Open to any 2D medium, including photography, that can hang on the Arakawa cable-and-hook system without extending more than six inches from the wall; there are no pedestals, tables or display cases. Applicants may submit existing work or propose a new body of work to be made for the show — submitted images are read as examples of the artist's practice. Work included must have been made in the last three years and not previously shown at Hill Center. All artwork must be available for sale. Open to artists 18 and over; the Galleries Director makes final determinations with input from jurors and colleagues.
calls.summary: Propose a solo show at Hill Center on Capitol Hill — six concurrent solo exhibitions, any 2D medium. DC, MD and VA artists.
prose: Hill Center Galleries occupies the Old Naval Hospital on Capitol Hill, a historic building whose three public floors have been divided into gallery spaces spread through the corridors and rooms where community activity runs all day. It is a nontraditional venue by design, and the call is explicit about what that means practically: work has to hang on the walls using the Arakawa cable-and-hook system, cannot project more than six inches out, and there are no pedestals, tables or display cases available.

The Solo Artist Exhibition is an annual programme in which approximately six artists each receive a solo show, all installed at the same time across the galleries. Participating artists share a joint opening reception, an artist panel talk, and a holiday reception during the run. The Fall 2027 installation is on view from August 29, 2027 to January 9, 2028.

Applications are open to artists from Washington DC, Maryland and Virginia, aged 18 and over, working in any 2D medium — photography included. Applicants may submit work already made or propose to create a new body of work for the exhibition; in either case the submitted images are treated as a representation of the kind of work that would be shown. Anything included in the final exhibition must have been made in the last three years and must not have been shown at Hill Center before, and all artwork must be available for sale.

The entry fee is $45 and up to ten images may be submitted. Selection is made by the Hill Center Galleries Director with input from jurors and colleagues, based on the information and images in the application. Selected artists sign a consignment agreement and Hill Center takes a 30% commission on sales; artists arrange and insure transport of their own work.

Submissions opened July 30, 2026 and close September 3, 2026, with artists notified in late September 2026. Drop-off and installation take place August 29–31, 2027, and de-installation on January 9, 2028.

calls.title: Beyond Borders II: Global Voices
calls.description: Juried exhibition at The Art Center in Johns Creek, Georgia exploring the complexity, nuance and lived experience of cultures around the world through deeply personal and authentic artistic perspectives. The call asks for work that reflects a global viewpoint not as a generalised or stereotypical concept but as something specific, individual and deeply felt — moving past simplified narratives and superficial multiculturalism toward the richness, tension, overlap and individuality within and between communities. Suggested themes include cultural heritage and identity, migration and diaspora, tradition and transformation, intersectionality and hybridity, cultural contrast and exchange, and personal narratives in a global context; entries may be celebratory, critical, bold or contemplative. Photography is among the eligible media, alongside mixed media, ceramics, drawing, fibre art, printmaking, painting, collage, digital art and sculpture. Juried by the curatorial staff of The Art Center. Up to three works for a $25 entry fee. On view September 11 – October 17, 2026, with an awards reception on the closing night.
calls.summary: Juried show on world cultures told through specific, personal perspectives. Photography eligible, $500 first place, $25 for 3 works.
prose: Beyond Borders II: Global Voices is the second edition of The Art Center's exhibition about world cultures, and the brief is unusually clear about what it does not want. It asks for a global viewpoint "not as a generalized or stereotypical concept, but as something specific, individual, and deeply felt", and states that the show aims to move past simplified narratives and superficial notions of multiculturalism toward the richness, tension, overlap and individuality that exist within and between communities.

Suggested themes include cultural heritage and identity, migration and diaspora, tradition and transformation, intersectionality and hybridity, cultural contrast and exchange, and personal narratives within a global context. Entries may be celebratory or critical, bold and expressive or quiet and contemplative — what the curators say they value above all is authenticity and specificity of voice.

Eligible media are enumerated and include photography, alongside mixed media, ceramics, drawing, fibre art, printmaking, painting, collage, digital art and sculpture. 2D work is capped at 48 × 48 inches framed and 20 lbs, works on paper must be framed with acrylic or plexiglas, and pieces must arrive dry and wired ready to hang. AI-generated work will not be considered.

Each artist may submit up to three works for a non-refundable $25 entry fee. First Place receives a $500 cash award, with additional cash prizes and recognitions presented as part of the exhibition. The show is juried and judged by the curatorial staff of The Art Center.

The deadline is August 14, 2026, with notification on August 21 and drop-off from August 31 to September 2. The exhibition runs September 11 – October 17, 2026, with the awards reception on October 17 from 6 to 7:30pm. Artists keep 75% of sales, with a 25% commission to The Art Center, which is a nonprofit in Johns Creek, Georgia.

calls.title: Art of Abstraction
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut inviting artists to explore the power of colour, shape, texture and movement beyond literal representation — from bold, expressive compositions to subtle, thought-provoking works, celebrating the many ways abstract art evokes emotion and invites personal interpretation. Photography is among the accepted media, alongside painting, mixed media, ceramics, sculpture, textiles, metal and illustration. Open to artists 18 and over; each artist may submit up to five pieces, and work must not have appeared in a previous ACE juried exhibit. No copies, no kits, no work made in a class and no AI-generated art. Entry is $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising per additional piece up to five. Shown in the Eureka Gallery, September 26 – October 31, 2026, with a reception and awards.
calls.summary: Abstraction beyond literal representation at Arts Center East, CT. Photography accepted, up to 5 works, from $35.
prose: Art of Abstraction is one of the juried shows Arts Center East runs through its year in Vernon, Connecticut. The call invites artists and viewers to explore the power of colour, shape, texture and movement beyond literal representation, and spans the range from bold, expressive compositions to subtle, thought-provoking works — the framing is about how abstract art evokes emotion and leaves room for personal interpretation rather than about any single style.

Photography is explicitly among the accepted media, listed alongside painting, mixed media, ceramics, sculpture, textiles, metal and illustration. This matters for photographers working non-representationally, who are often left guessing at all-media abstraction shows.

The show is open to artists 18 and over. Each artist may submit up to five pieces, and no work may have been included in a previous ACE juried exhibit. The rules are firm on originality: no copies, no kits, no work made in a class, and no AI-generated art. Wall-hung work must be wired with two loops and professional picture wire — sawtooth hangers and frames with triangular tabs are refused on arrival.
Entry is $35 for one piece, or $30 for ACE members, rising by $5 per additional piece up to five. Artists shipping work must include a paid return shipping label.

The submission deadline is September 4, 2026, with notification on September 11. The exhibition is shown in ACE's Eureka Gallery from September 26 to October 31, 2026, with a reception and awards during the run. Gallery hours are Thursday to Saturday, 1–5pm.

calls.title: Wellcome Photography Prize 2027
calls.description: Wellcome's biennial photography prize returns for 2027, open to everyone, everywhere, and free to enter. The prize brings photography and scientific imaging together around health and science: discovery research, mental health, infectious disease, and climate and health. There are three categories — Striking solo photography (a single photograph), A storytelling series (3–5 photographs), and The marvels of scientific and medical imaging (a single image made with a scientific or medical imaging technique). Each category winner receives £10,000, and a further 22 entries across the three categories are awarded £1,000 each; the prize draws extensive international media coverage and image makers may be invited to showcase their work at events. Eligible disciplines include documentary, clinical, studio and still-life photography, close-up photography and photomacrography, microscopy, and medical imaging such as CT, PET, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound and thermography, as well as new and emerging biomedical imaging technologies. Illustration, moving image and AI-generated images are not accepted. Images must have been taken after 31 December 2021 and submitted at print resolution. Judges weigh creativity and visual impact, storytelling and relevance, and technical excellence — the story behind an image counts as much as the image. Wellcome also publishes ethical storytelling guidelines developed with Eh!woza. Entries opened 14 July 2026; the top 25 entries and the winners are announced in summer 2027.
jury: Sumitra Upham, Associate Director of Curatorial and Public Practice, Wellcome Collection (Chair)
calls.summary: Free biennial Wellcome prize on health and science imaging. £10,000 to each of three category winners plus 22 × £1,000.

calls.title: Open Call for Emerging Artists
calls.description: Elliott Gallery in Amsterdam is shifting its open-call programme away from exhibition proposals and towards early-career photographers: recent graduates of universities and photography courses, current students, and self-taught photographers in the early stages of their careers, worldwide. The gallery is explicit that it is not looking for flawless, finished portfolios but for fresh voices, raw talent, authenticity and potential. There is no set theme; the gallery looks for a distinct perspective and a genuine passion for the medium, and accepts photography only. The prize is a personalised mentorship with the Elliott Gallery curatorial team — three 60-minute one-to-one sessions over three months covering how to refine an artistic identity and conceptual approach through intensive portfolio reviews, how to navigate the fine art market, price work, write statements and approach galleries, and how to curate work for digital and physical spaces, with the distinct potential for further collaboration such as digital exhibitions, group shows and print sales. Shortlisted artists also receive exposure across the gallery's website and social channels to its base of fine art photography collectors. Applicants submit a single public link to a folder or online portfolio plus a statement of up to 500 words, via Google Forms. Applications opened 24 July 2026 and close 9 August; the shortlist is announced 14 August and the winner on 21 August 2026. The €25 fee covers administration costs. Elliott Gallery is a physical gallery at Tussen de Bogen 91 and complies with the Gallery Fair Practice Code.

calls.title: Art Hop 2026
calls.description: Art Hop is a statewide juried exhibition run by Hill Country Arts Focus, a 501(c)(3) founded in 2007 to promote the arts in the northern Hill Country of central Texas. The 2026 edition runs the whole of October in Georgetown's historic downtown district, with selected work shown at the Georgetown Public Library and Lamppost Coffee, both just off the courthouse Square. Photography is one of six judged categories, alongside 2-D Representational, 2-D Abstract, 3-D Representational, 3-D Abstract and Digital Art; the photography category covers camera-generated photographic images. Awards run to $1,000 for Best in Show plus cash or prizes totalling almost $4,000 across the individual categories, announced at the reception ceremony. Judging happens in two rounds — online in late August, then in person before the exhibit opens, which determines placements and cash awards. Entry is $45 for up to three artworks or $55 for four or five, with a limit of five entries per artist, submitted through EntryThingy. Wall pieces including photography may be up to 48 inches on any side including the frame and must arrive ready to install with professional hardware. The call is open to any artist aged 16 or older residing in Texas.

calls.title: 110th Annual Open Juried Show
calls.description: The New Rochelle Art Association has run an annual juried show since 1912, when its first exhibition celebrated the opening of the city's new library and included work by sculptor Robert Aitken, painters G. Glenn Newell, Remington Schuyler and A.G. Heaton, and illustrators Norman Rockwell, Joseph C. Leyendecker and Victor Forsythe. The 110th edition is open to all artists 18 and over, with Photography one of the judged categories alongside Oil/Acrylic, Water Media, Graphics/Pastel, Mixed Media and Sculpture/Fine Craft. A minimum of $2,500 in cash awards is distributed across the categories. Each artist may submit up to two entries for a single fee of $35; acceptance into the show automatically brings NRAA membership. All 2-D work must be suitably framed at least 0.75 inches deep — gallery-wrapped canvas is acceptable — wired and ready to hang, with no sawtooth hooks, and must not exceed 36 × 48 inches including the outside edge of the frame. Work is hand delivered rather than shipped. The exhibition runs 28 September to 1 November 2026 in the Lumen Winter Gallery at New Rochelle Public Library, open daily with library hours, with a reception on Sunday 18 October during New Rochelle's Arts Fest.
calls.summary: Juried show running since 1912, photography a named category. $2,500+ in cash awards, at New Rochelle Public Library.

calls.title: The Art of the Automobile
calls.description: A juried show at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center in Carmichael, California, open to all art media with an automobile theme, with events around the exhibition sponsored by the United British Sports Car Club Sacramento. The judge is Kandi Thompson, a Sacramento-area watercolour painter of thirty-five years who has studied with nationally and internationally acclaimed artists, been a member of several art groups including the California Watercolor Association, and been published in Watercolor Magic and the Artists Magazine calendar. Photography is specifically accommodated: the rules exclude giclées and works made by any commercial printing process, but state the exception for photography. Work must be original, finished in the last three years, not previously shown in a juried show at Sac Arts, and available for sale, with a maximum size of 4 × 8 feet; hanging pieces must be wired with D-rings, and works over 29 × 35 inches must use plastic rather than glass. Up to three pieces per artist may be submitted at $25 each or three for $60, dropping to $20/$50 for members and $15/$40 for youth entrants. The centre retains a 50% commission on sales for non-members and 30% for members. Jury decisions are sent on 21 August, and the exhibition runs 8 September to 3 October 2026.

calls.title: Annual Show of Small Works 2026
calls.description: Parklane Gallery's Annual Winter Show of Small Works is a seasonal favourite in Kirkland, Washington, timed to the holiday shopping season so that visitors can buy work and take it home immediately rather than waiting for the show to close. Parklane is a co-operative gallery whose programme covers painting, photography, sculpture, glasswork and jewellery, and the call is open to any 2-D or 3-D artwork not previously shown at the gallery. Awards are $500 for first place, $300 for second and $250 for third, plus honourable mentions, additional special recognition awards, and separate miniature awards for pieces that meet the definition and quality of a miniature. The juror is to be announced. Hanging work must be no larger than 13 inches in height or width and 3-D work no more than 6 inches in any dimension; there is no lower size limit, and accepted pieces with an image area under 25 square inches may be shown in a separate Miniatures section. Entry is $25 plus $5 per piece for up to seven pieces per artist. The show is both hung and online: the juror chooses prizes from all accepted pieces, every accepted work goes into the online store when the show starts, and because wall space is limited some pieces hang in November and others in December. Notifications go out 28 September, accepted work is due 16 October, and the exhibition runs 4 November 2026 to 2 January 2027.

calls.title: Small Works, Big Joy 2026
calls.description: A curated show at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the power of small-format art and the craftsmanship, creativity and precision that flourish within limited dimensions. The exhibition hangs in the Eureka Gallery from 12 November to 19 December 2026 and stays open through the centre's popular Annual Holiday Artisan Fair. All media are welcome including painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, fiber, metal and textiles, so long as the work meets the size limit: no piece may exceed 12 inches in any dimension, and sculptural works must fit within a 12-inch cube. Artists are encouraged to price work under $200. Arts Center East's standing rules for juried exhibits apply — open to artists 18 and over, up to five pieces each, no work shown in a previous ACE juried exhibit, all work original with no kits and no AI-generated art, and nothing made under instruction in a class, workshop or lesson. Entry is $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising by $5 per additional piece up to five. Wall-hung work must be wired with two loops and professional picture wire; sawtooth hangers and frames with triangular tabs are refused on arrival. The centre takes a 35% commission on sales for non-members and 25% for ACE artist members.
calls.summary: Small-format show at Arts Center East, CT, open through its holiday artisan fair. Photography welcome; work under 12 inches.

calls.title: UNFOLD — Cambridge Photography Gallery
calls.description: Cambridge Photography Gallery's first annual physical exhibition, bringing together artists invited from its previous online shows alongside new voices found through this open call. Rather than setting a narrow theme, the gallery asks how your photography unfolds — as a story, a memory, a place, a relationship, an identity or a way of seeing. Some projects reveal themselves slowly while others leave questions unanswered; some look outward, others inward. Singles and series are both welcome, there is no fixed limit on how many images you may submit, and there is no right or wrong interpretation. Selected works are printed and presented as part of the group exhibition in Cambridge, UK, running 9 to 11 October 2026, and each participating artist receives a dedicated post on the gallery's Instagram and a digital certificate of participation. Submission is by email and free; a £30 participation fee applies only if your work is selected. For the selection stage files can be any size, format or orientation; selected artists are then asked for high-resolution files suitable for printing, around 300 ppi and at least 3000 pixels on the longest side.
calls.summary: Cambridge Photography Gallery's first physical show asks how your work unfolds. Free to enter; £30 only if selected.

calls.title: HALFTONE Print Fair 2026
calls.fee: €10 (free for International Centre for the Image members)
calls.description: The 12th edition of HALFTONE, PhotoIreland's annual print fair at The Library Project in Dublin's Temple Bar, running 28 November 2026 to 24 January 2027. Works are displayed salon-style and sold both at the venue and online at thelibraryproject.ie; the fair has raised almost €100,000 for artists since 2015 and supported the practice of over 800 participating artists, with sales to private, corporate and public collections. Applications are open to fine art printers, illustrators, designers, photographers and all visual artists and creatives, for works produced from 2024 onwards using any print technique — screenprint, stencil, risography, lithography, etching, inkjet printing and more — without any limitation of approach or concept. Submissions may include up to 10 artworks, with two images per work: the print itself and a photograph or mock-up showing it framed or mounted as it would be displayed. All submitted works must be available for sale. The gallery takes a 40% commission, which should be built into the price you submit, and artists invoice for the remaining 60% after the fair; PhotoIreland adds 13.5% VAT on top of the submitted price. Selected artists are contacted by 2 November 2026 and deliver work between 3 and 15 November, with unsold work collected 25 to 31 January 2027.

calls.title: 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative
calls.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme buys artwork outright for publicly accessible buildings across the state — amphitheatres, community centres, courthouses, educational institutions, fire stations, healthcare facilities, libraries, recreation complexes, rest areas and senior centres among them. The 2026 Southwest Artists Series Purchase Initiative aims to diversify the state collection by purchasing work from artists at every stage of their careers, and all media in all genres are considered; New Mexico Arts names photography explicitly among the mediums it accepts, alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, mosaic, graphic arts, etching, lithography, silkscreen, textile, fibre, wood, metal, glass, mixed media, collage and assemblage. Work must be durable, permanent, low-maintenance and compliant with ADA guidelines once installed, and suitable for interior or exterior display. The programme seeks artwork in the $5,000–$50,000 range, and the price must be all-inclusive: materials, labour, museum-quality framing under Plexiglas, security hangers, delivery, installation, insurance, taxes, commissions and both written and professional photographic documentation of the work. Since its inception in 1986 AIPP has placed more than 3,000 works of art across all 33 New Mexico counties, amounting to over $21 million paid directly to artists. Open to artists who reside in New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, Colorado, Oklahoma or Texas, and to galleries located in those states, which may submit on behalf of any artist they represent regardless of that artist's residency. A statewide Submission Review Committee of artists, arts professionals and community leaders scores applications, and the selected pool is then shown to local committees for purchase consideration.
calls.summary: New Mexico's public art programme buys work outright for state buildings, $5,000–$50,000. Free; Southwest US artists.

calls.title: FIGURES Mentorship & Dummy Book Program 2026/2027
calls.description: FIGURES, the Slow & Contemporary Photography platform behind the FIG001 book, is running its mentorship and dummy book programme for a second year, and is looking specifically for projects at the very earliest stage of creation — you do not need to show a single finished picture of the project to apply, and projects that are already too advanced will not be considered. Program winners get twelve monthly 1.5-hour one-to-one online sessions with founder and editor-in-chief Nicolas Blanchadell, covering every phase from deepening the initial concept through production, picture editing and sequencing; a renowned guest artist/curator joins for one mid-programme session, and a professional art-book graphic designer steps in at the end to finalise the cover and the more demanding pages. Each winner leaves with a printed dummy book plus the ready-to-print PDF and all supporting material. The number of selections scales with entries: for every 150 valid submissions FIGURES picks one program winner plus ten further projects for a one-hour individual review. All photographic practices are welcome — documentary, portrait, street, experimental, fashion — as are mixed-media projects where photography is central to the process or makes up at least half the final work. Entry is €10, or free with the discounted purchase of the FIG001 issue at €25; no further fees are asked of selected artists, and applicants facing financial hardship are invited to write to FIGURES directly. If fewer than 150 valid applications arrive, the programme is cancelled and €10 entrants are refunded in full.
calls.summary: A year of monthly one-to-one mentoring with FIGURES' editor, a guest curator and a book designer, ending in a printed photobook dummy.

calls.title: New Mexico Blue Bus Shelter Art
calls.description: New Mexico Arts' Art in Public Places programme, working with the North Central Regional Transit District's Art in Transit programme, is commissioning artists to create digital artwork to be printed onto perforated steel panels at three Blue Bus shelters in Taos, Española and Santa Fe. Selected artists create an original work — or digitise existing non-digital work — to fit a two- or three-panel shelter, each panel roughly 53 by 77 inches; all printing and installation is handled by NCRTD. The organisers ask for artwork that speaks to the local culture and community: cultural homelands, local languages, landscapes and agricultural practices, the diversity of lifeways, traditions and landmarks, and the artist's own lived experience and connection to the area. This is a request for qualifications, not a proposal call — do not make new work for it; submit up to ten images of completed artwork that demonstrate your style and technique, ideally digital work or work with local themes, plus an artist statement and answers on your transportation story and your connection to Northern New Mexico. Artists are paid $5,000 per completed artwork, inclusive of all fees and expenses. Entry is free. Open to all artists working in New Mexico, with preference given to those living in or with strong ties to Taos, Rio Arriba and Santa Fe counties; employees and family of employees of NMDCA or NCRTD are excluded. Selection is by the Art in Transit Committee, drawn from representatives across Northern New Mexico including Rio Arriba, Santa Fe, Taos and Los Alamos counties, Ohkay Owingeh and Taos Pueblo.

calls.title: Louvre Unbound Magazine — Celebration Edition
calls.description: A one-off anniversary edition marking Louvre Unbound's first year, published alongside an international event in Spain held with Luka Gallery for the inauguration of the gallery's new space inside the Castillo de Santiago, expected to draw 300–400 invited guests including curators, collectors, European press and cultural professionals. Selected artists are published in the Celebration Edition and also receive a two-month virtual exhibition, two months of promotion across the magazine's social channels, worldwide digital publication, global print-on-demand distribution via Peecho and Lulu, and a place on the printed event flyers handed to guests throughout the celebration. Submissions are open to visual artists worldwide working in any medium, photography included; submit up to four artworks through the magazine's Google Form. Submitting is free — participation fees apply only on acceptance, and for this edition alone they are quoted in euros: €89 for returning artists and €115 for new artists, covering a four-page featured-artist spread with one artwork per page plus contact links. Louvre Unbound states it is a non-profit platform and that the fee supports editorial work, design, printing and distribution. The edition will only be published if a minimum number of participating artists is reached; if it is cancelled, all registered artists are refunded in full.
calls.summary: Louvre Unbound's first-anniversary edition, launched at a Spanish castle gallery event. Free to enter; €89–€115 only if selected.

calls.title: Photobooks in Dialogue
calls.description: Centrum för fotografi (CFF), Sweden's member organisation for photographers, is calling for photobooks and zines for an exhibition in Gothenburg staged with Fotobok Gbg as part of Fotobok Fest. The curators are looking for photo-based publications in which dialogue, collaboration or exchange are central: an exchange of ideas between two photographers, between an artist and an archive, between image and text, or the close interplay of artist, designer and publisher. They describe it as a ping-pong match, where ideas bounce from one side to the other in fine balance without ever falling off the table — books and zines where the exchange between several voices is fundamental and has shaped the work from the ground up. The exhibition runs 25–27 September 2026 at the CFF gallery on Bangatan 10 in Gothenburg, with support from the City of Gothenburg and the Swedish Photographers' Association. Publications from anywhere in the world are welcome, but shipping to Sweden is at the applicant's own cost; books must arrive by 22 September. Applications are free and consist of a single PDF of no more than 10 MB containing a CV of up to two pages, a presentation of the publication of up to 300 words in Swedish or English, and 10–15 pages from the book. Selected participants are notified at the end of August. After the exhibition you can either donate your publication to the Hasselblad Foundation Library in Gothenburg or have it returned at CFF's expense.
calls.summary: CFF and Fotobok Gbg seek photobooks built on dialogue and exchange, for a Gothenburg exhibition. Free, open worldwide.

calls.title: Thin Air Magazine Issue 33 — The Oasis
calls.description: Thin Air is a print literary and arts magazine produced by graduate students in the MFA programme at Northern Arizona University in Flagstaff, and it is reading visual art for its 33rd print issue, themed 'The Oasis'. The editors take the dictionary definition — a fertile green area in an arid region; something that provides refuge, relief or pleasant contrast — and push at it: in a turbulent and at times desolate world, what is your oasis, where do you seek shelter, and what spaces sustain you? They are equally interested in the conditions that produce an oasis, since one can only exist when surrounded by a severe lack of something crucial to survival — so what is your desert, and what drives you to look for relief? The call also asks whether an oasis can be a form of resistance, thinking of the sanctuaries that form in the midst of violence, fear and escalating political tension. For this issue the editors are specifically looking for art, photography and comics that represent the notion of the oasis, with an interest in pieces that work as full-page spreads as well as graphic narratives and poetry comics; outsider art is always welcome, as is anything that surprises or subverts expectations. Colour submissions are open, with particular interest in high-contrast pieces that capture the shades and hues of the oasis. Photographers may send up to five pieces at a minimum of 300dpi with a short description of each work and a two to five sentence bio. Submitting visual art is free — the written-genre categories carry a $3 reading fee that visual art does not — and only unpublished work is considered, though simultaneous submissions are encouraged. Reading begins in August each year and runs until the deadline. One restriction to note: Thin Air does not accept work from anyone affiliated with Northern Arizona University within the last seven years.
calls.summary: NAU's student-run print magazine reads photography for its 33rd issue on refuge and scarcity. Free for visual art.

calls.title: Rawhead Issue 04 — Visual Art
calls.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of art and literature named after one of the folkloric bogeymen used to frighten children into obedience — a deliberate choice, since the editors read monsters as mirrors that force us to confront realities more disturbing than whatever lurks in the dark, and read art as a form of resistance. It is not a horror publication, but it is interested in work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft and surprising clarity. Rawhead is open for its fourth issue across poetry, visual art, fiction, creative nonfiction and hybrid work; submissions considered for Issue 04 may also be held for Issue 05. The visual art category takes three to ten pieces in any medium, explicitly including photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture, uploaded as high-quality images of at least 1500px. The art editor is looking for work that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty — not horror or gore, but work that dances along the edges of heightened emotion, citing Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Each issue Rawhead selects at least one outstanding artist and one standout writer for its Editor's Spotlight, a $100 award; every accepted piece is considered. Submission is free and the journal states it is fully committed to always offering free submissions, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that have no bearing on editorial decisions. Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and AI-generated content is not.

calls.title: Windows on the World
calls.description: Click! Photography Festival turns downtown Raleigh into a month-long photography city every October, spreading exhibitions, talks and screenings across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Windows on the World is its storefront show: selected photographs are printed by the festival and installed in and around the shop windows of City Market, the historic brick market district in downtown Raleigh, so the work is met by people walking past rather than by gallery visitors. The theme is JOY, and the call asks what joy looks like to you — a fleeting smile, a quiet landscape, a family celebration, an unexpected encounter, a moment of personal triumph. All genres are welcome, from documentary and street photography to portraits, landscapes, abstract and experimental imagery, and all photographic processes are accepted: alternative, film or digital. The call is open to photographers of all levels, from emerging talents to seasoned professionals, and international submissions are accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images. Artists do not ship work: everything selected is printed and displayed by the festival, with the possibility of a projection event on First Friday. The exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026 with an opening reception on Friday 2 October, and images not selected for the outdoor Plein Air exhibition are eligible for a travelling slide show presented around the Triangle through October. AI-generated images are not eligible.
calls.summary: Click! Festival prints and installs selected photographs in City Market shop windows, Raleigh. Theme: JOY. $45 for five images.

calls.title: Click! Plein Air
calls.description: Click! Plein Air is the flagship outdoor exhibition of the Click! Photography Festival, the month-long October festival spread across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill in North Carolina. For 2026 it moves from Moore Square, where the 2025 edition showed 35 photographers, to Dix Park — the 300-acre former state hospital campus that is now Raleigh's largest public park — where photographs are shown in the open air rather than on gallery walls. There is no set theme: photographers submit into open categories, and the festival is looking for striking, engaging work that holds up in front of a broad public audience outdoors. The festival's own page lists seven — abstract, documentary, landscape, people, creatures, street photography and still life — while the Smarter Entry form shows six, with portrait in place of people and creatures, so check the list when you upload. The call is open to photographers of all levels and to all photographic processes, alternative, film or digital, with international submissions accepted. Entry is $45 for up to five images, each of which must be titled. The juror is Jerome De Perlinghi. Jury selections are made by 6 September, the exhibition runs 1–31 October 2026, and the opening reception is on First Friday, 2 October. Images not selected for the outdoor exhibition remain eligible for a travelling slide show presented at venues throughout the Triangle during October.
calls.summary: Open-air photography exhibition at Dix Park, Raleigh, juried by Jerome De Perlinghi. No set theme, open categories, $45 for five images.

calls.title: SELF PORTRAITS 2026
calls.fee: £13 for 1 image, £6 each additional (£20 per print if selected)
calls.description: Matt Ford Studio is a photographer-run gallery and studio in Hackney Downs Studios, east London, whose programme leans toward sexuality, gender, identity and fashion. SELF PORTRAITS 2026 is its winter open call, exhibition and photo book, put together by Matt Ford after he began making self-portraits as a way of working through his own fears about AI, politics and the future of an artistic career, and became interested in self-portraiture itself — as vanity, as creativity, as self-expression, or simply as a record of where you are in your life. The call invites photographers worldwide to reflect on what it means to be human in the second quarter of the 21st century. Anyone 18 or over from any country may enter, at any level of skill, and both digital and analogue work is welcome — disposable cameras, phones and high-end DSLRs alike — along with collage and experimental work that still involves some element of self-portrait. Digitally enhanced images are accepted; AI-generated images are not. Judging for finalists and winners is done by the editors of ZERO.NINE Magazine. The winner receives £500 cash, the cover of the SELF PORTRAITS photo book, an 'On The Radar' feature in ZERO.NINE and a feature about their work; all semi-finalists appear in the photo book at no extra cost, and finalists are shown in the exhibition at the studio. Entry is £13 for the first photograph and £6 for each one after; if you reach the exhibition a further £20 per photograph shown covers printing (arranged with theprintspace) and exhibition admin, or you may send your own print at your own postage cost. Semi-finalists are announced 9 November, the book launch, private view and winners announcement is 10 December, and the exhibition is open to the public 11–14 December 2026. Work is for sale during the show, with 75% to the artist.
calls.summary: Photographer-run east London gallery's self-portrait show and photo book, judged by ZERO.NINE Magazine. £500 to the winner.

calls.title: Liquida Winter Edition 2026 — Single Photo
calls.description: Liquida Photofestival is the photography strand of Paratissima, the independent contemporary art event that has run in Turin since 2005 and is now one of the anchors of Turin Art Week. Its Winter Edition is the autumn spin-off of the main April festival, curated by Liquida's artistic director Laura Tota — an independent curator who has worked on Paratissima's photography programme since 2017 and is Exhibition Coordinator at PhEST, Photolux and Cortona On The Move. Single Photo is a new section for 2026: rather than a project, it asks for individual frames. Each entrant may submit between one and five photographs, which need not belong to the same body of work or even to the same line of research, and there is no set theme — the point is to leave photographers the widest possible margin of expression. Ten winning shots are chosen and shown as a collective exhibition inside the Liquida Winter Edition section, with each selected image coming from a different artist. The €25 participation fee is the only cost: Paratissima covers production, transport, shipping, installation and de-installation of the selected works, and the fee also includes the exhibition layout, wall captions, inclusion in the official ISBN catalogue, an artist badge and support for online and on-site sales. The catalogue itself is optional at €20 a copy. The festival runs 30 October – 1 November 2026 at the Real Collegio Carlo Alberto in Moncalieri, just outside Turin; the 2025 edition drew more than 20,000 visitors. Results are announced 12 September. Note that Liquida's separate Exhibition call, for full projects, works on a paid-wall-space model and is not this call.
jury: Laura Tota, Artistic Director, Liquida Photofestival

calls.title: The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins
calls.description: PhotoSC is a non-profit photography gallery in Columbia, South Carolina, built around a continuing dialogue about photography and the photographic canon. Marking photography's 200 years of experimentation, The Alternative Aesthetic: Chance at the Margins goes looking for the accident and the sleight of hand — the idea that chance has sat at the heart of photographic and scientific discovery from the very beginning, and that the non-traditional method has always been the alternative to the cultural order of photography. The call seeks historical techniques, photosensitive chemicals and unusual materials, and the textures, colours and effects that are impossible with standard digital or silver gelatin work; experimentation is explicitly encouraged. The juror is Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief of Analog Forever Magazine, founding editor of Catalyst: Interviews, an ongoing juror for Photolucida's Critical Mass and a former board member of APA/LA. Photographers may submit up to five works for $35, with submissions open from 5 August to 13 September 2026 and accepted artists notified by 4 October. Accepted work must be printed no smaller than 8×10 inches and no larger than 16×20, framed and ready to hang, and delivered by the 23 October receipt-of-work date on the call timeline (a line of prose lower down the same page still says 30 September, which predates the 4 October notification). The exhibition opens 29 October at 918 Lady Street, Columbia, with a reception the same evening, and hangs until 29 November 2026. Sales are encouraged at a 40/60 gallery/artist split; photographers retain copyright. No AI-generated imagery is accepted.
jury: Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief, Analog Forever Magazine

calls.title: The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers 2026
calls.description: The National Emerging Art Prize was founded in 2021 to give Australia's most promising emerging visual artists a national platform, and in 2025 it expanded into contemporary photography with a dedicated category — The Seed Prize for Emerging Photographers, sponsored by Seed Funds Management, now in its second year. The winner receives a $10,000 acquisitive cash prize, a solo exhibition at The Garden Gallery presented by Michael Reid Northern Beaches in 2027, and mentoring sessions with NEAP curator Amber Creswell Bell and the Michael Reid directors. NEAP is curated by Amber Creswell Bell, a writer and curator known for championing emerging Australian artists across a run of best-selling books on Australian art; she sits on the selection panel and works with the selected artists to curate the finalists' exhibition. The 2026 panel includes artists Tom Polo and Tamara Dean, Head On Photo Festival founder Moshe Rosenzveig OAM, Belle editor-in-chief Tanya Buchanan, Good Weekend senior writer Katrina Strickland, Decus founder Alexandra Donohoe Church, and collectors Edwina Bartholomew and Nicole Redden. There is no theme. The category is open to film and digital photographs presented as still, two-dimensional works, completed in 2025 or 2026. Prints must be at least 20cm square and no larger than 100cm on the longest side, editioned no higher than 15 (8 + 2AP recommended), and priced no higher than $3,000 unframed; finalists send work in tubes and it is exhibited unframed, pinned directly to the gallery wall, with NEAP retaining 50% of any sale. Artists must reside primarily in Australia and count as emerging — that is, not represented by a major commercial gallery; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists are encouraged to apply. There is no limit on entries per artist, but each work is submitted separately at $35. Finalists are announced 1 October and exhibited 29 October to 11 November 2026 at The Garden Gallery in Sydney's Royal Botanic Garden, with all work for sale.

Edwina Bartholomew, Art Collector & Television Presenter, Sunrise
Nicole Redden, Curator, Morgans Financial Collection

calls.title: Living Image 2026/2027
calls.description: The Halide Project is a nonprofit darkroom and gallery on North 2nd Street in Philadelphia, and Living Image is its annual juried exhibition of traditional and historic photographic processes — the show it builds its year around. The 2026/27 edition is juried by Amanda Smith, who founded A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas fifteen years ago and has run more than 200 juried and curated exhibitions there, alongside jury work for All About Photo, Analogue Forever, Dodho, Texas Photographic Society, the International Photography Hall of Fame and Critical Mass. Selected work hangs at The Halide Project gallery from 5 December 2026 to 17 January 2027 and is published in a printed catalogue; every selected artist receives a copy. One Grand Prize winner takes $250 and a slot to show a body of work in The Halide Project's annual Spring Invitational, with further sponsored prizes announced later. The medium gate is strict and specific: work must be made using traditional, pre-digital photographic printing — silver gelatin, c-prints, instant film, platinum/palladium, cyanotype, gum bichromate, wet plate collodion and other alternative and historic processes. Analog prints made from digital negatives are eligible; inkjet prints and digital c-prints are not, even if shot on film. Open to artists 18 or older in any country. Entry is $40 for up to three works and $10 for each additional, to a maximum of ten, with a $5 discount off the total for members. Accepted work must arrive framed and wired to professional standards by 7 November and must not exceed 30 inches in any dimension including the frame; artists cover shipping both ways, and the gallery retains a 25% commission on sales.
jury: Amanda Smith, Founder & Co-director, A Smith Gallery
