calls.title: INSIDE / OUTSIDE
calls.description: Second Street Gallery, founded in 1973 and the oldest nonprofit contemporary art space in Central Virginia, is running a juried regional exhibition for artists living and working in the Commonwealth of Virginia. INSIDE / OUTSIDE asks for work that sits on the line between interior and exterior worlds — home and environment, personal space and public life, private memory and shared history. The gallery invites broad interpretation: Virginia's natural landscape, the built environment, domestic interiors, social and cultural histories, or the psychological boundaries between inside and out. The juror is Kristen Chiacchia, Second Street's Executive Director and Chief Curator, an art historian whose curatorial practice centres on gender bias in the contemporary art market and on artists' ties to subcultural movements; she has curated more than 67 solo shows and 34 group exhibitions at the gallery and published nine catalogues. First place takes $300 plus a solo exhibition in the gallery's Dové space from 2 June to 21 July 2028; second is $200 and third is $100, with up to three honourable mentions at the juror's discretion. Accepted media are painting, works on paper, sculpture, photography and mixed media — no video, installation, performance, sound or AI-generated work. Work must have been made in the last three years and must not have been shown in Charlottesville in the preceding year. Applications open 15 August 2026 and close 15 November; artists are notified 15 January 2027, work is delivered in May, and the show runs 4 June to 16 July 2027 with a First Friday opening. All exhibited work must be available for purchase and the gallery retains a 50% commission.
jury: Kristen Chiacchia, Executive Director & Chief Curator, Second Street Gallery

calls.title: RED — Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Red tape, red flag, seeing red, painting the town red — the Lawrence Arts Center wants to know what it means to represent the colour red, and leaves the reading entirely to the artist. The theme can be taken as intense emotion or as warning, or turned toward flowers, birds and hearts; the call explicitly encourages both established and emerging artists. Submissions are open to any medium within the size limit, which is 24 inches in any direction including frame, and selected work is not required to be for sale. The juror is Travis Millard, the artist, musician and founder of Fudge Factory Comics, with twenty years of self-published zines and gallery shows behind him and illustration work for Playboy, The Hollywood Reporter, Mad, Wired and record covers for Dinosaur Jr and Kurt Vile. Prizes are $1,000 for first, $500 for second and $250 for third. The Arts Center is a long-running nonprofit in downtown Lawrence, Kansas, with three exhibition galleries, a 300-seat theatre and seven visual arts studios. Entries go through the SlideRoom portal, which opened 1 August and closes 25 September; a maximum of three original works may be entered for $25, one JPEG per piece under 5MB. AI artwork is not permissible. Notifications go out between 5 and 9 October, work is delivered 10–21 October, the opening reception and awards are on 30 October, and the show closes 12 December 2026.
jury: Travis Millard, Artist & Founder, Fudge Factory Comics
calls.summary: Open-medium juried show on the colour red at a Kansas nonprofit arts centre. $1,000 top prize, juror Travis Millard.

calls.title: Remember You Must Live: On Life, Loss, and Impermanence
calls.description: Guilford Art Center — a nonprofit school, gallery and shop on the Connecticut shoreline, whose gallery shows contemporary American art and craft year-round and free to the public — is assembling a memento mori show for its October slot. Remember You Must Live asks artists to sit with an inevitable phase of life rather than sensationalise it: not fear or spectacle, but cycles, transitions and the preciousness of what is here. The call is open to artists in Connecticut and the wider New England region, working in all physical mediums, and there is no entry fee. Each artist submits two works that respond to the theme, emailed with the completed submission form to the Center's exhibitions coordinator by 30 August; the in-house exhibitions team notifies artists of their status by Sunday 13 September. Accepted work is received 4 and 5 October, the exhibition runs 9 to 30 October 2026 with an opening reception on 10 October, and pick-up is 31 October to 1 November. Work must arrive in exhibition condition with identifying paperwork, and anything not for sale must be marked NFS with a stated insurance value. Guilford Art Center retains a 40% commission on sales, with cheques mailed within thirty days of the close of the show, and insures exhibited work for 50% of the artist's stated retail value against fire, theft and breakage from receiving to removal.
calls.summary: Free memento mori group show on the Connecticut shoreline, open to New England artists in all physical mediums.

calls.title: SATURATION
calls.description: projectART is a 501(c)(3) arts education nonprofit in Wimberley, Texas, running youth programmes, artist mentorships and a gallery — ARTSPACE on River Road — for rural Central Texas. SATURATION is its next group exhibition, a show about vivid colour, visual intensity and the idea of fullness. The call wants bold palettes, rich surfaces and immersive compositions, but equally work that treats saturation as a concept: abundance, excess, density, emotion, sensory overload. It also invites readings of saturation as a social, psychological, cultural or environmental condition — information overload, consumerism, identity, memory, being engulfed by a feeling, the point at which intensity transforms perception. All visual art media are welcome and submission is free. The exhibition opens with a reception on 9 October 2026 and stays on view at ARTSPACE through 9 January 2027, a three-month run.
calls.summary: Free open call on colour, excess and sensory overload for a three-month show at a Central Texas nonprofit gallery.

calls.title: Call for Solo Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: The St. Louis Artists' Guild has been showing regional work since 1886 and runs a free gallery on North Jackson Avenue in Clayton, just west of the city. Its open call for proposals is for solo exhibitions, from emerging and established artists alike, working in all media — a rare thing to find with no submission fee attached. Selected artists show in either the Guild's curated gallery or its ramp gallery; floor plans for both are published alongside the call so proposals can be pitched to the space. Applicants must live within a 150-mile radius of St. Louis, be 18 or older, and have a website of their own (Instagram and Facebook pages do not count). One proposal per artist. Two or more artists may collaborate on a proposal or pitch a group exhibition, but it must be submitted under a single name. Anyone who has already had a solo exhibition at the Guild must wait five years before showing again. Proposals go in through the Guild's Google Form by midnight on 5 September 2026.
calls.summary: Free solo-show proposals at a St. Louis guild running since 1886. All media, 150-mile radius, curated or ramp gallery.

calls.title: 2027 Galleries Call for Artists
calls.description: The City of San Ramon, 35 miles east of San Francisco, programmes five gallery spaces and this call fills their month-long exhibition slots for the whole of 2027. The venues vary in scale and in what they can take: the Dougherty Station Community Arts Center hangs 30-plus pieces across up to 115 linear feet of 2D and 3D; the Lindsay Dirkx Brown Gallery takes 25 to 30 pieces over 100 linear feet, also 2D and 3D; San Ramon City Hall holds 30-plus 2D pieces across 125 linear feet; the Alcosta Senior & Community Center takes 20 to 25 2D pieces; and the San Ramon Library shows 10 to 15. The city says the programme is deliberately open to artists at any age and any stage, and accepts both solo and group proposals, so long as the applicant has a body of at least ten completed works. Accepted media are two-dimensional or three-dimensional work with the sole exception of film, so photography qualifies; AI-generated work does not, work already shown in a San Ramon gallery in 2025 or 2026 cannot be repeated, and the city bars nudity, violence and what it calls otherwise inappropriate imagery or themes. There is no application fee — selected artists pay a $50 exhibition fee, due 30 November. Applications are made through CaFE with five image samples, an artist statement and a resume; the portal window runs 10 August to 27 September. The Arts Advisory Committee reviews on 21 October and notifications go out 2 November. Work may be sold during the run, with a 20% sales commission payable to the city.
calls.summary: Free application for a month-long 2027 show in one of five Bay Area civic galleries. $50 exhibition fee only if selected.

calls.title: International Mute Photo Festival 2027 — Nature Ate the Pixels
calls.description: Photonisos Arts & Culture, the Samos non-profit behind the East End – Samos Arts Festival, is launching the first International Mute Photo Festival with a single, uncompromising rule: every photograph must be captured and printed on a children's instant thermal camera — the cheap toy that spits low-resolution black-and-white images onto thermal paper. The festival frames this as a deliberate subversion, taking Guy Debord's warning about a world replaced by its own images and answering it with a medium too coarse to flatter anything. The theme, Nature Ate the Pixels, asks for work in which human presence sits inside the natural world rather than above it, split across four categories: Landscape (nature with no human trace), Symbiosis (the body meeting water, earth and flora), Rebirth (nature reclaiming the cityscape) and Future (children discovering the natural world). Post-processing is almost entirely forbidden — you may crop the printed timestamp and white borders and convert to black and white, and nothing else; the lines, marks and noise of the thermal print are treated as the work's core identity, not as faults. Entrants submit high-resolution scans of their original prints, and the jury may ask to see the physical strips to verify the medium. Fifteen adult series and five from the under-18 category are selected, printed and enlarged entirely at the festival's expense, published in a printed catalogue, and shown in July 2027 at the renovated Old Customs Warehouses at Karlovasi Port on Samos. The artist behind the most complete series gets travel and accommodation covered for the opening. Entry is free, and artists retain full copyright. calls.title: Food: Ritual and Identity
calls.fee: CA$10 per work (CA$20 more if selected)
calls.description: The artist-run ArtPod on southern Vancouver Island closes its 2026 season with a show about what feeds us. Food is never just food, the curators write — it is material, metaphor, ritual and resource, and it feeds identities, cultures, economies and memories as much as bodies. The call asks for work that traces the visible and invisible systems that sustain or exploit us, from harvest to hunger and feast to waste, and treats food as personal, political, ecological and sensual at once. The guiding question is what it means to be nourished in a time of both abundance and imbalance. The curatorial team is Anna Mar, Pierrette Vezina and Cindy McMath, with Janice Beaudoin jurying. Photography is explicitly welcome under the ArtPod's standing submission guidelines: limited-edition photographs and prints, including giclée, inkjet and archival prints, are accepted in editions of 25 or fewer, and photographs must be taken by the artist and may not reproduce another artist's work. On AI the ArtPod says it is still reflecting, but requires submitted work to represent the artist's own creative vision and authorship. Jurying is blind — the juror sees only the image, the medium and substrate, and an artist statement capped at 1,000 characters. Artists may submit up to three original works; diptychs, triptychs and small series count as one work if shown in a single photograph. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 7 feet high by 5 feet wide. Work must not have been shown in a juried exhibition or commercial gallery on southern Vancouver Island in the past year. Submission is CA$10 per artwork with a further CA$20 hanging fee per accepted work; the ArtPod takes 30% commission and all work must be for sale. The call runs 12 August to 9 October with results on 12 October, and the exhibition runs 23 October to 20 December 2026 with an opening gala on 24 October, 2–4 pm.
calls.ai: Must be the artist's own authorship
calls.summary: Blind-juried show on food as ritual, memory and system at an artist-run Vancouver Island gallery. Photo editions of 25 or fewer accepted.

calls.title: Truth in Art: A Juried Opportunity for MFA Students
calls.description: The Steffen Thomas Museum of Art is a single-artist museum — one of only fourteen in the United States by its own count — built around the work of German-born American painter and sculptor Steffen Thomas. Through its College Connections programme the museum runs this free juried exhibition for MFA students, and the point is as much the apprenticeship as the wall space: selected students work alongside museum mentors on curating, loan forms and condition reports, art installation, exhibition promotion and public speaking, so the show doubles as a first practical education in how a museum actually mounts an exhibition. The top three Best in Show selections receive a monetary award. Entry is free. Submissions close 29 August 2026 and the exhibition runs 26 September to 21 November 2026 in the museum's West Gallery in Buckhead, Georgia, in Morgan County about ten minutes from historic Madison.
calls.summary: Free juried museum show for MFA students, with mentoring in curating and installation and cash awards for the top three.

calls.title: PLAYFUL
calls.description: Arc is a mixed-use art centre on Folsom Street in San Francisco's South of Market district, founded in 2010 by four artist partners and running three galleries alongside ten artist studios. Its 2027 national juried call opens with Claes Oldenburg — "I am for the art of the underwear and the art of taxicabs" — and asks for work that embodies the playful spirit: light-hearted, lively, spontaneous, full of fun, amusement and wit. That can arrive as bright colour, whimsical typography, funny imagery or sly innuendo, and the gallery specifically names spontaneous street photography alongside interactive works that invite audience participation and works that hold on to child-like wonder and game-play. Photography is one of the accepted categories; jewellery, video, film, performance, installation and anything needing an external power source are not. The juror is Jennifer Farris, who has run STUDIO Gallery in San Francisco with her husband, artist Rab Terry, for over two decades. Three works chosen by the juror for the most imaginative reading of the theme receive a $250 check, a juror's award ribbon, a recognition certificate and the show catalogue; every selected work, gallery and online alike, appears in that catalogue. Entry is $35 for one to three images, with a maximum of two entries per artist, and the call is open to artists residing in the United States. Two-dimensional work is capped at 60 by 40 inches including frame, and accepted work must arrive ready to hang with plexi rather than glass. Submissions close 29 March 2027, notifications go out 16 April, and the exhibition runs 19 June to 17 July 2027 at 1246 Folsom Street.
calls.summary: National juried show on playfulness at an artist-run SF gallery; street photography named, three $250 awards, catalogue for all selected.

calls.title: Collectives' Hub 2026
calls.fee: Free (£150 group registration + £130 production contribution if selected)
calls.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led registered charity in Brighton that has run a biennial open-platform photography festival since 2003. The Collectives' Hub has been part of the festival since 2014 and is consistently one of its most visited and critically discussed exhibitions; for the twelfth edition, up to eight photography or lens-based collectives will be selected to build their own shows inside the main gallery at Phoenix Art Space, on view 2 October to 22 November 2026. Work should respond to Future Histories, the theme curating the Main Gallery this year — an invitation to consider how the past keeps configuring and sometimes overshadowing the present, and how what we do now is already writing tomorrow's history. Collectives interpret that freely. A collective needs at least three people, with no upper limit; spaces run between 3.5 and 5 metres wide and are allocated by Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco and Phoenix curator Laurence Hill. Work can be wall-hung or freestanding, collectives install and de-install themselves with a Photo Fringe technician on hand, and every selected group also makes an online exhibition on photofringe.org. Entry is free: apply by emailing up to 200 words on the proposed exhibition, up to 200 words on the collective, up to 12 JPEGs and a website or Instagram link — video applications in BSL or English and audio applications of up to three minutes are equally welcome. If selected, each collective pays the subsidised Photo Fringe 2026 group registration fee of £150 plus £130 towards production by 2 September, produces its own exhibition, and covers travel and transport; Phoenix Art Space takes 35% commission on sales. Submissions close 11.59pm on Sunday 9 August 2026 and shortlisted collectives hear back on 26 August.
jury: Lucy Day, Executive and Artistic Director, Phoenix Art Space
Laurence Hill, Curator, Phoenix Art Space
Ricardo Reverón Blanco, Producer, Photo Fringe
Rebecca Drew, Chair of the Photo Fringe Board of Trustees
calls.summary: Up to eight lens-based collectives show on the theme Future Histories at Phoenix Art Space during Brighton's Photo Fringe.

calls.title: Newhaven Open 26
calls.fee: Free (£125 solo / £150 group registration + £100 exhibition contribution if selected)
calls.description: A new open exhibition from Photo Fringe, the volunteer-led Brighton charity behind the biennial open-platform photography festival, staged on the top floor of BN9 Marine Workshops in Newhaven — a working-waterfront studio space run by Towner with Newhaven Enterprise Zone and Lewes District Council, with almost 200 square metres of hanging space. Ten solo or group exhibitions will be selected, running 2 to 31 October 2026 alongside the rest of the festival. Work should respond to the 2026 festival theme Feedback Loop, which asks artists to treat photography less as a static record than as part of a continuous exchange: conversations between communities and landscapes, stories circulating across generations, ecological cycles, industrial systems, acts of collaboration, the shifting relationship between artists and audiences. It should also connect meaningfully to Marine Workshops, Newhaven or its communities — the call is open to photographers and lens-based artists in any medium, including installation, moving image, sound and expanded photographic practice, and site-responsive proposals for new or existing work are both welcome. Collectives may apply. Apply free by email with up to 300 words on the proposal, up to 12 JPEGs or a screener link, and a website or Instagram link; BSL, English audio and video applications are accepted. One exhibiting artist receives a jury award of mentorship with Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco plus an in-depth interview published on the festival site. Selected artists install and de-install their own work with team support, invigilate for at least a day, and pay the subsidised registration fee of £125 solo or £150 group plus a £100 contribution towards exhibition costs by 2 September; Photo Fringe takes 35% commission on sales to cover staffing. Entries close 11.59pm on Sunday 23 August 2026, with notifications on 28 August.
jury: Ricardo Reverón Blanco, Producer, Photo Fringe
Rebecca Drew, Chair of the Photo Fringe Board of Trustees
calls.summary: Ten solo or group shows on the theme Feedback Loop at a Newhaven waterfront studio space, free to enter, with a mentorship award.

calls.title: Medium Gallery Open Call 2027
calls.description: Medium Gallery was founded on 8 January 1991 as part of the Academy of Fine Arts and Design in Bratislava, and its programme spans every form of contemporary art the school teaches — photography, painting, intermedia, graphic design, sculpture, applied arts, architecture, design, restoration, textiles and visual communication. For 2027 it is again inviting exhibition projects from students of art fields, beginning and established artists, and curatorial projects, from Slovakia and abroad; the gallery board deliberately balances student presentations against shows by established local and international artists. The 173-square-metre space can be partitioned, a practice begun by former gallery head Jana Kapelová in 2018, so applicants choose one of three configurations: SMALL, the back room, best for compact solo shows; MEDIUM, the two front rooms, for a solo or smaller group show; or LARGE, the whole gallery. Proposals are assessed by a five-person board of three school representatives, the gallery manager and one external member. The gallery covers the space and its running costs, invigilation, technical equipment, plinths and basic installation supplies, transport of works by agreement, graphic design and a print run of posters in the gallery's visual identity, press and social media, photographic documentation of the opening and installation views, the opening itself, and partial help installing; artists cover opening refreshments, their own installation labour, any equipment the gallery cannot supply, and returning the space to its prior state. Applications are free and go by email to the gallery, with a short and detailed project description, chosen space, CVs, an artist portfolio as a single PDF, a preferred exhibition date, an installation plan and any accompanying programme. Final bachelor's and master's theses are not eligible. The deadline is Sunday 16 August 2026.

calls.title: Emerald Renaissance: Celebrating 80 Years of Exhibiting Excellence
calls.org: Philadelphia Chapter of The Links, Incorporated
calls.description: A juried fine art exhibition marking the 80th anniversary of the Philadelphia chapter of The Links, Incorporated, the Black women's service organization founded in 1946. The theme asks how Black women — through friendship and service — have used the arts, education and cultural leadership to uplift communities across generations, and invites work that speaks to culture, history, connection and shared responsibility, interpreted through personal, cultural, historical or contemporary perspectives. Photography is explicitly among the eligible media, with painting, mixed media and works on paper. Open to artists living in Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery or Philadelphia counties, Pennsylvania; artists from historically underrepresented and underserved communities are strongly encouraged to apply, and emerging, mid-career and established artists are all welcome. Up to three works, free to enter; work must be original, made in the last three to five years, ready to install, at least 24 and no more than 36 inches wide and no more than 72 inches high. The jurors are Adrian J. Moody, gallerist and co-owner of Moody Jones Gallery; Rosalyn 'Roz' J. McPherson of The Roz Group, formerly Senior Vice President for the Science Center at The Franklin Institute; and Shelley R. Sylva, Head of Corporate Citizenship at TD Bank. Artists are notified 19 October 2026 and the exhibition is presented on 14 November 2026 at Founder's Hall, Girard College, alongside a live painting session and auction. All accepted work must be available for acquisition, with sales split 50/50 in favour of the artist; proceeds support the chapter's education, arts, health and mentorship programmes.
jury: Adrian J. Moody, Gallerist and co-owner, Moody Jones Gallery
Rosalyn J. McPherson, President, The Roz Group
Shelley R. Sylva, Head of Corporate Citizenship, TD Bank
calls.summary: 80th-anniversary juried show from Philadelphia's Links chapter. Photography named; five-county PA eligibility, three jurors.

calls.title: Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
calls.description: Alongside its photobook dummy exhibition, the Lisbon Photobook Fair runs a Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores — giving photographers who publish their own work, and the small presses that publish them, a place to sell at the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa, held 27–29 November 2026 at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma. The Authors' Space is managed by the fair's own organisation and asks a single one-off contribution rather than taking a cut: €10 covers up to two different titles and €20 covers three or four, in both cases with no limit on the number of copies you bring and, in the organisers' own words, no commission whatsoever on sales. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form submitted together with a maximum of six photographs of each photobook (72 dpi, 2 MB maximum, named for author and work) sent by WeTransfer to the fair under the subject 'Self-Publishers'. A registration only counts once the form, the images and the contribution have all been received. Pre-registration closes at 21:00 GMT on 12 October 2026, confirmations go out on 23 October, and books must reach the Arquivo Municipal by 16 November, delivered in person Monday to Saturday, 10am–6pm, or by post at the author's own cost; unsold copies are collected from the archive after the fair.
calls.summary: Sell your self-published photobooks at Lisbon's 16th photobook fair — €10–20 one-off contribution, no commission on sales.

calls.title: Small Works, Big Impact
calls.description: The 203 Art Space, a contemporary gallery and creative hub that opened in March 2026 on the 5th floor of the Stamford Town Center, invites submissions for its next monthly exhibition, "Small Works, Big Impact." The brief is bold pieces no larger than 24 x 24 inches that leave a lasting impression despite their scale — work where detail, colour, vibrancy and concept carry the memory. Photography is a named accepted medium alongside mixed media, digital, sculpture and painting. Artists may submit one to three pieces. All work must be wired and ready to hang; if stretcher bars are less than an inch and a half deep, the piece must be framed. Selections are announced 21 August and accepted work is dropped off in person at the gallery on 22 and 23 August. The show runs 26 August to 26 September 2026, with an opening reception on Saturday 29 August, 3–5pm. The gallery retains a 30% commission on work sold during the exhibition; the artist receives 70%. Entry is $40 for the first piece and $10 for each additional piece. Note that drop-off and pick-up are in person in Stamford, and no cash award is offered — the exhibition itself is the opportunity.
calls.summary: Stamford gallery seeks bold work under 24 x 24 inches — photography welcome. Physical show plus an opening reception.

calls.title: ANTHOLOGY 3
calls.description: ANTHOLOGY is Ephemere's cyclical curated group exhibition and publication series, and its third volume forms part of the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo. Exactly nine artists are selected each round — "nine distinct petals of a single flower" — a number chosen so individual narratives complement rather than compete with one another across the gallery walls and the pages of an accompanying photobook. Applicants submit a portfolio of 15 to 20 images; the curatorial team, led by Ephemere founder Anne Murayama and assisted by Alfred Ong, then selects the nine final images that will represent each artist in both the show and the book. Ephemere handles all printing, layout design, framing and installation. ANTHOLOGY 3 runs 17–27 October 2026 on the 3rd floor of Three Space Tokyo. Applying is free, but selected artists pay a strictly non-refundable all-inclusive participation fee — ¥27,500 for Japan-based artists, $275 for visiting artists — covering the 11-day gallery placement, curatorial administration, professional printing and installation, and one complimentary copy of the photobook. Attendance is mandatory: proxy representation is not allowed and selected artists must be physically present in Tokyo on their designated Artist Talk day to give a 10–15 minute presentation alongside their work. Travel and accommodation are the artist's own cost. Two group video meetings in September cover logistics, and artists who join the take-down on 28 October may take their prints home free of charge.
calls.summary: Nine photographers curated into a group show and photobook at Ephemere Photo Fest, Tokyo. Free to apply; Tokyo attendance required.

calls.title: Presentations of Authorial Projects — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
calls.description: The third of the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa's parallel open calls — alongside its photobook dummy exhibition and its self-publishing and small publishers space — this one offers photographers a speaking slot rather than a table. Selected authors present their own photobook project to fair visitors at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma, in sessions running across the fair: Friday 27 November between 5:30pm and 7:30pm, and Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November between 11:00am and 12:30pm and again from 2:00pm to 7:30pm. Each presentation runs a maximum of 25 minutes and a projector is available. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form and closes at 9:00pm on 12 October 2026; the fair's organisation confirms by 6 November whether the presentation will go ahead and at what time. There is no participation fee. The organisers note that authors whose project includes a photobook for sale should also register separately for the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores, and that dummies can be submitted in parallel for pre-selection in the dummy exhibition — the three calls share a deadline but are entered independently.
calls.summary: Present your photobook project to visitors at Lisbon's 16th photobook fair — free 25-minute slot, projector available.

calls.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 75: Clay Every Which Way
calls.description: The 75th issue of the UK independent art zine Haus-a-rest, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, takes clay as its subject — but explicitly not clay as pottery. The editors want work that goes beyond the pot, beyond tradition and beyond expectation: clay as unfired material, slip, earth pigment, digital simulation, or as a metaphor for transformation, identity, labour, geology, archaeology, ritual, play, memory and the body. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside sculpture, installation, painting, drawing, printmaking, textiles incorporating clay, mixed media, land art, performance documentation, video (YouTube links only) and digital works, and the call runs in parallel for writers submitting poetry, essays, short fiction, creative non-fiction and experimental texts. Conceptual responses are welcomed as warmly as material ones — the editors ask what it means to shape something with your hands, how clay remembers touch, and whether a material can carry history, culture or politics. Submit up to three artworks as JPEGs, or up to 1,000 words of writing, or a combination, together with titles, a statement of no more than 200 words explaining how the work fits the theme, and a biography of up to 150 words. An Instagram handle is required: selected contributors are asked to collaborate on sharing the posts. There is no submission fee, the call is open internationally to artists and writers at every career stage, and selected work is published in the online zine and gallery and promoted across the zine's social channels. Entry closes 3 September 2026 through CuratorSpace.
calls.summary: UK indie art/lit zine, theme 'Clay Every Which Way'. Photography named among accepted media. Free, publication only.

calls.title: Forms and Fragments
calls.description: The first annual online juried competition from Atlantic Gallery, the artist-run cooperative that has operated in Chelsea since 1974. Forms and Fragments asks artists to explore the relationship between what is transformed, remembered, assembled or broken, and the shapes those experiences become — the beauty of what remains, what is reconstructed and what emerges. Work may investigate memory, identity, landscape, culture, architecture, the body or abstraction through literal or symbolic fragments and evolving forms, considering how the parts relate to the whole, and the gallery invites personal, political, material and conceptual readings alike. The juror is Patricia Miranda, an artist, curator and educator who founded The Crit Lab and MAPSpace and the Lace Archive, and who has held residencies at the Textile Art Center, Vermont Studio Center, I-Park and Weir Farm. Photography is listed among the accepted media, alongside oils, acrylics, watercolours, pastels, drawings, traditional printmaking, original digital art, fibre art, mixed media and sculpture in any medium; digital or giclée reproductions of original artwork and AI-generated work are excluded. Entry is open to all artists 18 and over, at $30 for up to three works plus $10 for up to five more submitted at the same time, with no piece larger than 32 inches in any direction. Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running 1 October to 12 November 2026 and reproduced in an online digital catalogue, and every accepted piece is featured on the gallery's social channels. The award is the significant part: prize winners are selected for inclusion in Atlantic Gallery's physical group show in its Chelsea space, 1–19 December 2026, with work delivered in person or by proxy. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales.
calls.summary: Chelsea co-op's first online juried competition. Photography accepted; prize winners join the gallery's December group show.

calls.title: Jazz Got Loose at The Gallery at the Attucks
calls.description: Norfolk Arts, the City of Norfolk's public arts agency, is filling the next six-month rotation at The Gallery at the Attucks, inside the historic Attucks Theatre in downtown Norfolk, Virginia — a 1919 building financed, designed and built by African Americans and one of the oldest surviving theatres of its kind in the United States. Jazz Got Loose treats jazz not only as a musical form but as a cultural movement rooted in New Orleans' Black communities and defined by freedom, resistance, identity and transformation. The call seeks work exploring liberation, resilience, social change, individuality and the courage to push against convention; politically charged, narrative-driven and culturally critical work is welcome, and Black artists and artists whose work reflects the cultural legacy of the Attucks are especially encouraged to apply. Delegate Jackie Hope Glass will jury the exhibition and select up to 50 original works. Any 2-D or relief visual medium is eligible, so photography qualifies, provided pieces do not exceed 50 pounds and arrive exhibition-ready with secure hanging hardware; video and digital work must come with its own display equipment. Artists must be 18 or over with a connection to Hampton Roads, and submit up to three images with title, medium, dimensions, year and a brief description of each work, a bio of up to 250 words and a statement of up to 300 words. There is no entry fee. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, sales enquiries go straight to the artist, and Norfolk Arts takes no commission. The exhibition runs 29 October 2026 to 10 April 2027; artists deliver and collect their own work.
calls.prize: Six-month exhibition at the Attucks Theatre
calls.summary: Free call from Norfolk's city arts agency: up to 50 works on jazz and liberation, six months at the historic Attucks Theatre.

calls.title: River Margin — Issue 1
calls.description: River Margin is a new Australian and international literary journal founded in 2026 by the Melbourne-based visual artist, musician and writer Lana Eileen, and it is assembling its first issue. The focus is ecology, botany and wilderness: the journal was created as a space for overlooked aspects of the natural world — tiny wild-growing plants, threatened rivers, things hidden in the undergrowth. The name refers to the riparian zone, the natural border between water and land, and the editorial position follows from it: River Margin is a space where the liminal, the edge-dwelling, the peripheral and the unnoticed can find a voice. Photographers can submit up to seven images that relate in some way to ecology, botany, the environment, conservation or wilderness areas — rivers and bodies of water, insects, wildlife, fungi, plants, forests, mountains. Both digital and film photography are accepted; AI-generated work is not, and for visual art more broadly the journal excludes digital art as well. Files go by a file-sharing service such as WeTransfer to the journal's submissions address. Submissions are open worldwide and free, and the editors aim to respond within two weeks. The journal is candid that as a new publication compiling its first issue it is not in a position to pay contributors, so the return is publication in Issue 1 alongside poetry, essays, short fiction and creative non-fiction on the same themes. Submissions for the first issue close on 1 November 2026.
calls.summary: New Australian ecology and botany journal seeking photography for its first issue. Free, worldwide, no AI, publication only.

calls.title: Explorations: How We See Things
calls.org: The Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center
calls.description: The Norris Gallery's 2027 juried winter exhibition at the Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center in St. Charles, Illinois. Explorations has no fixed subject: entries should reflect what engages the artist and inspires their exploration — of subject matter, of art processes, of media, or of point of view. Artists may submit up to three original works in any 2D or 3D medium or art process, which places photography squarely within scope; the only medium bar is on reproductions, so no giclées, and no work previously exhibited in the Norris galleries. The entry fee is $35 and is non-refundable. Monetary awards and honourable mentions are presented at the artists' reception. Accepted work cannot be shipped: it must be delivered in person by the artist or a representative on 4 January 2027 and collected on 15 February, which in practice limits the show to artists within reach of the Fox Valley. All accepted work must be for sale and must remain on display for the full run, with the centre retaining 30% commission on anything sold; accepted work may also be posted on the Norris Galleries website as well as hung in the gallery. Entries close on Monday 16 November 2026, artists hear back by Friday 11 December, and the exhibition runs 9 January to 14 February 2027. The Norris is a long-running community arts centre near Chicago with a performance hall and a gallery programme, and it runs a second annual juried show, Watercolor, on a separate cycle.

calls.title: Building Blocks: What Are We Building With?
calls.description: A blind-juried open call from the St. Charles Arts Council for an exhibition at its gallery in historic downtown St. Charles, Illinois. The premise is elemental: every creation begins with a single component, whether a stroke of paint, a block of wood or a spark of imagination, and the council asks how the individual components an artist chooses dictate the meaning of the final structure — for the artwork, for a life, or for a community. All art mediums are accepted and three-dimensional and assemblage work is actively encouraged, which leaves photography fully eligible. Artists may enter one or two pieces; the fee is $35 for non-members and $20 for council members, chosen from a tiered drop-down at entry. Work must be original, created within the last seven years, and never previously shown in a St. Charles Arts Council exhibit, and all entries must be for sale. Awards are presented at the opening reception, timed so that every participating artist can arrive: $150 for Best in Show, $75 for second place, $50 for third and further honourable mentions at the judge's discretion. Entries close 11 August 2026; work is dropped off on 31 August, the exhibition runs from early September to 25 October 2026 with an opening reception on the evening of 10 September, and pick-up is 26 October. The council notes it has no storage space, so artists unable to attend drop-off or collection must send someone in their place.
calls.summary: Blind-juried all-media show in downtown St. Charles, IL. $150 Best in Show; $35 entry, $20 for council members.

calls.org: Gresham Area League for the Arts
calls.description: The Gresham Area League for the Arts' winter exhibition, hung in the Gresham Council Chamber Visual Arts Gallery in Oregon over the peak holiday season and mirrored in GALA's online galleries. The brief is scale: two-dimensional work must measure no more than 9 by 9 inches including the frame and no less than 5 by 5, and three-dimensional work must fit inside a 9-inch cube. Within that constraint the league is open across media and names photography directly alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, pottery, fibre art and other 3-D work. Artists may enter up to three pieces for a single $30 submission fee, and GALA retains 20% commission on sales. Preference goes to artists in the greater Gresham area, though the league may widen the pool depending on the number of submissions; in practice the binding constraint is that artists must live within 30 miles of Gresham, because accepted work has to be delivered to the gallery in person. Work featuring nudity or sexual content is not accepted. Entries close 28 October 2026 and the exhibition runs 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027.

calls.title: 49th Annual Photography Exhibit
calls.description: The Wassenberg Art Center's annual photography exhibition, now in its 49th year, hung in the centre's galleries in Van Wert, Ohio. Entries are juried across six subject categories — Nature (floral, wildlife, botanicals), Portraiture (including photojournalism), Architecture, Landscape (natural only), Abstract/Macro, and Film — with no more than two photographs per category and ten in total per photographer. The Film category asks for traditional analogue work and proof of negative may be requested. Awards run to $250 for Best of Show in Colour and another $250 for Best of Show in Black and White, plus seven $150 excellence awards, one per category and one for Youth Best of Show; the funds are administered by the Van Wert County Foundation. This is a physical, in-person exhibition: accepted work must reach the art center by the delivery deadline of 6 September 2026, and photographers outside driving distance may ship at their own cost both ways. Sales are handled by the art center, which takes a 30% commission. Work previously exhibited at the Wassenberg is not eligible, and no name, logo or title may be visible on the front of a print. Entries close 21 August 2026, jurying is announced 26 August, and the show runs 10 September to 8 October 2026.
calls.summary: Ohio art center's 49th annual photography show, six categories, $250 Best of Show in colour and again in black and white.

calls.title: IMPACT: A Celebration of Photography
calls.description: A free, blind-juried photography exhibition on the East End of Long Island, organised by a group of North Fork photographers and hosted in the gallery of the North Fork Arts Center, the 501(c)(3) nonprofit formed in 2023 to save the historic Greenport Theatre. Curators Paul Henry, an NFAC board member who previously ran a decade-long student film programme in Greenport, and Jeremy Garretson are looking for the photograph that stops you: not necessarily the technically perfect one, but the frame that holds a moment, reveals a beauty, or tells a story you cannot quite shake. The call is open to East End photographers of every experience level and age, professionals, enthusiasts, students and anyone who loves making pictures, and Henry has said he hopes it becomes the first step toward a broader photography programme for the community. Artists may enter up to three photographs of any subject, style or genre, made anywhere and at any time, each with a note of 100 words or fewer; there is no entry fee and images are reviewed blind, judged on overall impact and appeal alone. AI-generated or substantially AI-altered images are not eligible, though ordinary processing such as cropping, exposure and colour correction, dodging and burning, HDR blending, focus stacking and stitching is fine. Selected photographers supply a framed print in a black or white frame, no larger than 24 by 36 inches outside dimensions and wired for hanging, with assistance available to those who need it, and may add a sale price along with a website, gallery or portfolio link on the card beside the work. Entries close 24 August 2026, artists are notified 8 September, framed prints are due 8 October, and the exhibition opens with a public reception on Saturday 24 October, running to 22 November 2026.
calls.summary: Free, blind-juried photography show at the North Fork Arts Center gallery in Greenport, open to East End photographers.

calls.title: Photographers Without Borders Micro-Grants
calls.description: A $500 USD micro-grant awarded to a different photographer every month by Photographers Without Borders, the nonprofit registered in both the US and Canada that has built its programme around ethical, community-rooted visual storytelling. Submissions take the form of a photo essay posted to PWB's members' community platform, and the brief is explicit about relationship: it is aimed at photographers with strong connections to the communities in their stories, whether they come from those communities themselves or have built those relationships over time. Subjects range across land and water protection, Indigenous science and wisdom, climate change and regeneration, and everything intersecting in between, including human rights, Indigenous sovereignty and land back. Mixed-media photographers are welcome. Recipients receive $500 USD. There is no submission fee, but applicants must be PWB members: basic membership is $9.99 a month and includes access to the community platform, the Storytelling for Change learning series and digital copies of the PWB magazine, and the organisation offers a needs-based membership to anyone who cannot afford it. Grants are awarded monthly on a rolling basis, so there is no fixed closing date.
calls.summary: A $500 micro-grant awarded every month for a photo essay rooted in community, land, climate and Indigenous sovereignty.

calls.title: Standing on Their Shoulders
calls.description: A juried gallery exhibition at Clay Hand Studios on Fresno's Gallery Row, built around the history and legacy of striving for freedom: demonstrations, resistance, solidarity, celebration and injustice, read as past, present and future chapters on the same path. Artists are invited to submit original work depicting people, events, artifacts, histories, hopes or consequences, and the brief is deliberately wide — "from realistic portrayals to imaginative interpretations" — welcoming personal as well as historical perspectives. Although Clay Hand is a ceramics studio, the call is not a ceramics call: the organisers state they encourage submissions in all visual art mediums "including painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, mixed media, digital art, and more", and photography is listed among the accepted media on the entry form alongside ceramic, multimedia, painting, fiber, sculpture and drawing. Work is judged by William Raines and Piet Ogata, and cash prizes are awarded in each category, though the organisers do not publish the amounts. The show runs 1–31 October 2026 at 660 Van Ness Avenue, timed to coincide with Fresno's Taste of Freedom Celebration. Entrants may submit one to three pieces, one entry per artist. AI-generated art is explicitly not accepted. NOTE ON WHO MAY ENTER: the organisers state both "Open to California artists" and, under the Eligibility heading, "Open to all artists" — the two lines sit side by side on their own page and on the entry form, so photographers outside California should confirm with the gallery before paying the fee.
calls.summary: A Fresno gallery show on freedom, resistance and solidarity — photography explicitly welcome, cash prizes, two named jurors.

calls.title: MY MICHIGAN: Our Rivers, Our Lakes
calls.description: A juried themed exhibition at the Grosse Pointe Artists Association's gallery on The War Memorial campus in Grosse Pointe Farms, Michigan, asking artists to "prove the truth behind the slogan 'Water Wonderland' that was coined in 1963" — Michigan's rivers and lakes, however they are read. The juror is Alex Gilford, an artist and park ranger the association describes as noted for his efforts to strengthen the relationship between the arts and nature. Photography is one of the media the organisers accept, and the call's own banner image is a photograph, Donald Cronkhite's "Nankin Lake, After the Storm". Open to all artists over 18 and to alumni of GPAA's Promising Artists exhibitions; original work only, nothing made under an instructor, nothing previously exhibited with GPAA, and no large installation pieces. One to six pieces per artist, with the entry fee covering the first two and a $3 transaction fee added at checkout. There are no size limits, but 2D work must arrive framed and wired ready to hang; accepted work is delivered in person or shipped with a prepaid return label to the gallery on 26 September. Note two things before entering: the organisers publish no awards or prizes of any kind for this show — the return is the two-month hang — and work priced to sell carries a 35% gallery commission for members, 45% for non-members. Exhibition runs 1 October to 4 December 2026, with a gallery talk on the opening evening.
jury: Alex Gilford, artist and park ranger

calls.title: Echoes of Fall 2026
calls.description: All-media juried exhibition on fall-inspired work at the Medford Arts Center, a community arts centre on North Main Street in Medford, New Jersey. Michael Schweigart is juror of awards; chairs are Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Open to artists 18 and over, up to three original pieces each, none previously shown at MAC. Entry is $20 for the first work for members and $30 for non-members, plus $10 for each additional piece. Every accepted work goes into the online exhibition and into a brochure and YouTube video; artists who can hand deliver also have the option of showing their pieces in the gallery at 8 N. Main St. The show runs 4 September to 1 October 2026; artists are notified by email on 1 September, and the awards and online exhibit go up on 5 September. Cash awards for first place, second place and three honourable mentions, though the centre does not publish the amounts. All work must be for sale and Medford Arts takes 30% commission; artists ship sold work to the buyer themselves.

calls.title: MacDowell Fellowship — Spring/Summer 2027
calls.description: MacDowell's Spring/Summer 2027 cycle, for residencies running March 1 – August 31, 2027 at the 450-acre estate in Peterborough, New Hampshire. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations and three prepared meals a day for up to eight weeks; there are no residency fees, and Fellows may apply for need-based stipends and travel reimbursement covering direct travel, rent, lost income and childcare. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, which MacDowell describes as spanning "photographers and printmakers to sculptors and creators of large-scale installation". The sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence and artists at any stage of practice may apply, but applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking program during the residency season and may submit only one application every 24 months; the reference-letter requirement is temporarily suspended. Applications are open: the Apply Now button at the foot of MacDowell's apply page leads to its own Hub portal. A $30 processing fee applies, with waivers available on request for financial hardship.

calls.title: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists 2027–28
calls.description: The eighth iteration of the Queens Museum's fellowship for emerging visual artists living in the five boroughs of New York City. Two artists each receive $20,000, professional development consultations with QM staff, and four mentorship and feedback sessions over the year with an established New York artist of their choosing. Each fellowship runs one year and culminates in a solo project exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028; the award covers the artist fee, materials and production costs for the work made for that show. Emerging is defined as at least two but no more than ten years of practice outside a degree programme, with no solo exhibitions at established commercial galleries or museums and no major grants; age and formal training are not factors. Applications are reviewed by QM curatorial staff and two guest jurors, with in-person interviews for shortlisted candidates in November.

calls.title: Brightwork Fellowship 2027
calls.description: Anchorlight's flagship studio-based fellowship for one North Carolina artist a year at a pivotal moment in their career: a 500-plus square foot studio at Anchorlight in Raleigh, a solo exhibition in its zero-commission gallery, and an unrestricted award of $50,000. Anchorlight is home to 28 artist studios and a 1,500 square foot gallery; the Brightwork programme began in 2017 and relaunched under the current model in 2022, with the Brightwork Foundation formed in late 2025 to steward it. Applicants must have lived in North Carolina full time for at least twelve consecutive months and commit to staying for the fellowship. The same cycle also offers two Brightwork Grants to NC-based visual artists — a $2,000 Professional Development Grant and a $3,000 Studio Project Grant — but you may apply for only one of the three. Practising visual artists 21 and over of any career stage are eligible; performers, filmmakers, musicians and writers are not.

calls.title: ON::View Artist Residency — February–May 2027
calls.description: A fully funded residency in a street-level storefront studio at ARTS Southeast in Savannah's Starland District, where large east-facing windows let the neighbourhood watch the work happen around the clock. The residency provides free use of the 12-by-12-foot studio, free lodging at the nearby 5th Dimension Apartment and a $500 stipend that may go to travel, materials or anything the resident chooses, for an artist or curator making new work, continuing a project or doing research. Residents are encouraged to give a public lecture, workshop or other interactive event, and must work in the studio during ARTS Southeast's public open hours at least one day a week. Open internationally and to collaborative teams; artists may work in any medium suitable for the space, and current or recent ARTS Southeast studio members are not eligible. Programme partners include the SCAD Museum of Art and Telfair Museums. The $50 application fee can be waived on request if it is an undue burden.
calls.summary: Fully funded Savannah storefront-studio residency — free studio, free lodging and a $500 stipend, any medium.

calls.title: SKOG Open Call 2027
calls.description: SKOG, a cross-disciplinary exhibition space in Oslo dedicated to progressive contemporary art, photography and collectible objects, invites proposals for its 2027 exhibition programme. Both solo and group exhibition proposals are accepted, from emerging and established artists worldwide at any career stage and in any medium or technique. Applications are free and reviewed by SKOG's curatorial team; many of its exhibitions are developed collaboratively, so selected artists may be invited to show alongside others in a curated group presentation. Applications ask for a portfolio, CV, project description, and the materials, techniques and dimensions of the proposed work, against the gallery floor plan and its 2,750 mm ceiling height, and may be written in English or in Norwegian, Swedish or Danish. SKOG is seeking grant funding towards transport costs and artist fees but says it is unlikely to cover travel or accommodation in Oslo, and will discuss costs with shortlisted artists before deciding.
calls.summary: Free open call for solo and group exhibitions in 2027 at SKOG, an Oslo space dedicated to contemporary art and photography.

calls.title: (Not) Food Porn — From Feed to Culture
calls.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, timed to the International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste on 29 September. The brief asks lens-based artists to work critically at the intersection of food imagery, consumption and culture: highly stylised "food porn" has reshaped how we perceive, desire and celebrate what we eat, and opposing feeds lean into raw, unedited aesthetics, while behind both sits massive global food waste and a rapidly shifting relationship to sustenance. Submissions are one project of up to 10 images, cohesive and not previously featured by Der Greif. Selected work is presented in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, and selected artists are invited into a small-group online roundtable critique facilitated by Der Greif staff as part of its Face-to-Face programme, with visibility across Der Greif's international community and a possible invitation to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio for sales and commissions. Selection is judged on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community. Der Greif describes this as a free submission with an optional €5 or €10 donation, but the Picter entry page carries a flat €10 fee; artists who cannot contribute financially can email the organiser for a 50% or 100% discount code. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction.
calls.summary: Der Greif call on food imagery, desire and waste, timed to the UN food-loss day. Online exhibition on Pulse plus a peer critique.

calls.title: 34th Tewksbury Juried Art Show
calls.description: The Tewksbury Historical Society's juried art show returns for a 34th edition at the Zion Lutheran Christian Education Building in Oldwick, New Jersey, from 3 to 10 October 2026. Any two-dimensional media may be entered, photography explicitly included, with only giclees excluded; work on paper must be matted, framed, glazed and wired ready to hang. Each artist may enter up to five juried works, of which only one may reach 40 inches in any direction including frame. One $35 entry fee covers the juried entry and also opens the show's Small Works showcase (pieces up to 14 x 18 inches, priced at $500 or less) and its Portfolio showcase (up to ten works shown in a floor-standing print rack) at no extra charge. Six judging categories carry the awards: Animal Kingdom, Abstract/Non-Objective, Natural Environment, Figurative, Still Life/Florals and Built Environment. Show awards are $400 for Best in Show, $300 for Best of Tewksbury (a recognisable local building, site or scene) and the $200 Marion Katnack award for a Tewksbury landscape, with $125, $75 and $25 plus honourable mentions in each category. Artists are notified on 21 August, deliver work in person on 27 or 28 September, and collect unsold work on 10 October, with $25 a day charged on anything left unclaimed; the Society retains 30% commission on sales.
jury: Helen Marie Farrant, artist and ceramic sculptor
calls.summary: A 34th-edition New Jersey juried show, photography a named medium. One $35 fee covers juried, small works and portfolio entries.

calls.title: On Rose
calls.description: Looking Glass, the independent photographic outfitters in Berkeley, launches On Rose to mark its move to a new home on Rose Street. Photographers are invited to interpret 'rose' as broadly as they like — as a flower, a colour, a symbol, a place, a story, an act of resistance or a moment of renewal. A rose does not need to appear in the picture, but the connection should be visible and meaningful. Each photograph is assigned to one of six categories: The Botanical Rose; Symbol, Story and Metaphor; Rose as Colour; Celebration, Honor and Community; On Rose Street; and They Rose Up. Entry uses a sliding-scale contribution of $5, $10, $15, $20, $25, $30, $40 or $50 — the amount chosen has no effect on judging, selection or awards — and one entry covers up to three photographs. Work is judged anonymously by Bay Area photographers Becky Jaffe, Sarah Deragon and Brandon Ruffin on interpretation of the theme (40%), visual voice and emotional resonance (40%) and photographic execution (20%). The overall winner, category winners and honourable mentions are exhibited at Abrams Claghorn Gallery & Shop in Albany, California in October 2026, with an opening reception; the overall winner also receives a commemorative trophy. Selected photographers are expected to be notified in October 2026. Photographs may be made on film, digital cameras or phones, and older work is welcome, but every entry must begin as a real-world capture by the entrant.
calls.prize: Exhibition at Abrams Claghorn Gallery + trophy
jury: Sarah Deragon, portrait photographer and founder of Portraits To The People

calls.title: Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant 2026
calls.description: Printed Matter's annual programme of unrestricted grants for artists' book publishers, now in its third year and supported by the Wagner Foundation. In 2026 three grants of $10,000 each go to independent presses with a publishing history of one or more years, alongside a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair, with the table provided free of charge. The award is unrestricted: funds can cover production and development costs, artists' fees, equipment, studio rent or hired assistance, with no obligation to deliver a specific project. Eligible imprints should be small in scale and published with an independent spirit, without major ongoing distribution support; commercially run studios that only publish client work, and imprints attached to well-resourced institutions, are generally not eligible. The jury is broadly interested in presses that treat the book as a site for experimental artwork, that engage social and political themes with nuance, that give voice to marginalised perspectives, and that back emerging and underrepresented artists regardless of sales prospects. The grant is not aimed at artists seeking to fund a book of their own work, though artists who actively publish others are welcome. Open to publishers based anywhere; international applications encouraged. Past Publisher Work Grant winners cannot apply a second time.
calls.summary: Three $10,000 unrestricted grants for independent artists' book publishers, plus a free Art Book Fair table. Open worldwide.

calls.title: 1st Digital Art Exhibition
calls.description: The Philadelphia Sketch Club — founded in 1860 and the oldest artists' club in the United States — opens its first ever Digital Art Show, an open juried exhibition at its Camac Street galleries. Every submitted work must include a substantial amount of digitally created content, which suits composited, layered and heavily manipulated photo-based work; the club runs a separate annual PHOTOgraphy exhibition for straight photography and does not publish where the line between the two falls. Work must be original, not previously shown at the PSC, framed and wired for hanging, no larger than 24 inches in any dimension excluding the frame and no heavier than 30 lbs; prints deemed low-quality on delivery will not be hung. Artists may submit up to ten works, with a maximum of two accepted per artist. Works made with generative AI are not eligible in any PSC exhibition. Juror Perry Santulli selects the show, and prizes of $300, $200 and $100 are awarded with Contemporary Sketch Club Medals and certificates, plus at least three honourable mentions, presented at the reception on 11 October. All work must be for sale; the club takes 25% commission. The exhibition runs 4–25 October 2026.
calls.summary: The 166-year-old Philadelphia Sketch Club's first digital show — work must be substantially digitally created, no generative AI.

calls.title: The Artist's Vision
calls.description: National open call with no theme at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, filling both exhibition rooms. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are asked simply for their finest work — any theme, style or subject matter, traditional, experimental or a synthesis of the two — and the prospectus states plainly that all photographic processes are welcome. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works, with no cutoff date on when the work was made. The CaFE entry window runs 10 to 31 August 2026. Awards include an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery's second room, an optional $200 Director's Choice, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from every artist shown at the gallery during the year. Framed or gallery-wrapped work up to 48 inches, wired for hanging; plexiglass preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 24 January – 21 February 2027.
jury: Anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers & academics

calls.title: Dezi Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Two $1,000 unrestricted cash grants for early-career visual artists, run by Dezi, a career-support platform for artists launching in 2026. calls.title: Photo Fringe 2026 — Feedback Loop
calls.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led registered charity that has run an open-platform photography festival on a DIY, collectively-funded model since 2003. Registration is now open for the 2026 edition, which runs 2–31 October across Brighton & Hove, Portsmouth and Newhaven with launch events on Friday 2 October. Anyone can take part: artists, photographers, collectives, curators and organisations register their own self-curated exhibition and are then listed in the official festival programme and on photofringe.org, given marketing resources and exhibitor guidance, and folded into a city-wide trail that helps audiences find the work. Exhibitors are responsible for finding and managing their own venue, though the festival shares venue leads and connects artists looking for larger shared spaces; online-only exhibitions are equally welcome, and Photo Fringe events such as artist talks, workshops and photo walks are listed free. The 2026 theme is Feedback Loop — a cycle of action and response, thinking about how images circulate and change as they are seen, shared, interpreted and reworked, and what becomes possible when work is made with others rather than alone. Responding to the theme is encouraged but not compulsory. Contributions towards the festival are £125 for a solo exhibition at a venue and online, £150 for a group exhibition, £60 for solo online-only and £100 for group online-only, all subsidised; a small number of bursaries are available for exhibitors who cannot afford a contribution, by emailing the festival. All registered exhibitors are automatically entered for the Danny Wilson Memorial Awards, supported by Photoworks, whose prizes include a bursary, mentoring sessions and artist talks. Registration closes 1 September 2026.

calls.title: The Fifty: 50 Billboards 50 States
calls.description: Nationwide open call selecting fifty US-based photographers — one from every state — to have their work printed on billboards across the country, licensed and paid for by VSCO. calls.summary: Fifty US photographers, one per state, get their work on a billboard — licensed and paid by VSCO. Free to enter.
prose: The Fifty is VSCO's nationwide recognition programme for photographers working in the United States: one photographer from each of the fifty states is selected to have an image printed on a billboard in their home state. The framing is deliberately anti-metropolitan — the pitch is that you can build a photographic career where you already live, documenting your own community.

There is no entry fee and no separate application portal. Photographers submit by posting work to a VSCO account with the hashtag #TheFifty and the hashtag for their state, adding a short caption about the image or series and putting their state in their profile bio. VSCO recommends three to five images, particularly if they form a cohesive series. A free VSCO account is sufficient to enter.

Beyond the billboard, VSCO states that selected work may be carried into editorial features, curation and licensing opportunities, and that selected photographers are licensed and compensated for the use of their images. Anyone selected will be asked for a high-resolution file suitable for large-format printing, and images containing recognisable people require a model release. VSCO's fine print adds two qualifications: billboard formats vary by state, so selected work may instead appear as an alternative large-format display, poster or public installation, and submitting grants VSCO the right to review the work and, if selected, use it for the campaign and on social media, with a release or licence agreement possible on request.

The call is open to photographers aged 18 and over residing in the United States; VSCO says international opportunities are planned separately. The deadline is September 10, 2026. The curation team reviews every submission and notifies selected photographers on a rolling basis rather than on a single announcement date, with selections also published on the VSCO journal.

calls.summary: One-month analog residency in an Airstream darkroom across NYC. $1,500 stipend, free film and chemistry. No fee.
prose: Worthless Studios' Photographer in Residence programme is built around a single object: a 1973 Airstream trailer restored and converted into a professional-grade black-and-white darkroom. Because the darkroom is mobile, each resident is embedded in a specific community or site for a month and makes work there with the processing equipment on hand, rather than shooting in one place and printing in another.

For 2027 seven artists are selected, one per month from April through October, each for a four-week residency in one of the five boroughs of New York City. Partner sites include Alice Austen House on Staten Island, Inspiration Point in the Bronx, The Green-Wood Cemetery and The Center for Arts and Advocacy in Brooklyn, The Lower Eastside Girls Club in Manhattan, and NYC Parks across all five boroughs. Applicants may also propose their own site, provided they can resolve permission and parking for the trailer.

Residents receive 24/7 access to the Airstream darkroom, a $1,500 artist stipend, darkroom chemistry, film and photo paper, two free workshops on scanning and digital printing run by Brooklyn PrintWorks, press packet materials, and the option to host a public program. The darkroom holds two enlargers (a Beseler 23II and an Omega type D) and film carriers for 35mm, 6x6, 6x7, 6x9 and 4x5; it is set up for black-and-white and alternative processes only, with no colour processing or printing. In residence, artists produce twenty images: ten original photographs and ten documenting their time with the Airstream.

Eligibility is aimed at artists who lack darkroom access or want to work close to a particular community or site. Prior independent darkroom experience is expected, and residents commit a minimum of twenty hours per week in the trailer. Applicants cannot be enrolled in an art-related degree program, nor planning to start one in the coming year. Applicants need not be based in New York, but Worthless Studios does not cover housing, travel or visas, and non-US citizens need valid US work authorisation at the time of the residency. Collaborative duos may apply, though the stipend and materials are shared.
Applications are free and open August 10 to September 30, 2026 via SlideRoom. Finalists are notified in October 2026 and interviewed virtually, with residents confirmed in December 2026.

Accepted work must arrive gallery-ready and wired to hang, and may be delivered in person or shipped with a prepaid return label. The exhibition runs November 24, 2026 to January 9, 2027, with a reception on Friday, December 4.

calls.description: National call for portraiture at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, filling both exhibition rooms. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are invited: traditional or non-traditional imagery of a single individual, a couple or a group, from a close-up of a face to a half-length or full-body pose, made to read as idealised, neutral, psychological, satirical, celebratory or cultural. All photographic processes are welcome and there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. calls.title: Group Show #19
calls.description: Open call for seven solo wall presentations in Group Show #19 at New & Abstract's gallery in central Berlin, staged during Berlin Art Week. The gallery asks for new and innovative positions across all media — painting, drawing and printmaking through sculpture, installation and wall-mounted objects, and explicitly photography, digital works and mixed media — and says only: surprise us with your style. Seven winners are chosen to show physically, each given three to four metres of wall on which one or more works are hung in consultation with the gallery; a further twenty honourable mentions are featured on the gallery's Instagram feed and stories. Work must be no larger than 200 × 200 cm, available for the exhibition and offered for sale both on site and in the online gallery, with the artist keeping 60% of any sale. Exhibited works are insured for the run; work must reach Berlin at the artist's own arrangement, and the artist covers return shipping if a piece comes back. Founded in 2019 as an Instagram platform, New & Abstract has shown more than a hundred artists on 100 square metres in Berlin since June 2024. Entry is a €20 processing fee per artwork submitted, non-refundable, and the gallery states plainly that no further costs arise if you are selected for the exhibition, the online gallery or Instagram promotion. Open worldwide to artists aged 18 and over. Winners and honourable mentions are announced by 24 August; work must reach Berlin by 7 September; the show runs 10–24 September 2026 with an opening reception on 10 September.

calls.title: Exposure 2027 International Open Call
calls.description: The Exposure Photography Festival is a month-long celebration of photography that takes over Alberta every February. Its International Open Call is for photographers and visual artists anywhere in the world, at any stage of their career, who incorporate, celebrate or challenge the photographic medium. Ten fee waivers are available to artists facing economic hardship, decided first come first served with a reply inside 48 hours, and photographers based in non-high-income countries can apply free through a separate form. calls.title: Exposure 2027 North West Showcase
calls.description: The North West Showcase is the Exposure Photography Festival's spotlight on emerging photographic talent in western and northern Canada, running alongside its international call each February. It is open to emerging artists resident in Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Yukon and the Northwest Territories; Exposure defines an emerging artist as someone in the early stages of publicly presenting or publishing their work, a definition that deliberately does not rest on age, formal education or traditional career milestones. There is no theme. Work can be shot in any format with any camera and may include collage or experimental approaches, and jurors weigh artistic strength, contemporary relevance, exhibition potential and the curatorial breadth of the selection as a whole. Selected artists show in a group exhibition at TRUCK Contemporary Art in Calgary for the whole of February 2027, free to the public, and receive a CA$456 artist fee set by CARFAC guidelines, a CA$50 production expense allocation and a 40 per cent discount with print partner ABL Imaging. Selected images also go up in a public billboard exhibition on Pattison Outdoor digital screens across Calgary, with an artist profile on Exposure's site plus social and press promotion. Showcase artists are additionally eligible for Exposure's Emerging Photographer of the Year Award, which gives its recipient a solo show at the following year's festival. Submit at least eight images from a connected series with a short statement; the fee covers up to ten images, with further images CA$5 each to a maximum of fifteen. Ten hardship fee waivers are available first come first served, and Alberta's Immigrant Council for Arts Innovation submits five free applications for its members each year. The jury will be one national juror, two representatives of Calgary's photography community, an Exposure board member and the festival manager, to be announced. Notification October 31, 2026.
jury: Five-person jury: a national juror, two Calgary photography representatives, an Exposure board member & the Festival Manager
