calls.title: Convergence of Creativity 2026 — Unexpected: Look Again!
calls.description: The City of San Ramon's third annual juried exhibition takes 'Unexpected — Look Again!' as its theme, asking artists to find the surprising, unconventional, humorous, mysterious or unforeseen in everyday objects, nature, relationships, memories, materials or imagination, whether read literally or conceptually. Photography is one of six named categories, alongside mixed media and printmaking, painting, drawing, ceramics, sculpture and textiles, and digital art; both two- and three-dimensional work is accepted. It is an annual event featuring work from artists around the country, open to anyone aged 16 through senior adults. Work must be original and conceived and created entirely by the entering artist, with no AI-generated work accepted, and pieces shown in last year's San Ramon juried exhibits are not eligible. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 30 by 40 inches including the frame and 40 pounds; three-dimensional work must stay within 18 inches each way and 50 pounds. Accepted work is hung on a Walker display system and must arrive exhibit-ready, cleanly framed and wired with D-ring hangers. Up to three entries per artist at $15 each, with a $5 student rate via a coupon code. Selection and awards are decided by a blind jury that does not see personal information, and the awards are gift certificates: $150 for Best in Show overall, then $100, $75 and $50 blue, red and white ribbons in each category. The exhibition runs November 14 to December 16 at the Lindsay Dirkx Brown Gallery in the San Ramon Community Center, with a public artists' reception on November 14; sales carry a 20 per cent commission to the city and work must be hand delivered and collected on set dates. Note that the CaFÉ application portal does not open until August 14, 2026, at cityofsanramon.info/unexpected; artists are notified October 16.

calls.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026
calls.description: Three fellowships of up to A$7,500 for emerging South Australian creatives, funded by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. The fellowships are self-determined: applicants propose their own bold, ambitious project, which may be the creation of new work, an exhibition, a residency or internship, touring, specialised training, a longer professional development programme, or a combination. Photography is one of nineteen disciplines on the application form, alongside painting, sculpture, moving image, printmaking, new media and curatorial practice. Applicants must be final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, Flinders University, the University of Adelaide or the University of South Australia, and must currently reside in South Australia; master's and PhD candidates qualify only through their undergraduate or honours study. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning and level of ambition, and require an artist CV, academic transcript, budget on the Academy's template, timeline, project confirmations, two letters of support and four to six images or one to two audio-visual demos. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 31 December 2027. There is no application fee. Outcomes are notified within four weeks of the closing date and fellowships are presented at a private event in October.

calls.title: Josephine Ulrick and Win Schubert Photography Award 2026
calls.description: Queensland's richest acquisitive photographic prize returns to HOTA Gallery on the Gold Coast: A$25,000 and acquisition into the HOTA Collection for the winner, plus a A$5,000 People's Choice Award decided by public vote. Submissions are invited across the traditional and expanded medium, including photocollage, sculpture, projection, installation and cameraless photography. Finalists are chosen by a panel of 2018 award winner Tamara Dean, UNSW Galleries director José Da Silva and independent writer and curator Mikala Tai, and are shown in the award exhibition at HOTA Gallery from 28 November 2026 to 7 March 2027. Previous winners include Polly Borland, Merilyn Fairskye, Shaun Gladwell, Polixeni Papapetrou, Darren Sylvester and Justine Varga. Entrants must be 18 or over and Australian citizens or permanent residents; individuals and groups may enter, but nobody may appear in more than one submission. Entry is limited to one artwork, created on or after 11 May 2025 and no larger than 300 cm in any dimension including frame or mount, and work must be available for the full exhibition period. AI may be used provided the extent of that use is clearly described in the submission. The entry fee has been reduced to A$15, with A$10 Mob Tix for First Nations applicants. Finalists are notified by email or phone and have seven days to accept; the winner is announced at the exhibition opening.
jury: José Da Silva, Director, UNSW Galleries

calls.title: MYPH Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: The third annual, free prize from the MYPH school of conceptual and art photography, open to Ukrainian citizens living in Ukraine or abroad who have no more than five years of active practice with the photographic medium — which MYPH defines as conscious, regular, consistent work in art photography, from making one's own projects and series to exhibitions, competitions, residencies, portfolio reviews, publication and engagement with the artistic community. Fine art, conceptual and documentary photography are all invited, and every photographic technique and form of visual manipulation is accepted, from analogue shooting to digital collage and experiment. Applicants submit a series or project of eight to ten photographs made in 2025 or 2026; ongoing projects are welcome, and last year's winners may enter with new work. The Grand Prix takes a Fujifilm X-series camera and lens, a 50,000 UAH MYPH tuition certificate, membership of the Ukrainian Association of Professional Photographers, and showings at Art Market Budapest and Art Kyiv Fair; second and third places take MYPH tuition certificates of 25,000 and 10,000 UAH rather than prize money, and a separate Fujifilm 'Best Debut' prize goes to an author showing a series publicly for the first time. Eight finalists exhibit together at Dymchuk Gallery in Kyiv, with the show travelling in Ukraine and abroad as part of MYPH Photo Festival, and partner prizes include a 15,000 UAH cash award for one woman photographer, print production, photobooks and further tuition certificates. Applicants must be 18 at the time of applying. Finalists are announced on 13 October 2026 and the winners at the exhibition ceremony on 23 October.
jury: Steve Bisson, Paris College of Art

calls.title: Fragments of the Everyday
calls.description: Exposure Photo Gallery's third open call invites photographers to submit images that find meaning in the world around us — places, people, gestures, scenes and moments, from the extraordinary to the seemingly ordinary. There is no single way to interpret the everyday: it can be found on a street or in a remote landscape, in a face, a piece of architecture, an object, a spontaneous scene or a deliberate composition; what matters is the photographer's perspective. The juror is Steve McCurry, the American photographer whose Afghan Girl is among the most recognisable photographs in the world and who has spent more than five decades portraying cultures, people and scenes of everyday life. Selected work is shown in a group exhibition at the gallery in Río Tercero, Córdoba: a Gold, a Silver and a Bronze Award, ten Honorable Mentions whose prints hang in the physical show, thirty-seven Juror's Selections shown digitally, and special recognitions reserved for photographers from Córdoba Province. The Gold Award winner also takes US$500 and a solo exhibition at the gallery, on a date arranged with the artist. Selected and winning works appear in a print-on-demand exhibition book, and an Online Gallery Special Recognition marks roughly the top 7.5 per cent of entries. All awards are issued as digital diplomas. Fees are tiered by image count and there is no cap on how many photographs may be submitted. Entries close 31 March 2027 at 11:59 PM Pacific time; winners are announced 3 May 2027 and hi-res files are due 14 May.

calls.description: The second edition of the S. L. Kirloskar CSR Foundation's annual grant for lens-based practitioners, supporting artists whose work interrogates contemporary relationships between people, environments and systems in an age of globalisation, digital saturation and cultural transformation. The Foundation frames photography and moving image not only as tools of representation but as instruments for questioning dominant narratives and creating new ones, and invites proposals engaging critically with sustainability and environment, science and innovation, biodiversity and nature, culture and heritage, or community and social change. Two recipients — one photographer and one moving-image artist — are selected by a jury, each receiving a production grant of INR 5 lakh, of which up to 35 per cent may be taken as an artist fee or honorarium, plus opportunities to show the completed project at Kirloskar Group premises and other venues across India. Applications are open to emerging practitioners working in documentary, conceptual, experimental or new media formats who reside in India and hold Indian citizenship; individuals and artist duos or collectives may apply. Submissions go by email and comprise a project proposal of up to 1,000 words, a 500-word artist statement, a portfolio of five to ten captioned images or videos as a PDF under 5 MB, a CV, a budget breakdown and a project timeline. Equipment purchases are not covered, though project-related consumables such as film, cards, ink and paper are. The project period runs 21 September 2026 to 21 March 2027, and copyright remains with the artist.

calls.title: Photographic Nights of Selma 2026
calls.description: The seventh edition of a festival founded by French photographer Stéphane Kossmann — who also founded Les Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert — in partnership with Foot Soldier Park and Arts Revive in Selma, Alabama. Around thirty selected artist projects are shown each evening on a giant outdoor screen, with daytime given over to exhibitions across the Selma area, encounters between photographers and the public, portfolio readings and conferences. There is no set theme: the artistic committee asks only for a unique perspective and a clearly asserted point of view in a series of fifteen to thirty photographs, and is looking for a broad panorama of recent work of all kinds — reflections on society, landscape, fashion, portraiture, still life, explorations of intimacy, or proposals diverging from the current zeitgeist. Selected series are presented as photo-sound montages of no more than four minutes; the festival's video and sound editors can build the montage, or photographers may submit their own edit, and an original soundtrack may be supplied. Each selected photographer commits to attending the evening of their screening and the following day; photographers stay in local homes for the duration, limited to fifteen places, with lunches covered by the festival and travel at the photographer's own expense. Prizes are awarded at the end by a jury of figures from photography and the arts and by the public, and the Jury Prize carries an invitation with travel expenses covered to the Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert in the south of France in the last week of July 2027. Applicants must declare any use of image-generation tools. The festival runs 6–7 November 2026 and access to exhibitions, screenings and conferences is free.

calls.title: Santu Mofokeng Foundation Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: A new national award from the Santu Mofokeng Foundation, established in honour of one of South Africa's most influential photographers and dedicated to recognising and supporting outstanding emerging photographers working in the country. Through a national open call the Foundation seeks artists whose work shows a thoughtful and compelling engagement with the photographic medium, reflecting the depth, sensitivity and critical awareness that characterised Mofokeng's own practice, and aims to provide recognition, visibility and professional support at a pivotal stage in a career. The inaugural award carries a R100,000 cash prize together with editorial support, an artist profile and opportunities for future exhibition presentation through the programmes of Latitudes, the Foundation's promotional and platform partner. Entry is open to independent practitioners living and working in South Africa; the application form sets an age ceiling of 45 and asks for a cohesive body of ten to fifteen photographs made within the past five years, alongside a portrait image, a recent biography and statements describing the applicant's practice, the submitted body of work and why they would be a strong recipient. The Foundation was established in 2015, when Mofokeng donated his photographic work and copyright to it, and works to preserve, research and share his legacy while supporting contemporary photographic practice through exhibitions, publications and public programmes. Applications close on 15 October 2026.

calls.title: 2027 Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: PS122 Gallery, the not-for-profit alternative exhibition space that has run out of the city-owned 122 Community Center in New York's East Village since 1979, invites proposals for its 2027 season. A three-person jury of arts professionals will select six curator- and/or artist-led exhibitions, each running for a month in the gallery's roughly 1,000 square foot space, with exhibitions scheduled across February, March, April, June, September and October 2027. Proposals must involve at least two artists working in any medium, and either the curator or the artists must live in one of the five New York City boroughs; collectives are encouraged, as are experimental uses of the space, in which case public programmes with an aesthetic component are welcomed but not required. Currently enrolled students are not eligible and each applicant is limited to one submission. The application is free and asks for a 500-word exhibition proposal, the names of the confirmed participating artists, a combined PDF of up to ten images of work, installation shots or a proposed layout with captions, and a combined PDF of CVs for everyone involved. Held annually since the 1986-87 season and restarted in 2023, the open call helped define the gallery's history: it gave early exhibitions to Peter Halley, Keith Haring and Amy Sillman, and the programme has shown Nan Goldin, Barbara Kruger, Louise Bourgeois, Glenn Ligon, Alfredo Jaar, Kiki Smith and David Wojnarowicz among hundreds of others. The gallery is a programme of Painting Space 122 Inc, an artist-run cooperative, and is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs. Applicants are notified in October 2026.

calls.title: Forum Box Open Call 2028
calls.description: Forum Box is an artist-run cooperative gallery on the Helsinki waterfront with roughly 300 square metres of exhibition space, and it is now taking proposals for its 2028 programme. Artists, curators and working groups may apply for the whole space or for one or two of its three rooms — Permanto (about 65 m², three continuous walls, 5.6 m ceiling), Monttu (about 70 m², divided by stairs) and Parvi (about 90 m², 4.2 m ceiling and the most wall space). The standard slot is five weeks including installation, and for 2028 shorter project-based exhibitions and performances can also be proposed. Selection is made by an exhibition working group of member artists together with the executive director, and every selected artist is offered a member of Forum Box as a peer contact through the process. Applying is free: a single PDF of no more than 4MB containing the gallery's application form, an exhibition or project plan of up to two A4 pages, CVs and around ten images of recent work, emailed by 1pm Finnish time on 7 September 2026. Exhibiting artists currently pay a space rent — €280 for four weeks in the whole gallery or €100 for one room, dropping to €125 and €70 for a single week — which covers communication, marketing, invigilation and sales handling, and the cooperative states it aims to be entirely rent-free by 2028 and has reduced rents every year since 2020; a 40% commission (plus VAT) applies to work sold. Two conditions are worth reading before applying: solo exhibitions carry a five-year minimum interval between shows at Forum Box, and artists may not hold a solo exhibition elsewhere in the Helsinki metropolitan area in the twelve months before their own. A separate, rent-free strand in the same application window seeks a proposal for the Lux Galleries programme of the Lux Helsinki light art festival, on view 30 December 2027 to 9 January 2028, for which the five-year interval does not apply. All applicants hear by the end of October 2026.

calls.title: The Fool's World Vol. 2.2
calls.description: The Fool's World is a small travel literary magazine of poetry, prose and visual art, launched by the team behind Raleigh Review, and its summer reading window closes on 1 September. The visual art category is open to photographers in two forms: up to five individual works submitted as separate files, or a single PDF photo essay or series of up to twelve images, sequenced in the order it should be published and unified in theme or style, with a short statement. The editors read travel broadly — 'a deliciously ambiguous term', in their words — and say the work may be inspired by travel, depict travel itself, or simply reflect movement, as long as the experience is the photographer's own. Only previously unpublished work is considered and AI-generated submissions are banned outright. Submissions are free through the magazine's Duosuma portal, and the team aims to respond within four to six weeks. Physical works should be photographed cleanly, without glare or visible canvas edges unless that is an intentional choice, and accepted work may be asked to be rephotographed to meet print standards.
calls.summary: Travel literary magazine reading photo essays and single images for its next issue. Free to submit, AI banned.

calls.description: The Indian Photo Festival invites photographers, visual storytellers, artists, curators, collectives, archives, galleries and organisations worldwide to submit work for the exhibitions of its 12th edition, held in Hyderabad from 26 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. Selected exhibition projects are professionally produced and exhibited by the festival at no cost to the participant, which bears the production costs of exhibition prints and display materials. calls.title: The Gift of Art 2026
calls.description: Hal Bromm established Tribeca's first contemporary gallery in 1975, showing early minimal and conceptual work by Carl Andre, Rosemarie Castoro, Victor Burgin and John Hilliard, and giving early solo exhibitions to Krzysztof Wodiczko, Keith Haring and David Wojnarowicz. The gallery shows photography as a matter of course: its summer 2026 exhibition photo·graph surveyed contemporary photographic practice with work by Bernd and Hilla Becher, Renate Aller, Slava Mogutin and others. Since the 1980s THE GIFT OF ART has been the gallery's annual holiday tradition, in which artists are invited to make unique, saleable artworks as ornaments to adorn the gallery tree - often with overtly political themes that challenged the usual sugar plums and Christmas angels. Last year's edition featured over 100 handmade ornaments by more than 60 artists from around the globe. For 2026 the gallery is expanding the show to include artist-made prints, so the work can live in a home year-round. Each artist may submit up to three ornaments and two prints, and may enter one or both categories. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis and artists are notified no later than 10 October 2026. Both ornaments and prints are for sale at the gallery throughout December, with 30% of proceeds going to Rehabilitation Through the Arts, which has run arts programming in New York prisons since 1996. The exhibition runs 1 to 19 December 2026.
calls.summary: Tribeca's first contemporary gallery invites ornaments and artist prints for its December show; 30% of sales fund prison arts.

calls.title: beauty
calls.description: A Smith Gallery's juried online exhibition on the theme of 'beauty' — grace, charm, refinement, allure, delicacy, elegance. Juror Wendi Schneider, a visual artist whose hand-gilded photographs are printed on vellum and Japanese kozo with precious metals applied to the verso, selects up to 47 images. Selected work is featured across the gallery's online exhibition, Facebook and Instagram, a GalleryTalk, the online store and an exhibition catalogue, with 27 images chosen for 'The 27' hardbound fine-art book. The Juror's Award and the Directors' Award each bring an online solo exhibition, 'The 27' and a feature on the gallery blog; a $100 Visitors' Award goes to the most Instagram likes. Jurying is blind — images are renamed and numbered before the juror sees them. Open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums; international entries are welcomed, work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible, and the gallery states it prefers not to accept images created with artificial intelligence while copyright questions remain unsettled. Entry is $40 for the first 5 images and $5 per additional image with no limit on the number submitted, and photographers entering 13 or more images receive a complimentary review from the gallery directors. Entries are due 28 September 2026, results are emailed 9 October, and the exhibition runs 16 October to 26 November 2026 with a reception on 31 October. The gallery retains 30% on sales.

calls.title: Small Works 2026
calls.description: The Winterville Cultural Center Gallery, in the renovated 1950s high school just outside Athens, Georgia, invites artists across the United States to submit small-scale work for its National Juried Small Works Exhibition 2026. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture, fiber and mixed media; no reproductions or giclees, and AI-generated artwork is not eligible. Work may not exceed 14 inches in any direction including the frame, and three-dimensional work may not exceed 14 inches in height, width or depth. Yu-Kai Lin, founder and director of Kai Lin Art in Atlanta, selects the exhibition and all three awards: Best in Show $500, Juror's Award $250 and a People's Choice Award of $100, $850 in cash in total. Up to three works may be entered for a single fee. Acceptances are sent September 12, shipped work is due September 23 and hand delivery runs September 24 to 26; the show opens to the public on October 7 with a reception on October 9 and closes December 15, 2026. All accepted work must be for sale for the run of the exhibition, with 65 percent of any sale to the artist and 35 percent to the gallery, and artists cover shipping both ways. Two-dimensional work must arrive framed and wired, with no sawtooth hangers. Entries are JPEG only, cropped to the artwork edges, 2 MB maximum.
jury: Yu-Kai Lin, Founder & Director, Kai Lin Art, Atlanta
calls.summary: National juried show of works 14 inches or under near Athens, Georgia. Photography named, $850 in cash awards, juried by Yu-Kai Lin of Kai Lin Art.

calls.title: Where I Sleep
calls.description: Forum 301 is a gallery and discussion space at 301 W. Ohio Street in Chicago's River North, built around open-ended forums that use exhibitions as a starting point for conversation between artists, scholars and students. For its September exhibition the gallery is seeking artists experimenting in the photographic medium. Where I Sleep presents artists who investigate the nuances of “home” through various photographic practices, each examining the complexities of connecting to a physical space, with the works drawing viewers to consider the isolated opportunities seated inside an individual's sense of home, including the potential to encourage memory, seeing and story. Accepted works include photographic prints, and the gallery explicitly encourages artists to think beyond a photo on a wall, whether that means projections, sculptural work, work in book form or something else. Four submissions are allowed for a single $20 fee, and applications are made through a form on the gallery's own site that asks for an artist statement or bio plus materials, dimensions and year for each work. Applications close August 23, 2026 and the exhibition runs September 4 to October 4, 2026.

calls.title: Anemone Vol. 1, No. 2
calls.description: Anemone is a print magazine published out of Bozeman, Montana by pulphead, a community writing and coffee space, and is built around what it calls the analog perspective: a framing rooted in continuity, tangibility, lived experience, slowness, emphasis on process and “grace for imperfection”, set against one of replicability, speed, binary outcomes and optimization. Its first issue came out in July 2026 and submissions are now open for Vol. 1, No. 2. Photography and visual art sit alongside short fiction, creative nonfiction, reportage and poetry as full submission categories, and the theme is stated broadly as the world as told by Montanans; all styles and all subjects are welcome, with the subject asked to evoke the themes, pitfalls, joys and moments of the day as best one reasonably can. Photographs must be unpublished, though exceptions are made for work self-published to an online portfolio or personal socials, and files are uploaded through a form on the magazine's own site as JPEG, JPG or PNG at 150 to 300 dpi and under 20 MB, accompanied by a single written document captioning each image with date, location, title, medium and inspiration. There is no submission fee. The magazine is emphatic about generative tools: “use AI to originate work and you will be choked out with a Full Nelson, then disqualified.” Contributors are paid — the guidelines state that no work will be published without net-ninety payment arranged from the date of publishing, at negotiated per-word or per-placement rates — and unselected work is held in a slushpile for possible use in a later edition.
calls.summary: Print-only Montana magazine open to photography for its second issue. No fee, contributors paid, and firmly anti-AI.

calls.title: Community Art Gallery — Fall 2026 Show
calls.description: The City of San Marcos established its Community Art Gallery in 2024 in the lobby of City Hall, as a space to share art with residents and visitors and to elevate the arts in the community. For the Fall 2026 show the city is accepting work from artists aged 18 and over living in Hays, Caldwell, Comal and Guadalupe Counties in central Texas. All two-dimensional and three-dimensional media that can be safely hung on the walls are eligible, so photography qualifies; the only content restrictions are that work for this family-friendly public venue must be apolitical, non-violent and G-rated, with no nudity even if tasteful and artistic. Applicants submit an artist bio and up to three artworks available for loan for the duration of the exhibition, sized between 8 by 10 inches and 24 by 36 inches and weighing no more than 30 pounds, arriving ready to hang with hardware installed. A three-member jury makes the selection and space is limited, so inclusion is not guaranteed. There is no entry fee. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, the gallery retains no commission, and any sale is conducted directly between artist and buyer. The submission window runs August 12 to 31, applications are reviewed September 1 to 9, artists are notified September 10, art intake is Saturday October 3 from 10am to 1.30pm, and the exhibit hangs from October 2026 through March 2027.
calls.summary: Free juried show in San Marcos City Hall's community gallery, hanging six months. Open to four central Texas counties.

calls.title: Candace Freeland Photography of Merit Award 2026
calls.description: A free, cash-funded photography award for young photographers, founded by the photojournalist Candace Freeland (1952-2021) — an Associated Press, Charlotte Observer, New York Times and Washington Post contributor whose exhibitions included Forced Out: The Agony of the Refugee in Our Time for Amnesty International — and now run by The Mitford Museum in Hudson, North Carolina, the museum founded by her mother, the novelist Jan Karon. US residents aged 8 to 22 are invited to submit photographs made on a cell phone on the theme Food and Family. There are two categories, colour and black and white, judged in two age groups, 8-15 and 16-22; you may enter one photograph in each category provided the two images are markedly different, and entering both still leaves you eligible for only one juried award. Files must be high resolution and able to resize to an 11 by 14 inch print. The jurors are Maggie Flanigan, director of the AFA Visual Arts programme at Caldwell Community College, whose own lens-based work looks at religion and community in the rural South; Tim Barnwell, an Asheville photographer with work in the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Asheville Art Museum; and Tom Rankin, who heads Duke University's MFA in Experimental and Documentary Arts. Each of the four category-and-age-group slots carries a $500 Grand Prize, a $250 Runner-Up and a $250 People's Choice voted by the public, and the museum runs free smartphone photography workshops in the run-up. Winners are announced at a reception on 9 October 2026. Note that the museum's two surfaces disagree: its Merit Awards page gives a 1 November deadline and a $750 top prize for the 16-22 group, while the official rules attached to the entry form give 1 September, $500 across all four slots, and the October reception. The form is the document entrants agree to, so enter by 1 September.
jury: Maggie Flanigan, Director, AFA Visual Arts, Caldwell Community College
Tim Barnwell, photographer and instructor, Asheville
Tom Rankin, Professor of the Practice, Duke University
calls.summary: Free cash award for US photographers aged 8-22 — cell phone photos on Food and Family, judged by a serious panel.

calls.title: Midwest Regional 2027
calls.description: Artlink's annual juried group exhibition for artists living in the American Midwest, open to any medium and any size and shown across the gallery's main space. Artlink is a nonprofit contemporary gallery in the Auer Center for Arts & Culture in downtown Fort Wayne, running since 1978 and funded in part by Arts United and the Indiana Arts Commission. Eligible states are Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska and Kansas; entrants must be 18 or over, and work must have been made in the last five years and not shown at Artlink before. Reproductions are not accepted. Entry is $12 per work with a limit of ten entries, and the juror gives three cash awards for first, second and third place — Artlink does not publish the amounts. Accepted work must arrive ready to install, framed pieces included, and anything damaged or differing from what was accepted may be turned away. A 35% sales fee applies to work sold, with artists paid by cheque after the show closes; work is insured while at the gallery but not in transit. The exhibition runs 7 January to 7 February 2027, opening with a reception on 7 January from 5 to 8pm.
calls.summary: Artlink's annual juried show for artists across twelve Midwest states — any medium, $12 an entry, three cash awards.

calls.title: Freezer Festival 2026 Open Call — Lo Real
calls.fee: $12 / €10 (free for UNLP photography students and staff)
calls.description: The third edition of Argentina's Freezer festival takes Lo real — the real, or something real — as its theme, asking what survives of photography's claim on reality in a world saturated with digital simulation. The call selects one artist for a solo exhibition in La Plata, ten photographers whose single images are shown in venues across the city, and twenty photographic projects presented as one-to-five-minute audiovisual pieces. Selected work joins the official November 2026 programme across La Plata, Berisso, Ensenada and Buenos Aires alongside national and international artists, with production support for the solo show and promotion through the festival's press and platforms. This edition also forms part of the 8th Biennial of Art and Culture of the Universidad Nacional de La Plata, marking fifty years since the 1976 dictatorship, and the organisers explicitly invite work on archives, material memory and the histories that resist erasure. Open to photographers, visual artists and collectives of any nationality; submit up to fifteen photographs. Entry is a symbolic $12 USD or €10 by PayPal, waived for photography students and teachers at FDA UNLP and for retirees resident in Argentina.
calls.summary: Argentina's Freezer festival picks one solo show, ten single images and twenty audiovisual projects on the theme Lo real.

calls.title: The Power of the ARTS — 8th Annual Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Marion Cultural Alliance marks twenty-five years of championing artists in Marion County with a juried exhibition about the arts themselves — a favourite discipline, a memorable performance, a beloved book, an inspiring mentor. Artists of all levels working in all media are invited, photography included, and interpretations may be realistic or abstract, traditional or contemporary. The show hangs at the Brick City Center for the Arts from 2 to 31 October 2026, opening with a reception on 2 October where the juror's awards are presented: $250 Best of Show, $150 first, $100 second, $50 third and two honorable mentions, alongside an MCA 25th Anniversary Award, a LILAC Foundation Purchase Award, executive staff recognitions and a Community Choice Award decided by public ribbon voting. Up to two original works per artist, suggested maximum forty inches in any direction, gallery-ready; no prints, reproductions or work previously shown at the Brick. All accepted work must be for sale, split 70 percent to the artist and 30 percent to MCA. An active MCA artist membership is required to participate, from $35 a year, and work is dropped off and collected in person in Ocala.
calls.summary: MCA's 25th-anniversary juried show on the arts themselves — all media, $250 Best of Show, at the Brick City Center for the Arts.

calls.title: Alaska AIR Artist in Residence 2027–2028
calls.description: Bunnell Street Arts Center, a multidisciplinary non-profit founded in 1991 in a historic Trading Post building in Homer, Alaska, runs Alaska AIR: juried, fully funded residencies of generally one month, scheduled across the Alaskan fall, winter and spring of 2027 and 2028. One to four are awarded annually, and each carries a $2,000 stipend for a month (pro-rated if shorter), round-trip travel to Homer up to $1,000 in value, a $250 materials stipend and a private bedroom with private bath in a shared apartment above the arts centre or nearby in the Old Town neighbourhood. The studio is Bunnell's 1,000 sq ft main exhibition gallery, open to the public during gallery hours, and the equipment list includes a darkroom (no enlarger), an HD video camera and tripod, an HD/3D projector, a nipping press and a small printing press. Bunnell accepts artists working in mediums "including (but not limited to) visual arts, literary arts, performing arts, social and civic practice, ephemeral art, moving image, movement and dance, music composition and performance", and looks for a clear, unified body of work alongside a specific proposal with a strong community engagement component — collective art-making, an Artist in Schools programme, a workshop, an exhibit, screening or reading. Residents generally give an introductory artist talk plus that community component. Open to international, US and Alaska artists; applications are accepted 1 September to 15 October and applicants are notified by 31 December. The $25 application fee can be waived on a needs basis by emailing the programme before applying.
jury: Prior artists in residence, community members, and Bunnell staff and board

calls.title: Art at Emerson Hall: An Emerging Artist Community Showcase
calls.description: Emerson Hall was built in 1870 as a Universalist church and named for Ralph Waldo Emerson; it is a rare surviving example of English Country Gothic architecture, with stained glass, a curving loft and an exposed-beam cathedral ceiling, sitting on the National Register of Historic Places at the corner of Forest and Bedford Streets in downtown Stamford. The Emerson Hall Foundation, incorporated in 2023 to keep the building working as a venue for artists, musicians and educators, is filling it for three days with the work of eight to ten local emerging artists. The organisers are explicit about who they want: artists with little to no prior exhibition experience — "If you've never had a 'real' show before, this is your moment." Painting, drawing, sculpture, photography, textiles and jewellery are all accepted for review. Applicants must be based in the Greater Stamford area and be 16 or older, with parent or guardian permission required under 18. There is no entry fee and applications close 15 August 2026. Work is chosen by a four-person selection committee of Stamford-area artists and educators, and the programme is presented with the Unitarian Universalist Congregation in Stamford with support from a City of Stamford Arts & Culture Commission grant.
calls.summary: A free three-day showcase in an 1870 Gothic hall for 8-10 Stamford-area emerging artists with little or no exhibition history.

calls.title: Between Here and There
calls.description: The Greenwich Art Society's annual member exhibition is juried this year by Antonia Pocock, a curatorial assistant at the Whitney Museum of American Art, who organised Claes Oldenburg: Drawn from Life and has written for Art in America, Texte zur Kunst and Nka. The theme is the space between where we were, where we are and where we are going — physical, emotional, personal or imagined — and the society invites work reading it as movement, memory, transformation, discovery or simply a moment of pause. Photography is a named category alongside painting, drawing, pastel, watercolour, sculpture, original digital art, fibre arts, traditional printmaking, mixed media and collage; digital prints of original art and AI-generated work are excluded, and entrants confirm the work is their own and not AI-generated. Work must have been completed in 2023 or later and must not have been shown before in the Bendheim, Flinn or GAS Galleries or accepted into a previous GAS juried exhibition. Wall works are limited to 36 inches wide by 60 inches high framed or unframed, wired and ready to hang. Entering makes you a member of the society through August 2027: $75 covers membership plus one or two pieces, $100 covers three. Over $2,000 in cash and other awards is presented at the closing reception. Accepted work is posted on 10 October 2026, drop-off is 17-18 October, and the exhibition runs 22 October to 19 November 2026 at the Bendheim Gallery in Greenwich. All work must be for sale, with 30 per cent of each sale divided between GAS and the Bendheim Gallery.
jury: Antonia Pocock, Curatorial Assistant, Whitney Museum of American Art

calls.title: SELF PORTRAIT Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Decode Gallery invites photographers worldwide to submit their best self portrait work for a themed gallery show in Tucson, Arizona. The gallery frames self portraiture as an exploration of identity and an intimate glimpse into the life of the artist, and is looking for work that reveals a story rather than simply records a likeness. At least twenty-six images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode Gallery after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper, and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats in a range of sizes. Submitted files are never cropped, only scaled for the best fit in the mat. One print is made per accepted image and archived in a flat file for two years after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs, open to amateurs and professionals alike. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due two days later. The exhibition runs November 7 to 28, 2026, opening on November 7. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with the gallery taking a 50 per cent commission and all rights to the file and print remaining with the photographer.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder

calls.title: HUMOROUS: The Art of Laughter
calls.description: The Armory Art Center's juried gallery exhibition for Florida-based artists, hung alongside the tenth annual Creative Market on its historic West Palm Beach campus in Howard Park. The theme is humour in all its registers: playful portraiture and caricature, visual puns and wordplay, absurd and surreal scenes, comics and graphic narratives, everyday life with a twist, pop-culture and nostalgia parody, and animal antics. The Armory argues that humour in art does more than amuse, that it shifts perspectives, crosses language and cultural lines, and gives satire a way to critique politics and social norms. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside oil, acrylic, water media, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fibre, wood, ceramics and digital art; AI-generated work is not accepted, and diptychs and triptychs must be uploaded as a single image. Entry is $43 plus processing for up to two pieces, each judged individually, so the jury may take neither, one or both. The show is curated and juried by Armory staff with an anonymous juror, and first, second and third awards are given. Open to amateur and professional artists eighteen and over living in Florida. Notification is by October 16 and the exhibition runs November 2 to December 26, 2026 with a reception on November 19. All work must be for sale, with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and artists cover shipping both ways.
jury: Armory Art Center staff with an anonymous juror

calls.title: 2027 Exhibition Proposals
calls.description: The City of San Rafael invites artists, groups and organisations to propose exhibitions for the 2027 calendar at two civic venues: Falkirk Cultural Center, an 1888 Queen Anne mansion on the National Historic Register whose three second-floor rooms have shown art since the City took it on in 1974, and the recently renovated San Rafael Downtown Library, one of California's Carnegie libraries, open again after a restoration that preserved the 1909 building. Falkirk hosts five or six exhibits a year, each running roughly six weeks, with most openings timed to the Downtown San Rafael Second Friday Art Walk. Proposals are judged on community interest, quality of work and a track record of achievement, and applicants are asked to show they can curate an exhibit large enough to fill one gallery room at Falkirk or the Library's display shelves, which are built for three-dimensional work. There is no medium restriction and no residency requirement stated. Proposals go first to City staff, then to the Public Art Review Board in October, and selected proposals move into a contract. Exhibitors handle their own transport, installation, take-down, title cards and opening reception, and provide images good enough for the City to build a virtual version of the show for accessibility; the City provides staffing during open hours, show cards and promotion. Sales run through the City on a 70/30 split in the artist's favour. Application is $5 through CaFE.
jury: City of San Rafael staff and the Public Art Review Board

calls.title: Nocturne: Photography After Dark
calls.description: International juried online exhibition on the night — what becomes visible once daylight recedes and darkness, limited visibility and artificial light reshape the world. Streetlights isolating gestures, windows glowing against dark buildings, long exposures stretching time, flash revealing what the eye would miss; beyond the city, moonlight, stars, weather and deep shadow remaking the landscape. Urban night photography, nocturnal landscapes, astrophotography, nightlife, interiors, staged scenes, low-light portraits, light painting and experimental work are all welcome, with night read as a physical setting, a psychological condition or simply a space where ordinary life behaves differently. Digital, film, alternative process, documentary, fine art, conceptual and mixed-media photographic work accepted. Blind review wherever possible, with emphasis on the work rather than biography or exhibition history; approximately 30 images are selected for the curated online exhibition and permanent website archive, running 1–21 November 2026. Fee waivers are offered on the honour system for artists experiencing financial hardship.

calls.description: Submit up to 5 images on the theme of environmental wildlife — animals shown in the context of the landscape they live in — for the 'One Thing This Month' reader competition (OP 333) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). The winner receives a Cumulus Moonrain Jacket (RRP £325). Entries need captions of up to 75 words covering where, why and how each image was taken, plus full technical details in the magazine's stated order (camera and lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture, tripod or handheld). The magazine publishes work taken outside in the landscape, wildlife, nature, adventure and travel genres, and asks that images be made ethically and with sensitivity to environmental and conservation issues.

calls.title: Create! Magazine Issue #60 — The Artist's World
calls.description: Open call for Issue No. 60 of Create! Magazine, an artist-led print and digital publication for contemporary art. The theme, The Artist's World, asks what it means to build a world as an artist — a universe made through the work, an independent practice that makes its own opportunities, or simply inhabiting the planet; the brief is open to all interpretations and all subjects and media are welcome, photography among them. Juried by Marina Granger, founder of the New York advisory The Artist Advisory, former guest curator of the magazine's 2024 Women's Print Issue and curator of Lunation at Warnes Contemporary and The Feminine Divine at Kaliner Gallery. Selected artists receive a four-page spread in the print and digital editions, website and social features, and a complimentary digital issue. Submit up to 10 works (cohesive bodies and series encouraged) with a 300-word bio and artist statement; $35 covers three images. Open to artists worldwide with no academic background required, and there are no further fees if published.
jury: Marina Granger, founder of The Artist Advisory, New York

calls.title: XIV «Galicia» Award of Contemporary Photography
calls.description: The fourteenth edition of the Premio «Galicia» de Fotografía Contemporánea, founded in 2013 within the International Outono Fotográfico Festival and run by the Asociación OF. Outono Fotográfico with the Xunta de Galicia, the Deputación de Lugo and the University of Vigo's Ourense campus. It seeks complete photographic projects on a free theme, judged above all on how they sit within the discourse of contemporary photography, and is open to any author working with photography or the photographic regardless of nationality. Two awards are made from the same pool of entries. The Jury Prize produces an exhibition of the winning project with a curator appointed by the association, opening in Lugo and touring Galicia and Portugal for two years before the exhibition becomes the artist's property, plus a book in the "Galicia Contemporary Photography Prize" series from Difusora de Letras, Artes e Ideas, distributed in bookshops with a percentage of the print run to the author. The Organisation Prize produces a comparable exhibition at the Alterarte Gallery on the Ourense campus with an accompanying booklet. Projects must have been made between October 2016 and October 2026 and must not have been fully funded by another competition or published in full. Submit up to 15 images (minimum 3,000 px on the long side) with a synopsis of up to 2,500 characters and a 1,500-character biography. Entry costs €22 per project.

calls.title: Emergency Grants
calls.description: Created in 1993, the Foundation for Contemporary Arts' Emergency Grants provide urgent, project-based funding to visual and performing artists and poets who have sudden, unanticipated opportunities to present their work to the public with insufficient time to seek other funding, or who incur unexpected or unbudgeted expenses for projects close to completion with committed exhibition dates. FCA receives around 100 applications a month and makes roughly 15 to 20 grants of $500 to $3,000 each; applicants may request any amount in that range and the average grant is currently $2,200. The panel is made up of established practising artists from the disciplines FCA supports and meets monthly, weighing the urgency of the request, the significance of the opportunity, the impact the money would have and the strength of the work samples. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, and the foundation's mission is explicitly to support experimental and contemporary practice. Applicants must have a US Tax ID, must be individual artists rather than curators, producers or organisations, must have a confirmed presentation with specific dates at the time of applying, and must not be enrolled in any degree-granting programme. FCA asks that artists apply eight to ten weeks before the public presentation date. Grants may cover artist fees, airfare, accommodation, materials, shipping, fabrication and production; work-in-progress showings, projects presented by commercial galleries or art fairs, and any opportunity that requires the artist to pay to participate are not eligible.

calls.title: States — Open Call 2026
calls.description: The Belarusian Association of Photographers (BAP) invites photographers to its open call «States», framed by the organisers as "more than the emotions of one person — a frame, a canvas, a boundary and a portal at once". The call asks photographers to stop and consider how the world is refracted inside a person through what they live through, both literal and metaphorical, and to look at those inner worlds without black and white — in all their shades, colours, reflections and registers of perception. What interests the organisers is not only what a person feels but what brings them into that state, how it alters their perception of the world around them, and how that world is itself able to immerse a person in particular states. No genre, style or manner of interpreting the theme is prescribed: documentary story, portrait, autobiographical statement, observation of an environment, conceptual series or a visual investigation of a social phenomenon are all welcome, provided the work carries the author's own vision of a state and its connection to person and world. Entries go into one of two categories — Solo, a single self-standing image, or Series, four to ten photographs held together by one idea, theme or visual concept and read as a single statement. Work must have been made no earlier than 2024, files are JPEG at a minimum 4000 px on the long side and up to 5 MB, and a description of up to 300 words covering a short biography, the title, the work itself and its relation to the theme must accompany the application. Works created entirely with generative neural networks are not accepted. Entry is free and one person may submit a single application in one category. Selected authors become participants in the project's final exhibition, which opens on 26 September 2026 in Zhodishki, Belarus. Applications are sent by email with «Состояния» in the subject line; finalists are announced on 12 September 2026.
calls.summary: Free Belarus-wide open call on inner states — solo image or 4–10 series, exhibition in Zhodishki from 26 September.

calls.title: BEERS London 40-Day Residency
calls.fee: £20 (£25 with the group exhibition open call)
calls.description: BEERS London runs a rolling, year-round 40-Day Residency for artists working in any medium, based in the UK or internationally, who are able to come to London. For forty days a selected artist receives studio and work space, an honorarium towards lodging, flight and materials, curatorial and professional development support, and the freedom to shape their own working schedule; the programme is designed to balance focused studio time with studio visits, professional development and optional public engagement, and concludes with a public presentation or exhibition of the work developed during the residency. Selected artists also receive professional documentation of finished works and promotion through the gallery's mailing list and social channels. Between two and four residency sessions are held each year and there is no application deadline: once submitted, an application stays valid for twelve months and is considered for every residency scheduled in that period, after which an artist may reapply. Applications are reviewed by the BEERS London team and guest curators on quality, clarity of proposal and feasibility, up to five artworks may be uploaded, and shortlisted applicants are contacted by email. The application fee is £20, or £25 if applying concurrently to the gallery's open call group exhibition; the gallery states the fee covers administration, selection review, platform and processing costs and does not guarantee acceptance. Participation does not guarantee representation or sales, and a standard 50/50 commission applies to any work sold. The inaugural resident, announced for the spring 2026 session, was the painter Georgia Dymock, whose residency closed with a solo exhibition in July 2026.
jury: BEERS London team and guest curators

calls.title: Rawhead & Bloody Bones — Halloween Special Issue
calls.description: Rawhead is an independent online journal of poetry, fiction, nonfiction and visual art, named after one of the folkloric bogeymen once used to frighten children into obedience. It is not a horror publication, but it is interested in work that unsettles through emotional depth, sharp craft and surprising clarity, and it reads the arts as a form of resistance. In folklore Rawhead is half of a monstrous duo, Rawhead & Bloody Bones, and every year in time for Halloween the journal teams up with the other half of its namesake for a special issue celebrating that myth. Submissions for Bloody Bones are open from August 15th to October 1st. The editors are seeking work that explores shadowed corners of being — ghosts, folklore, grief, hunger, rage, queerness, transformation — with monsters as metaphor or as real as the artist needs them to be. Poetry, prose, hybrid work and visual art are all welcome, and submission standards are the same as for regular issues: the visual art category takes three to ten pieces in any medium, explicitly including photography alongside illustration, digital collage, mixed media, painting and sculpture, uploaded as high-quality images of at least 1500px. The art editor's standing brief is work that explores the delicate threshold between fear and beauty rather than horror or gore, citing Louise Bourgeois, Francis Bacon, Man Ray, Joseba Eskubi, Anna Weyant and Jinyoung Yu as touchstones. Submission is free and the journal states it is committed to always offering free submissions to all writers and artists, with optional paid expedited and priority response tiers that have no bearing on editorial decisions. Simultaneous submissions are accepted, and previously published work is welcome where rights have reverted and at least six months have passed. AI-generated content is not accepted. Rawhead actively seeks submissions from creators of all backgrounds and lived experiences, naming BIPOC, Indigenous, refugee and diaspora, LGBTQIA2S+, disabled, neurodivergent, incarcerated and economically precarious creators among others.
calls.summary: Rawhead's annual Halloween special issue reads photography on ghosts, folklore, grief and transformation. Free.

calls.title: Flanelle Print No. 48 — October 2026
calls.description: Flanelle is a Montreal-based fashion, arts and culture magazine founded in 2012, known for raw editorials, a heavily image-led approach and a coffee-table production standard on quality paper. It publishes quarterly — January, April, July and October — in both print-on-demand and digital editions, distributed internationally, and its pages are built from editorial contributions by independent photographers. Print No. 48 publishes in October 2026 and is open to photographers, artists and designers worldwide. Each photo set should include a minimum of ten photographs following the issue's theme and mood board, and editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle; for fashion and beauty editorials the magazine asks for at least three looks and six photographs, with full team and wardrobe credits entered at submission. Review runs in two phases: an initial decision on submission, then a second round about a week before the deadline, so the magazine advises submitting closer to the deadline rather than early. Standard print submission is free. Optional paid upgrades exist for cover placement, advertorials and priority publishing, and the magazine charges a $20 revision fee for credit corrections after submission and a $100 fee to withdraw a series once it has been accepted into print. Selected work appears in the quarterly print issue and digital edition, with possible exposure across the magazine's social channels; published teams receive a free digital version on request.
calls.summary: Montreal fashion and arts quarterly, est. 2012. Free to submit for the October print issue; 10+ image editorials.

calls.title: Art & Noise
calls.org: Women's Caucus for Art of Greater Washington, DC
calls.description: The Washington, DC chapter of the Women's Caucus for Art invites women and non-binary artists based in DC, Maryland or Virginia to make work about how sound and silence shape a creative life. The premise is the music blasting in a studio, the ambient hush of a museum, the rhythm and harmony artists reach for without words. Photography is named among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, fiber work, mixed media and free-standing sculpture; commercially produced prints, giclees, jewellery and performance are not accepted, and video or film needing an external power source is considered case by case. Work is juried by LaPrea Rich, an abstract expressionist from Prince George's County, Maryland who has shown in more than twenty juried exhibitions since 2023 and is a member of the Arlington Artists Alliance, the Maryland Federation of Art and the McLean Art Society. Selected work hangs at the Harmony Hall Arts Center in Fort Washington, Maryland from November 30, 2026 to January 9, 2027, with an artist reception on December 5. Two-dimensional work must be no larger than 72 inches in any direction including its frame and must arrive exhibition-ready with wire and D-rings; sawtooth hangers are refused. Harmony Hall takes 25 percent of any sale and WCADC takes no commission. The chapter is entirely volunteer-run and directs entry fees to its Visual Arts Scholarship and to artist relief.

calls.title: Raw Blood and Nerve — Artist Showcase
calls.description: Dickinson Publishing Group is a small horror fiction imprint working out of Brooklyn, New York. It is launching a magazine called Raw Blood and Nerve that will carry short fiction alongside one section per issue given over entirely to a single artist's work, and this open call is for that section. Giger and Junji Ito on the other, with the editor cheerfully admitting to being a layman about art-historical precision. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside painting, sketch and graphite drawing. Between five and twelve pieces may be submitted, one entry per artist, and there is no fee. Work made with AI is refused outright, and the imprint states that an AI submission will cost the artist consideration of any future submission as well.

calls.title: 2026 Members Show
calls.description: Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts brings its annual Members Show back in person for a second year. The top fifty selected works go up on the gallery's Community Walls in Portland, with a broader selection of submitted work shown on the Blue Sky website. There is no theme: the gallery asks only for your best work. Any Blue Sky member in current good standing may submit up to three high-resolution images, one submission per artist, with an optional artist statement of up to 100 words about your practice. Membership is not a closed gate — the call page links straight to Blue Sky's join page, and the $50 Champion tier lists eligibility to submit to the Annual Members Exhibition among its benefits, so any photographer can become eligible by joining. The exhibition opens Thursday, October 1 at 5 PM. Blue Sky is a non-profit founded in 1975 by a group of five young photographers as the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, now in its fiftieth-anniversary year, and the Members Show is the point in its calendar where the membership itself gets the walls.
calls.prize: Exhibition on Blue Sky's Community Walls
calls.summary: Blue Sky's annual members show returns in person; top 50 works on the Community Walls in Portland. Free to enter with membership.

calls.title: A Latin America & Caribbean Exhibition
calls.description: The Stamford Art Association's second annual Latin America and Caribbean show, presented at the Townhouse Gallery in Stamford and online on the SAA website. The theme is open to all media and all interpretations, and the association is explicit that you do not need to be of Latin American or Caribbean descent to enter: submissions are open to anyone whose work engages with or is inspired by these regions and themes. Up to nine works may be submitted. The returning juror is Valeria Ochoa, SAA's gallery manager and board secretary, a literature and language educator with an MA in linguistics and an MA in curriculum and instruction who works in Norwalk Public Schools; a first-generation Colombian, she writes and photographs around ancestry, roots and lineage and their ties to land and belonging. Work must be original and not previously shown at the SAA gallery, no larger than 48 by 60 inches framed, wired for hanging and hand delivered — there is no shipping option, with receiving on September 18 and 19 and pickup on October 23 and 24. Photographs are exempt from the rule requiring prints to be signed and numbered as a limited edition; giclees are not accepted. The gallery takes 30 percent commission on work sold. The show runs September 24 to October 22, 2026, opening Thursday September 24, 5:30 to 7 PM.
jury: Valeria Ochoa, Gallery Manager and Board Secretary, Stamford Art Association
calls.summary: SAA's second annual Latin America and Caribbean show at the Townhouse Gallery. Open theme, any medium, juried by Valeria Ochoa.

calls.title: BBA Artist Prize 2027
calls.description: BBA Gallery's flagship all-media prize, running since 2018 and open to anyone eighteen or over working in any medium, photography included. There is no theme and no restriction on training, nationality or career stage; the only structural bar is that entrants must not be under an exclusive gallery contract, and that artists already represented by BBA are ineligible. Entrants submit up to five works with a statement of no more than 300 words and a CV. A jury of industry professionals selects a longlist of fifty artists, who are promoted by the gallery and receive a certificate of nomination, and from those fifty a shortlist of twenty who exhibit at BBA Gallery in Berlin. First prize is €1,000 with a solo exhibition at BBA Gallery, an Artsy profile and press, newsletter and social promotion; second is €700, third €500, and an Audience Award carries €300, each with an Artsy profile and promotion. Past first-prize winners include Jaroslav Drazil of Austria, Chung-Kun Wang of Taiwan, Dominik Adamec of the Czech Republic and László Máthé of Romania. Entry is through the BBA Prizes platform, where earlybird access is already open and work can be uploaded at any point before the deadline.
calls.summary: BBA Gallery Berlin's all-media prize, photography eligible. €1,000 and a solo show to the winner; 20 shortlisted artists exhibit.

calls.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Best Portfolio 2027
calls.description: Blank Wall Gallery's annual international portfolio contest, run to find and promote a single photographer rather than a single strong image. The winner receives a two-week solo exhibition at the gallery's new premises in Athens, with Blank Wall producing and financing up to 40 prints (40x50cm and 50x70cm) in its own labs at no cost to the artist, and covering everything else needed to stage the show even if the photographer cannot attend. The gallery sends newsletter invitations to its full contact list, issues a personalised press release to magazines, presents the exhibition on its website alongside its other solo shows, and afterwards compiles a detailed folder of publications, installation photographs, posters and other material and sends it to the artist. The winner also receives a certificate of achievement and a free entry to the following year's competition. Two further portfolios receive certificates of honourable mention and the right to submit ten photographs to one of Blank Wall's group contests, and every entrant gets a 25% discount on prints made at the gallery lab through the end of 2027. Entry is open to amateurs and professionals over 18; each artist may submit up to three portfolios of 10 to 20 photographs each. Submission is by email, WeTransfer or Dropbox after paying the fee.
calls.summary: Athens gallery's annual portfolio prize: a two-week solo show with 40 prints produced free, worth over €2,200.

calls.description: 17th annual juried international exhibition of fine art photography at Perspective Gallery, a not-for-profit photography cooperative in Evanston, Illinois. All subject matter and photographic processes are welcome except AI, and the call is open to photographers nationally and internationally. Juried by Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director and Curator of the Houston Center for Photography and previously Dean and Managing Director of Education at the International Center of Photography in New York. Exhibition March 4-28, 2027, with an opening reception and awards March 6 and a virtual artists' talk March 11. Artists receive 60% of the sale price of any work sold. The entry window opens 23 September 2026 — the gallery's prospectus states the date only inside its fee line ("Early Bird Submission ($35) opens on September 23"), and the portal is closed to entrants until then.

calls.title: Relative Impulse
calls.org: Joseph Gross Gallery, University of Arizona
calls.description: A free open call from the Joseph Gross Gallery, the 2,000-square-foot contemporary space inside the University of Arizona School of Art in Tucson, next door to the University of Arizona Museum of Art. Relative Impulse features artworks for which the making — or destroying — of family archives is material and metaphor: "Funny, heart-wrenching, or bizarre, using the ephemera of memory itself or a copy of a copy, each artwork reminds us that everything's relative." Artists of any career stage and any media or material process are eligible, and work made at any time qualifies; up to three artworks may be submitted, each on its own form with two to four images, and there are no size restrictions. Curated by gallery director lydia see, with jurying, preparation, installation and marketing handled by the School of Art's Gallery Praxis class and its student gallery managers. There is no entry fee, but selected artists ship or hand-deliver their own work and provide a return shipping label — the gallery says shipping assistance may be available to artists for whom the cost would be a barrier to exhibiting. Notifications go out 8 September, work must arrive by 29 September, the exhibition runs 13 October 2026 to 28 January 2027 with a reception on 22 October, and packages are mailed back by 10 February 2027. Current University of Arizona students, staff and faculty may also submit. No living or organic matter may be exhibited, and selected works cannot be withdrawn before the exhibition closes.
jury: lydia see, Curator and Gallery Director
Gallery Praxis class and student gallery managers, University of Arizona School of Art
calls.summary: Free University of Arizona gallery show on family archives as material and metaphor — any medium, no size limit, 3-month run.

calls.title: Misfits & Mayhem
calls.description: The Denison Arts Council closes its exhibition year at 517 Gallery in the downtown Denison Cultural Arts District in north Texas with the one show on its calendar that has no theme at all. Misfits & Mayhem opens the doors to “the artists and artworks which didn’t quite mesh with the themes of our previous shows” — the council writes that any size, medium, subject matter and style is welcome, and pitches it as a chance for emerging artists to test the waters and for established artists to show something they haven’t previously had the chance to show. Applications are made through a Google Form linked from the call page, which states plainly: “There is no fee for submission or participation in the exhibition.” The gallery keeps a 20% commission on work sold. Artists may enter 2-D wall pieces or prints, with limited shelf and pedestal space for 3-D work, plus small low-priced pieces for the gallery boutique. Work must arrive wired and ready to hang — sawtooth hangers are not accepted, though staff will wire a piece for $10 — and must be the artist’s own original or a reproduction of their own work; AI-generated images are not eligible. Selected artists complete a W-9. The gallery committee responds on 16 October, work is dropped off on 8 November, and the exhibition opens with a reception on 14 November from 4 to 6 pm, has a midway reception on 12 December, and closes on 3 January 2027 when artists collect their work.
calls.summary: No-theme, no-fee group show at Denison's 517 Gallery in Texas — any medium, any size, a two-month run over the holidays.

calls.title: 42nd Annual International Exhibition
calls.description: The Department of Art and Art History at The University of Texas at Tyler runs one of the longest-running juried competitions in the region, now in its 42nd year, shown at the university's Meadows Gallery. The 2027 edition is juried by Diana Roberts, an arts writer, curator and arts administrator in San Antonio who has been Director of The Center for Spirituality and the Arts, Curator of the Airport Art Spaces at San Antonio International Airport, and Gallery Director for Galeria Ortiz Contemporary. The call is explicitly open to two-dimensional media, and photographs are named alongside paintings, drawings, prints and fiber art; work must have been made in the last three years. Awards take the form of purchase awards: the department buys three to six works from the exhibition each year and adds them to its permanent collection, much of which hangs across the UT Tyler campus as a teaching resource. Entry is $35 for up to three works, judged from digital files; the CaFE entry window opens on 24 August 2026. Framed works must use Plexiglass rather than glass and weigh under 50 pounds; artists cover shipping both ways and must include a pre-paid return label. Notification is 14 December 2026, work is due at the gallery by 8 January 2027, and the exhibition runs 19 January to 5 March 2027 with a reception and juror's presentation on 4 March.
jury: Diana Roberts, curator and arts writer, San Antonio

calls.title: Solastalgia — 16th Annual International Juried Exhibition
calls.org: A.D. Gallery, University of North Carolina at Pembroke
calls.description: The A.D. Gallery at UNC Pembroke builds its 16th annual international juried exhibition around solastalgia — the term coined by philosopher Glenn Albrecht for the distress caused by environmental change experienced while still living in the place that is changing. The gallery describes it as "a form of homesickness felt without ever leaving home: the grief of watching a familiar landscape change around you — receding shorelines, vanishing species, drought-cracked earth, wildfire smoke over childhood streets, development replacing the sounds of nature." Interpretations may be personal, political, poetic, documentary, speculative or abstract, and suggested threads include loss of place-identity to climate change or extraction, memory and landscape as before/after, solastalgia as distinct from nostalgia, collective environmental grief, and Indigenous and generational knowledge of land in flux. Two-dimensional and three-dimensional works, installations and digital media including video up to five minutes are all eligible. Juror Carla Rokes is an artist and educator originally from the Carolinas with a BFA from UNC Charlotte and an MFA from Pratt Institute. Prizes are $400, $200 and $100. Entry is $35 for up to three works, with an artist statement on how the work engages the theme and a one-page CV required. AI-generated work will not be considered, and work must be original and made in the last three years. Notification is 15 December 2026, accepted work must reach Pembroke, North Carolina between 19 and 22 January 2027, and the exhibition runs 11 February to 3 March 2027. This is a non-profit gallery supported by the university, so work is not for sale during the show.
calls.summary: UNC Pembroke's 16th international juried show on environmental grief — $400/$200/$100 prizes, all media, juror Carla Rokes.

calls.org: Visual Arts Gallery, Governors State University
calls.description: The Visual Arts Gallery at Governors State University, south of Chicago, launches its first National Juried Exhibition and invites artists living anywhere in the United States to submit contemporary work. She will select works on artistic merit, conceptual strength and craftsmanship. Entry is $35 for up to three original works made in the past three years, submitted with an artist statement and full details for each piece. Work previously shown at the gallery is not eligible; Governors State alumni are welcome to apply. The exhibition is on view 7–18 December 2026 and 4–22 January 2027, with a closure across the university holiday break.

Hand deliveries are taken on 20 November and shipped work must arrive by 25 November with return paperwork and pre-paid postage included; the opening reception is 9 December and the show closes 23 January 2027.

calls.description: Artspace, a 501(c)(3) artist-run nonprofit gallery in Richmond, Virginia, opens its annual call for exhibition proposals for the 2027 season. calls.title: Roadblocks

The show hangs in Studio Montclair's Leach Gallery at 641 Bloomfield Avenue. Entry is free for Studio Montclair members and $42 for non-members, for a maximum of three works. Work must have been completed within the past five years, must not have been shown in any previous Studio Montclair exhibition, and giclée reproductions of original art are not accepted.

calls.title: Arnold Newman Prize for New Directions in Photographic Portraiture 2026
calls.description: A $20,000 unrestricted prize awarded annually to a photographer whose work demonstrates a compelling new vision in photographic portraiture, funded by the Arnold & Augusta Newman Foundation and administered by Maine Media in Rockport, Maine. A submission is a cohesive selection of up to 12 images plus an artist statement (500 words), a bio, a CV and a short statement on how the prize would further the applicant's career; artists may enter as many submissions as they like at $65 each. Fee waivers are offered through partner organisations including The Authority Collective, Black Women Photographers, Diversify Photo, Foto Feminas, Indigenous Photograph, Women Photograph and Indigo Arts Alliance, requested by September 11, 2026. Entries open August 19 and close 11:59pm EST on September 23, 2026, which the organiser states is final with no extensions. All entrants are notified by the end of October 2026.

calls.title: Book Artist in Residence 2028
calls.description: A four-week residency on Maine Media's campus in Rockport, Maine, running April 1-29, 2028, for artists who combine word and image in book form. The resident has unlimited access to the Charles Altschul Book Arts Studio - a Vandercook Universal I press, two etching presses, a photopolymer platemaker and bindery equipment - which sits next to the school's alternative-process photography lab. The programme is open to emerging and practising artists, book artists, letterpress printers and photographers who combine word and image, and is designed to help the resident complete a proposed, editioned project. Residents needing housing receive a $350 weekly stipend, up to $500 for materials and travel, campus meals when the cafeteria is open, and an apartment with a kitchen within walking distance; an applicant within driving distance who needs no housing receives $1,000 plus $500 for supplies. Collaborations are considered, with the same funding regardless of the number of participants. Selection is in two rounds - a written proposal, then an invited physical maquette of the proposed book, actual size, with at least two spreads. The resident donates two pieces from the edition to the Maine Media Gallery, gives a public lecture or other public engagement, and hosts an open studio. Applications are sent by email with an artist statement and CV, a one-page project description, an outline budget and ten images of recent work.
jury: Panel of artists and professionals in photography and book arts
calls.summary: Four weeks in Maine Media's book arts studio, with stipend, materials budget and housing, for photographers working with word and image.
