calls.title: Instant Open Call — 200 Years: Almost Now
calls.description: ZRNO, the Macedonian international festival of alternative photography, is selecting 22 artists for "200 Years: Almost Now", a group exhibition of contemporary instant photography that travels across Europe. Work made with any instant process is eligible, with no restriction on format, camera, film or technique - Polaroid, Instax, integral and peel-apart film, expired film, manipulated instant photographs, transfers, lifts, emulsion experiments and hybrids are all welcome. The curatorial frame takes the 200th anniversary of Niépce's first permanent photograph as its starting point and asks what defines photography as an artistic practice today, with particular emphasis on work that expands, manipulates or recontextualises the instant image through physical intervention. The exhibition is confirmed for Analogmania in Timișoara (October 2026), the Rotlicht Festival in Austria (November/December 2026), ZRNO in Macedonia (spring 2027) and Novi Sad in Serbia (2027), with further international venues possible. Submission is free and open to artists worldwide at any career stage, and the festival explicitly encourages women, queer, ethnic-minority and non-European applicants. Selected artists pay a participation fee of €200 for early applications or €250 later, covering press and media relations, promotional design, exhibition setup and dismantling at every venue, transport of the works between venues, gallery rental in Skopje and Vienna, opening events and a printed catalogue with a curatorial text; artists cover the cost of sending their work.
calls.summary: Instant photography selected for a group show touring Skopje, Vienna, Timișoara and Novi Sad, with a printed catalogue.

calls.title: 22nd International Alternative Processes Competition
calls.fee: $45 for 5 images, $5 per additional image up to 15
calls.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 22nd International Alternative Processes Competition, the annual juried show devoted to historic and handmade photographic processes at New York's longest-running co-operative photography gallery. Accepted processes include, but are not limited to, albumen, cyanotype, Van Dyke brown, platinum/palladium, gum bichromate, bromoil, salt print, tintype, ziatype, daguerreotype, image transfers, liquid emulsion, anthotypes, photogravure and chemigrams, as well as handmade prints made from digital negatives - the gallery's rule is that the image must originate in an alternative process and must not be AI-generated. There is no limitation on subject matter, and no image may measure more than 40 inches on its longest side. The juror is Amy Arbus, who photographed downtown New York for The Village Voice from 1980 to 1990 (the work that became On the Street 1980-1990), has published The Inconvenience of Being Born and The Fourth Wall, has taught at the International Center of Photography and Maine Media Workshops, and whose prints are held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, MoMA and the New York Public Library. Selected work is exhibited at the gallery's West 23rd Street space in Chelsea from 2 to 20 December 2026, with an opening reception on 3 December. Prizes are $300, $200 and $100 plus four honourable mentions, and the gallery takes 30% commission on sales during the show. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over, excluding Soho Photo Gallery members. Note that sohophoto.com's own competition page has not yet been rolled over from the 2025 edition - the current prospectus, dates and juror are on the CaFE listing linked here.
calls.summary: Historic and handmade photographic processes juried by Amy Arbus, exhibited in Chelsea. Cyanotype to daguerreotype welcome.

calls.title: The Streets
calls.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on street photography in all its registers - the photographer moving through public life as both observer and participant, attentive to gesture, chance, humour, tension and the fleeting relationships between people and place. Praxis seeks work that explores the streets from all angles, including people, public spaces, urban structures and documentary subject matter, in black and white or colour, traditional or experimental. The juror is Jonathan Pavlica. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (17 October - 14 November 2026) and featured on the gallery's online exhibition page. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future calls), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, printed catalogue and online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing.

calls.title: Street Photographers Foundation Awards 2026
calls.description: The Street Photographers Foundation's annual awards, open worldwide to professionals, students and enthusiasts alike, for photographs made on the street in the broadest sense of the word - mobile and analogue, conceptual and documentary, street portraits, urban, street fashion, road trips, street art, travel, architecture, abstract, graphic and large format. As the foundation puts it, the tools you use are not important. Entries are made either as a single photograph judged on its own or as a series of four to ten photographs judged together as one work. The 2026 jury is Chloe Coleman (photo editor at the Washington Post), Cheryl Dunn, Mary-Irene Marek of Leica Camera, foundation founder Masoud Gharaei, Magnum photographer Richard Kalvar and Stefano Mirabella of the Italian Street Photo Festival. First prizes of €1,000 go to the strongest single image and to the strongest series, each exhibited and given a featured article, and fifteen Jurors' Picks are selected for the exhibition. Photographers retain full copyright, entries stay private until results are announced, and winning work travels - the 2020 and 2021 awards became an exhibition of 62 photographs by 43 photographers at Galerie Joseph Le Palais in Paris. Photographs are accepted regardless of when they were taken. Entrants must be 18 or over, and for compliance reasons entries cannot be accepted from Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria or the regions of Crimea, Luhansk and Donetsk. A limited number of discretionary single-photo fee waivers is available to photographers who genuinely cannot afford the entry fee.
jury: Chloe Coleman, photo editor, Washington Post

Black Whimsy asks what happens when Black imagination has no limits, inviting artists to picture the ethereal, fantastical and otherworldly possibilities of Black life and creativity across the diaspora — the many surreal and dreamlike worlds in which Black people can exist — and to escape reality for a while. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; all art is accepted except corporate logos, personal advertising and video, and still JPEGs only, so photographic work is eligible. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after September 21, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.

calls.title: CURRENTS
calls.description: Shutter & Light Collective and Photographic Center Northwest present CURRENTS, a group exhibition exploring the versatility of analog photography and the photography culture growing throughout the Northwest. Work is welcomed from across the analog spectrum — scanned film, darkroom prints, instant film, pinhole, direct-positive processes, cyanotypes, alternative and experimental processes, and multimedia — and the show is curated through analog process, visual style and storytelling. There is no required subject matter and the theme is open. Artists may submit up to five works or series; prints should generally be no larger than 16 × 20 inches, and alternative presentations and unframed work are considered on request. Artists are responsible for printing and framing, with guidance offered by the organisers. The $3 fee is described as cost recovery only, with no-questions-asked waivers for artists facing financial or access barriers, and sales carry a voluntary 20% commission. Attendance at the November 12 opening is required of participating local artists. Exhibition runs November 2 – December 16, 2026 at PCNW in Seattle.

calls.title: Refusing Rehearsing Resisting
calls.org: VBKÖ – Austrian Association of Women Artists
calls.description: VBKÖ, the Austrian Association of Wom*n Artists founded in Vienna in 1910, invites proposals for its annual programme running March 2027 to February 2028. Following feminist, queer, anti-racist, anti-colonial and anti-authoritarian traditions, the call asks for projects that nurture communal care and build a platform for collective rehearsals imagining alternative futures — work that allows for tenderness, is not afraid of ugly feelings, and holds different truths. Proposals must bring together multiple artists, collectives or collaborative practices; solo exhibitions and single-artist presentations are not supported. Exhibition formats activated by public programming — screenings, performances, workshops, lectures — are encouraged. Each selected project receives a total budget of €4,000 covering artist fees and production, plus the VBKÖ space and shared kitchen, graphic design of promotional material, press announcements, photo documentation, up to 10 hours of technical support and use of the house technical equipment. Projects run 4 to 6 weeks. Applicants based outside Vienna must cover travel, accommodation and shipping from the project budget or external funding; VBKÖ provides invitation and support letters to help secure it. Applications go by email as a single PDF with a programme description, CVs for all participants, a financial plan based on Fair Pay principles, and three high-resolution images. Selected proposals are announced at the beginning of October 2026.
jury: VBKÖ board with an external jury member
calls.summary: Vienna's 1910-founded women artists' association funds a 4–6 week queer-feminist group programme; €4,000 per project, free to apply.

calls.title: The 9th John Ruskin Prize — Not for Present Delight
calls.description: Founded by the Guild of St George in 2012 and managed by Parker Harris under the administrative umbrella of The Big Draw, the John Ruskin Prize is a multidisciplinary art prize open to artists, designers and makers worldwide, amateur or professional, aged 18 and over. The ninth edition takes its theme, Not for Present Delight, from The Seven Lamps of Architecture, where Ruskin urged makers to build for their descendants rather than the present moment: the call asks what it means to create with an awareness of consequence, while also posing the challenge of whether art must serve a purpose beyond itself. Photography is named explicitly among the accepted media, alongside "Photographic Elements, Including Those Manipulated or Collaged" and "Collage, in all materials, including photography"; the prize has honoured photographers in past editions. Work must have been made in the past four years and submissions are judged digitally, with installations, diptychs and triptychs counted as a single artwork. The selection panel shortlists up to 80 artists for an exhibition at Trinity Buoy Wharf in London, running 28 January to 21 February 2027 with an awards evening on 27 January. Four winners share £9,500: a £3,000 first prize from the Guild of St George, the £1,000 Alan Davidson Under 26 Prize, the £3,000 Ruskin Mill Trust Prize for a beautifully crafted functional object, and the £2,500 Chelsea Arts Club Trust Prize for a mid-career artist without gallery representation. A GreatArt People's Choice Award adds £500 of materials. International entrants pay a reduced fee and are not obliged to ship work, showing online and in the catalogue instead. Entrants confirm at submission that the work was created by a human.
jury: Nichola Johnson, Chair, director of the Guild of St George
Clare Twomey, clay artist and curator
Adam Nathaniel Furman, artist and designer
calls.summary: Ruskin-inspired multidisciplinary UK prize naming photography outright. £9,500 across four awards plus a Trinity Buoy Wharf show.

calls.title: Wings of Hope Bird Photography Contest
calls.description: Knowing Hope, a US non-profit that funds medical care for children with chronic and catastrophic illness in under-resourced communities across Asia, has launched its first annual bird photography contest as a fundraiser. Photographers of all levels may enter four categories — Birds in Flight, Perched & Portrait, Behavior & Interaction, and Juvenile & Nesting — across two divisions: a novice division for those who have not sold prints, won photography awards or worked professionally, and an advanced division for everyone else. Entries are open to photographers aged 16 and over, with up to ten entries each and one to four photographs per entry; photographs may be spread across any combination of categories. AI-generated images are barred and basic adjustments are allowed, but elements may not be added, removed or substantially altered. Eight category and division winners receive equipment prizes including a Cotton Carrier harness, Vortex binoculars, a Delkin CFexpress card, a Wimberley Monogimbal head, a Think Tank backpack and a KelbyOne Pro membership. Judging is by Duade Paton, an Australian bird photographer and BirdLife Australia contributor; Marina Scarr, whose avian work has appeared in National Wildlife, Nature's Best Photography and Living Bird; and David Lindo, The Urban Birder, a judge for Bird Photographer of the Year and the British Wildlife Photography Awards. Each photograph is scored 1–5 on technical quality, composition and artistic merit, moment and impact, and overall impression. Photographers keep full copyright, granting the organisers a non-exclusive licence for promotional and fundraising use with credit. Winners are announced between 1 and 14 November 2026.
jury: Duade Paton, bird photographer and educator

calls.title: Dublin Art Book Fair 2026 — Artist Book Open Call

calls.title: 62nd Annual Open Juried Art Competition
calls.description: The Anaheim Art Association has run an open juried competition every year since the 1960s, and for the 62nd edition it again partners with the MuzeO Museum and Cultural Center, showing the selected work in the museum's main gallery in the Carnegie Building in downtown Anaheim. Photography is a judged category in its own right, split into Basic Photography and Manipulated Composite, with its own judge; the other categories are oil, acrylic, watercolour, drawing and pastel, and mixed media. There is no theme and no restriction on when the work was made. Cash awards and honourable mentions are given at the jurors' discretion, and a category is merged into the next smallest if it draws fewer than twelve entries. Work must be original, with no class work, nothing made under instruction and no AI-created or AI-assisted work; no reproductions or giclee copies of another artist's work are accepted, and where a photograph has been used as source material the photographer's written permission is required. Entries are capped at four per artist and at 43 inches in either direction including the frame, and everything must be framed or gallery-wrapped with wire hangers; the MuzeO takes a 30 per cent commission on sales. Note that everyone submitting may be asked either to help at check-in or to sit the gallery for one two-hour shift during the run, and that accepted work is hand-delivered on 6 or 7 November.
jury: Joe A. Oakes, landscape painter (fine art)
calls.summary: Photography is its own judged category with its own judge at this 62-year-old juried show inside the MuzeO Museum.

calls.title: Exhibition Submissions
calls.description: Waterworks Visual Arts Center in Salisbury, North Carolina is a non-collecting art museum accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, and it keeps a standing portfolio-review route into its exhibition programme. Each year the museum mounts three major rotating exhibitions of contemporary fine art and craft by local, regional, national and international artists, plus an annual outdoor sculpture show, and its past programme has repeatedly given solo shows to photographers. Submissions are read twice a year, after deadlines on 30 September and 30 January, and are reviewed within sixty to ninety days; the museum is clear that this is review only and not a guarantee of a show. Because the exhibition calendar is planned eighteen to twenty-four months ahead, a successful submission buys real time to prepare or make new work. Applicants send a current CV detailing education, grants, fellowships, awards, teaching, gallery affiliations, major exhibitions and collections, an artist statement written specifically about the body of work submitted and its influences, research, media and concepts, and ten to twenty high-quality images of current work that is available to exhibit, each labelled with title, medium, size, weight and completion date. All work must have been made within the last five years. Everything goes through the museum's SlideRoom portal.
calls.summary: Twice-yearly $10 portfolio route into an AAM-accredited museum that regularly gives photographers solo shows.

calls.title: The Truth about Cats and Dogs
calls.description: Not Shockboxx is a queer-owned gallery in Hermosa Beach that describes itself as artist-forward and built for work that does not fit neatly inside traditional systems. This call is for its online programme: artwork about the creatures we live with, admire, rescue, fear or simply cannot stop thinking about. The brief is deliberately wide — domestic, wild, mythical or microscopic, anything with fur, feathers, scales, shells, tentacles, hooves, wings or too many legs — and the gallery is explicit that cute is optional and weird is encouraged. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture, fiber, ceramics, printmaking, assemblage and video. Selected artists are shown in a two-month exhibition on Artsy, where the gallery is a partner, running 1 September to 31 October 2026. Entry is $20 per artwork with up to three works per artist, and the gallery says it cares about the work rather than the résumé, education, exhibition history or follower count. Artists 18 and over anywhere in the world may apply where they can meet shipping requirements. All accepted work must be priced for sale because Artsy does not permit NFS listings, and artists keep possession unless a piece sells. Work made wholly or partly with generative AI is ineligible.

calls.title: The Good Stuff
calls.description: Marking Suicide Prevention and Awareness Month, Not Shockboxx asks artists to notice what makes life worth staying for — not milestones or picture-perfect moments but the smaller, deeply personal things: the first quiet hour of the morning, a perfectly made cup of coffee, the particular way sunlight enters a room, a dog asleep at your feet, an inside joke, a song played a thousand times. The gallery is clear that a submitted piece does not need to address suicide or mental health directly; this call is about the other side of that conversation. Work can be joyful, tender, funny, strange, nostalgic, imperfect or almost impossible to explain, and the organisers suggest you may already have made it without realising where it belonged. All media and approaches are welcome, and the exhibition runs online through Artsy from 21 September to 20 November 2026 so audiences beyond the Hermosa Beach gallery can see it. Entry is $20; gallery artists and Backboxx Artist Society members apply free. Not Shockboxx welcomes work that is provocative, political, sexual, unsettling, profane or experimental, and it does not accept work made wholly or partly with generative AI. Accepted work must be priced for sale, since Artsy will not list NFS pieces.
calls.summary: For Suicide Prevention Month: the small things that keep you here. A two-month Artsy show, $20 entry, all media.

calls.title: The Food We Share
calls.description: Schack Art Center in Everett, Washington runs an annual Arts Education in Action exhibition, and for 2027 it wants work about food in its broadest sense: culture, family, connection, recipes, ritual, aesthetics, agriculture, nutrition, nostalgia, evolution, insecurity, comfort, entertainment and art. Photography is named explicitly among the media sought, next to painting, drawing, sculpture, furniture, printmaking, fiber, glass and video, and installation proposals are encouraged. Out of respect for those facing food insecurity the gallery discourages work made of food, and every accepted artist is asked to supply a favourite recipe for a booklet visitors take home. The call is open to artists living and working in the Pacific Northwest; entry is $5, with up to six pieces per artist, and work must not have shown at Schack before. Accepted pieces hang in the Main and Mezzanine Galleries from 25 March to 22 May 2027. All work must be for sale for the run of the show and Schack takes 40 percent. Nothing made in whole or part by AI is accepted.

calls.title: Prix Yzza Slaoui de la Découverte
calls.description: The Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech has created a new prize in memory of Yzza Slaoui, aimed at revealing and supporting one Moroccan photographer whose work shows a personal vision and real artistic quality. Entry is free and open exclusively to photographers of Moroccan nationality who own the rights to the images; the project must be unpublished in Morocco, or at least never have had a solo exhibition there. Dossiers may be written in French or English, and one project per photographer. A first selection is made by the festival's artistic committee before the international jury deliberates on 9 October 2026.
jury: Abdellah Oustad, Director, Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech
Adrian Radzyminski, Director, Fondation Yzza Slaoui

calls.title: Artist Residency Program
calls.description: The Art Center in Dover, New Hampshire gives three artists a four-month studio residency in its space at the Washington Street Mills, and thanks to a local benefactor it costs the selected artists nothing — the gallery values the opportunity at $2,500. Residents also help coordinate two artists' receptions and hang one exhibit during the term. This is studio space only; housing is not included, so it suits artists already within reach of the Seacoast. Applicants must be 18 or older and pay a $25 application fee, plus a $100 damage deposit returned at the end of the residency. The gallery takes 30 percent commission on work sold from the exhibition, and artists keep full rights to their images. Applications go through a form on the gallery's own site, with five examples of work, a CV and two character references sent by email.

calls.title: Beyond the Image Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Via Gluck 62 AIR, a non-profit cultural association with its own space on via Gluck in Milan, has launched the first edition of the Beyond the Image Art Prize, an international open call for contemporary photography, video art, experimental film, moving images and hybrid or installation-based practices that use photographic and audiovisual language. Its full title is "Who Are You Beyond the Image? Art, Neuroscience and Algorithmic Narration of Experience", and it grows out of SatisFace, a research project on the face, self-image perception and the neuroscientific, psychological and cultural implications of representing identity. The prize wants work that reflects on identity, image, body perception, digital technology and the algorithmic narration of experience, read through documentary, conceptual, poetic, critical or installation approaches. Two projects are selected, one by an emerging artist and one by an established artist, and each gets a solo exhibition in the association's Milan space plus a place in the official programme of the Milano Centrale Festival 2026, curatorial and organisational support, promotion, and a possible contribution towards production costs agreed with the artist. Entry is open to any nationality with no age, education or career requirements, and collectives may apply. Applicants send a project proposal of up to 2,500 characters with up to five supporting images, a CV and a portfolio, all under 25 MB total. The €19 fee is paid by bank transfer. The exhibition runs 2–30 October 2026, opening during the festival.
jury: Prof. Clelia Di Serio, Academic Board
Guido Nosari De Danieli, Artists Board
StayOnBoard Art Gallery, Galleries and Archives Board
Archivio Gabriele Basilico, Galleries and Archives Board

calls.title: Open Theme 2026
calls.description: An all-media open call from The Lab on Santa Fe, the gallery at 840 Santa Fe Drive that sits in the middle block of Denver's Art District on Santa Fe, where the gallery says the First Friday Art Walk pulls the largest crowds in the state. “Open theme” means no theme: the organisers want artists to take control and test what the space can hold, and they name photographers alongside painters, illustrators, printmakers, sculptors, video artists, installation artists, collage and assemblage artists, textile and fibre artists and ceramists. Nature, humanity, politics, chaos, transcendence — whatever pulls at you. They ask to feel the rigour inside your process, saying risk, intensity and the possibility of failure are all part of the atmosphere, but are emphatic that this is not meant to exclude anyone: all mediums, all styles, all subject matter, the only rule being to show you are open to your muse rather than trying to please. Entry is $34 for one or two works and one application per artist. Location eligibility is listed as national rather than Colorado-only. All submitted art must be for sale, measurements on applications must be accurate, and work can be turned away at drop-off for improper wiring; sales are split 58% to the artist and 42% to the gallery. The exhibition runs 5 to 27 February 2027.
calls.summary: No theme, all mediums, photographers named — a February 2027 show at a Denver Art District gallery. $34, 1–2 works.

calls.title: Solo Exhibition at Gallery VERY
calls.description: Gallery VERY, which describes itself as one of Boston's longest-running independent artist-run galleries, is looking for one artist to give a five-week solo exhibition in its 500-square-foot space in the SoWa arts district. No exhibition proposal is required — the gallery says it is selecting an artist, not a pre-planned exhibition, and Gallery Director John Guthrie will then work with the selected artist to develop a show for the space roughly six months after selection, with new work considered as the exhibition takes shape. Photography is named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, installation, video and interdisciplinary practices, and there are no restrictions on age, education, career stage or professional status. The gallery provides professional installation, an opening reception, a public artist talk, promotion, sales representation for the run of the show, and a permanent exhibition page on its website; sales are split 50/50, the artist covers transport both ways, and work is not insured by the gallery. Applications ask for 8–10 work samples that show a broad picture of your current practice (video artists may send 2–3 clips of up to three minutes with stills), a 200-word statement, a 100-word bio and a two-page CV. Location eligibility is regional: artists must live and work within approximately 250 miles of Boston, and the selected artist is expected to be present in person for the opening and the talk. VERY marks ten years in 2026 and presents four to five exhibitions a year. The CaFE portal opens on 24 August.
calls.summary: A five-week solo show at a ten-year-old Boston artist-run gallery. No proposal needed; photography named. $35.

calls.title: Chasing Ghosts 10: Piercing the Veil through Remembrance, Legacy & Beyond
calls.description: The tenth edition of Chasing Ghosts, the series Verum Ultimum's director conceived when the Portland gallery was celebrating its third year and describes as a favourite with artists and collectors alike. This year's edition is virtual. The emphasis, as always, is the idea of revealing the unseen, and “ghost” is not meant to be read literally — the gallery suggests this round's interpretations might be loaded with the added turmoil of the current social, health, environmental and political climate. It asks whether you express your deepest fears or concerns through your work, what parts of the past leave their mark on it, whether a legacy is revealed through your work or your process, and whether memory is a vital vehicle of expression for you. Any interpretation of the call is encouraged, and all mediums and modes of expression are welcome. Entry is $25 covering two images, with additional images at $5 each up to six; applicants must be 18 or older and the call is open internationally. Selected work is shown in Verum's virtual viewing galleries, which display work at scale, and carried through an exhibition book, an exhibition page, the website at large and blog posts, with social media promotion staying on the show for four weeks. Work may be listed for sale or entered as exhibition-only; the gallery takes a 30% commission on sales, provides prepaid shipping labels when work sells, and allows no substitutions of accepted work. The exhibition opens in mid-October and runs for a month.
calls.summary: Tenth edition of Verum Ultimum's long-running series on revealing the unseen — virtual this year, all media, $25.

The show runs 10 October to 8 November 2026 with an opening reception on 10 October from 4 to 6.30pm; acceptances go out on 20 September. No juror is named and no cash awards are listed.

calls.title: Fellowship Program 2027–2028
calls.description: Gallery Route One, the artist-run nonprofit in Point Reyes Station on the Marin coast, is offering two 24-month Fellowships running January 2027 to December 2028 to artists aged 21 to 40. Each Fellow receives a minimum of ten exhibition opportunities — including a solo exhibition in the Annex Gallery in 2027 and a two-person exhibition in the Center Gallery in 2028 — plus a $1,500 stipend to support the production and presentation of that work, mentoring and assistance producing the exhibitions, publicity and promotion, ongoing exposure on GRO's website and social media, and access to all GRO-sponsored professional development. Fellows also become eligible to be hired as Teaching Artists in GRO's Artists in the Schools programme, and work alongside the gallery's practising artist members curating and installing solo and group shows; GRO's call page adds that Fellows “do some volunteer work” during the fellowship period. Applicants must be aged 21 to 40, live and work in the greater Bay Area within commuting distance of Point Reyes Station, have a serious fine arts practice built on training, education and/or experience, and hold a cohesive portfolio of work completed within the last five years together with a developing focus or current area of inquiry and experimentation. GRO has run the Fellowship since 2014, and photography sits comfortably inside it — one past Fellow describes using the two years for a large-scale photography and oral history project, and the gallery separately runs a standing Latino Photography Project. The application asks for 8 to 10 images with dimensions in the filenames, an artist statement referencing two or three of them, a description of your studio practice, a CV and one reference, and it carries no entry fee. Applications are accepted only between 1 and 30 September 2026.

calls.title: Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program 2027: Thrive
calls.description: Thrive is the 2027 edition of the Kennedy Center's Access/VSA Emerging Young Artists Program, a Jean Kennedy Smith Arts and Disability Program that runs as a juried career development programme and exhibition for visual artists with disabilities aged 16 to 25 who live in the United States. The theme asks disabled artists to consider how their life and their art are flourishing: how the work is evolving and changing, and how the person is developing and growing. Fifteen artists are selected by a jury of industry professionals; each receives a $3,000 stipend and has one of their submitted pieces included in an exhibit in Washington, D.C. Winners are required to attend three virtual workshops (3 April, 1 May and 5 June 2027) and an all-expenses-paid series of career development workshops in Washington from 14 to 18 June 2027. Entry is free. All visual art forms and media are eligible if they meet the handling rules — 2D work no larger than 60 inches in height or width, 3D no larger than 48 inches in any direction when packed, nothing perishable — and work must have been completed in the last three years and after the onset of disability. Applicants submit images or video of at least three different pieces, and are told to show a portfolio rather than several views of one work, alongside four 300-word answers on themselves, their process, the perspective they would bring and their future plans. Previous programme winners cannot reapply, group projects are not considered, and artwork created with generative AI is ineligible. Selected applicants are asked to document their disability, age and right to work in the US before the final round, and must be willing to publicly disclose that they have a disability in all materials and public appearances associated with the programme. Accommodations and alternate application formats can be requested until 30 October 2026. The submission portal opens on 24 August.
calls.summary: Fifteen disabled US artists aged 16–25 each win $3,000 and a Washington, D.C. exhibition. Free to enter.

calls.title: Open Door: 2027 Exhibition & Residency
calls.description: Open Door is Kinhouse's annual call for its next programming year, and the 2027 round wants exhibition proposals from emerging and mid-career artists and curators — solo, two- and three-person shows, collaborations, artist collectives, performances, installations and site-specific work, as well as proposals from curators wanting to organise a show in the space. Three or four proposals are selected by Kinhouse Director Kaylan Buteyn, and every chosen exhibition is paired with a fully funded six-night residency at the Kinhouse Residency, a three-bedroom house with a detached studio a three-minute drive from the gallery, timed so that the opening reception falls on the Friday of the residency week. Shows then hang for the month following that First Friday opening and are promoted through the gallery's channels, its newsletter and the Broadway Arts District's First Friday programming, with professional documentation provided and installation support on site. All art mediums are accepted for consideration, though video and screen-based submissions may require extra support, and work samples may be works in progress or ideas still waiting to be developed rather than finished pieces. The gallery says it is especially drawn to work engaging community, care, belonging, the domestic, parenting, craft and lineage — the values that shape its programme — but proposals do not have to sit inside that scope. Entry is $34 for one proposal and up to three proposals may be submitted. Work does not have to be for sale, though it is preferred; selected artists sign an exhibition contract with a 20% gallery commission, paid out within two weeks of the show closing. The call is open internationally, but Kinhouse cannot cover travel or shipping, and artists ship work both ways unless it sells.
calls.summary: A funded six-night Indiana residency paired with your own show at an artist-run Fort Wayne gallery. All media, $34.

calls.title: 61st CAIN National
calls.description: An open-theme, all-media national juried exhibition at Del Mar College's Joseph A. Cain Memorial Gallery in Corpus Christi, founded in 1966 and formerly the Annual National Drawing & Small Sculpture Show — renamed to reflect a broader range of media. Photography is named among the accepted 2-D categories alongside drawing, painting, printmaking in traditional media and original watercolor; sculpture of any media is also considered, though nothing requiring ceiling suspension. $10,000 in Purchase Awards are decided by the juror and the college art faculty, and purchased work joins Del Mar's permanent collection. This year's juror is Jamie Bates, a ceramic artist and Associate Professor of Ceramics at the University of Oklahoma, who also gives a free public art talk on February 18. Open to artists residing in the United States, excluding full-time Del Mar art faculty; work must have been created in the last three years and must not have been shown previously in the Annual Show. Each artist may submit three works, one image per artwork. Entries open on CaFÉ on September 1, 2026 and close November 30, 2026; notification goes out January 8, 2027, accepted work must arrive by January 30, and the exhibition runs February 19 – April 19, 2027. Work does not have to be for sale — the gallery publishes a price list and connects artists with buyers but takes no other part in sales — and artists are responsible for all return shipping costs.
jury: Jamie Bates, Associate Professor of Ceramics, University of Oklahoma

calls.title: Art Omi: Artists Residency 2027
calls.description: A three-and-a-half-week summer residency on Art Omi's 300-acre campus in New York's Hudson Valley, gathering roughly two dozen international artists to work, collaborate and share ideas. Residents are given a private bedroom in shared living quarters, a private studio and three meals a day at no cost, and are responsible for their own travel and materials unless eligible for one of the fellowship travel grants. Two critics or curators join each session as Critics-in-Residence, leading discussions and making individual studio visits, while the Visitors Program brings critics, curators, gallerists and established artists to the campus; the session ends with a public Open Studios event. Facilities include indoor and protected outdoor studios, a kiln and basic hand tools, with professional colour photography labs in nearby Ghent. Open to artists anywhere in the world who have been professionally active for at least the past five years — disciplines include visual arts, sound art, performance and social practice, and having studied art is not a requirement, though a CV must show five years of practice. Current BFA and MFA students are not eligible, nor are past Art Omi residents; applicants must be 18 or over, submitted work must date from the past ten years, and applications must be written in English. Several fellowships add stipends of $500 to $2,000 plus travel grants, flagged inside the same application and in some cases awarded automatically to every eligible artist, among them the American Dream Fellowship for an artist who has never been to the United States, the Every Page Foundation Fellowship for a female artist from an underserved community, and the Unlimit Art Fellowship for artists with disabilities. Artists legally resident in Australia, the Basque Country or Croatia are told by the application form to use their own dedicated fellowship calls instead, while the residency page says they may enter both pools, which separate panels review. In 2026, 24 artists attended out of 1,395 applicants, and Art Omi aims for roughly 75% of residents to come from outside the US. Applications close September 14, 2026, decisions are sent January 1, 2027, and the session runs June 17 – July 12, 2027.

calls.title: Portsmouth Open 26
calls.description: A new curated group exhibition at Art Space, Portsmouth, staged as part of Photo Fringe 2026 by the volunteer-led Brighton photography charity behind the biennial open-platform festival. The show reads archives as feedback loops — how photographs, documents, objects, memories and stories are continually revisited, reinterpreted and reshaped — and looks for artists whose practice engages with personal, family, community, institutional, cultural, historical, digital or found archives, or that questions what constitutes an archive at all. Rephotography, appropriation, collage, installation, moving image, sound and text are all welcomed, and existing or new work may be submitted provided the relationship to the curatorial premise is clear. Open to photographers and lens-based artists working in any medium; solo artists and collectives may both apply. There are no submission fees. Apply by email with up to 300 words — or a BSL, English audio or video application of no more than three minutes — up to 12 JPEGs (72 dpi, each under 3MB) or a screener link for moving image, and a website or Instagram link. Selected artists print and provide their own work with suitable hanging options, install and de-install with support from the Photo Fringe team, and contribute to the invigilation timetable; Photo Fringe takes 35% commission on sales to help cover staffing, and travel, transport and accommodation cannot be reimbursed unless otherwise agreed. Applications are assessed by Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco, who also selects one artist from the exhibiting cohort for a jury award of mentorship plus an in-depth written interview published on the Photo Fringe website. Entries close 8 September 2026, the shortlist is notified 15 September, the private view is 23 October and the exhibition runs 24–25 October 2026, during the 2–31 October festival.
jury: Ricardo Reverón Blanco, Producer, Photo Fringe
calls.summary: Free Photo Fringe open call for a Portsmouth group show on archives as feedback loops, with a mentorship jury award.

calls.title: 2027 Workspace Artist Residency
calls.description: Center for Book Arts awards up to four New York-based emerging and mid-career artists a six-month keyholder residency running April to September 2027, inviting them to explore the book as a time-based medium — "a sequence of spaces, each space perceived at a different moment", in Ulises Carrión's phrase — and as a tool for political engagement, since printmaking and independent publishing have long been central to social and cultural transformation. Residents receive 24/7 keyholder access to shared studio space for six months, a $1,500 honorarium, a $500 material stipend, storage space, basic supplies and tools, free classes in bookbinding, letterpress and RISO, consultations and professional development with staff and visiting curators, scheduled site visits to partner institutions working with artists' books and publishing, support from volunteers, access to Materials for the Arts, and opportunities to present work in exhibitions and public programs. Applications are reviewed blind by an independent panel of arts professionals from a broad range of backgrounds. The program promotes experimentation in book arts and artists from all disciplinary backgrounds are encouraged to apply — CBA aims for a balanced cohort of experienced book artists and artists working in other disciplines with a clear interest in exploring the field. Applications ask for an artist statement and CV, a portfolio of work samples, and a brief proposal naming the projects you would pursue and the equipment, tools and classes at CBA that most interest you. Housing is not provided. The selection panel meets in early October, shortlisted artists are interviewed virtually in mid-October, residencies begin in April 2027, and residents present their work in an artist talk at the end of the program and take part in a group exhibition in 2029.
calls.summary: Six-month keyholder residency at Center for Book Arts for New York-based artists, with a $1,500 honorarium and free classes.
